title: Trump Says Tariffs Politically Risky, But He’s Not Rushing Deals
content: President Donald Trump acknowledged that his sweeping tariff program had risked imperiling him politically, but said he would not rush deals to appease nervous investors during a town hall on Wednesday.

title: South Korea’s Export Growth Stalls as US Tariffs Sap Demand
content: South Korea’s export growth stalled in April in a worrisome sign for the trade-driven economy as officials scramble to cope with Donald Trump’s sweeping tariff campaign.

title: US Has Reached Out to China to Initiate Tariff Talks, CCTV Says
content: US President Donald Trump’s administration has been seeking contact with Beijing to initiate talks on the massive tariffs Washington has imposed on China, according to a state-run media outlet.

title: Labour Should Be Ready to Bend Rules During Trade Talks, IPPR Says
content: The UK’s Labour government must be willing to bend international rules and ease its concerns over other countries’ human rights records when negotiating new trade partnerships, the left-wing Institute for Public Policy Research think tank said.

title: Goldman Sachs’ CEO Talks Policy Uncertainty, Tariffs
content: On today’s Big Take: How Goldman Sachs CEO David Solomon is assessing the economic impact of Donald Trump’s trade war.

title: EU to Present New Trade Proposals to US Negotiators Next Week
content: The European Union is planning to share a paper with the US next week that will set out a package of proposals to kick-start trade negotiations with the Trump administration.

title: Colombia Stuns and Cuts Rates to 9.25% After Petro’s Demands
content: Colombia’s central bank unexpectedly cut its interest rate by 25 basis points, handing President Gustavo Petro a win while raising more doubts over monetary policy that’s been clouded by public spending and global volatility.

title: Mexico Economy Narrowly Dodges Recession Amid US Trade Chaos
content: Mexico’s economy expanded slightly in the first quarter on a jump in agricultural output, allowing President Claudia Sheinbaum to avoid recession as she steers the nation through an unpredictable US tariff policy.

title: Russia Raises 2025 Deficit Target on Lower Revenue Expectations
content: The Russian Finance Ministry increased its budget deficit target for this year after expectations for revenue and the oil price were reduced.

title: Loonie Gains on Trump Saying Carney Wants to Make a Deal
content: US President Donald Trump said newly elected Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney plans to visit the White House within the next week.

title: Gold Pares Losses as Traders Assess Fed Rate Path After US Data
content: Gold pared losses as traders assessed the Federal Reserve’s interest-rate path after US data showed signs of downside risks under President Donald Trump’s trade agenda.

title: Trump’s ‘Erratic’ Tariff Policy Prompted Bank of Canada Pause
content: Bank of Canada officials considered cutting interest rates at their April meeting before opting to wait for more information as they weighed the volatile changes in US President Donald Trump’s trade policy.

title: How Donald Trump Became India’s New Best Friend
content: On this episode of Trumponomics, we discuss why India stands to gain from the US trade war with China and the rest of the world.

title: Why Did the US Economy Shrink in Early 2025?
content: What’s the single best way to measure the health of a country’s economy? For most experts, there is little debate that gross domestic product, a quarterly tally of all the goods and services a country produces, is the gold standard for assessing and comparing economic activity.

title: Zimbabwe Traders Face a Future of Losses From Once-Bullish Stock Market
content: Zimbabwe stock traders, long used to profiting from currency chaos that has spurred demand for equities, are counting their losses as a liquidity crunch curtails business.

title: Trump Says He’s Off to Best Start as President. The Economy Says Something Else
content: Trump’s second term begins with a decline in US GDP, while jobs and prices hold steady. On almost all fronts, the outlook is getting worse.

title: US Consumer Spending Jumps While Key Inflation Gauge Slows Down
content: US consumer spending jumped in March while a key measure of inflation decelerated, a welcome reprieve before tariffs are expected to broadly drive up prices.

title: US Economy Contracts for First Time Since 2022 on Imports Surge
content: The US economy contracted at the start of the year for the first time since 2022 on a monumental pre-tariffs import surge and more moderate consumer spending, a first snapshot of the ripple effects from President Donald Trump’s trade policy.

title: Australian House Prices Hit Record High Ahead of Saturday’s Vote
content: Australian home prices climbed for a third straight month to a record high ahead of an election on Saturday, while defying rising uncertainty over the economic fallout from US-driven global trade turmoil.

title: US Pending Sales of Existing Homes Increase by Most Since 2023
content: Pending sales of previously owned US homes rose in March by the most in more than a year as a brief dip in mortgage rates and a rising supply of houses brought out spring shoppers.

title: Tanzania Says $42 Billion LNG Deal Delayed On Local Content Use
content: Tanzania’s Deputy Prime Minister Doto Biteko said the government wants to agree the terms of a long-delayed $42 billion liquefied natural gas facility with international oil companies by October.

title: Rolls-Royce Backs 2025 Outlook, Says Tariffs Are Manageable
content: Rolls-Royce Holdings Plc expressed confidence the aircraft engine supplier can meet its financial goals for the year despite the uncertainty caused by the introduction of new tariffs.

title: US Vaccine Watchdog Effort Begins as Measles Surge Draws Alarm
content: The Center for Infectious Disease Research and Policy at the University of Minnesota has quietly begun to steer a national initiative to safeguard the scientific foundations of US vaccine policy — a bold move at a time of mounting political interference and an escalating measles outbreak.

title: Lloyds Income Boosted as Homebuyers Rushed to Beat Stamp Duty
content: Lloyds Banking Group Plc ramped up lending in the first quarter, helping it broadly meet earnings expectations even as it set aside more to prepare for a worsening economy.

title: Tesla Chair Says Report of CEO Search to Replace Musk ‘False’
content: Tesla Inc. Chair Robyn Denholm denied a report that the board had looked to replace Chief Executive Officer Elon Musk, saying directors are “highly confident” in his ability.

title: Macau Gaming Revenue Better Than Feared Ahead of Golden Week
content: Macau’s gaming revenue rose 1.7% in April, exceeding analyst expectation for a decline, signaling stronger tourism demand ahead of China’s May “Golden Week” holiday starting Thursday.

title: FDA to Mandate Placebo-Controlled Trials for New Vaccines
content: The US Food and Drug Administration will require all new vaccines to undergo placebo-controlled trials before approval — a policy shift that could reshape how immunizations are developed.

title: Quebec Government Won’t Rescue Bankrupt Bus Maker Lion Electric
content: Canadian electric bus and truck maker Lion Electric Co. is unlikely to survive as the Quebec government turned down an opportunity to put money into the firm along with local investors.

title: Starbucks Seeks to Slash Million-Dollar Store Renovation Costs
content: Starbucks Corp. is looking to cut how much it spends upgrading stores, which could help address investor anxiety over the price tag of turning the chain around.

title: TSG Consumer Nears Investment in Cookie Chain Crumbl
content: Private equity firm TSG Consumer Partners is in advanced talks to invest in Crumbl, the fast-growing cookie and dessert chain, according to people with knowledge of the matter.

title: FC Barcelona to Move US Headquarters to Miami From New York City
content: FC Barcelona will move its US commercial operations to Miami from New York, burnishing the South Florida city’s reputation as an American soccer hub.

title: Big Price Hikes Undercut Trump Bet China Will Absorb Tariffs
content: Donald Trump says China will likely bear the brunt of his 145% tariff on the world’s second-largest economy. But prices from some of the most popular sellers of made-in-China goods already suggest US shoppers will be paying a major portion of the bill.

title: Trade War Leads Canadian Pacific Kansas City Railway to Lower 2025 Guidance
content: Canadian Pacific Kansas City Ltd. cut its financial outlook for this year due to the uncertainty caused by the US administration’s tariff and trade policy.

title: Telefonica’s Movistar Faces Venezuela Data Leak, NGO Says
content: A local non-profit reported a massive data leak from Spain’s Telefonica SA subsidiary in Venezuela, Movistar, which exposed the personal data of millions of clients, highlighting the vulnerability of the country’s digital communications.

title: Loose Cigarettes, Shorter Calls Mark Slowdown for Mexican Firms
content: As US tariff threats continue to wreak havoc on the Mexican economy, consumers are cutting back on everything from cell service and coffee to cigarettes and tequila. That’s hitting the country’s biggest companies including billionaire Carlos Slim’s wireless provider America Movil SAB and retail conglomerate Femsa.

title: For Musk, By Musk: World’s Richest Man Adds a Texas City to His Empire
content: With this weekend’s vote to incorporate, the billionaire’s takeover of Starbase will be complete.

title: Robinhood Tops Estimates Amid Volatility as Crypto Slows
content: Retail investors flocked to Robinhood Markets Inc. as President Donald Trump’s global tariffs roiled markets, boosting the company’s revenue and earnings, even as growth in cryptocurrency revenue slowed.

title: Disney, Universal Score China Film Dates Despite Trade Woes
content: China is keeping the door open for Hollywood movies, even with the ongoing trade dispute with the US.

title: Wingstop Shares Rebound After Projecting Return to Growth
content: Wingstop Inc. shares gained the most in more than two years Wednesday after flagging that same-stores sales will recover in the second half of the year.

title: Airbus Tells US Airlines They’ll Need to Pay Their Own Tariffs
content: Airbus SE said it won’t cover the cost of tariffs on its planes imported by US airlines, setting up a clash with carriers unwilling to shoulder surcharges imposed by President Donald Trump.

title: Visa CEO Says AI Shopping to Push Advertising, Payments to Adapt
content: Visa Inc. Chief Executive Officer Ryan McInerney said advertising will be forced to evolve as shoppers turn to artificial intelligence agents to help them browse products and make purchases.

title: Rivian Stockpiled EV Batteries From Asia Ahead of Trump Tariffs
content: Rivian Automotive Inc. quietly built a reserve of electric-vehicle batteries from Asia ahead of President Donald Trump’s tariffs, giving the company a measure of insurance against the upheaval in trade policy now pressuring the automotive supply chain.

title: Brazil Denies Plans for Red Soccer World Cup Jersey After Political Backlash
content: Brazil’s iconic yellow soccer jersey has become such a potent conservative political symbol that many leftists refuse to wear it. Now, rumors the team might don a different color with deep associations to the left at the 2026 World Cup are inflaming the right.

title: Argentina’s Flagship Airline Won’t Be Subsidized for First Time Since 2008
content: Argentina’s flagship airline won’t need state subsidies for the first time since the government nationalized the company almost two decades ago, according to a press release Wednesday.

title: Ford to Delay Price Increases to See How Rivals React to Tariffs
content: Ford Motor Co. won’t increase the price of its vehicles until it sees how competing carmakers respond to higher costs imposed by President Donald Trump’s tariffs.

title: America Movil’s Profit Misses on Slowing Mexican Economy
content: Billionaire Carlos Slim’s wireless provider America Movil SAB missed net income projections for the first quarter after an economic slowdown in its two biggest markets led to more than a million prepaid subscribers disconnecting their service.

title: CDC Launches Team to Manage the Fallout From Deep Staff Cuts
content: The US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention is creating a temporary strike force to manage the fallout of sweeping workforce cuts, according to an email obtained by Bloomberg News.

title: BlackRock-Backed Suez Taps HSBC to Review China Assets
content: Suez SA is reviewing its Chinese water infrastructure assets, people familiar with the matter said, as the French water utility looks at potential ways to streamline its global operations.

title: Spain’s Antitrust Agency Set to Clear BBVA’s Sabadell Bid
content: Spain’s antitrust agency approved with strict conditions BBVA SA’s €13 billion ($14.8 billion) bid to buy smaller rival Banco Sabadell SA, setting the stage for the government to have a final say in the year-long takeover fight, according to a person familiar with the matter.

title: BBVA Hires Bankers Including L’Heureux in LevFin Shake-Up
content: BBVA SA has hired a trio of leveraged finance bankers, including Louis L’Heureux, into newly-created roles as Spain’s second-biggest bank looks to bulk up its presence and capabilities in the asset class.

title: JPMorgan Names Kresse Co-Head of Unit Catering to Silicon Valley
content: JPMorgan Chase & Co. named Andrew Kresse to co-lead the innovation economy business in its commercial bank, a key growth area as the biggest US bank seeks to become the go-to firm for startups and their venture-capital backers.

title: Legislators propose upgraded tax credit for short line rail maintenance
content: New legislation would upgrade a federal tax credit short line railroads depend on for infrastructure spending.

title: Subscription scams surge across hundreds of fake websites - how to stay safe
content: Subscription scams are popping up on social media sites, attempting to trick users out of their credit card information.

title: Trump’s Trade War Is Helping Unite Chinese People Around Xi
content: This week we look at how attitudes toward President Xi Jinping’s government have shifted among businesses and the broader public in China when it comes to the US-China trade war.

title: Europe Nears Inflation Target While Fretting Over Tariffs
content: Welcome to the Brussels Edition, Bloomberg’s daily briefing on what matters most in the heart of the European Union.

title: Romania’s Testy Election Rerun Raises Risks for Investors
content: Hi, this is Irina Vilcu and Andra Timu in Bucharest. Welcome to our weekly newsletter on what’s shaping economics and investments from the Baltic Sea to the Balkans. You can subscribe here.

title: Point72 Macro Portfolio Managers Ng and Blanchard Leave Firm
content: Point72 Asset Management macro portfolio manager Yau Ng has retired from the nearly $37 billion hedge fund giant after more than six years, said people with knowledge of the matter.

title: Big Farming’s Big Battleground: an English Village Makes a Stand
content: If Britain is going to wean itself off pig and chicken meat imports, producers argue output should rise. But locals disagree.

content: AI and automation are becoming part of the American manufacturing landscape. We meet with a predictive maintenance company and visit a research facility to understand how AI might reshape factories. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Waltz Leaving Top NSA Position | Balance of Power: Late Edition
content: "Balance of Power: Late Edition" focuses on the intersection of politics and global business. On today's show, Senator Chris Coons, Greenwich Media Strategies Founder, CEO, and National Security Council Former Director for Syria and Lebanon Hagar Chemali, Rep. Raja Krishnamoorthhi, The Madison Group Managing Partner and Republican Strategist Robb Watters, Former Aide to President Obama and Democratic Strategist Robert Fisk. (Source: Bloomberg)

content: Source: Bloomberg, 4:40

title: Chemali on Trump Adding Secondary Iran Oil Sanctions
content: Greenwich Media Strategies Founder, CEO, and National Security Council Former Director for Syria and Lebanon, Hagar Chemali gives her thoughts on President Trump adding secondary Iran oil sanctions and says China will be hurt by this. She speaks with Kailey Leinz and Joe Mathieu on "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Trump Deportations Under Wartime Law Blocked by US Judge
content: A federal judge in Texas ruled that President Donald Trump improperly invoked a 227-year-old wartime law to deport accused Venezuelan gang members to an El Salvador prison, setting up what may become another high-stakes battle at the US Supreme Court.

title: Medicaid Standoff Splits Republicans
content: The Madison Group Managing Partner and Republican Strategist Robb Watters says there will not be Medicaid cuts. Former Aide to President Obama and Democratic Strategist Robert Fisk believes we'll see a slowing of the growth of Medicaid. They speak with Kailey Leinz and Joe Mathieu on "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Australia Election: What's At Stake
content:
Australians will soon vote in a national election that's been dominated by cost of living concerns, but also hasn't escaped the shadow of Donald Trump's trade war.

Here's what is on the ballot. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Election Countdown Begins as Albanese Seeks a Second Term
content: Good morning, it’s Amy in Melbourne with your election eve newsletter. Today’s must-reads:• Opposition releases policy costings • Billionaire pledges money for Trump• Test looms for banking stocks

title: Harris Condemns Trump, Skips Governor Talk In Reemergence Speech
content: Questions on her potential run for California office were left hanging

title: Hegseth Should Be Fired: Sen. Coons
content: Senator Chris Coons says he thinks Pete Hegseth is who should be fired after "Signalgate." In an interview on "Balance of Power," Senator Coons tells Kailey Leinz and Joe Mathieu he's willing to vote "no" for the nomination of Mike Waltz for UN ambassador, but will keep an open mind.  (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Temu Ditches Chinese Imports Model to Avoid Trump’s Tariffs
content: Temu is abandoning the model centered around cheap Chinese imports that catapulted it to success in the US, aiming to sell only goods from local merchants to American consumers for the foreseeable future.

title: OpenAI Can’t Dodge Musk’s Fraud Claims in Restructuring Suit
content: A judge narrowed claims in Elon Musk’s lawsuit alleging that OpenAI broke its promise to function as a public charity by making plans to transform itself into a for-profit business.

title: What’s the De Minimis Tariff Loophole That Trump Has Closed?
content: A Latin term that used to be little-known outside the world of customs brokers has become the stuff of headlines. That’s thanks to a decision by US President Donald Trump to close a tariff loophole for “de minimis” merchandise from mainland China and Hong Kong from May 2.

title: Toyota, Nintendo Face Tariff Risk: Asia Earnings Week Ahead
content: Toyota Motor Corp. kicks off Japanese automotive earnings on the heels of President Donald Trump signing directives this week that eased the worst investor fears about US tariffs.

title: Blue Owl-Owned Stack Seeks $833 Million Loan for Asia Growth
content: Blue Owl Capital-owned data center operator Stack Infrastructure Inc. is seeking an about A$1.3 billion ($833 million) loan, according to people familiar with the matter, as demand for artificial intelligence and cloud services accelerates in Asia.

title: Prosecutors May Widen Charges in Singapore Nvidia Fraud Case
content: Singaporean prosecutors secured eight more weeks to deepen a probe and potentially bring more charges against three men accused of fraud in shipping servers likely containing Nvidia Corp. chips banned from China.

title: Apple to Source Billions of US-Made Chips in Supply Chain Shift
content: Apple Inc. plans to source more than 19 billion chips from the US this year, part of a global supply chain shift to gradually lessen its reliance on China and elevate India for iPhone production.

title: Microsoft Raises Xbox and Game Prices, Citing Rising Costs
content: Microsoft Corp. is raising prices on its Xbox games, consoles and accessories amid broader uncertainty about how the ongoing trade war will impact supply chains and the gaming industry.

title: Apple Renews Fears About Tariffs, China Slump With Wobbly Report
content: Apple Inc.’s much-awaited quarterly earnings report failed to soothe investor concerns about its biggest challenges, including escalating tariff costs and a slowdown in China.

title: Whole Foods Union Victory Upheld by US Labor Board Official
content: Whole Foods Market’s effort to overturn a unionization vote at a Philadelphia store was rejected by a US labor board official, a step towards requiring Amazon.com Inc.’s grocery chain to collectively bargain with US employees for the first time.

title: Block Shares Sink After Payments Company Cuts Profit Guidance
content: Shares of Block Inc. sank in late trading after the digital-payments company led by Jack Dorsey posted first-quarter results below analysts’ estimates and lowered its full-year profit guidance as a result of a more challenging macroeconomic environment.

title: Amazon Braces for Tougher Business Climate Amid Trump Trade War
content: Amazon.com Inc. said it’s bracing for a tougher business climate in the coming months, echoing concerns from a range of companies that tariffs and related economic turmoil could crimp consumer spending.

title: CIA Boosts Social Media Campaign to Recruit Chinese Officials
content: The Central Intelligence Agency released two videos Thursday aimed at recruiting Chinese officials who might be disillusioned by their prospects in government in a bid to get them to share top secrets about China with the US.

title: Apple’s Sales to Rise in ‘Low to Mid-Single Digit’ Percent Range
content: Apple Inc. said it expects revenue in the current period to grow in the “low- to mid-single digit” percentage range from a year earlier.

title: Apple Says Tariffs Will Add $900 Million in Costs This Quarter
content: Apple Inc. Chief Executive Officer Tim Cook said that planned US tariffs on foreign imports will add $900 million in costs in the current period.

title: Duolingo Boosts Outlook as AI Drives Top-Tier Subscriptions
content: Duolingo Inc. raised its full-year sales and profit outlook as artificial intelligence offerings drive users to its higher-priced subscriptions.

title: Reddit Surges After Posting Sales Beating Analyst Estimates
content: Reddit Inc. shares jumped after it said revenue in the current quarter will be better than estimates, a sign that a broader dip in the economy hasn’t yet dented the digital advertising industry.

title: Harrods Is Latest UK Retailer to Battle Against Hacking Attacks
content: London’s luxury department store Harrods Ltd. reported hacking attempts Thursday, just days after two other UK retailers said they were attacked.

title: Instacart Gives Rosy Outlook After Best Order Growth Since 2022
content: Instacart posted its strongest order growth since 2022 for the first quarter and projected better-than-expected earnings for the current period, a sign of resilience in its core delivery business and growing grocery software and advertising unit.

title: Airbnb Gives Weak Outlook, Citing Softness in US Travel Demand
content: Airbnb Inc. issued a weak outlook for the second quarter, following online travel peer Booking Holdings Inc. in blaming economic uncertainties for softer travel demand in the US.

title: ‘60 Minutes’ to Air Story on Trump’s Targeting of Law Firms
content: Less than three weeks after President Donald Trump criticized 60 Minutes for what he said were too many critical stories, the newsmagazine announced plans to air a piece about his efforts to target law firms through executive orders.

title: The Danger of AI Chatbots Saying Exactly What You Want to Hear
content: OpenAI is taking steps to make ChatGPT less sycophantic, though the problem may be tough to solve completely. But first...

title: Microsoft, Meta Allay Tariff Fears; Apple Dealt a Blow | Bloomberg Technology
content: Bloomberg’s Caroline Hyde and Ed Ludlow discuss Microsoft’s and Meta’s earnings beats. Plus, Carolina Milanesi, president and principal analyst at Creative Strategies, explains what investors are waiting to hear from Apple when the iPhone maker reports results. Andy McLoughlin, managing partner at Uncork Capital, also joins to talk about the firm's new $300 million fund and its search for the next big AI startup. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Lightspeed Is Latest Firm to Shift Away From Classic VC Model
content: Lightspeed Venture Partners, one of Silicon Valley’s largest venture capital firms, has changed its regulatory status to broaden its range of investments — following similar moves by Sequoia Capital, Andreessen Horowitz and General Catalyst as they shift away from the traditional VC playbook.

title: Trump-Tied Stablecoin Used for MGX’s $2 Billion Binance Deal
content: World Liberty Financial, the Trump family’s decentralized finance project, said its new stablecoin is being used for a $2 billion investment in crypto exchange Binance Holdings Ltd. by Abu Dhabi’s MGX.

title: Uber Launches Product for Seniors, With Rival Lyft Following Suit
content: Uber Technologies Inc. debuted a simpler version of its rideshare app to make it easier for older adults to get around, prompting rival Lyft Inc. to move up the launch announcement of a similar feature it had in the works.

title: Can Anyone Supplant Joe Rogan as the Most Popular Podcaster?
content: The comedian’s influential show has sat at No. 1 on the chart of the most popular podcasts in the US for over five years

title: Apple’s Chaotic Month Culminates in Tariff-Focused Earnings Test
content: Apple Inc. shares have clawed back a good portion of the ground they lost in the historic tariff-induced selloff last month, but that doesn’t mean investors are in the clear.

title: LinkedIn Shares Advertising Revenue With Creators In Video Push
content: LinkedIn will begin sharing advertising revenue with creators for the first time, as video content boosts the amount of time people spend on the site.

title: Ocado’s Total Bond Bill Set to Be Triple Last Year’s Amount
content: With Ocado Group Plc having wrapped up the sale of its latest bond, the company’s total annual interest bill is now close to £100 million ($133 million) — more than triple what it was paying this time last year.

title: Japan’s Kato Says US Treasury Holdings Could Be Negotiation Card
content: Japan’s Finance Minister Katsunobu Kato said the country’s US Treasury holdings could be a card in its trade talks with Washington, referring to the largest stockpile of US debt held by a foreign nation.

title: What’s the De Minimis Tariff Loophole That Trump Has Closed?
content: A Latin term that used to be little-known outside the world of customs brokers has become the stuff of headlines. That’s thanks to a decision by US President Donald Trump to close a tariff loophole for “de minimis” merchandise from mainland China and Hong Kong from May 2.

title: China Shipping Loophole Closed by Trump, Raising Prices for US Consumers
content: Small-value packages shipped to the US from China will no longer be exempted from tariffs starting Friday, when President Donald Trump’s move against an exception he called a “big scam” takes effect.

title: Romania Politics Set to Stoke EU’s Highest Bond Yields For Now
content: Romania faces a prolonged period of elevated funding costs as a contentious presidential election risks further delaying steps to curb the European Union’s widest budget deficit.

title: China Says It’s Assessing US Talks, Hinting at Possible Thaw
content: China said it is assessing the possibility of trade talks with the US, the first sign since Donald Trump hiked tariffs last month that negotiations could begin between the two sides.

title: Asia’s Factories Suffer Major Blow as Trump’s Tariffs Hit Demand
content: Manufacturing activity across most of Asia contracted in April, with companies struggling with weaker demand and pausing new orders in the face of US President Donald Trump’s baseline 10% tariff.

title: Japan Sees Trade Talks Speeding Up, Hopes for June Agreement
content: Japan aims to achieve a trade agreement with the US in June, with the high-stakes bilateral discussions expected to gain momentum in mid-May, Tokyo’s chief negotiator said after concluding the latest round of talks in Washington.

title: Australian Retail Sales Climb for Third Straight Month in March
content: Australian retail sales rose for a third straight month, reflecting a recent pickup in consumer spending and suggesting the economy was in reasonable shape before US tariffs set off a wave of volatility across global markets.

title: Japan’s Job Market Stays Tight, Supporting Wage Momentum
content: Japan’s labor market remained largely tight in March, supporting momentum for wage hikes, while uncertainties over the global trade war continue to darken the outlook.

title: South Korea’s Steady Inflation Gives BOK Scope to Cut Rates
content: South Korea’s consumer prices rose at the same pace in April, giving the central bank scope to consider resuming the rate-cut cycle at its policy meeting later this month.

title: UK Sickness Welfare Surge Not Due to Hospital Waits, Study Finds
content: Britain’s ballooning welfare benefits bill has not been caused by the surge in hospital waiting lists since the pandemic, according to research by the Institute for Fiscal Studies that challenges current official assumptions.

title: US Hiring Seen Slowing, With Brunt of Tariff Impact Coming Later
content: US employment growth probably decelerated in April and the jobless rate held steady, illustrating healthy yet moderating labor demand entering a period when trade policy risks chilling the hiring decisions.

title: US Jobless Claims by Federal Employees Have Declined After Spike
content: New applications for unemployment benefits filed by federal employees have been largely flat in the past five weeks after a brief spike when the Trump administration started to fire workers across agencies.

title: Port Leaders Warn Tariffs Bring ‘Radical Uncertainty’ to Economy
content: Leaders of major West Coast ports warned that a sharp drop in ship traffic tied to President Donald Trump’s steep tariffs on Chinese goods will threaten jobs, raise prices and ripple through the broader US economy.

title: Summers Says Wrong to Say Markets Tell Fed It Should Cut
content: Former Treasury Secretary Lawrence Summers said that bond-market pricing doesn’t amount to a judgment call on what the Federal Reserve ought to do with interest rates, and that it would be a “very serious error” for policymakers to ease next week.

title: US Toymakers Scramble to Adjust to Trump’s China Tariffs
content: America’s toymakers outsourced manufacturing to China in the 1980s to cut costs. Nearly half a century later, that decision could bankrupt them.

title: Yen Slides as Bank of Japan Pours Cold Water on Rate Hikes
content: The yen fell sharply against the dollar after the Bank of Japan said it will take longer than it previously thought to hit the inflation target, leading traders to pare bets on further interest-rate hikes.

title: Peruvian Inflation Accelerated More Than Expected in April
content: Inflation in Peru’s capital rose faster than expected in April, but remains comfortably within the central bank’s target band.

title: US Manufacturing Activity Shrinks by the Most Since November
content: US manufacturing activity shrank in April by the most in five months as lean order books and the repercussions from tariffs prompted the steepest output contraction since 2020.

title: US Jobless Claims Jump on Spike in New York During Spring Recess
content: Applications for US unemployment benefits rose to the highest level since February during the week that followed Easter and spring recess at New York City public schools.

title: Trump’s Effort to Blame Biden for Economy Ignores Tariff Fallout
content: President Donald Trump has started vacillating between telling Americans to be patient in the face of bad economic news and blaming his predecessor for it, leaving him vulnerable to losing the support of voters who elected him to improve the nation’s economy.

title: Traders Fully Price Four More BOE Quarter-Point Cuts This Year
content: Traders boosted wagers on Bank of England policymakers speeding up the pace of interest-rate cuts as concerns grow that weakness in the US economy may spread globally.

title: EU to Present Trade Proposals to US Negotiators Next Week
content: The European Union is planning to share a paper with the US next week that will set out a package of proposals to kick-start trade negotiations with the Trump administration.

title: Europe Is Set to Test Trump’s Bandwidth to Discuss Trade
content: With just over 60 days to go until President Donald Trump’s reciprocal tariffs are set to snap into force, the race to do trade deals with the US is expanding beyond a few export powers in Asia.

title: Trade Has a Recent History of Dragging US GDP Down
content: I’m Ben Holland, an economics editor in Washington. Today we’re looking at trade and GDP. Send us feedback and tips to ecodaily@bloomberg.net. And if you aren’t yet signed up to receive this newsletter, you can do so here.

title: Yellen Warns US Recession Risk Is ‘Way Up’ After Trump’s Tariffs
content: Janet Yellen warned that the risk of a US recession has “gone way up” after Donald Trump’s sweeping tariffs rattled financial markets, consumers and businesses.

title: UK Mortgage Approvals Dip as Time Ran Out to Beat Tax Hike
content: UK mortgage approvals fell for a third month in March as house hunters ran out of time to tie up purchases before a property transaction tax went up at the start of April.

title: Bank of Japan Pushes Back Inflation Target Due to Trade War
content: The Bank of Japan pushed back the timing for when it expects to reach its inflation target and slashed its growth forecasts as the global trade war initiated by US President Donald Trump darkens the economic outlook.

title: Russia Triples 2025 Deficit Target With Less Energy Income Seen
content: The Russian Finance Ministry more than tripled its budget deficit target for this year after expectations for revenue and the price of oil were reduced amid US President Donald Trump’s tariffs.

title: Musk Says DOGE Should Examine Federal Reserve Renovation Costs
content: Billionaire Elon Musk said he is considering sending his government efficiency team to the Federal Reserve, citing a costly renovation of the central bank’s Washington, DC, headquarters as an example of potential government waste.

title: StanChart Traders Ride Volatility to Lift Quarterly Profit
content: Standard Chartered Plc reported first-quarter profit that topped analyst expectations as the firm’s traders benefited from the market volatility wrought by US President Donald Trump’s trade war.

title: BASF Warns It Needs More Time to Assess Tariff Impact on Outlook
content: BASF SE warned that uncertainty caused by President Donald Trump’s trade tactics means it can’t make reliable predictions for its business this year.

title: Shell Sticks With Payouts, Spending Plans Despite Oil’s Drop
content: Shell Plc stuck to its plans for investor returns and capital spending, taking on extra debt to fill the gap in its cash flow stemming from the drop in oil prices.

title: Vedanta Weighs Zambia Copper IPO to Fund $1 Billion Investment
content: Vedanta Resources, the mining and energy company controlled by Indian billionaire Anil Agarwal, is considering listing its Zambian copper unit to raise the funds it needs to invest in the asset.

title: NatWest Says Full-Year Income Set to Hit Upper End of Guidance
content: NatWest Group Plc beat estimates in the first quarter and pointed to improving earnings this year as the bank’s customers proved resilient to the unfolding strains on the global economy.

title: Philippines $3.5 Billion Subway No Longer Feasible, Builder Says
content: A $3.5-billion subway project in the Philippines’ main financial hub is no longer feasible following an inter-city dispute, according to its developer on Friday.

title: Dangote Reiterates $30 Billion Revenue Target Despite US Tariff
content: Aliko Dangote, Africa’s richest person, said his group is on track to generate total revenue of $30 billion next year, even as companies fret over the potential impact of US President Donald Trump’s tariffs.

title: Danske Bank Confirms 2025 Guidance as NII Beats Forecasts
content: Danske Bank A/S, the largest lender in Denmark, confirmed its full-year guidance following a solid first quarter, driven by better-than-expected net interest income and strong credit quality.

title: ING Unveils Buyback But Pushes Out Capital Goal Amid Tariffs
content: ING Groep NV announced a fresh buyback of €2 billion while giving itself more time to draw down capital.

title: Factories Key to Trump’s ‘Golden Age’ Urge China Tariff Relief
content: Almost as swiftly as he has erected his tariff wall around the US over the past 100 days, President Donald Trump has issued exemptions for a select but growing family of products like auto parts and smartphones.

title: Gold Road Halts Trading Due to Speculation Over Transaction
content: Gold Road Resources Ltd. shares were suspended from trading in Sydney, with the miner citing “media speculation regarding a potential change of control transaction”.

title: Norway’s Equinor Offloads Stake in Brazilian Oil Field for $3.5 Billion
content: Norwegian energy explorer Equinor ASA has agreed to sell its 60% stake in the Peregrino oil and gas project off the Brazilian coast for $3.5 billion, it said in a statement.

title: Kohl’s Fires CEO for Directing Millions to Romantic Partner
content: Kohl’s Corp. said it fired its chief executive officer only months into his tenure after the board uncovered that he directed millions of dollars of business to someone he has had a personal relationship with that wasn’t disclosed.

title: HSBC Investors With $1.6 Trillion Seek Reassurance on Net Zero
content: A group of 30 HSBC Holdings Plc investors is asking the bank to confirm it’s still committed to cutting CO2 emissions, amid concerns Europe’s biggest lender is backing away from its climate pledges.

title: Obesity Drug Price Wars Heat Up as CVS Picks Novo Over Lilly
content: The obesity drug price wars are finally starting.

title: US Claims Medicare Insurers, Brokers Used Illegal Kickbacks
content: The US sued top health insurance companies and brokers, alleging they used illegal kickbacks to steer members into certain private Medicare Advantage plans.

title: Frontier to Cut Capacity, Outlays to Save Extra $300 Million
content: Frontier Group Holdings, Inc. said it plans to reduce capacity through November and cut spending to save at least $300 million more than prior expectations.

title: CN Railway Defies Tariff Gloom, Keeps 2025 Growth Outlook
content: Canadian National Railway Co. kept its financial outlook for 2025 intact despite rising economic risks, but management acknowledged that uncertainty is leaving many customers in limbo.

title: JAB Seeks $2.5 Billion for Keurig Dr Pepper Share Block
content: JAB Holding Co. is seeking to raise as much as $2.5 billion from the sale of Keurig Dr Pepper Inc. shares, according to people familiar with the matter, as it continues to sell down its holdings of the beverage company.

title: Xcel CEO Says AI Power Needs Raise Prospect of New Large Nuclear
content: It’s been more than a decade since the US last broke ground on a large-scale nuclear power plant that came online. Xcel Chief Executive Officer Bob Frenzel is raising the idea that it’s time to start again.

title: AIG Investment Gains Help First-Quarter Profit Top Estimates
content: American International Group Inc.’s investment income gains helped the insurer’s operating profit beat analysts’ estimates, in a period otherwise marked by extraordinary losses from the Los Angeles wildfires.

title: Whirlpool’s Ratings Cut to Junk by S&P Amid Revenue Pressure
content: Whirlpool Corp., the owner of the KitchenAid and Maytag brands, was cut to junk status by S&P Global Ratings, which cited the company’s high debt levels and potential pressure on revenue as tariffs ramp up.

title: Tesla Board in Spotlight After Cashing In $1.2 Billion With Musk
content: Almost like clockwork since mid-November, Tesla Inc. board chair Robyn Denholm has been selling the company’s stock. During that time, shares whipsawed and the company’s sales slowed — and then cratered — around the world.

title: Eli Lilly’s Shares Sink on Investor Concerns About CVS Move
content: Eli Lilly & Co.’s shares saw the biggest one-day drop since 2008 after CVS Health Corp. announced a plan to drop its blockbuster weight-loss drug Zepbound from its preferred list, making rival Wegovy more widely available.

title: Amgen Beats on Profit as Obesity Drug Moves Toward Market
content: Amgen Inc. outperformed Wall Street’s quarterly profit estimates as it moves forward with plans to crack the multibillion-dollar market for novel weight-loss medicines.

title: American Airlines Agrees to $4 Billion Dallas Airport Expansion
content: Dallas Fort Worth International Airport and American Airlines Group Inc. reached an agreement on a $4 billion expansion project.

title: CVS Drops Lilly’s Zepbound as Preferred Drug in Win for Novo
content: CVS Health Corp.’s drug-benefits unit negotiated a deal to make Novo Nordisk A/S’s Wegovy more widely available to its members, a blow to rival Eli Lilly & Co.’s Zepbound that was moved off the company’s list of preferred drugs.

title: Multistrategy Hedge Funds Turn a Rocky April Into More Gains
content: Some of the biggest multistrategy hedge funds turned a wild April into steady gains as they navigated sharp volatility amid Donald Trump’s tariff announcements and pauses.

title: Delta’s Endeavor Regional Airline Chief Executive to Step Down
content: Delta Air Lines Inc. says the head of its Endeavor Air regional carrier will step down, but remain with the parent company.

title: College That Sold Georgia O’Keeffe Art Cut to Junk by Moody’s
content: Valparaiso University, a Lutheran school in Indiana struggling to enroll more students, was downgraded two notches to junk by Moody’s Ratings.

title: Elon Musk, DOGE team credit fed workers for helping trim waste, fraud
content: Elon Musk and his DOGE team expressed their gratitude Thursday to the federal employees partnering with the cost-cutting agency as they work around the clock to eliminate wasteful spending and modernize the workforce.

title: Hong Kong Buys Record Amount of US Dollars to Defend Peg
content: Hong Kong intervened to defend its peg, buying a record amount of US dollars after the city’s currency rose to the upper end of its trading band.

title: Trump vs. Powell, 50 Years of Vanguard, South Korea Demographics | Wall Street Week
content: This week, former Treasury Secretary Lawrence H. Summers and Columbia’s Kathryn Judge discuss the importance and evolution of the Fed's independence. And, how will Trump’s tariffs influence trade in the long run? Plus, Vanguard’s 50th anniversary. Later, South Korea’s baby bust — is the country’s economy at risk? (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Elon Musk’s 100-Day Bet
content:
Since Donald Trump returned to the White House, Elon Musk has been a scene-stealer, gutting agencies and sparking litigation. But DOGE hasn’t fully lived up to its billing, and Tesla has become collateral damage.

title: Stocks Rise for Second Week as Tariff Shock Fades | Bloomberg: The Close 05/02/2025
content: Bloomberg Television brings you the latest news and analysis leading up to the final minutes and seconds before and after the closing bell on Wall Street. Today's guests are Katie Nixon, Northern Trust, Lydia Boussour, EY, Mike Wirth, Chevron CEO, Gene Munster, Deepwater Asset Management, Mark Palmer, Benchmark, Melissa Brown, Simcorp, Jay Berry, JPMorgan, Hayley Berg, Hopper, Bryan Eshelman, AlixPartners, Mac Harman, Balsam Hill, Mauricio Umansky, The Agency. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Big Oil Refuses to Budge on Production Ahead of OPEC+ Decision
content: The largest western oil producers are mostly sticking with their growth plans for now, despite a 16% decline in crude prices during April and the potential for further increases in output from OPEC+.

title: Key Federal Reserve Supervision Official to Depart at Year-End
content: Michael Gibson, director of the Federal Reserve’s supervision and regulation division, will leave at the end of the year following more than three decades at the US central bank, according to people familiar with the matter.

title: Apple Renews Fears About Tariffs, China With Wobbly Report
content: Bloomberg's Mark Gurman breaks down Apple's wobbly earnings report, the impact of Trump tariffs and what they both mean for the tech giant's future. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Speculators Turn Most Bearish on the Dollar Since September
content: Speculative traders have become more bearish on the dollar than at any time since last September as concerns about US assets continue to circulate despite a recovery in the equity markets.

title: Tiny Logistics Firm’s Shares Surge on Plan to Buy Trump Coin
content: A small logistics company’s plan to hold President Donald Trump’s memecoin as a treasury asset is fueling its blistering stock rally.

title: US Treasuries Slide as Solid Jobs Market Gives Fed Room on Rates
content: US Treasuries fell after stronger-than-expected US employment data showed tariff uncertainty hasn’t hit the nation’s jobs market yet, prompting traders to trim bets on imminent interest-rate cuts.

title: Stocks Extend Winning Streak on Trade Optimism, Jobs
content: US stocks tallied a second week of gains, with the S&P 500 Index powering through its longest winning streak in more than 20 years and wiping out all losses from April’s tariff turbulence as strong jobs data and progress on international trade talks unleashed a wave of buying.

title: Stocks Surged After Solid Jobs Report | Closing Bell
content: Comprehensive cross-platform coverage of the U.S. market close on Bloomberg Television, Bloomberg Radio, and YouTube with Romaine Bostick, Alix Steel, Scarlet Fu, Carol Massar and Emily Graffeo. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: In Wall Street’s Epic Comeback, Unsolved Market Mysteries Abound
content: It was the week Wall Street got its swagger back. Stocks staged a gravity-defying rebound to wipe out all losses from April’s tariff shock, Corporate America unleashed billions in pent-up bond sales and speculative assets from crypto to unprofitable tech companies surged.

title: I Squared Nears Deal for $5 Billion Matterhorn Pipeline
content: A consortium led by I Squared Capital is considering buying Matterhorn Express Pipeline in a deal that would value the Texas natural gas conduit at about $5 billion including debt, according to people familiar with the matter.

title: Stocks Rise for Second Week as Tariff Shock Fades: Markets Wrap
content: Wall Street’s risk-on brigade pushed the S&P 500 to its longest winning streak in two decades, with scars from April’s tariff shock healing on fresh signs of US-China diplomacy.

title: Very High Uncertainty For Consumers, Businesses: Berro
content: JPMorgan Asset Management Fixed Income Portfolio Manager discusses the current economic data in an interview with Sonali Basak on "Real Yield." (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Bloomberg Real Yield 05/02/2025
content: Vonnie Quinn highlights the market-moving news you need to know. Today's guests: JPMorgan Asset Management Fixed Income Portfolio Manager Kelsey Berro, Oaktree Capital Management CO-CEO and Portfolio Manager Robert O'Leary, and Bloomberg's Ira Jersey. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Bringing the Workforce Along With Tech Advances
content: A new initiative from ADP aims to fight the mismatch between skills and labor force needs amid rapid technological advancements. Nela Richardson, ADP chief economist and ESG officer, speaks with Caroline Hyde and Ed Ludlow on “Bloomberg Technology." (Source: Bloomberg)

title: What Does GDP Data Mean For Markets?
content: The GDP data came in lower than expected even with steady job growth in April. JPMorgan Asset Management Fixed Income Portfolio Manager Kelsey Berro and Bloomberg's Ira Jersey explain how this impacts the bond market. They speak with Sonali Basak on "Real Yield." (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Apple’s China Problem Isn’t New: IDC’s Popal
content: Apple is facing a challenging year but Nabila Popal, senior director at IDC, says the company’s long-term outlook remains strong. She speaks with Caroline Hyde and Ed Ludlow on “Bloomberg Technology”.  (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Amazon Prepares for Tougher Business Climate
content: Amazon’s seller density will be an important factor for its growth in the face of tariffs, says Brad Erickson, internet analyst at RBC Capital Markets. He joins Caroline Hyde and Ed Ludlow on "Bloomberg Technology."  (Source: Bloomberg)

title: DC Accelerates $1.5 Billion Debt Sale Amid Investor Demand
content: The District of Columbia accelerated the sale of $1.5 billion of municipal bonds by a day, taking advantage of a rally in US state and local debt that helped buoy demand for the securities.

title: Chevron Cuts Buybacks As Oil Plunges
content: Chevron and Exxon reported high earnings even after Chevron said it would reduce it's share buybacks because of tumbling oil prices and a trade war. Meanwhile, Exxon is sticking with its's share buyback plans as it's earnings met analysts' estimates. Goldman Sachs Head of North American Natural Equity Research Neil Mehta has more on the story.  (Source: Bloomberg)

title: US Designates Gangs Destabilizing Haiti as Terrorist Groups
content: The US designated two powerful Haitian gangs it accused of destabilizing the country and threatening US interests as “Foreign Terrorist Organizations,” escalating pressure on the groups that control much of the country’s trade.

title: Oil Falls as OPEC+ Weighs Another Major Production Increase
content: Oil slumped as OPEC+ discussed making a second major production increase, inflaming concerns about swelling global supplies that have dragged down crude prices this year.

title: Oaktree's Co-CEO on Tariff Impact, Private Credit, Bankruptcies
content: Oaktree Capital Management Co-Chief Executive Officer Robert O’Leary discusses the impact of tariffs and says it's reasonable to assume "we are in for higher and more volatile interest rates" and as a consequence of that "we're in for more volatility in the credit market." He also discusses private credit and says discounts are going as low as the “50 cent range.” Robert O’Leary joins Sonali Basak on "Real Yield." (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Take-Two Delays Grand Theft Auto VI
content: Take-Two Interactive is pushing back the release of Grand Theft Auto VI to May of 2026, delaying what’s expected to be one of the most lucrative video games ever. Bloomberg's Jason Schreier discusses the reason with Caroline Hyde and Ed Ludlow on “Bloomberg Technology”.  (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Australians Vote in Election as Polls Show Labor Will Win
content: Australians began voting Saturday in an election that opinion polls said favored Prime Minister Anthony Albanese, putting him in a position to become the first leader to win consecutive ballots in more than two decades.

title: India Bans Imports From Pakistan as Tit-for-Tat Measures Widen
content: India banned the import of all goods originating from or transiting through Pakistan as tensions between the two nuclear-armed nations escalate in the wake of a deadly terror attack last month.

title: Singapore Heads to Vote in Biggest Test Yet for Ruling Party
content: Singaporeans voted Saturday in the ruling party’s biggest electoral test in decades amid concerns over global economic turmoil and high living costs in the Southeast Asian city-state.

title: Germany’s Red Tape Creates a Berlin-Sized Hole in Energy Shift
content: Military airspace restrictions are holding up wind-power projects, highlighting the challenges for Germany’s energy and defense plans.

title: Serbia’s Vucic Cuts US Visit Short on Health Reasons, RTS Says
content: Serbian President Aleksandar Vucic suddenly fell sick while in Florida on Friday and will return home, canceling his planned meetings in the US, state broadcaster RTS reported.

title: Cuomo Holds $3 Million of Undisclosed Options in Nuclear Startup
content: Former New York Governor  Andrew Cuomo has $3 million in options to a shoestring nuclear startup that he failed to disclose to an ethics board as he mounts a comeback bid to be the mayor of New York City.

title: Starmer Plots Harder Line on Migration to Counter Farage Threat
content: Prime Minister Keir Starmer is preparing tougher measures on immigration to stem a record flow of arrivals across the English Channel and stave off the threat posed by Nigel Farage’s Reform UK party after it made sweeping gains in this week’s local elections.

title: Transportation Department Plans to Cut Workforce at End of May
content: Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy told employees in a town hall Friday that he’s planning to reduce the department’s workforce at the end of this month.

title: Key Federal Reserve Supervision Official to Depart at Year-End
content: Michael Gibson, director of the Federal Reserve’s supervision and regulation division, will leave at the end of the year following more than three decades at the US central bank, according to people familiar with the matter.

title: Trump Wants to Pull Harvard’s Tax Exemption. Can He?
content: President Donald Trump is escalating his campaign to pressure elite universities into making a wide range of policy changes by threatening to strip Harvard University of its tax-exempt status.

title: Trump Will Celebrate Army’s Birthday - And His Own - With a Parade
content: President Donald Trump will host a military parade marking the 250th birthday of the US Army — as well as his own 79th birthday — on June 14, the administration announced Friday.

title: US Approves $3.5 Billion Weapons Sale to Saudi Arabia
content: The US approved the sale of weapons worth an estimated $3.5 billion to Saudi Arabia ahead of a planned visit by President Donald Trump to the Gulf kingdom this month, as Washington seeks to strengthen ties with a key partner and ratchet up pressure against Iran.

title: US Settling Suit Over Trump Supporter’s Death in Jan. 6 Riot
content: The US has reached a settlement in principle with the estate of Ashli Babbitt, the protester who was shot and killed by a police officer as she tried to force her way into the chambers of the House of Representatives during the Jan. 6, 2021, Capitol riot.

title: US Approves Up to $350 Million in Ukraine F-16 Training, Support
content: The US State Department approved F-16 fighter-jet training and services for Ukraine worth up to $350 million, signaling that the White House will keep supporting Kyiv in the fight against Russia despite President Donald Trump’s impatience to end the war.

title: How ‘Signalgate’ Cost Michael Waltz His NSA Job
content: In March, the editor of the Atlantic magazine revealed that national security adviser Michael Waltz had inadvertently included him in a group texting thread with other top officials in President Donald Trump’s administration about a US military operation in Yemen. The revelations set off a firestorm of criticism against Waltz, Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, and others in the group for discussing highly sensitive matters on Signal, a commercial messaging app that is off-limits for US officials t

title: Nigel Farage’s Reform Upends UK Politics With Election Surge
content: Nigel Farage’s Reform UK landed its biggest blow yet against Britain’s political establishment in Thursday’s local votes, winning a string of victories that highlight how the populist right-wing party is shifting Britain’s electoral landscape.

title: Door Opens a Crack for Talks With China on Tariffs
content: This is Washington Edition, the newsletter about money, power and politics in the nation’s capital. title: Trump Asks Supreme Court for DOGE Access to Social Security Data
content: The Trump administration asked the US Supreme Court to let Elon Musk’s Department of Government Efficiency have access to sensitive Social Security information, escalating a privacy fight that could affect millions of people.

title: Trump Stokes Harvard Feud by Threatening Tax-Exempt Status
content: President Donald Trump said Harvard University would lose its tax-exempt status, stepping up his attack on the Ivy League school with a threat that was decried as out of his jurisdiction.

title: NY Fires Back in Congestion Fight With Trump to Keep Toll Alive
content: New York fired a salvo in the fight to shield its congestion pricing program from the Trump administration’s push to shut it down, indicating it is now poised to seek an immediate court order in its lawsuit to protect the traffic tolling plan.

title: US Presses for Google to Share Data by Citing Yahoo Japan Deal
content: US antitrust enforcers reached back to a deal Google struck 15 years ago to argue that the Alphabet Inc. unit should once again share information with third parties, this time to end its illegal monopoly of online search.

title: Trump’s Ex-IRS Commissioner Pushes Back on Harvard Tax Attack
content: Donald Trump’s promise to strip Harvard University of its tax-exempt status prompted criticism Friday from a former Internal Revenue Service commissioner in the president’s first term, who said the process would take years and need a judge’s approval.

title: NJ Transit Strike Would Be ‘Disaster’ for Region, Sherrill Says
content: New Jersey Transit is on the brink of a “huge crisis” as a train engineers strike threatens to upend commutes as early as May 16, according to US Representative Mikie Sherrill.

title: US Sends Envoy to Monitor Romanian Election, Bucharest Says
content: President Donald Trump’s administration dispatched a senior official to Romania to monitor a contentious presidential election on Sunday, the government in Bucharest said.

title: Portugal Says Defense Investment May Have Reached 1.58% of GDP
content: Portugal’s defense investment may have reached an estimated 1.58% of gross domestic product in 2024, more than previously forecast.

title: Energy Chief Says US Won’t Move Forward With With Billions in Biden-Era Loans
content: Energy Secretary Chris Wright said his agency doesn’t plan to move forward with billions of dollars worth of Biden-era loans as the Trump administration reviews the department’s $400 billion-strong green bank.

title: FCC’s Simington Seeks to Cap Networks’ Local Revenue Share
content: Nathan Simington, a Republican member of the Federal Communications Commission, proposed capping the share of revenue that TV networks can collect from local stations, saying he wants to “rein in corporate media monopolies.”

title: Israel Hits Damascus After Plea for Help From Druze Minority
content: Israel struck a target near the presidential palace in the Syrian capital after the Druze community in both countries called for help following a series of violent clashes between the minority group and Syrian government forces.

title: Trump Seeks to Squeeze Drugmakers’ Revenues to Pay for Tax Cuts
content: President Donald Trump has set his sights on the pharmaceutical industry to shoulder part of the cost of his tax cuts, pressing congressional Republicans to force drugmakers to accept lower prices on prescriptions covered by Medicaid.

title: China Hints at Possible Thaw With US in Weighing Trade Talks
content: China said it is assessing the possibility of trade talks with the US, the first sign since Donald Trump hiked tariffs last month that negotiations could begin between the two sides.

title: Investors Eye Nigeria's Cinema Industry
content: After Netflix and Amazon stopped commissioning original films, Nigeria’s financiers spotted an opportunity to break into the industry. Nollywood, as Nigeria’s freewheeling filmmaking industry is called, is a booming business. Hard figures are difficult to come by, but the country produces the second-highest number of movies in the world every year after India, and at least a million people are estimated to work directly or indirectly in the sector. Jennifer Zabasajja reports. (Source: Bloomberg)
