title: Google Can Train Search AI With Web Content Even After Opt-Out
content: Google can train its search-specific AI products, like AI Overviews, on content across the web even when the publishers have chosen to opt out of training Google’s AI products, a vice-president of product at the company testified in court on Friday.

title: Tiny Logistics Firm’s Shares Surge on Plan to Buy Trump Coin
content: A small logistics company’s plan to hold President Donald Trump’s memecoin as a treasury asset is fueling its blistering stock rally.

title: Tariffs Weigh on Big Tech, Increasing US Energy for AI | Bloomberg Technology
content: Bloomberg’s Caroline Hyde and Ed Ludlow discuss a busy week of tech earnings. Plus, US Energy Secretary Chris Wright explains the Trump administration's plans to boost US electricity output to support AI development. And Roblox CEO David Baszucki talks about the company’s earnings and growth strategy. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Apple Renews Fears About Tariffs, China With Wobbly Report
content: Apple Inc.’s much-awaited quarterly earnings report failed to soothe investor concerns about its biggest challenges, including escalating tariff costs and a slowdown in China.

title: UK Grocer Co-op Says Hackers Obtained Customer Data
content: The UK supermarket chain Co-op said hackers were able to access and extract customer data from one of its systems during a recent cyberattack.

title: DOJ Asks Federal Judge to Break Up Google’s Ad-Tech Tools
content: The US Justice Department asked a federal judge on Friday to force Alphabet Inc.’s Google to sell key parts of its advertising technology and share realtime data with competitors to address a ruling that the technology giant illegally monopolizes much of the market for placing ads around the web.

title: US Presses for Google to Share Data by Citing Yahoo Japan Deal
content: US antitrust enforcers reached back to a deal Google struck 15 years ago to argue that the Alphabet Inc. unit should once again share information with third parties, this time to end its illegal monopoly of online search.

title: UK Tells Businesses to ‘Wake Up’ After Marks & Spencer Hack
content: A senior UK minister next week will warn businesses to protect themselves against cyber threats after a spate of attacks on retailers including Marks & Spencer Group Plc.

title: Players Have Too Many Options to Spend $80 on a Video Game
content: As Xbox announces a price hike, the year’s best-reviewed games are all budget titles

title: Apple, Anthropic Team Up to Build AI-Powered ‘Vibe-Coding’ Platform
content: Apple Inc. is teaming up with startup Anthropic PBC on a new “vibe-coding” software platform that will use artificial intelligence to write, edit and test code on behalf of programmers.

title: Shein’s London IPO Stalled Amid US Tariff Fallout
content: Shein Group Ltd.’s initial public offering plan has slowed to a crawl as the retailer assesses the impact of US tariffs on its business and awaits regulatory approvals, according to people familiar with the matter.

title: Block Shares Sink Most in Five Years on Reduced Profit Guidance
content: Shares of Block Inc. are on a downward spiral after the parent of the popular money-transfer app Cash App reported results that suggest weakness in the company’s efforts to convert millions of active users into full-fledged banking customers.

title: Amazon Buys NYC Fifth Avenue Office Tower Near Grand Central
content: Amazon.com Inc. added to its Manhattan real estate holdings with the purchase of an office tower on Fifth Avenue.

title: Disinformation Experts Band Together as Online Abuse Escalates
content: Elon Musk's X account on a smartphone arranged in Germantown, New York, US, on Thursday, April 24, 2025. Elon Musk's X Holdings Corp. is evolving from a social media platform powered by mainstream advertisers to one betting on dollars generated from artificial intelligence and subscriptions, a change that appears to have buoyed its revenue lately. Photographer: Gabby Jones/Bloomberg

title: Uber, China’s Momenta to Partner on Robotaxi Rollout in Europe
content: Uber Technologies Inc. announced it’s partnering with Beijing Momenta Technology Co. to deploy robotaxis on the ridesharing platform in various global markets, starting in Europe in early 2026.

title: Why Are Deepfakes Everywhere? Can They Be Stopped?
content: The internet is awash in deepfakes — audio, pictures or video made using artificial intelligence tools in which people appear to do or say things they didn’t, be somewhere they weren’t, or that change their appearance. Some involve nudification, where photos are altered to depict someone unclothed. Other deepfakes are deployed to scam consumers, or to damage the reputations of politicians and other people in the public eye.

title: Harrods Latest UK Retailer to Battle Against Hacking Attacks
content: London’s luxury department store Harrods Ltd. reported hacking attempts Thursday, days after two other UK retailers said they were attacked.

title: Singapore Steps Up Fraud Probe Involving Nvidia’s AI Chips
content: Singaporean prosecutors secured eight more weeks to deepen a probe and potentially bring more charges against three men accused of fraud in shipping servers suspected of containing Nvidia Corp. chips banned from China.

title: Amazon, Apple Earnings Show Tariffs Are Coming for Big Tech, Too
content: Recessionary fears. Global economic and geopolitical conditions. Tariff and trade policies.

title: Apple Hit With Downgrades as Tariff, Growth Worries Increase
content: Apple Inc. received at least two downgrades on Friday, following quarterly results that reinforced concerns over tariffs and its growth potential.

title: Take-Two Delays Release of Grand Theft Auto VI to May 2026
content: Take-Two Interactive Software Inc. pushed back the release of Grand Theft Auto VI to next year, giving the team more time to finish what’s expected to be one of the most lucrative video games ever. The shares tumbled the most in two-and-a-half years.

title: Amazon Braces for Tougher Business Climate as US Tariffs Hit
content: Amazon.com Inc. said it’s bracing for a tougher business climate in the coming months, echoing concerns from a range of companies that tariffs and related economic turmoil could crimp consumer spending.

title: Amazon, Apple Show Big Tech Not Immune From Tariff Pain
content: Welcome to Tech In Depth, our daily newsletter with reporting and analysis about the business of tech from Bloomberg’s journalists around the world. Today, Brody Ford writes that Apple and Amazon’s quarterly results show that Big Tech can’t avoid the pain of US tariffs.

title: How an Israeli Hostage Negotiator Outsmarts Ransomware Hackers
content: Moty Cristal honed his talent for high-stakes negotiations dealing with Hamas and Hezbollah before expanding to talks with ransomware gangs.

title: TikTok Fined €530 Million for Illegally Sending EU Data to China
content: TikTok owner ByteDance Ltd. was fined €530 million ($600 million) by the European Union for illegally sending user data to China, and warned that it didn’t do enough to keep that information out of reach from Chinese state services.

title: Oyo Postpones Its Third Attempt at an IPO After SoftBank Balks
content: Oyo Hotels is delaying its plans for an October IPO after opposition from SoftBank Group Corp. and a tumultuous turn in the stock market this year.

title: US Black Women See Jobless Rate Surge, Adding to Year-Long Trend
content: The unemployment rate for Black women rose by a full percentage point in April, following a year-long deterioration in labor conditions for that category.

title: Portugal Says Defense Investment May Have Reached 1.58% of GDP
content: Portugal’s defense investment may have reached an estimated 1.58% of gross domestic product in 2024, more than previously forecast.

title: GM Cuts Workers at Canada Truck Plant, Citing Trade Turmoil
content: A General Motors Co. assembly plant in Canada that makes pickup trucks mostly for export to the US will cut down to two shifts from three because of the trade war.

title: China Hints at Possible Thaw With US in Weighing Trade Talks
content: China said it is assessing the possibility of trade talks with the US, the first sign since Donald Trump hiked tariffs last month that negotiations could begin between the two sides.

title: ECB Can Be Optimistic on Inflation, Guindos Tells Die Presse
content: The European Central Bank can be confident on returning inflation to the 2% goal, according to Vice President Luis de Guindos.

title: Carney, Trump Prepare to Talk Trade and Security at White House
content: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney said he’ll meet with US President Donald Trump in Washington on Tuesday, their first face-to-face encounter since he won an election in part because of an anti-Trump message.

title: Namibia Joins Central Banks’ Gold Rush to Hedge Against Shocks
content: Namibia’s central bank plans to join others that are adding gold to their foreign-exchange reserve mix as a buffer against global uncertainty that’s intensified since US President Donald Trump slapped tariffs on its trading partners.

title: Trump’s Auto Tariff Relief Shields USMCA Auto Parts From 25% Tax
content: President Donald Trump’s revised auto tariff plan continues — at least for now — an exemption for parts that comply with the free trade agreement spanning North America, a concession desperately sought by industry.

title: Barclays Pushes Forecast for Next Fed Cut to July From June
content: Economists at Barclays delayed the timing of their predication for the Federal Reserve to cut rates to July, from June, following a stronger-than-expected payroll report.

title: Global Manufacturing Activity Contracts for First Time This Year
content: Global manufacturing activity contracted for the first time this year in April, dragged down by shrinking orders and employment.

title: Zambia, Zimbabwe Court Investors to Revive $5 Billion Hydro Dam
content: Zambia and Zimbabwe are ramping up efforts to secure investment for the long-delayed $5 billion Batoka Gorge hydropower project, as they revive a controversial plan to potentially source water from the Democratic Republic of Congo.

title: US Employers Add 177,000 Jobs, Solid Pace in Face of Uncertainty
content: US job growth was robust in April and the unemployment rate held steady despite deep uncertainty over President Donald Trump’s trade policies, which economists expect will dent hiring plans over the coming months.

title: Auto Workers Welcome Trump’s Tariffs, No Matter What’s Happening on Wall Street
content: Some auto workers like James Benson Jr. are all-in on President Donald Trump’s trade war — and they don’t mind if it causes some short-term pain for both Wall Street and Main Street.

title: US Treasury Sanctions Cartel Leader in Fuel Theft Crackdown
content: The US Treasury Department announced sanctions on three Mexican nationals and two Mexican companies involved in fuel theft and smuggling by the Cartel Jalisco Nueva Generacion.

title: Bank of Ireland Starts to See a Pause in Foreign Investments
content: Some of Bank of Ireland Group Plc’s corporate and foreign direct investment customers paused investments in the first quarter because of global business uncertainty, according to the lender.

title: Chile Economic Activity Bounces Back on Mining Output Surge
content: Chile’s economic activity bounced back in March on a surge in mining, while other sectors posted more muted gains as government officials and the central bank warn of a turbulent global outlook ahead.

title: Here Are the Takeaways From the US Jobs Report for April
content: Here are the key takeaways from the US employment report for April, released Friday:

title: US Jobs Strength Unlikely to Move Fed as Trade War Looms
content: A worker moves spools of copper wire between rod breakdown machines. Photographer: Justin Hamel/Bloomberg

title: Food Inflation Heats Up But Some Relief May Be in Store
content: As worries about the impact of tariffs on the economy and consumer demand persist, there’s a sliver of good news on the horizon: The World Bank expects food commodity prices to actually drop.

title: The Ricochet Effect From Trump’s Trade War
content: I’m Craig Stirling, a senior editor in Frankfurt. Today we’re looking at the inflation impact on Europe of Chinese exports. Send us feedback and tips to ecodaily@bloomberg.net. And if you aren’t yet signed up to receive this newsletter, you can do so here.

title: Tariff Concerns Drive Global Food Prices to Two-Year High
content: Global food prices rose to a two-year high in April, a sign that tariff uncertainty is starting to put a squeeze on trade.

title: No Fed Cuts Until September Despite Rising Risks, Economists Say
content: Economists see a darkening outlook for the US economy but are sticking by projections for two interest-rate cuts from the Federal Reserve this year.

title: Euro-Zone Inflation Holds Above Target as ECB Weighs Cuts
content: Euro-area inflation unexpectedly held steady and an underlying measure jumped in an awkward report for officials weighing how to respond to the economic hit from US tariffs.

title: China Quietly Exempts About a Quarter of US Imports from Tariffs
content: China has quietly started to exempt some US goods from tariffs that likely cover around $40 billion worth of imports, in what looks like an effort to soften the blow of the trade war on its own economy.

title: Hong Kong’s Growth Unexpectedly Picks Up on Tourism, Export Boom
content: Hong Kong’s economy expanded at the fastest pace in more than a year, benefiting from a recovery in tourism and an export bump before Donald Trump’s drastic tariff hikes.

title: South African Factory Mood Sours in April Amid Trump Trade War
content: South African manufacturers turned more gloomy last month, blaming uncertainty fanned by global tariffs and domestic political strains.

title: Pakistan’s Inflation Slows in April Ahead of Rate Decision
content: Pakistan’s inflation slowed last month, though risks to price gains from global trade disruptions will likely keep the central bank cautious.

title: Japan Seeks US Trade Deal in June Amid Report of Standoff
content: Japan’s chief negotiator expressed hopes of reaching a trade agreement with the US in June, even as a media report indicated the two sides remained at odds on the key issue of its car exports.

title: American Airlines Sues Chicago Over O’Hare Gates for United
content: American Airlines Group Inc. sued the city of Chicago in a fight with rival United Airlines Holding Inc. over valuable gate space at O’Hare International Airport.

title: Google Can Train Search AI With Web Content Even After Opt-Out
content: Google can train its search-specific AI products, like AI Overviews, on content across the web even when the publishers have chosen to opt out of training Google’s AI products, a vice-president of product at the company testified in court on Friday.

title: JetZero’s Triangle-Shaped Jet On Track to Fly By Late 2027
content: JetZero Inc., the start-up aiming to take on planemakers Airbus SE and Boeing Co., is on track to fly the first full-scale model of its manta ray-shaped jetliner by late 2027, executives said Friday.

title: NTSB Probing Aborted Landings at Reagan Due to Army Chopper
content: The National Transportation Safety Board is investigating aborted landings by two flights into Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport due to a nearby US Army Black Hawk helicopter that was traveling to the Pentagon.

title: United to Cut Newark Operations as FAA Issues Snarl Flights
content: United Airlines Holdings Inc. will cut 35 daily round trips at Newark Liberty International Airport after Federal Aviation Administration technology failures and an air traffic controller shortage snarled flights for a full week.

title: Transportation Department Plans to Cut Workforce at End of May
content: Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy told employees in a town hall Friday that he’s planning to reduce the department’s workforce at the end of this month.

title: Big Oil Refuses to Budge on Production Ahead of OPEC+ Decision
content: The largest western oil producers are mostly sticking with their growth plans for now, despite a 16% decline in crude prices during April and the potential for further increases in output from OPEC+.

title: US Approves $3.5 Billion Weapons Sale to Saudi Arabia
content: The US approved the sale of weapons worth an estimated $3.5 billion to Saudi Arabia ahead of a planned visit by President Donald Trump to the Gulf kingdom this month, as Washington seeks to strengthen ties with a key partner and ratchet up pressure against Iran.

title: US Approves Up to $350 Million in Ukraine F-16 Training, Support
content: The US State Department approved F-16 fighter-jet training and services for Ukraine worth up to $350 million, signaling that the White House will keep supporting Kyiv in the fight against Russia despite President Donald Trump’s impatience to end the war.

title: I Squared Nears Deal for $5 Billion Matterhorn Pipeline
content: A consortium led by I Squared Capital is considering buying Matterhorn Express Pipeline in a deal that would value the Texas natural gas conduit at about $5 billion including debt, according to people familiar with the matter.

title: Nike, Adidas Call on Trump to Exempt Footwear From Tariffs
content: A trade association representing footwear producers has asked the Trump administration to consider tariff exemptions for its products, saying the levies will drive up the cost of shoes in the US and cause businesses to shutter.

title: Sun Country Airlines CEO Says Demand Woes Risk Extending Into Summer
content: The pace of air travel early this summer is uncertain as consumers who drove a sharp decline in demand last quarter remain worried about the economy, the top executive of Sun Country Airlines Holdings Inc. said.

title: Chevron Cuts Buybacks and Exxon Sits Tight as Oil Plunges
content: Chevron Corp. will reduce share buybacks this quarter after oil prices tumbled, indicating that President Donald Trump’s trade war is hurting a key US industry he pledged to help.

title: GM Cuts Workers at Canada Truck Plant, Citing Trade Turmoil
content: A General Motors Co. assembly plant in Canada that makes pickup trucks mostly for export to the US will cut down to two shifts from three because of the trade war.

title: Shein’s London IPO Stalled Amid US Tariff Fallout
content: Shein Group Ltd.’s initial public offering plan has slowed to a crawl as the retailer assesses the impact of US tariffs on its business and awaits regulatory approvals, according to people familiar with the matter.

title: US Measles Cases Hit 935 as RFK Jr. Pushes Treatment Study
content: The US reported 51 new measles infections on Friday, an increase of 6% from the previous week as Robert F. Kennedy Jr., the nation’s top health official, pushed for research into unproven treatments.

title: Trump Administration Proposes Cutting $6 Billion From NASA’s Budget
content: President Donald Trump’s proposed budget for next year calls for sweeping cuts to many of NASA’s programs, including a plan to phase out the agency’s Boeing Co.-made moon rocket, reduce crews and operations on the International Space Station and gut science initiatives.

title: Trump’s Auto Tariff Relief Shields USMCA Auto Parts From 25% Tax
content: President Donald Trump’s revised auto tariff plan continues — at least for now — an exemption for parts that comply with the free trade agreement spanning North America, a concession desperately sought by industry.

title: Retailer Claire’s to Defer Debt Interest Payments Amid Tariff Tensions
content: Claire’s Stores Inc. is choosing to defer interest payments on its debt as a way to conserve cash as the US-China trade war roils retailer supply chains.

title: Norway’s Equinor Offloads Stake in Brazilian Oil Field for $3.5 Billion
content: Equinor ASA agreed to sell its 60% stake in the Peregrino oil and gas project off the Brazilian coast to PRIO SA for $3.5 billion, as the Norwegian energy explorer seeks to streamline international operations. Rio de Janeiro-based PRIO gained.

title: Xcel CEO Says AI Power Needs Boost Chance of New Big Nuclear
content: It’s been more than a decade since the US last broke ground on a large-scale nuclear power plant that came online. Xcel Chief Executive Officer Bob Frenzel is raising the idea that it’s time to start again.

title: Auto Workers Welcome Trump’s Tariffs, No Matter What’s Happening on Wall Street
content: Some auto workers like James Benson Jr. are all-in on President Donald Trump’s trade war — and they don’t mind if it causes some short-term pain for both Wall Street and Main Street.

title: Medical Equipment Makers Stryker, Becton Eye Price Hikes to Offset Tariffs
content: Medical equipment makers including Stryker Corp. and Becton Dickinson & Co. are looking to pass on at least some of the estimated tariff hit to customers by raising prices.

title: Wendy’s Adds to Restaurant Woes on ‘Challenging’ US Market
content: Wendy’s Co. lowered its sales outlook for this year, the latest restaurant chain to take a hit from consumer unease about shaky economic conditions in the US.

title: Diamond’s Atlas Raises About $150 Million for Regional-Bank Bets
content: Bob Diamond’s Atlas Merchant Capital raised roughly $150 million so far for a fund dedicated to investing in US regional banks, according to a person with knowledge of the matter.

title: How an Israeli Hostage Negotiator Outsmarts Ransomware Hackers
content: Moty Cristal honed his talent for high-stakes negotiations dealing with Hamas and Hezbollah before expanding to talks with ransomware gangs.

title: Japan’s Buffett-Backed Trading Houses Brace for Tariff Impact
content: Major Japanese trading houses, backed by Warren Buffett, this week released cautious profit forecasts for the year, setting aside millions to hedge against persistent tariff uncertainty.

title: Shell Shows Its Strength by Sticking to Plans Amid Oil Downturn
content: Shell Plc stood out from its peers by sticking to plans for investor returns and capital spending even as oil prices entered what could be a prolonged downturn.

title: Cigna Lifts Forecast After Quarterly Profit, Sales Top Estimates
content: Cigna Group raised its annual forecast and posted first-quarter earnings that beat Wall Street expectations, offering reassurance to investors still rattled by UnitedHealth Group Inc.’s shock forecast cut.

title: Gold Fields in Talks to Acquire Australian Miner Gold Road
content: Gold Fields Ltd. said it’s in talks to acquire Gold Road Resources Ltd., hours after the Australian company’s shares were suspended from trading in Sydney, following media speculation over a deal.

title: Your AI-powered credit card will shop for you now
content: We're not lazy enough, so Visa and Mastercard have hired AI personal assistants to do our shopping

content: Volkswagen AG’s Audi continues to struggle with low returns as the German carmaker contends with tepid demand in Europe and intensifying competition in China.

title: Santander Sells 49% in Polish Unit to Erste for €6.8 Billion
content: Banco Santander SA agreed to sell 49% of its Polish unit to Erste Group Bank AG for about €6.8 billion ($7.7 billion), in one of the largest banking transactions in Europe in recent years.

title: Oil Sinks as OPEC+ Supply Surge Threatens to Swamp Global Market
content: Oil buckled on concerns of a global glut after OPEC+ agreed to another bumper output increase, adding to supply at a time when demand is challenged by the drag from the trade war.

title: Emerging Asia Currencies Rally, Spurred by Trade Deal Hopes
content: The currencies of Taiwan and Malaysia led advances among Asian peers on Monday, with sentiment lifted by hopes of a thaw in China-US trade tensions.

title: Swiss Inflation Drops to Zero as SNB Mulls More Rate Cuts
content: Swiss inflation slowed to the weakest in more than four years as the strong franc drives down the costs of imported goods.

title: Taiwan’s Markets Shaken as Currency Surges Most Since 1980s
content: Taiwan’s dollar surged as much as 5% on Monday, the biggest intraday gain in over three decades, on speculation exporters are rushing to convert their holdings of US dollars to the island’s currency.

title: Insight with Haslinda Amin  5/5/2025
content: Insight with Haslinda Amin, a daily news program featuring in-depth, high-profile interviews and analysis to give viewers the complete picture on the stories that matter. The show features prominent leaders spanning the worlds of business, finance, politics and culture. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: US Stock Futures Fall With Weak Dollar, Oil Drops: Markets Wrap
content: The dollar weakened and US equity-index futures dropped, threatening to end the S&P 500 Index’s longest winning streak in two decades, as US trade policy uncertainty hung over markets.

title: Taiwan Dollar Sees Generational Gain Against Greenback
content: Taiwan’s dollar surged on Monday, the biggest intraday gain in over three decades, on speculation exporters are rushing to convert their holdings of US dollars to the island’s currency. Bloomberg MLIV Strategist Mark Cranfield shares his insights. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: China Resumes Spot LNG Purchases to Take Advantage of Price Drop
content: Chinese firms are purchasing liquefied natural gas shipments from the spot market, a reversal of months of relative inactivity from the world’s top buyer, after prices slumped to the lowest level in about a year.

title: Dollar’s Decline Is Fueling Dislocations Across Asian FX
content: Asian currencies ripped higher against the US dollar Monday, extending a move that’s hurting exporters, weighing on equities and forcing central banks to intervene in the market to curb excessive gains.

title: Dubai Ruler’s Investment Firm Plans to List Residential REIT
content: An investment conglomerate owned by Dubai’s ruler plans to list a portfolio of residential property assets on the local bourse, seeking to capitalize on the emirate’s real estate boom.

title: India Removes Top Envoy to IMF Who Criticized Fund’s Analysis
content: India recalled its top representative to the International Monetary Fund, a former adviser to Prime Minister Narendra Modi who publicly criticized the fund’s analysis.

title: Adani Camp Met US Officials in Push to End Bribery Cases
content: Bloomberg has learned that representatives for Indian billionaire Gautam Adani and his companies met Trump administration officials about dismissing the criminal charges levied against him in an overseas bribery probe. Bloomberg's P R Sanjai shares what we know so far. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Bloomberg: The Asia Trade 5/5/2025
content: "Bloomberg: The Asia Trade" brings you everything you need to know to get ahead as the trading day begins in Asia. Bloomberg TV is live from Tokyo and Sydney with Shery Ahn and Haidi Stroud-Watts, getting insight and analysis from newsmakers and industry leaders on the biggest stories shaping global markets. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Trump Says He’s Willing to Lower China Tariffs 'at Some Point'
content: US President Donald Trump says he is willing to lower tariffs on China "at some point" because the levies now are so high that the world’s two largest economies have essentially stopped doing business with each other. Bloomberg's Minmin Low has the latest. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Asian Finance Chiefs Call for Regional Unity Amid Tariff Talks
content: Asian finance ministers and central bankers called for unity and reaffirmed their commitment to fair and free trade amid rising protectionism that they said weighs on the global economy.

title: How Trump's 100% Tariff on Overseas Films May Play Out
content: President Donald Trump says he plans to impose a 100% tariff on films produced overseas, extending his restrictive trade policies on US imports to the entertainment sector for the first time. Alpha CEO Steven Wolfe Pereira, a former Univision executive, suggests this will be difficult to implement as a way to boost "made in America" because most productions are global in nature, and foreign markets like China — the world's second-largest market for films — are key to a movie's success. He speaks on Bloomberg's The China Show. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Option Traders Bet on Aussie Outshining Kiwi as Trade Fears Ebb
content: Investors are buying currency options on the Australian dollar, wagering it will outperform its New Zealand counterpart as global trade tensions ease.

title: TechnologyOne CEO: We Need a 'Team Australia' Approach
content: The head of ASX-listed TechnologyOne, provider of software as a service (Saas), says the next Australian government needs to back of the nation's business community when the rest of the world "is not going to do us any favors." He adds that the government also has to face up to the twin crises of collapsing R&D investment and sliding productivity. TechnologyOne CEO and Managing Director Ed Chung speaks from Brisbane with Haidi Stroud-Watts and Shery Ahn on "Bloomberg: The Asia Trade." (Source: Bloomberg)

title: 'More Weakness' to Come in US Economy: Morgan Stanley's Craig
content: Despite a bounce back in US equities as markets hope for light at the end of the tunnel in Trump's tariff war, there may still be "more weakness to come" in the US economy, according to Morgan Stanley's Kerry Craig. Speaking on Bloomberg TV, Craig adds that while he currently recommends global diversification, the US still has some "really good, high quality" companies that will continue to deliver. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Vietnam Keeps Growth Target at 8% Despite Tariff Challenges
content: Vietnam’s prime minister said the nation’s economic growth target remains unchanged this year despite the many challenges it faces, as the threat of US tariffs creates uncertainty for exporters and businesses.

title: Asian Finance Chiefs Call for Regional Unity Amid Tariff Talks
content: Asian finance ministers and central bankers called for unity and reaffirmed their commitment to fair and free trade amid rising protectionism that they said weighs on the global economy.

title: Albanese’s Win Offers Rare Chance to Fix Australia’s Economy
content: Prime Minister Anthony Albanese shocked Australia by securing an historic win in Saturday’s election. Now the question is whether he’ll use that mandate to push through tough measures to overhaul the nation’s economy.

title: Indonesia Seen to Cut Rate Twice This Year Amid US Tariff Talks
content: Indonesia’s central bank is expected to resume monetary easing after holding its rate unchanged for three consecutive meetings, moving to bolster economic growth against the backdrop of rising tariffs and trade policy uncertainty.

title: Billionaires and CEOs Gather for Milken in a Reeling LA
content: The second-largest US city is bearing the brunt of climate, housing and political challenges, with tariffs and deportations threatening more pain.

title: Maldives Plans $8.8 Billion Financial Hub Backed by Qatari Royal
content: The government of Maldives said it plans to build an $8.8 billion financial hub backed by Dubai-based MBS Global Investments as the country seeks to address a debt crisis.

title: Trade Chaos Is Part of the Plan for Trump, Nightmare for Powell
content: Jim Tuchler, a Chicago-area retailer, and Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell have a lot in common these days.

title: French Premier Says Referendum May Be Needed for Reform Plan
content: French Prime Minister Francois Bayrou said he intends to present a plan to reduce the country’s debt pile and boost production in the euro area’s second-biggest economy, and didn’t rule out a referendum to secure public backing for the reforms.

title: Oil Sinks as OPEC+ Supply Surge Threatens to Swamp Global Market
content: Oil buckled on concerns of a global glut after OPEC+ agreed to another bumper output increase, adding to supply at a time when demand is challenged by the drag from the trade war.

title: Trump Plans 100% Levy on Foreign Films, Deepening Trade War
content: President Donald Trump announced Sunday that he plans to impose a 100% tariff on films produced overseas, extending his restrictive trade policies on US imports to the entertainment sector for the first time.

title: JetZero’s Triangle-Shaped Jet on Track to Fly by 2027
content: JetZero Inc., the start-up aiming to take on planemakers Airbus SE and Boeing Co., is on track to fly the first full-scale model of its manta ray-shaped jetliner by late 2027, executives said Friday.

title: US Prepares Air-Traffic Overhaul as Vulnerabilities Rock Newark
content: The Trump administration’s plan to modernize the aging US air traffic-control system has gained fresh urgency after vulnerabilities with the existing system pushed United Airlines Holdings Inc. to cut flights at the second-busiest hub serving New York City.

title: Saudi Chemicals Giant Posts Another Surprise Earnings Loss
content: Saudi chemicals giant Sabic recorded a surprise loss in earnings for a second straight quarter as the company suffers a slowdown in sales and undertakes a restructuring of its business to reduce costs.

content: The Russo bros. reportedly directed Thunderbolts*' post-credits scene, which suggests it's more closely linked to Avengers: Doomsday than it seems.

title: European Gas Prices Rise on Concerns Over Global LNG Competition

content: Horizons Middle East & Africa is your daily spotlight on one of the world's fastest-growing regions. Live from Dubai, we bring you the latest global markets and analysis, plus news-making interviews, with a special focus on MEA. All that and more, as you head to the office in the Gulf, pause for lunch in Hong Kong, or start your day in London or Johannesburg.  (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Vestas Keeps Earnings Forecast Despite ‘Global Uncertainty’
content: Vestas Wind Systems A/S maintained profit guidance for this year as it continues to execute on a turnaround plan after steep losses in recent years.

title: Indian E-Scooter Maker Ather’s Shares Reverse Early Listing Gain
content: Ather Energy Ltd.’s shares reversed early gains to fall Tuesday in their Mumbai debut, as traders look to India’s first major initial public offering this fiscal year for clues on the local equity capital market outlook.

title: Insight with Haslinda Amin  5/6/2025
content: Insight with Haslinda Amin, a daily news program featuring in-depth, high-profile interviews and analysis to give viewers the complete picture on the stories that matter. The show features prominent leaders spanning the worlds of business, finance, politics and culture. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Vakhshouri: Oil Markets Expected OPEC+ Response
content:
Oil prices tumbled as the trading week began after OPEC+ agreed to increase output further in June. Sara Vakhshouri, President & Founder of SVB Energy International, spoke to Horizons Middle East and Africa anchor 
Joumanna Bercetche on the move from the oil producers (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Sudan’s Crucial Port Rocked by Blasts as Civil War Intensifies
content: Explosions rocked the airport and port at Sudan’s main coastal city on Tuesday, the latest escalation in two years of conflict between the North African nation’s army and the Rapid Support Forces militia.

title: How Ambani's Campa Cola is Hurting Coke, Pepsi in India
content:
Asia's richest man, Mukesh Ambani, is challenging Coca-Cola and PepsiCo's dominance in India with Reliance Industries' Campa Cola brand.
Bloomberg's Satviki Sanjay appeared on Insight with Haslinda Amin to discuss what's behind the growing success of the brand. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Saadi: Sentiment Rather Than Tariffs Impact Mideast Markets
content: Equity capital markets in the Middle East are defying the volatility induced by US President Donald Trump's tariffs. Dubai Holding, an investment conglomerate owned by Dubai's ruler plans to list a portfolio of residential property assets on the local exchange to capitalize on the emirate's real estate boom. Rudy Saadi, Managing Director and Head of MENA ECM at Citi told Horizons Middle East and Africa anchor Joumanna Bercetche on the timing of the REIT. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Bloomberg: The China Show 05/06/2025
content: “Bloomberg: The China Show” is your definitive source for news and analysis on the world's second-biggest economy. From politics and policy to tech and trends, Yvonne Man and David Ingles give global investors unique insight, delivering in-depth discussions with the newsmakers who matter. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: What Albanese's Win Means for Australian Businesses
content: Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese won a historic re-election on the promise of bolstering the economy, addressing the cost of living crisis, and tax cuts. Australian Chamber of Commerce and Industry CEO Andrew McKellar discusses the outlook for Australian businesses and the impact of Trump's tariff war on "Bloomberg: The Asia Trade." (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Tariffs Force Bank of England to Consider Faster Pace of Cuts
content: The Bank of England is set to cut interest rates by a quarter point this week and may even pave the way for a series of back-to-back reductions for the first time since 2009 as it responds to America’s global trade war.

title: Ex-ArcelorMittal Dealmaker Seeks $1 Billion for Latest Fund
content: Synergy Capital, founded by former ArcelorMittal SA executive Sudhir Maheshwari, is looking to raise $1 billion by next year for its latest fund that focuses on private credit in Asia, particularly in India.

title: Chinese Media Reports Holiday Travel Surge
content: Chinese media are reporting a surge in travel and retail spending over the May Day holiday, with cross-regional passenger traffic up 8%. But as Bloomberg's China correspondent, Minmin Low, explains - not all of the data so far paints a rosy picture. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: South Korea to Seal Nuclear Deal With Czech Republic This Week
content: A South Korean group, led by Korea Hydro & Nuclear Power Co., will sign a final agreement to build two nuclear reactors at the Dukovany complex in the Czech Republic this week, Seoul’s industry ministry said in a statement.

title: Gold Extends Gains on Demand From China Following Holidays
content: Gold extended gains — following a surge of almost 3% on Monday — as the world’s biggest bullion buyer came back from holiday, boosting demand despite a firmer dollar.

title: Bloomberg: The Asia Trade 5/6/2025
content: "Bloomberg: The Asia Trade" brings you everything you need to know to get ahead as the trading day begins in Asia. Bloomberg TV is live from Tokyo and Sydney with Shery Ahn and Haidi Stroud-Watts, getting insight and analysis from newsmakers and industry leaders on the biggest stories shaping global markets. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: JPMorgan and BofA Stick With CATL Deal Despite US House Opposition
content: JPMorgan Chase & Co. and Bank of America Corp. have forged ahead working on the blockbuster listing of Contemporary Amperex Technology Co. Ltd. despite a US congressional committee calling for the American lenders to drop out of the deal.

title: Thai Inflation Turning Negative Set to Aid More Rate Cuts
content: Thailand’s inflation turned negative for the first time in more than a year on cheaper fuel prices and increased fresh food supplies, creating more room for the central bank to cut rates further to deal with the impact of the trade war.

title: Shanghai Gold Exchange to Expand Warehouse Network to Hong Kong
content: The Shanghai Gold Exchange plans to expand its warehouse network to Hong Kong, helping to raise the profile of its yuan-denominated products, including for the precious metal, beyond mainland China.

title: Chinese Trade Flow Resilient at End of April Despite US Tariffs
content: China’s trade flows increased at the end of April, indicating the damage from US tariffs has yet to manifest in actual shipments even though the trade war is widely expected to eventually slow the world’s second-largest economy.

title: SMFG Said to Be in Talks to Buy Minority Stake in Yes Bank
content: Sumitomo Mitsui Financial Group Inc., Japan’s second-biggest lender, is in talks to buy a significant minority stake in India’s Yes Bank Ltd., according to people familiar with the matter.

title: Oil Gains From Four-Year Low as Technicals Hint Slide Overdone
content: Oil climbed from the lowest close in four years after a technical measure signaled the recent slump was overdone.

title: Clearlake Seeks to Triple Assets at Credit Unit to $100 Billion
content: Clearlake Capital Group is aiming to triple its credit business with the launch of a unit to help the buyout firm grab a bigger slice of the booming asset class.

title: Hong Kong Ramps Up FX Intervention to Defend Currency Peg
content: Hong Kong authorities ramped up sales of the local dollar as the greenback’s slide threatened the foreign-exchange peg.

title: Wall Street Banks Said to Steer Clear of Chery’s $1.5 Billion Hong Kong IPO
content: One of this year’s biggest listings is coming together in Hong Kong without the involvement of Wall Street banks.

title: Russia Mulls Tightening Budget Rule Over Slumping Oil Prices
content: Russia is considering changing its key budget-building mechanism in response to sliding oil revenue, in a sign the Kremlin expects crude prices will remain lower for longer while the war in Ukraine continues to drain state coffers.

title: Myanmar Junta Extends Post-Quake Truce Amid Reports of Breaches
content: Myanmar’s military, also known as the Tatmadaw, announced an extension of a ceasefire until the end of this month, though there have been multiple reports of continued air strikes and mortar attacks on rebel-held territories during the recent truce.

title: Sudan’s Crucial Port Rocked by Blasts as Civil War Intensifies
content: Explosions rocked the airport and port at Sudan’s main coastal city on Tuesday, the latest escalation in two years of conflict between the North African nation’s army and the Rapid Support Forces militia.

title: Pakistan Says India Chokes River Flow as Tensions Rise
content: Pakistan alleged that India has almost entirely stopped the flow of water across the border through the Chenab river as fears of a clash between the two neighbors mount following a deadly attack in Kashmir.

title: Merz to Start as German Chancellor, Replacing Scholz
content: Friedrich Merz will take over as German Chancellor on Tuesday, replacing Olaf Scholz. After a confirmation vote in the lower house of parliament in Berlin, the conservative leader will be sworn in as the head of a coalition government of his center-right CDU/CSU bloc and the center-left party Social Democrats. Bloomberg’s Oliver Crook reports.

title: German Conservative Merz Wants a Fast Start as New Chancellor
content: Friedrich Merz has vowed to hit the ground running when he takes over as German chancellor on Tuesday, pledging swift action to galvanize Europe’s biggest economy, restore Berlin’s leadership role on the global stage and address voter concerns about irregular migration.

title: NY Acts to Bar Trump DOT From Denying Funds in Congestion Case
content: New York asked a judge to stop the Trump administration from withholding federal approvals or funds in the president’s push to end Manhattan’s congestion pricing program.

title: India Offers Zero-for-Zero Tariffs on Auto Parts, Steel From US
content: India has proposed zero tariffs on steel, auto components and pharmaceuticals on a reciprocal basis up to a certain quantity of imports in its trade negotiations with the US, people familiar with the matter said.

title: Trump Blocks Harvard From New Research Funding in Latest Blow
content: The Trump administration is declaring Harvard University ineligible for new research grants from the federal government in the latest escalation between the White House and the Ivy League school.

title: Hegseth Says ‘Lean and Mean’ Military Requires Cutting Officers
content: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth ordered a reduction of the US military’s highest-ranking officers — potentially setting up a clash with Congress, which must approve any such adjustments.

title: Sri Lanka’s President Seeks Reform Mandate From Local Elections
content: Sri Lankan President Anura Kumara Dissanayake swept to power last year with an unprecedented super-majority government. Now, he arguably faces an even more crucial election.

title: Stablecoin Coalition Cracks as Democrats Threaten Filibuster
content: A bipartisan alliance backing stablecoin legislation shattered in the US Senate as a key group of Democrats threatened to block a bill that Republicans had hoped to pass this month — unless “numerous” fixes are made.

title: Alberta’s Smith Plans Talks With Carney, Says Separation Vote Possible
content: Alberta Premier Danielle Smith said she’s appointing a group to negotiate with the Canadian government on removing laws that restrict energy production, adding that a referendum on the province separating from Canada may be on the ballot as soon as next year.

title: Trump Administration Offers Migrants $1,000 to Self-Deport
content: The Trump administration is offering undocumented migrants $1,000 and paid travel if they agree to leave the US voluntarily, the latest effort to ramp up mass deportations and slash enforcement costs.

title: New Zealand’s National Party Seeks Social Media Age Restrictions
content: New Zealand’s governing National Party wants to restrict access to social media for those aged under 16 years, mirroring a move in Australia that sparked criticism from global tech giants.

title: Milken Crowd Warms Up to Tariffs While Condemning All the Chaos
content: Scott Bessent walked on stage at the largest gathering in months of Wall Street’s champions of global trade, aiming to explain why President Donald Trump is putting up hurdles to global trade.

title: US Space-Based Missile Defense Could Cost $542 Billion, CBO Says
content: The US may need to spend up to $542 billion over 20 years to develop and launch a network of space-based interceptors, the Congressional Budget Office said, putting a rough cost estimate on an unproven part of President Donald Trump’s proposed “Golden Dome” defense system.

title: FCC’s Carr Calls for Spectrum, AI Leadership in China Race
content: The Trump administration is focused on freeing up more electromagnetic spectrum to power wireless communication, the chairman of the Federal Communications Commission said on Monday, a move that could generate $80 billion in government revenue and help the US better compete with China.

title: Trump Signs Order Targeting Gain-of-Function Virus Research
content: President Donald Trump signed an executive order looking to limit federal funding for gain-of-function research that involves altering pathogens, suggesting the efforts could have been responsible for the outbreak of the Covid-19 pandemic.

title: Adani Camp Meets Trump Officials in Bid to End Bribery Cases

content: Israel’s security cabinet voted to intensify military operations in Gaza and call up of tens of thousands of extra reservists, while also deciding on a means of distributing aid in the Palestinian territory.

content: President Donald Trump said the sliding price of oil is intensifying pressure on Russia and boosting the odds for a deal to end its war in Ukraine.

title: US Army Puts Chopper Training Flights Around Pentagon on Pause
content: The US Army is suspending helicopter training flights around the Pentagon and Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport as authorities investigate an incident last week that saw two passenger jets abort landings to avoid a Black Hawk in the area.

content: California Governor Gavin Newsom called for federal tax credits of at least $7.5 billion and a partnership with the Donald Trump White House to help bring more filmmaking to the US.

content: Microsoft Corp. expanded its deal to buy carbon removal credits from heat-plant operator Stockholm Exergi AB, increasing volumes first agreed last year by more than 50%.

content: Elon Musk’s attorney said OpenAI’s decision to partly walk back its plan to restructure as a for-profit business “changes nothing,” a sign the billionaire may continue with his legal crusade against the startup led by Sam Altman.

content: Most people in the developing world expect artificial intelligence to boost productivity over the next year, the United Nations found, with new technologies potentially helping to counter an “unprecedented slowdown” in human development.

content: Hasan Sukkar, founder and chief executive officer of the artificial intelligence startup 11x AI Inc., has stepped down, according to a LinkedIn post. He will transition to the role of non-executive chairman.

title: FCC’s Carr Calls for Spectrum, AI Leadership in China Race
content: The Trump administration is focused on freeing up more electromagnetic spectrum to power wireless communication, the chairman of the Federal Communications Commission said on Monday, a move that could generate $80 billion in government revenue and help the US better compete with China.

title: Bessent on AI, Hollywood Shaken by Tariff Threat | Bloomberg Technology
content: Bloomberg’s Caroline Hyde discusses the drop in media stocks following President Trump’s proposal to impose 100% tariffs on foreign-produced movies. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, speaking from the Milken Institute Global Conference, says the US must win the race to develop artificial intelligence as China closes the gap. Daniel Morgan, senior portfolio manager at Synovus Trust, explains what's behind the market dip after a four-day rally. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: GameStop Sells Its Canadian Business to Toy Entrepreneur
content: French-Canadian entrepreneur Stephan Tétrault has acquired GameStop Corp.’s Canadian stores, according to a Monday press release.

title: DoorDash Is the Latest Tech Firm to Commit Millions to NYC Elections
content: DoorDash Inc. is committing $5 million to back political candidates in New York City and state-level races in New Jersey this year, becoming the latest technology company to disclose its lobbying efforts ahead of local elections in the tristate area.

title: OpenAI Walks Back For-Profit Plan, Nonprofit to Keep Control
content: OpenAI is backtracking on plans to become a more conventional for-profit company after facing mounting pressure from former employees, academics and rivals, including billionaire Elon Musk.

title: Goldman Sees Buy-the-Dip Opportunity in AI After Big Tech Earnings
content: Better-than-expected results late last month from some of the biggest technology companies using artificial intelligence signal an opportunity for investors to pick up shares in the cohort after the recent slump, according to a group of analysts at Goldman Sachs.

title: Message App That Waltz Was Seen Using Is Probing Possible Breach
content: TeleMessage, the message-archiving app that former National Security Adviser Michael Waltz appeared to be using in a photograph of him communicating with other Trump administration officials, is investigating whether hackers exploited its technology.

title: Palantir’s History of Blowouts Faces Highest Multiple on Wall St
content: Palantir Technologies Inc. investors have been betting that the results coming after the markets close on Monday will be another blowout, but the recent run up has given the stock a high bar to clear.

title: Rivian Deepens Illinois Ties With $120 Million EV Supplier Park
content: Rivian Automotive Inc. is investing $120 million in a new supplier park in Illinois, another win for Governor JB Pritzker after the company announced a $1.5 billion plan to expand its plant in the state.

title: Macron Urges US Scientists to Choose Europe After Trump Upheaval
content: French President Emmanuel Macron made a plea to US-based researchers who have been affected by Donald Trump’s policies to choose Europe.

title: Saudi-Backed Port Developer Weighs South Africa Harbor Deal
content: Saudi Arabian ports operator Red Sea Gateway Terminal, backed by the kingdom’s $925 billion sovereign wealth fund, is evaluating whether to bid to develop and run a fresh-produce terminal at Africa’s biggest maritime hub.

title: Starlink Rival Eutelsat Replaces CEO With Telecom Executive
content: Eutelsat Communications SA, the French satellite operator that Europe is trying to position as a homegrown alternative to Elon Musk’s Starlink, is replacing its chief executive officer.

title: Apple Reaches Critical Juncture With Tariffs, AI and Services Turmoil
content: Apple is facing one of its toughest periods yet as it copes with the threat of tariffs, supply chain challenges, AI struggles and potential turmoil in its services business. Also: The company’s China AI launch will likely be part of iOS 18.6, reorganizations extend to Apple’s music and global affairs teams, and flying taxi startup Archer hires a new head of AI.

title: Effort to Close De Minimis US Tariff Loophole ‘Could Get Messy’
content: Welcome to Tech In Depth, our daily newsletter with reporting and analysis about the business of tech from Bloomberg’s journalists around the world. Today, Spencer Soper reports that closing the de minimis duty-free loophole for low-cost goods into the US is likely to have ripple effects across the economic landscape.

title: Chinese Consumers Weather Trade War in First Big Holiday Test
content: Chinese consumers persevered at malls and restaurants during one of the country’s busiest holiday periods, though sentiment remains shaky against the backdrop of a new trade war with the US.

title: Swedbank Sees Riksbank Delivering Two More Rate Cuts This Year
content: Analysts at Swedbank AB now expect the Riksbank to cut its key interest rate twice by the end of the third quarter, to 1.75%, saying that lower inflation would allow policymakers to bolster the still-sluggish economy.

title: Tariffs Force Bank of England to Consider Faster Pace of Cuts
content: The Bank of England is set to cut interest rates by a quarter point this week and may even pave the way for a series of back-to-back reductions for the first time since 2009 as it responds to America’s global trade war.

title: Thai Inflation Turning Negative Set to Aid More Rate Cuts
content: Thailand’s inflation turned negative for the first time in more than a year on cheaper fuel prices and increased fresh food supplies, creating more room for the central bank to cut rates further to deal with the impact of the trade war.

title: Chinese Trade Flow Resilient at End of April Despite US Tariffs
content: China’s trade flows increased at the end of April, indicating the damage from US tariffs has yet to manifest in actual shipments even though the trade war is widely expected to eventually slow the world’s second-largest economy.

title: Developing Nations Expect AI Productivity Boost Soon, UN Finds
content: Most people in the developing world expect artificial intelligence to boost productivity over the next year, the United Nations found, with new technologies potentially helping to counter an “unprecedented slowdown” in human development.

title: Moody’s Sees Key Risk to Malaysia Credit Rating From Tariffs
content: Tariff shocks pose a major threat to Malaysia’s sovereign credit rating, given the potential disruption to economic growth and fiscal consolidation, according to Moody’s Ratings.

title: India Offers Zero-for-Zero Tariffs on Auto Parts, Steel From US
content: India has proposed zero tariffs on steel, auto components and pharmaceuticals on a reciprocal basis up to a certain quantity of imports in its trade negotiations with the US, people familiar with the matter said.

title: Philippines Signals More Rate Cuts After Inflation Slowdown
content: The Philippine central bank on Tuesday signaled further monetary easing ahead after inflation slowed to the lowest level since 2019, and warned of a “more challenging external environment.”

title: China Services Activity Slips, Adding Risk of Rapid Slowdown
content: China’s services activity deteriorated more than expected in April, a private survey showed, the latest setback for an economy already under pressure from US tariffs.

title: Australia’s Household Spending Surprisingly Drops on Cyclone Hit
content: Australia’s household spending unexpectedly declined in March, snapping five months of increases as the impact of a major storm in the nation’s northeast disrupted activity.

title: Macquarie CEO Says Australia Is Resilient Despite Tariffs
content: Macquarie Group Ltd. Chief Executive Officer Shemara Wikramanayake said Australia’s economy is looking resilient and is set up well to withstand the shocks emanating from US trade policy.

title: Non-Dom Changes May Cost UK More Than It Raises, Research Warns
content: The UK’s tax overhaul for wealthy foreigners will start costing more than it raises if one in four of those affected leaves the country, according to the Centre for Economics and Business Research.

title: CBO Chief Still Sees US Treasury ‘X-Date’ Coming Late Summer
content: The head of the nonpartisan Congressional Budget Office said the US Treasury Department can likely keep paying the government’s bills until late summer before Congress must act to raise or suspend the debt ceiling.

title: Milken Crowd Warms Up to Tariffs While Condemning All the Chaos
content: Scott Bessent walked on stage at the largest gathering in months of Wall Street’s champions of global trade, aiming to explain why President Donald Trump is putting up hurdles to global trade.

title: California Warns of 9% Drop in Foreign Visits in Trump Backlash
content: California warned that a plunge in international travel is set to hit tourism revenue after record spending from visitors last year.

title: Nigeria’s Tinubu Set to Sign Order Prioritizing Local Industries
content: Nigeria’s President Bola Tinubu plans to sign an executive order that will prioritize the procurement of goods and services from local firms, a move that bears some semblance to President Donald Trump’s “America First” agenda that champions US interests.

title: Bessent Touts US as ‘Premier Destination’ for World Capital
content: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent touted the US as the “premier destination” for global capital and argued that the Trump administration’s policies will solidify that position — countering the so-called sell America theme that materialized last month.

title: ECB’s Stournaras Says Interest-Rate Cuts Are Likely to Continue
content: The European Central Bank is set to carry on cutting interest rates, according to Governing Council member Yannis Stournaras.

title: Growth at US Service Providers Picks Up After Slumping in March
content: Activity at US service providers accelerated in April after a slumping in the prior month, while materials prices increased in response to escalating tariffs.

title: Saudi Arabia’s Budget Deficit Soared Even Before Oil’s Slump
content: Saudi Arabia’s budget deficit ballooned in the first quarter, even before oil’s latest drop put additional pressure on the kingdom’s finances.

title: Tariff Concerns Dominate First Day of Milken Conference
Brazil Economists Cut Interest-Rate Forecast on Eve of Policy Meeting
content: Brazil economists cut their 2025 year-end benchmark interest rate forecast just hours before central bankers gather to start debating the size of their next — and perhaps last — borrowing cost hike of their cycle.

title: US Border Towns Are Being Ravaged by Canada’s Furious Boycott
content: Economically dependent on their northern neighbor, business owners in Washington state are laying off employees and shutting their doors.

title: Pakistan Cuts Rate to Shield Economy From Tariff Disruptions
content: Pakistan cut its benchmark interest rate to shield the South Asian nation’s economy from global tariff-related disruption.

title: The Buffett View of Trade Deals
content: The most pertinent thing Warren Buffett said at the weekend beyond announcing his retirement at age 94 wasn’t his thoughts on the tariffs roiling the global economy (he’s not a fan) but his defense of Berkshire Hathaway’s $350 billion cash pile. It was, he said, a consequence of abiding by his principle to invest only in deals that offered meaningful returns and his view there had not been many lately.

title: ‘Strategic Uncertainty’ in US Trade Strategy Toughens Fed’s Job
content: I’m Chris Anstey, an economics editor in Boston, and today we’re looking at reporting by Craig Torres and Michael Sasso on uncertainty and the Fed. Send us feedback and tips to ecodaily@bloomberg.net. And if you aren’t yet signed up to receive this newsletter, you can do so here.

title: South Africa’s Eskom Sees Low Power-Cut Risk as Demand Rises
content: South Africa’s state power utility said the increased reliability of its electricity network will reduce the risk of outages this winter, when demand is expected to increase.

title: Malaysia Seeks to Bring US-Imposed Tariffs Down to Zero in Talks
content: Malaysia is negotiating with the US to bring its tariffs on the Southeast Asian nation down to zero, from the 24% that President Donald Trump pledged to impose, according to Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Zafrul Aziz.

title: AB Foods Confirms Talks With Endless on Future of Bread Unit
content: Associated British Foods Plc said it’s in talks with Endless over a potential combination of the Kingsmill and Hovis brands, two of the UK’s best-known bread producers.

title: Fortress Co-CEO Leaves Texas for London to Lead European Growth
content: Fortress Investment Group co-chief executive officer Josh Pack is moving to London from Dallas as the alternative asset manager ramps up plans to expand in Europe.

title: Vestas Keeps Earnings Forecast Despite ‘Global Uncertainty’
content: Vestas Wind Systems A/S maintained profit guidance for this year as it continues to execute on a turnaround plan after steep losses in recent years.

title: Uniper Reports First-Quarter Loss After Decline in Energy Prices
content: German utility Uniper SE confirmed a first-quarter loss after a drop in energy prices since the start of the year.

title: South Africa’s Second-Largest Asset Manager Eyes East Africa for Growth
content: South Africa’s second-biggest asset manager plans to grow its market share in East Africa to take advantage of the continent’s fastest growing region.

title: Ex-ArcelorMittal Dealmaker Seeks $1 Billion for Latest Fund
content: Synergy Capital, founded by former ArcelorMittal SA executive Sudhir Maheshwari, is looking to raise $1 billion by next year for its latest fund that focuses on private credit in Asia, particularly in India.

title: Shanghai Gold Exchange to Expand Warehouse Network to Hong Kong
content: The Shanghai Gold Exchange plans to expand its warehouse network to Hong Kong, helping to raise the profile of its yuan-denominated products, including for the precious metal, beyond mainland China.

title: Oil Gains From Four-Year Low as Technicals Hint Slide Overdone
content: Oil climbed from the lowest close in four years after a technical measure signaled the recent slump was overdone.

title: India Offers Zero-for-Zero Tariffs on Auto Parts, Steel From US
content: India has proposed zero tariffs on steel, auto components and pharmaceuticals on a reciprocal basis up to a certain quantity of imports in its trade negotiations with the US, people familiar with the matter said.

title: Ambani’s 12-Cent Cola Is Eroding Coke, Pepsi Dominance in India
content: Asia’s richest man is challenging the decades-long dominance of Coca-Cola Co. and PepsiCo Inc. in the most-populous country using a playbook he has practiced to perfection in other sectors: price disruption.

title: UBS Will Pay $511 Million to End Credit Suisse US Tax Probe
content: UBS Group AG agreed to pay $511 million to settle a US investigation into how Credit Suisse Group, the Swiss bank it bought, helped rich Americans evade taxes even after pledging to stop the practice a decade ago.

title: Ford Pulls Outlook, Sees $1.5 Billion Hit From Trump Tariffs
content: Ford Motor Co. suspended its full-year financial guidance and said President Donald Trump’s auto tariffs will take a toll on profit, joining rivals stung by volatile global trade policies.

title: Hims Reiterates 2025 Sales Guidance With Future in Flux
content: Hims & Hers Health Inc. reiterated its 2025 revenue forecast after posting better-than-expected sales for the first quarter, raising questions about the future as it shifts from making copycat weight-loss drugs to selling discounted versions of Novo Nordisk A/S’s blockbuster Wegovy.

title: Rite Aid Files for Second Bankruptcy, Announces Job Cuts
content: Less than a year after completing a restructuring that was supposed to turn the troubled pharmacy chain around, Rite Aid Corp. has filed for bankruptcy again.

title: Northwestern CIO Warns of ‘Destructive’ Tax on University Funds
content: Northwestern University is preparing for a potential tax increase on endowments, a move its chief investment officer labeled as “destructive” for higher education institutions in the US.

title: Vertex Says 20,000 Prescriptions Filled for Non-Opioid Pain Drug
content: Vertex Pharmaceuticals Inc. said more than 20,000 prescriptions have been dispensed for its new non-addictive painkiller, a sign that the drug is gaining some early traction as it attempts to displace opioids.

title: Newark Radar Failure Left Controllers Blind for 90 Seconds
content: Air traffic controllers guiding planes bound for Newark Liberty International Airport lost radar and radio communication for more than a minute early last week before flights at the key hub were snarled for days, according to people familiar with the matter.

title: Nike President O’Neill Out in Latest Shake-Up Under New CEO
content: Nike Inc. is reorganizing its senior leadership team as its new chief executive officer shakes up several top roles at the world’s largest sportswear company.

title: Telemarketers Are Using a Weird Trick to Sell Bare-Bones Health Plans
content: How a former TV comedy writer’s fake-job loophole could blow up Obamacare.

title: Bristol Myers Promises $40 Billion US Investment Over Five Years
content: Bristol Myers Squibb Co. said it will spend $40 billion in the US over the next five years, joining a slew of drug companies promising to bolster their domestic investments as President Donald Trump threatens to impose tariffs on the pharmaceutical industry.

title: Nearly Quarter of People on Long-Acting Opioids Develop Addiction
content: More than one in five people prescribed extended-release painkillers such as OxyContin developed an addiction within a year, according to a newly released study mandated by the US Food and Drug Administration.

title: Clorox Lowers Sales Outlook as Consumers Cut Back on Shopping
content: Clorox Co. lowered to top end of its full-year sales outlook as the worsening economic backdrop saw consumers cut back on spending.

title: UK Reaffirms Support for Film Industry After Trump Tariff Threat
content: The UK government will shortly unveil a new industrial policy for its film sector, as it reaffirms support for its creative industries after US President Donald Trump revealed plans to hit movies produced overseas with a 100% tariff.

title: New York Times Leads Pulitzers With Four; Bloomberg Wins One
content: The New York Times won four Pulitzer Prizes, including the Explanatory Reporting award for its examination of the failures and missteps made by the US in Afghanistan. Bloomberg News won its second Pulitzer — for Alexandra Lange’s criticism on architectural design.

title: Private Bus Operator Boxcar Ramps Up as NJ Transit Strike Looms
content: Private bus operator Boxcar Inc. aims to ramp up service as a potential New Jersey Transit rail workers strike threatens to strand commuters as early as May 16.

title: Oil Drops as OPEC+ Supply Surge Threatens to Swamp Global Market
content: Oil dropped after OPEC+ agreed to another large output increase, raising concern that additional supply could lead to a global glut just as the trade war threatens demand.

title: Mehmet Oz Questions Federal Funding for Medicaid Expansion
content: Mehmet Oz, the US Centers for Medicaid and Medicare Services leader, suggested he supports reducing federal Medicaid funding for the millions of people who gained access to the program through the Affordable Care Act.

title: Trump Vows to Meet Hollywood on Tariff Plan That Shook Industry
content: President Donald Trump said he would meet with Hollywood executives after confounding the US film industry over his plan to impose a 100% tariff on movies made overseas.

title: Citi CEO Says Conflicting Data a Challenge to Fed Rate Decision
content: Conflicting economic signals including strong payrolls and weak consumer sentiment are making the job of Federal Reserve policymakers especially tricky, according to Citigroup Inc. Chief Executive Officer Jane Fraser.

title: 3G Capital to Take Tariff-Hit Skechers Private for $9.4 Billion
content: 3G Capital will acquire footwear maker Skechers USA Inc. for $9.4 billion, marking a splashy return to dealmaking for the investment firm after nearly four years.

content: Global venture funding totaled $23 billion in April 2025, flat year over year and down significantly month over month from $68 billion invested in March, Crunchbase data shows.

title: Chinese Stock Gains Fizzle as Focus Shifts to US Trade Talks
content: Chinese stocks pared earlier gains driven by the central bank’s stimulus, as investors remained wary ahead of trade talks with the US set to start later this week.

title: Oil Extends Gain With US and Chinese Officials Set to Talk Trade
content: Oil pushed higher after rallying more than 3% in the previous session as the US and China agreed to start trade negotiations, raising optimism that tensions between the world’s two biggest economies may ease.

title: Trump Says US Will Stop Houthi Strikes

title: Pakistan Stocks Drop, Indian Assets Steady After Military Strike

title: Shionogi Falls on Report of $1 Billion Offer to Buy Torii Pharma

content: "Bloomberg: The Asia Trade" brings you everything you need to know to get ahead as the trading day begins in Asia. content: India’s targeted military strikes against Pakistan have left analysts debating the possibility of a further escalation in the tensions and its impact on the nations’ economies and markets.

title: US-China Trade Talks to Start This Week
content: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer will travel later this week to Switzerland for trade talks with China led by Vice Premier He Lifeng, seeking to de-escalate a tariff standoff that has threatened to hammer both economies. Bloomberg's Minmin Low has the latest on what we know so far. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: HK Dollar Interest Rate Falls Most Since 2008 After Intervention
content: The Hong Kong dollar’s funding costs plunged the most since 2008, as the monetary authority’s intervention to defend the currency peg helped boost liquidity in the financial system.

title: China Cuts Key Rate, Reserve Ratio to Aid Economy Hit by Tariffs
content: China reduced its policy rate and lowered the amount of cash lenders must keep in reserve, as Beijing ramps up efforts to help an economy caught in a second trade war with the US.

title: Hot, Dry Weather Threatens Output in China’s Wheat-Growing Belt
content: Hot and dry weather is threatening wheat production in China’s top growing region, potentially disrupting output of a key staple grain just as Beijing attempts to bolster food security during a trade war with the US.

title: India’s Defense Stocks See $5 Billion Rally as Border Tensions Escalate
content: Indian defense firms have added more than $5 billion in market valuation since tensions escalated between the country and neighboring Pakistan following a brutal attack on tourists in Kashmir two weeks ago.

title: China Taps New Animal Feed Sources After Falling Out With Canada
content: Chinese traders are scouring the globe for alternative sources of rapeseed, as tensions with Canada, their top supplier, risk choking imports of a key ingredient in animal feed.

title: Dollar Faces $2.5 Trillion ‘Avalanche’ of Asian Sales, Jen Says
content: The dollar may face a $2.5 trillion “avalanche” of selling as Asian countries unwind their stockpile of the world’s reserve currency, according to Stephen Jen.

title: Taiwan’s Currency Surge Steps Up Pressure for Economic Overhaul
content: The Taiwan dollar’s most extreme surge since 1988, along with prospects for continued appreciation, has triggered calls for one of the most export-dependent Asian economies to overhaul its growth model.

title: A Remote and Disputed Corner of Africa Is Cheering Trump
content: The territory of Western Sahara is turning into an ‘El Dorado’ after the US recognized Morocco’s claim over the region.

title: Czechs Set to Cut Rates But Keep Hawkish Tone
content: Czech policymakers will probably cut interest rates again after inflation slowed more than expected, but they may also signal a lengthy pause is now in store due to persistent price risks.

title: Polish Central Bank to Cut Rates Just Before Election Yet Again
content: Poland’s central bank is set to cut interest rates for the first time since 2023 and like the last time the decision will come just days before an important election.

title: Indian LNG Buyers Embrace US Benchmark to Balance Volatility
content: Indian liquefied natural gas importers have signed a flurry of long-term purchase agreements linked to the US price benchmark, the latest effort by the nation’s buyers to protect themselves from volatile markets.

title: Philippines Signals It Won’t Intervene to Cap Peso Strength
content: Philippine central bank Governor Eli Remolona signaled authorities are unlikely to intervene to curb the strength in the peso, sending the local currency to the highest in more than a year.

title: Iron Ore Climbs on PBOC Reserve Cut, US-China Trade Talks
content: Copper fell and iron ore pared gains after China delivered long-awaited rate cuts to shield the top metals-consuming nation from the impact of US tariffs.
