title: CrowdStrike Cuts 500 Jobs as Cyber Firm Works to Lift Sales
content: CrowdStrike Holdings Inc. is cutting about 500 jobs, representing about 5% of its global workforce, as it works toward a goal of generating $10 billion in annual recurring revenue.

title: France’s Mistral Releases AI Model Tailored for Businesses
content: Mistral is releasing a new artificial intelligence model that’s tailored for business use cases, as the French startup tries to capitalize on Europe’s concerns about being overly reliant on technology from Silicon Valley.

title: Uber Posts Quarterly Bookings Miss, Citing Less Travel to US
content: Uber Technologies Inc. reported weaker-than-expected quarterly gross bookings, citing lower US inbound travel that’s led to slower gains in its rideshare business.

title: Bitcoin Rises as US-China Trade Talks Spark Bullish Crypto Bets
content: Bitcoin rose for a second day as optimism over a potential de-escalation in the US-China tariff standoff bolstered demand for riskier assets.

title: Netflix Investors Unfazed by Tariffs With Growth Engine Humming
content: Netflix Inc. has been such a strong performer that not even the threat of massive tariffs on films has been enough for investors to question its prospects.

title: Malaysia Keeps Rate Unchanged as Risks Loom Large From Tariffs
content: Malaysia kept interest rates unchanged on Thursday, saving its policy ammunition amid looming risks to growth from US President Donald Trump’s tariffs.

title: Maersk Cuts Global Container Market Outlook on Tariff War
content: A.P. Moller-Maersk A/S, the Danish container giant, lowered its forecast for the global transport market rattled by Donald Trump’s trade war.

title: AIB Proceeds With 1.2 Billion Buyback with Irish State
content: AIB Group Plc’s board will proceed with a €1.2 billion ($1.4 billion) share buyback from the Irish state, after shareholders approved the deal that will put the bank on the brink of full private ownership.

title: Trump Expected to Unveil US-UK Trade Pact After Talks on Tariffs
content: President Donald Trump is expected to announce a trade agreement with the United Kingdom at a news conference Thursday morning in Washington, according to people familiar with the matter.

title: Turkish Central Bank Chief Defends Interventions to Bolster Lira
content: Turkey’s monetary chief defended the central bank’s decision to sell tens of billions of dollars of reserves to stabilize the lira in recent weeks, striking a defiant tone in the face of criticism from politicians.

title: UK House Prices Post First Gain in Three Months, Halifax Says
content: UK house prices rose for the first time since January as demand proved resilient in the face of higher taxes and a gloomier economic outlook, according to one of Britain’s largest mortgage lenders.

title: German Industrial Production Increased Before US Tariff Barrage
content: German industrial production rose in March, a period in which looming trade barriers by the US administration probably boosted foreign demand.

title: Trump Says He’ll Raise Jimmy Lai’s Case in China Trade Talks
content: President Donald Trump said he will raise the case of ex-media mogul Jimmy Lai as part of US trade talks with China, a move likely to antagonize Beijing just days before the two sides meet.

title: RBI Bumper Payout to Help Offset Weak Revenues, Analysts Say
content: India’s central bank is expected to pay a record dividend to the government, offsetting shortfall in tax revenues due to slow growth and helping meet any emergency spending needs, economists said.

title: Trump Aid Cut Threatens Africa’s Growth, AfDB Candidate Warns
content: US President Donald Trump’s plan to cut hundreds of millions of dollars of funding to the African Development Bank will hit growth on the continent, said Samuel Maimbo, a candidate to take over the leadership of the lender.

title: Thailand Braces For ‘Temporary’ Investment Freeze As US Tariffs Remain Uncertain
content: Thailand may see a slowdown in new foreign direct investments due to global trade uncertainties, while the Southeast Asian country seeks to negotiate with Washington to soften the blow from the threat of a 36% tariff.

title: India’s Global Rise Imperiled by Perpetual Pakistan Conflict
content: India and Pakistan on Wednesday hit each other with military strikes for the sixth time since 1947, when Britain pulled out of the subcontinent and both nations won independence.

title: Taiwan Doesn’t Expect to Be Named Currency Manipulator by US
content: Taiwan’s central bank governor dismissed the possibility of being labeled a currency manipulator by the US Treasury.

title: Philippines GDP Growth of 5.4% Misses, Even Before Tariff Impact
content: The Philippine economy expanded slower than expected in the first quarter, underscoring challenges for policymakers even before the Trump administration’s trade war rocked markets and hurt global sentiment.

title: Mid-Term Vote Holds Key to Philippines Riding Out Tariff-Linked Risks
content: The Philippines’ May 12 midterm election is putting investors on alert for any changes to government policies, as the global trade war exposes weaknesses in one of Asia’s fastest-growing economies.

title: Xi Fortifies China Economy Before First Trade Talks With US
content: President Xi Jinping’s government provided a jolt to China’s economy ahead of landmark trade talks with the US, with officials unveiling a range of policies designed to strengthen Beijing’s hand in negotiations.

title: Willis Queried RBNZ Rates, Meeting Frequency Before Orr Quit
content: New Zealand Minister of Finance Nicola Willis asked the central bank to explain why it planned to keep interest rates at a restrictive level in the week prior to the sudden resignation of Governor Adrian Orr, documents obtained under the Official Information Act show.

title: Mexican Leaders Cheer Apollo’s Rowan for Pushing US-Mexico Deal
content: Mexican business leaders and executives lauded statements from Apollo Global Management Inc. Chief Executive Officer Marc Rowan emphasizing the need for a trade partnership between the US and Mexico, which propelled a view that a global trade war could make the US’ southern neighbor a winner amid uncertainty.

title: JLR, Diageo Among Winners as UK-India Sign Model Trade Deal
content: India’s decision to slash tariffs on UK-made cars to whiskey as part of a sweeping trade pact could create a line of winners, including Jaguar Land Rover and Diageo Plc.

title: Brazil Lifts Interest Rate to Nearly Two-Decade High of 14.75%
content: Brazil’s central bank raised its interest rate by a half-point and kept its options open for either another hike or a pause at its next decision as policymakers face above-target inflation and global economic uncertainty.

title: Corporate Defaults Start Piling Up in Argentina as Milei Policies Kick In
content: Cracks are starting to appear as Javier Milei removes the distortions that once characterized the Argentine economy, hurting companies that bulked up on debt by exploiting exchange rate gaps.

title: UK House Sales Gauge Hits Lowest Since 2023, Estate Agents Say
content: A closely watched indicator of the UK housing market plunged to the lowest level in almost two years after a property tax increase and Donald Trump’s trade war sent buyers into hiding.

title: Bank of England Set to Turn Dovish as US Tariffs Risk Growth
content: The Bank of England is expected to cut interest rates by a quarter percentage point Thursday and may signal that another move is likely in June, potentially putting the central bank on course for its first back-to-back reductions since 2009 as the US trade war darkens the outlook for growth.

title: Starmer Pledges UK Workers to Gain From Military Spending Boost
content: Prime Minister Keir Starmer said British workers would benefit from the UK’s plans to boost military spending, as his government tries to convince a skeptical and disgruntled electorate of the merits of increased outlays on defense.

title: Reeves to Break Fiscal Rule by £57 Billion Ahead of Next Budget
content: Chancellor of the Exchequer Rachel Reeves is on track to miss both her fiscal rules by tens of billions of pounds in the UK’s autumn budget, according to a prominent economic think tank, leaving her no option but to raise taxes or cut spending.

title: Powell Says Fed Won’t Be Rushed, Outlook Depends on White House
content: Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell made clear he won’t be rushed into lowering borrowing costs until there’s more certainty on the direction of trade policy, which will have to come from the White House.

title: Trump’s Migrant Crackdown Adds to Miami’s Real Estate Woes
content: President Donald Trump’s immigration crackdown is making it harder for foreigners to buy and rent homes, threatening a key pillar of Miami’s half-decade-long economic boom.

title: Looking to Nixon for a Peek at Trump’s Future
content: Niall Ferguson and Fareed Zakaria join this week’s Trumponomics to place Donald Trump’s ambitious plans for the US economy in historical perspective.

title: Goldman Boosts Forecast for US Inflation as Dollar Slides
content: Economists at Goldman Sachs Group Inc. boosted their forecasts for US inflation this year and next, in part to account for a weaker dollar following the Trump administration’s tariff announcements.

title: Next Lifts Guidance Again as UK Shoppers Buck Economic Gloom
content: Next Plc’s shares rose after the retailer raised its guidance for the second time this year, driven by stronger-than-expected UK sales and disruption facing rivals’ operations.

title: JLR Restarts Shipments to US After Pause Over Tariffs
content: UK automaker Jaguar Land Rover has resumed shipments of vehicles to the US after pausing them following the announcement of tariffs by President Donald Trump’s government.

title: Maersk Cuts Global Container Market Outlook on Tariff War
content: A.P. Moller-Maersk A/S, the Danish container giant, lowered its forecast for the global transport market rattled by Donald Trump’s trade war.

title: Oil Edges Higher as Trump Signals Announcement on Trade Deal
content: Oil rose after Donald Trump flagged a Thursday announcement on a trade deal, which is expected to be with the UK, as the US president faces political pressure following tariffs that rattled global markets.

title: $73 Billion Stonepeak Expands Middle East Presence with Riyadh Office
content: Infrastructure specialist Stonepeak is opening an office in Saudi Arabia — its second in the Middle East, a region eager for foreign institutional investment.

title: Chinese Automakers Crank Up Sales of Cars With Combustion Engines in Europe
content: Chinese electric vehicles are losing momentum in Europe, but the nation’s automakers are selling more cars than ever in the region by throttling up deliveries of hybrids and combustion engine-powered models.

title: ANZ Extends Share Buyback Period Amid Trump’s Tariff Uncertainty
content: ANZ Group Holdings Ltd. moved to extend the time it has to complete its A$2 billion ($1.3 billion) share buyback, citing uncertainty in global conditions.

title: Australia’s US Envoy Calls Trump Film Tariffs a ‘Tax on Bluey’
content: Australia’s Ambassador to the US Kevin Rudd labeled Donald Trump’s plan to impose a 100% tariff on foreign-made films as a “tax on Bluey,” bringing the hugely popular children’s character into a series of recent trade disagreements between the two countries.

title: Blackstone, Vanguard, Wellington to Launch Private Markets Fund
content: Blackstone Inc., Vanguard Group and Wellington Management Co are launching a fund that will invest in public equities, bonds and private markets, as part of their effort to expand private-market offerings to retail clients.

title: Cash-Strapped Beyond Meat Gets $100 Million From Diet Non-Profit
content: Beyond Meat Inc. raised $100 million in debt financing from a plant-based diets advocate, as the company continues to search for funds to shore up its liquidity.

title: Carvana Sees Stronger Profit on Used-Car and Loan Sales
content: Online used-car retailer Carvana Co. doubled its profits in the first quarter with record vehicle volume and a substantial gain in loan sales.

title: FAA Moves to Bolster Newark Airspace Strained by Failures
content: The US aviation regulator plans to upgrade technology infrastructure and staffing levels for air-traffic controllers that oversee flights bound for Newark Liberty International Airport after a critical outage led to more than week of severe flight disruptions.

title: BYD, Tsingshan Drop Chile Lithium Projects After Price Rout
content: Two Chinese companies dropped plans to develop lithium-processing projects in Chile after the price of the battery metal tumbled, undermining the nation’s bid to add more value to its mineral exports.

title: APA Reaches Deal to Sell New Mexico Assets to Permian Resources
content: APA Corp., a US oil explorer with wells from Egypt to Alaska, said it’s selling some of its assets in the world’s busiest shale patch to Permian Resources Corp. as it streamlines its portfolio.

title: Battery Company Fluence Plunges as Tariffs Curb Projects
content: Fluence Energy Inc. shares fell as much as 28% in late trading after the company lowered its full-year guidance, citing the pause of certain US projects due to tariff policy.

title: Trump Taps Means as Surgeon General After Pulling First Pick
content: President Donald Trump is tapping Casey Means to be the next US surgeon general after his prior nominee was withdrawn shortly before her confirmation hearing.

title: AppLovin Sales Jump, Sells Mobile-Games Unit to Tripledot
content: AppLovin Corp. agreed to sell its video-games unit to London-based Tripledot Studios to focus on its advertising technology business.

title: Musk’s xAI to Use Tesla Batteries at Memphis Supercomputer
content: Elon Musk’s xAI is using Tesla Inc.’s Megapack batteries to shore up its “Colossus” supercomputer in Memphis, another example of the overlapping interests between Musk’s companies.

title: Rite Aid to Sell Customer Prescriptions to Rival Pharmacies
content: Rite Aid won court approval to run an expedited process to sell customers’ prescription information to rival pharmacies as the bankrupt firm prepares to unload or close its stores.

title: FanDuel-Parent Flutter Results Miss After March Madness Setback
content: Flutter Entertainment Plc, parent of the FanDuel online betting business, reported sales and earnings that fell short of Wall Street projections after coming up on the losing side of a number of college basketball bets.

title: NY MTA Gets $500 Million Loan Backed by Congestion Toll Revenue
content: New York’s Metropolitan Transportation Authority entered into a $500 million loan agreement with a group of investors that’s backed by congestion pricing revenue as the Trump administration tries to end the tolling program, according to a loan document.

title: Amtrak to Cut 20% of Top-Level Staff Amid Trump Uncertainty
content: Amtrak is cutting roughly 20% of its top-level management staff in an effort to reduce costs amid uncertainty about President Donald Trump’s plans to invest in infrastructure, according to people familiar with the matter.

title: Oil Falls as Fed Holds Rates Steady, China Trade Tensions Linger
content: Oil slumped after Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell said officials aren’t in a hurry to adjust rates and as tensions between the US and China linger ahead of trade negotiations.

title: Ramaswamy’s Strive Plans Bitcoin Treasury Firm by Reverse Merger
content: A subsidiary of Strive Enterprises Inc. co-founded by Vivek Ramaswamy is merging with Asset Entities Inc. to form a Bitcoin treasury company, the latest in a string of firms to mimic Michael Saylor’s Strategy.

title: US Airports Have Outlook Dinged by Moody’s on Trade Concerns
content: Moody’s Ratings has revised its outlook for the US airport sector to negative from stable, citing an expected hit to air travel from the global trade war as a key reason for its view.

title: Newark? No Thanks: Flyers Avoid Airport Over Safety Fears
content: Rattled flyers are deciding that trips through Newark just aren’t worth it.

title: FedEx Director Steiner Is Leading Candidate to Run Post Office
content: The United States Postal Service is zeroing in on FedEx Corp. board member David Steiner to be the country’s next postmaster general, according to people familiar with the matter.

title: Gramercy Partner Maloney Departs After a Decade With Hedge Fund
content: Matt Maloney, a partner at Gramercy Funds Management, has left after a decade with the emerging-market focused hedge fund, people familiar with the matter said.

title: Hedge Fund Eisler Cuts 15% of Staff in Overhaul to Trim Costs
content: Eisler Capital has dismissed about 15% of its workforce as it looks to reduce costs amid declining assets and trading losses.

title: Disney Shares Surge as Parks, Streaming Results Lift Outlook
content: Walt Disney Co. reported fiscal second-quarter results that beat Wall Street estimates and raised its outlook for the full year, citing strong performances from theme parks and streaming TV. The shares jumped as much as 12% in New York.

title: Trump’s UK Trade Framework Leaves Many Key Details for Later

content: Robert Francis Prevost, a 69-year-old cardinal from Chicago, has been declared Pope Leo XIV. Pope Francis elevated him to cardinal in 2023. When Leo XIV spoke to crowds from the balcony of St. Peter’s Basilica, his first message was against all forms of division and war. Bloomberg’s Chiara Albanese reports.

title: Commerzbank CEO Orlopp on Earnings, Guidance, Merz
content: Commerzbank AG Chief Executive Officer Bettina Orlopp discusses the bank’s forward guidance after reporting first-quarter profit which unexpectedly rose 12% from a year earlier to €834 million ($936 million), well ahead of analysts’ estimates. Speaking on Bloomberg Television, Orlopp also comments on German Chancellor Friedrich Merz’s new government and the outlook for Italian rival UniCredit SpA’s possible interest in buying the firm.

title: Macquarie CEO Says Tech Push in Bank Brings Profits, Staff Drop
content: Macquarie Group Ltd. Chief Executive Officer Shemara Wikramanayake expects a years-long push to invest in technology within its banking and financial services division to reap further gains. It’s also resulted in lower staff levels.

title: What to Expect From Trump’s Visit to the Middle East
content: US President Donald Trump is set to visit Saudi Arabia, Qatar and the United Arab Emirates next week. Bloomberg’s Sam Dagher and Dan Williams discuss what to expect from Trump’s visit to the Middle East and what this may mean in the broader geopolitical context.

content: Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping held bilateral meetings in Moscow, emphasizing an alliance they claim will create a multipolar world order. Xi’s four-day trip to Moscow started on Wednesday and coincides with Russia’s 80th-anniversary commemorations of the end of World War II. title: Ex-Northvolt CEO Gets New Funds for AI Startup in Manufacturing
content: Two former executives from bankrupt battery maker Northvolt AB have launched a new venture in Sweden that will utilize artificial intelligence to help manufacturing processes.

title: TSMC April Sales Surge After US Tariffs Spur Device Rush Orders
content: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co.’s revenue jumped 48% in April, underscoring how electronics firms scrambled to acquire essential components before global tariffs took effect.

title: China’s Top Chipmaker SMIC Plunges After Projecting Lower Sales
content: Semiconductor Manufacturing International Corp. plunged Friday after China’s leading chipmaker warned sales could fall as much as 6% this quarter because of production disruptions.

title: NTT Announces 200 Billion Yen Buyback in Capital Efficiency Push
content: Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corp. said it plans to buy back as much as ¥200 billion ($1.4 billion) of its shares, joining a growing string of such measures bolstering the Japanese market.

title: At OpenAI, Fidji Simo to Bring Lessons From Instacart and Meta
content: Simo has been appointed CEO of applications at OpenAI, where she will oversee executives and broaden the company's hit chatbot, ChatGPT, into a Swiss Army knife of artificial intelligence software.

title: Taiwan’s Exports Surge to Record, Fueling Currency Gains
content: Taiwan’s exports climbed to a record in the year through April, driven by a rush to ship goods ahead of US tariffs and continued strong demand for the island’s tech products.

title: Nidec Withdraws $1.8 Billion Hostile Bid for Makino Milling
content: Nidec Corp. is withdrawing a ¥257 billion ($1.8 billion) unsolicited tender offer for machine tool maker Makino Milling Machine Co., bowing to strong resistance from its target.

title: Ryan Reynolds’ MNTN Weighs IPO Launch Soon as Next Week
content: Connected TV advertising platform MNTN Inc. is considering launching its initial public offering as soon as next week, according to people familiar with the matter, after delaying its plans amid tariff-induced market volatility.

title: Celsius Founder Mashinsky Gets 12 Years for Crypto Fraud
content: Alex Mashinsky, the founder of cryptocurrency lender Celsius Network, was ordered to spend 12 years in prison for defrauding hundreds of thousands of customers lured by his firm’s high interest rates on digital-asset deposits.

title: Pinterest Surges as AI Expected to Lure Advertiser Spending
content: Pinterest Inc. surged in extended trading after second-quarter revenue guidance topped estimates at the midpoint, further easing concerns of an advertising slowdown.

title: From Apple to GM, Tariffs to Cost Companies Tens of Billions
content: From Apple Inc. to General Motors Co., corporate America is bracing for tens of billions of dollars in damages from Trump’s trade war — and that’s before most affected goods have landed.

title: Coinbase Posts Jump in Revenue, Drop in Quarterly Earnings
content: Coinbase Global Inc.’s first-quarter revenue jumped while profit declined as the largest US crypto exchange navigated the volatile price swings of the digital asset market.

title: Trump to End Biden-Era Program to Bridge Digital Divide
content: President Donald Trump said he would end a program that provides billions to extend internet access in underserved communities, casting it as unfairly providing grants on the basis of race.

title: Silicon Valley Is Coming for the Pentagon’s $1 Trillion Budget
content: The Trump administration wants startups to remake the US military, setting the stage for a battle over the world’s biggest defense budget.

title: Adobe to Cut Software Price for US Government After DOGE Review
content: Adobe Inc. will offer a package of its products to the government at a discounted rate following scrutiny on software spending by the Trump administration.

title: BCE Cuts Dividend by 56%, Strikes Fiber Deal With PSP
content: BCE Inc. cut its dividend for the first time in 17 years and unveiled a deal with a Canadian pension fund to help finance growth in Ziply, the US broadband provider it’s trying to acquire.

title: Big Tech Is on Trial. What That Means for the Future of the Internet
content: Today on the Big Take podcast: Will the antitrust cases against Google and Meta help innovation flourish, or kill America’s chances at AI dominance?

title: Lyft Posts Bookings and Outlook Beat, Expands Buybacks
content: Lyft Inc. reported better-than-expected gross bookings in the first quarter, drawing a sharp contrast with the disappointing results issued by its much-larger ride-hailing rival Uber Technologies Inc. a day earlier.

title: Crypto-Backed Stablecoin Bill Blocked Amid Furor Over Trump Memecoin
content: Senate Democrats blocked stablecoin legislation backed by the digital assets industry amid a furor over President Donald Trump’s extensive and growing portfolio of crypto ventures.

title: Instagram Chief Says App Has Feared TikTok Threat for Years
content: A small portion of Instagram’s content comes from users engaging with family and friends as the app focuses more on video offerings to compete with TikTok, the platform’s chief Adam Mosseri said, seeking to fend off government claims that Meta Platforms Inc. monopolizes social media.

title: Consumer Watchdog Halts Biden-Era Google Payment Supervision
content: The Consumer Financial Protection Bureau discontinued its order designating the supervision of Alphabet Inc.’s Google Payment Corp., reversing a Biden-era decision to monitor the nonbank financial platform.

title: Podcast Deals Heat Up Again in Wake of Trump’s Victory
content: As the linear TV business falters, broadcasters are eyeing podcasters while investors pump cash into independent networks

title: Apple Is Developing Specialized Chips for Glasses, New Macs and AI Servers
content: Apple Inc.’s silicon design group is working on new chips that will serve as the brains for future devices, including its first smart glasses, more powerful Macs and artificial intelligence servers.

title: Bitcoin Retakes $100,000 Amid an Easing of Global Trade Tensions
content: Bitcoin crossed the $100,000 threshold for the first time since February, fueled by expectations for an easing of global trade tensions.

title: Meta Taps New Head of AI Lab After Staffer’s Return From Google
content: Meta Platforms Inc. told staff that it’s chosen Robert Fergus to helm its artificial intelligence research lab, elevating an employee who helped start the lab before a stint at competitor Alphabet Inc.

title: Tech Executives Urge Senators to Rethink Regulations for AI
content: The leaders of some of the biggest technology and artificial intelligence companies appeared before Congress on Thursday with a wish list of sorts that at its top has doing away with regulations they say inhibit their firms’ growth and, by default, sends business to China.

title: Shopify Falls on Narrowing Profit as It Spends to Boost Revenue
content: Shopify Inc. shares fell after the company projected slowing profit growth in the current quarter, with executives pledging to keep spending to boost sales growth.

title: Arm Tumbles After Weak Forecast, Spurring Slowdown Fears
content: Arm Holdings Plc declined in Thursday trading after giving a disappointing sales forecast for the current quarter, stoking concerns about a tariff-fueled slowdown for the chip industry.

title: MercadoLibre Gains on Earnings Marked by Argentina Rebound
content: E-commerce and fintech giant MercadoLibre Inc. rallied after first quarter earnings beat analyst expectations led by a stronger-than-expected rebound in Argentina.

title: Norway Core Inflation Slows More Than Seen, Fueling Rate Bet
content: Norway’s underlying inflation slowed more than forecast last month, fueling odds of an interest-rate cut by Norges Bank before the fall.

title: Hungary Inflation Slows Toward Central Bank’s Tolerance Band
content: Hungary’s consumer price growth slowed less than forecast last month, edging closer to the top end of the central bank’s tolerance band.

title: Trump Team Seeks Tariff Cuts, Rare Earths Relief in China Talks
content: The Trump administration is weighing a dramatic tariff reduction during weekend talks with China to de-escalate tensions and temper the economic pain both are already starting to feel.

title: Chinese Exports to US Slump 21% But Soar to Asia and Europe
content: China’s exports rose more than forecast in April even as shipments to the US slumped sharply in the first month after President Donald Trump targeted its goods with tariffs above 100%.

title: Hong Kong Property May Bottom as Borrowing Costs Drop, Jefferies Says
content: Declining interest rates in Hong Kong are increasing the chances the residential property market bottoms out, according to Jefferies.

title: China Is Said Seeking Argentina Crops as It Skirts US Tariffs
content: China signed a letter of intent with exporters in Argentina to buy about $900 million of soybeans, corn and vegetable oil, the latest indication that the Asian nation will avoid sourcing from the US during President Donald Trump’s trade war.

title: Japan’s Slower Wage and Export Growth Backs Case for BOJ Caution
content: Gains in Japan’s wages cooled more than expected in March while early trade figures for April showed export growth slowing, adding to the case for the Bank of Japan to proceed cautiously with interest-rate hikes as economic risks at home and abroad continue to mount.

title: Japan’s Early Exports in April Slow as US Tariffs Hit Firms
content: Japan’s exports slowed in the first 20 days of April as the US tariff campaign intensified with new car and across-the-board levies.

title: Taiwan’s Exports Surge to Record, Fueling Currency Gains
content: Taiwan’s exports climbed to a record in the year through April, driven by a rush to ship goods ahead of US tariffs and continued strong demand for the island’s tech products.

title: Lutnick Warns No 'Fast Deals' for Japan and South Korea
content: Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick said that trade deals with South Korea and Japan could take significantly more time to complete than the framework agreement President Donald Trump announced Thursday with the UK, in a signal that some Asian partners may have to wait for tariff relief.

title: Colombian Inflation Surprises All Analysts With April Jump
content: Colombian inflation unexpectedly jumped in April in an unwelcome surprise for policymakers who restarted monetary easing last week.

title: Peru Cuts Rate to 4.5% With Slow Inflation, Tariff Risks
content: Peru resumed monetary easing with inflation firmly under control and US tariffs posing mounting risks to its economy.

content: Some of Asia’s richest families are cutting exposure to US assets, saying President Donald Trump’s tariffs have made the world’s largest economy much less predictable.

content: President Donald Trump announced a trade framework with the UK, hailing it as a “breakthrough” that US officials hoped would unlock other deals to expand market access for American goods.

title: Three-Year Inflation Views at Highest Since 2022 in Fed Survey
content: Americans’ expectations for inflation in the medium-term climbed to an almost three-year high in April while their views on the job market worsened, according to a monthly survey from the Federal Reserve Bank of New York.

title: UK Homeowners Can Thank Trump for Nudging BOE Toward a Rate Cut
content: US President Donald Trump’s trade policy is upending long-held alliances, threatening global growth and causing mayhem for business. For UK homeowners, though, it is working out quite well.

title: Despite Trump's Criticism, Powell Keeps Congress on His Side
content: Under relentless attack from President Donald Trump, Jerome Powell needs all the allies he can get — and he has plenty in Congress, including among Republicans who show little appetite for ditching the Federal Reserve chief.

title: Trump Says ‘Substantive’ China Talks Could Yield Tariff Cut
content: US President Donald Trump said he believed trade negotiations launching this weekend with China would result in tangible progress, predicting Beijing would be willing to make concessions and saying he could consider cutting punishing tariffs against the country if there was significant momentum.

title: Mortgage Rates in US Stay Stuck at 6.76%
content: Mortgage rates in the US stayed put at levels reached last week, keeping the pressure high for homebuyers.

title: How Trade War Can Elevate Mortgage Stress in Canada, in Charts
content: The Bank of Canada warned that a severe and long-lasting global trade war may cause more mortgage borrowers to fall behind on their payments — even beyond levels reached in the global financial crisis.

title: Nigeria Pays Off IMF’s $3.4 Billion Covid Loan to Exit Debt List
content: Nigeria has paid off $3.4 billion borrowed from the International Monetary Fund during the Covid-19 pandemic, exiting the list of countries that are in debt to the Washington-based lender.

title: Chile Annual Inflation Slows as Policymakers Keep Guard Against Price Pressures
content: Chile’s annual inflation eased past all forecasts last month in good news for policymakers who had warned they’re not out of the woods yet on fears of near-term price pressures and a more turbulent global economy.

title: Trump Says He’ll Raise Jimmy Lai’s Case in China Trade Talks
content: President Donald Trump said he will raise the case of ex-media mogul Jimmy Lai as part of US trade talks with China, a move likely to antagonize Beijing just days before the two sides meet.

title: Wall Street's A-List Worries About the Economy in Private, While Showing Public Calm
content: Attendees of this week’s Milken Institute Global Conference heard a lot of upbeat chatter from the stages of the Beverly Hilton hotel, where billionaires and executives frequently took a sanguine tone about the state of markets and the global economy.

title: ECB Officials Briefed on Military Threat Posed by Putin’s Russia
content: The European Central Bank Governing Council was given an in-depth analysis of the risks posed by potential Russian military aggression in eastern Europe at the start of its last rate-setting meeting, according to people familiar with the discussion.

title: Landlord LondonMetric Buys Urban Logistics in £699 Million Deal
content: LondonMetric Property Plc agreed to buy Urban Logistics Reit Plc in a deal valuing the company at about £699 million ($925 million).

content: Oil extended gains as the market turned its attention to trade talks between the US and China this weekend after President Donald Trump announced an agreement with the UK.

title: Monte Paschi, Mediobanca Profits Beat as Investors Eye Deals
content: Banca Monte dei Paschi di Siena SpA joined rival Mediobanca SpA in posting higher than expected profits during the first three months of the year, as investors are focused on their respective acquisition plans.

title: Thai Billionaire’s Frasers Property Posts Higher Profit on Singapore Housing Business
content: Frasers Property Ltd., the developer controlled by Thai billionaire Charoen Sirivadhanabhakdi, indicated it is still exploring opportunities in Shanghai and other Chinese cities despite the country’s ongoing property crisis.

title: Japan’s Top Hotels Under Scrutiny For Potential Price Collusion As Tourism Booms

title: China Teapots Make Rare Murban Oil Purchases for Quick Delivery
content: At least two independent Chinese refiners have made a rare foray into the broader international crude market, snapping up cargoes of Middle Eastern oil for delivery next month.

title: Fiera’s Desjardins to Step Down as CEO, Succeeded by Menard
content: Fiera Capital Corp. founder Jean-Guy Desjardins is stepping down as chief executive officer and will be succeeded by Maxime Menard, who currently heads the firm’s Canada unit.

title: Sweetgreen Cuts Outlook With Diners Reducing Salad Budgets
content: Sweetgreen Inc. cut its annual guidance, citing a sharp decline in consumer sentiment following the announcement of new tariffs in the US.

title: From Apple to GM, Tariffs to Cost Companies Tens of Billions
content: From Apple Inc. to General Motors Co., corporate America is bracing for tens of billions of dollars in damages from Trump’s trade war — and that’s before most affected goods have landed.

title: Speedcast Mulls Breakup, Sale of Ground Stations Unit
content: Speedcast, a provider of satellite communications and information technology services, is considering a sale of its ground stations business for more than $1 billion, people with knowledge of the matter said.

title: CIP to Invest $500 Million in BKV Carbon Capture Joint Venture
content: BKV Corp. and a clean energy-focused investment fund of Copenhagen Infrastructure Partners have agreed to form a joint venture to expand carbon-capture projects in the US.

title: Illumina Cuts Guidance on Threat From Tariffs and China Ban
content: Illumina Inc. cut its full-year adjusted profit guidance for the second time in three months as it grapples with the impact of tariffs and China banning imports of its gene-sequencing machines.

title: Mattel Names Paul Ruh CFO, Replacing Anthony DiSilvestro
content: Mattel Inc. has appointed Paul Ruh as chief financial officer, succeeding Anthony DiSilvestro.

title: Costco in Deal With Affirm Giving Shoppers Monthly Payment Plans
content: Costco Wholesale Corp. is tapping Affirm Holdings Inc. to let the retailer’s online shoppers pay over time for a transaction, an option that’s been helping many merchants sell bigger-ticket items and gives consumers more comfort in buying them.

title: British Airways Parent to Buy 30 Boeing Jets in Win for US
content: British Airways parent IAG SA is poised to order about 30 Boeing Co. 787 Dreamliner aircraft, according to people familiar with the matter, as the US planemaker snags an early win under President Donald Trump’s new trade deal with the UK.

title: Oil Advances as US Trade Deal With UK Stokes Risk-On Appetite
content: Oil rose as President Donald Trump announced a trade framework with the UK, spurring some optimism about deals to come.

title: Shell’s LNG Canada Plans First Exports as Soon as Late June
content: Shell Plc’s liquefied natural gas project in Canada, the country’s first large-scale export terminal for the fuel, is preparing to begin overseas sales as soon as late June.

title: Duffy Pitches Six New Air Traffic Control Centers After Mishaps

title: Health Crisis Deepens in Colombia as Hospitals Shut Down Units
content: The cash crunch in Colombia’s health system is forcing hospitals in the nation’s capital to close down units in order to focus efforts on other services.

title: UBS in Talks to Sell Its Hedge Fund Unit O’Connor to Cantor
content: UBS Group AG is in talks to sell its hedge fund unit O’Connor to Cantor Fitzgerald LP, a move that would end a more than three-decade run of ownership by the Swiss bank, according to people familiar with the matter.

title: Bradesco Soars Most Since 2020 as Turnaround Takes Shape
content: Brazilian bank Banco Bradesco SA has finally begun to reap the results of a turnaround process that started when Chief Executive Officer Marcelo Noronha took the reins about a year and a half ago.

title: Ford Is Hanging On to High-Grade Rating by a Thread, BI Says

title: Warner Bros. Rises as Deal Speculation Overshadows Slow Quarter

title: Bill Gates’ Charity Vows to Give Away 99% of His Fortune by 2045

title: Germany’s Defense Minister Wants €50 Billion Fund, Rheinmetall CEO Says

title: Jefferies 28-Year-Old Banker Died of Toxic Drug Mix, Report Says

title: Krispy Kreme Slumps as Dividends End, McDonald’s Plan Paused

title: Citi’s Banamex Focused on IPO as CEO Rules Out Direct Sale of Bank
content: Citigroup Inc.’s Mexican retail bank Grupo Financiero Banamex is focused on preparing for an initial public offering as soon as the end of this year, Banamex Chief Executive Officer Manuel Romo said, dashing speculation that Citi could seek to revive plans for a direct sale of the bank.

title: Tariffs, Volatility And The Startup Exit Dilemma

title: Europe’s VC Funding Stayed Flat In Q1, Even As Healthcare Added A Third

title: Latin America Startup Funding Fell Sequentially In Q1
content: Latin America startup investment declined sequentially in the first quarter of this year, driven by a drop in later-stage dealmaking. Even so, funding was above the depressed levels seen a year ago, and early-stage dealmaking showed signs of strength.

title: SignalFire Closes On $1B To Invest In Applied AI

title: North America Startup Investment Spiked In Q1 Due To OpenAI, But Seed And Early Stage Fell

title: Trump Vows to Meet Hollywood on Tariff Plan That Shook Industry
content:
President Donald Trump said he would meet with Hollywood executives after confounding the US film industry over his plan to impose a 100% tariff on movies made overseas. 
“So we’re going to meet with the industry,” Trump said Monday afternoon. “I want to make sure they’re happy with it, because we’re all about jobs.”
Film and entertainment figures on Monday struggled to interpret Trump’s directive, posted to his social media account on Sunday evening, which said the American movie industry is “DYING” and cast foreign films as a national security threat that spread propaganda to US audiences.
“WE WANT MOVIES MADE IN AMERICA, AGAIN!” Trump said.
Shares of Netflix Inc., Paramount Global, Warner Bros. Discovery Inc. and other media and entertainment companies slid as Wall Street and Hollywood tried to discern what aspect of filmmaking would qualify for such tariffs and why it should be targeted like other industries. (Source: Bloomberg)

content: Prime Minister Keir Starmer said he would end the UK’s “experiment in open borders” with tougher plans to curb migration, seeking to head off the growing electoral threat from Nigel Farage’s populist Reform party.

title: Poland to Close Another Russian Consulate Over Sabotage Claims
content: Poland ordered the closure of the Russian consulate in Krakow after saying it has proof that a large fire in the country’s capital last year was ordered by Moscow’s secret services, according to the Polish foreign minister.

title: Pharmaceutical Stocks Tumble on Trump Plan to Cut US Drug Prices
content: Shares of pharmaceutical companies fell across the world after US President Donald Trump said he planned to order a cut in US prescription drug costs to bring them in line with other countries, prompting concern that profits will take a hit.

title: Global Stocks Climb After US, China Agree to Cut Tariffs for 90 Days
Albania’s Premier on Track to Win Unprecedented Fourth Term
content: Albania’s premier is on track to win an unprecedented fourth term as he seeks to finally take the Adriatic country into the European Union and cement its status as a tourist destination.

title: What Outlawed PKK Laying Down Arms Means for Turkey and the Kurds
content: Tens of thousands of people have been killed in the four decades since Kurdish separatist group the PKK took up arms against the Turkish government.

title: India Envoy Rejects US Calls for Mediation in Kashmir Issue
content: A top Indian envoy said the dispute over Kashmir is a bilateral issue with Pakistan, rejecting any external mediation on the matter despite the US saying it wanted to facilitate talks.

title: Hamas Says It Will Free Last Living American Hostage in Gaza
content: Hamas said it will release the last living American hostage held in Gaza after renewed talks with the US over a truce deal with Israel.

title: Trump’s Ukraine Push Comes to a Head With Challenge to Putin
content: Donald Trump’s effort to secure peace in Ukraine is reaching a decisive moment with Ukraine’s Volodymyr Zelenskiy challenging Vladimir Putin to engage in talks this week.

title: US and China Tout Progress in Trade Talks, Offer Few Details
content: The US and China both reported “substantial progress” after two days of talks in Switzerland aimed at de-escalating a trade war, marking what Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng called “an important first step” toward resolving differences.

title: Australia’s PM Keeps Chalmers, Wong in Roles in Second Term
content: Australia’s Prime Minister Anthony Albanese retained Treasurer Jim Chalmers and Foreign Minister Penny Wong in their portfolios as he unveiled changes to his lineup just over a week after decisively winning an election.

title: Words Are Enough to Give Markets a Roadmap for US-China Success
content: Monday’s moderate market reaction to progress in US-China trade talks at least gave investors a roadmap for how a significant breakthrough might play out.

title: US House to Claw Back Biden’s Climate Law to Fund Trump Tax Cuts
content: US House Republicans plan to help pay for an extension of President Donald Trump’s massive tax cuts by clawing back unused funds from scores of programs and grants in his predecessor’s signature climate law.

title: Japan Rules Out Trade Deal With US That Excludes Auto Tariffs
content: Japan won’t accept any initial trade agreement with the US that excludes an accord on autos, according to Prime Minister Shigeru Ishiba.

title: Americans Embrace Road Trips as Economic Fears Discourage Flying
content: Kristin Herman and her partner had been planning a European getaway with stops in Paris and Rome, but with the US economy suddenly wobbling, the couple instead drove to Oregon’s nearby redwood forests and Cannon Beach — even camping some nights to save on hotels.

title: After Driving Down Oil, Saudi Arabia’s MBS Looks for Trump Dividend
content: Donald Trump and Saudi Arabia's MBS both want to monetize their relationship. It just might not be in the way Trump had envisaged.

title: Medicaid Work Requirements Sought in Bill to Fund Trump Tax Cuts
content: House Republicans want to impose work requirements on some Medicaid recipients up to 64 years old and impose more costs on some beneficiaries to help pay for President Donald Trump’s planned sweeping tax package.

title: S. Korean Conservatives Choose Right-Winger as Campaign Begins
content: South Korea’s ruling conservatives opted for a right-wing candidate in the mold of ousted leader Yoon Suk Yeol to take on frontrunner Lee Jae-myung as the official campaign for the June 3 presidential election kicked off.

title: Trump Set to Accept Luxury Jet as Gift From Qatar, ABC Says
content: President Donald Trump’s administration is likely to accept a luxury Boeing 747-8 jumbo jet from Qatar’s royal family, in what may be the most valuable gift ever received from a foreign government, ABC News reported Sunday.

title: US, China Agree to Lower Tariffs in Temporary Trade Truce
content: Good morning. Markets breathe a sigh of relief as the US and China agree to a temporary truce in their trade war. Donald Trump vows to cut US drug prices. And the president may get a very luxurious gift from Qatar. Listen to the day’s top stories.

title: Pierrakakis: Bailout Loans Should Be ‘Behind Us By 2031’
content: Greek Finance Minister Kyriakos Pierrakakis says the nation plans to repay loans from its first bailout program 10 years ahead of schedule. The last repayment of this set of loans was scheduled for 2041, but Pierrakakis tells Bloomberg’s Oliver Crook “it should be completely behind us by 2031.” He adds: “We plan to continue de-escalating our debt. We don’t plan to pass the bill to the next generation as all the previous generations in Greece did.”

content: Welcome to the Brussels Edition, Bloomberg’s daily briefing on what matters most in the heart of the European Union.

title: Cynics About Trump Tariffs Should Focus on Markets
content: An awful lot is now riding on the administration never having meant a word it was saying.

title: Pan American Silver to Buy Smaller Rival MAG for $2.1 Billion
content: Pan American Silver Corp. agreed to buy smaller producer MAG Silver Corp. in a transaction valued at about $2.1 billion, giving the bigger producer access to a major mine in Mexico.

title: Apple Weighs Raising IPhone Prices in New Lineup, WSJ Says
content: Apple Inc. is weighing raising prices for the iPhone lineup coming out later this year, the Wall Street Journal said, citing people familiar with the matter whom it didn’t identify.

title: The iPhone Is a Nicer Place With Fewer Restrictions After Ruling
content: Welcome to Tech In Depth, our daily newsletter with reporting and analysis about the business of tech from Bloomberg’s journalists around the world. Today, Austin Carr looks at the impact of the latest ruling ordering Apple to reform its App Store practices.

title: SoftBank Stargate Venture With OpenAI Hits Snags on Tariff Fears
content: SoftBank Group Corp.’s plans to invest $100 billion in artificial intelligence infrastructure in the US have slowed, with economic risks stemming from Washington’s tariffs holding up financing talks.

title: Air-Taxi Startup Vertical Goes Hybrid in Pivot Toward Defense
content: Vertical Aerospace Ltd is building a hybrid variant of its battery-powered air taxi, in a bet that a longer-range aircraft will attract investment from the lucrative defense sector.

title: Mazda Withholds Profit Guidance as Suzuki Dodges Trump’s Tariffs
content: Mazda Motor Co. withheld its annual profit guidance after its short-term future, along with most global carmakers, was muddied by US President Donald Trump’s trade war.

title: Xiaomi Shares Drop as Consumers Complain About Marketing of EVs
content: Xiaomi Corp. shares dropped as much as 5.7% in Hong Kong on Monday after a local media report over the weekend that said more than 300 people want to cancel their SU7 Ultra electric vehicle orders on “false advertising” about the design of the vehicle’s hood.

title: Golub-Backed Saudi Firm Starts AI Fund to Drive US-Mideast Ties
content: A Saudi Arabia-based venture capital firm that’s backed by the family office of US billionaire Lawrence Golub is launching a $50 million fund to invest in artificial intelligence startups across the Middle East and the San Francisco Bay Area.

title: AI Drug Firm METiS Considering $200 Million Hong Kong IPO, Sources Say
content: Artificial intelligence-driven drug firm METiS Pharmaceuticals is considering an initial public offering in Hong Kong to raise as much as $200 million, according to people familiar with the matter.

title: Amazon-Backed Scale AI Plans Middle East Expansion With New Saudi Arabia Office
content: Scale AI, a startup backed by Amazon.com Inc. that helps companies develop artificial intelligence products, plans to open an office in Saudi Arabia by the end of the year in a broader regional expansion.

title: Activist Dalton Seeks Talks With Fuji Media to Avoid Proxy Fight
content: Dalton Investments’ co-founder James Rosenwald said he wants to avoid a proxy fight with Fuji Media Holdings Inc., calling on the Japanese broadcaster to negotiate a settlement.

title: New Zealand Steps Up Plans to Ban Under-16s From Social Media
content: New Zealand Prime Minister Christopher Luxon said a proposal to ban children under the age of 16 from social media will be part of the government’s work program, increasing its chances of becoming law.

title: OpenAI, Microsoft in Talks to Reset High-Stakes Partnership: FT
content: OpenAI and Microsoft Corp. are revising the terms of their partnership that will enable the ChatGPT maker to go public at a future date while preserving the software giant’s access to artificial intelligence technology, the Financial Times reported Sunday.

title: Apple’s 2027 Product Blitz Can’t Come Soon Enough
content: Apple is planning a monumental year for new devices in 2027, but its current lack of breakthrough designs could make that wait feel interminable. Also: The company is working on an iOS 19 feature that syncs hotel Wi-Fi access details across devices, and it’s preparing for an era after Google search.

title: CATL to Bar Some US Funds From World’s Biggest Listing of 2025
content: Contemporary Amperex Technology Co. Ltd., the world’s largest maker of batteries for electric vehicles, is planning to limit the types of US investors that can participate in its Hong Kong listing, an indication that US-China tensions may be spilling into the IPO market.

title: Hungary Freezes Some Spending After Budget Gap Hits $8 Billion
content: Hungary’s government deficit rose to a record through April as interest payments outpaced tax income growth, leading the government to announce a spending freeze in parts of the budget.

title: The Polite Ways Companies Say Trump Tariffs Hurt
content: One of the remarkable things emerging from President Donald Trump’s tariff wars is a rebirth of the art of the polite slight. Or the “thanks but no thanks, sir” in the coded messages companies and industry lobbyists are putting out in public statements and submissions to government requests for comment about forthcoming tariffs. title: Low-Income US Families Face Growing Gap Between Earnings, Costs
content: There’s a growing gap between what low-income families earn and what it actually costs to live in the US, according to a new study that says headline measures of inflation fail to capture the burden on these households.

title: US, China to Slash Tariffs in Step Back from Decoupling Brink
content: The US and China will temporarily lower tariffs on each other’s products in a dramatic ratcheting down of trade tensions that buys the world’s two largest economies three months to work toward a broader agreement.

title: BOE’s Lombardelli Voted to Cut Rates as ‘Insurance’ Against Trade Wars
content: Bank of England Deputy Governor Clare Lombardelli said growth in UK wages and services prices is still too high to be consistent with bringing inflation back to the 2% target but she voted to cut interest rates last week to provide “insurance” against the risk of an economic slowdown caused by global trade wars.

title: IMF Plans Kenya Debt Scrutiny to Weigh Funding Needs in New Deal
content: The International Monetary Fund plans an in-depth review of Kenya’s debt to determine the nation’s financing needs under a new program.

title: ECB to Cut by More as Inflation Undershoots 2%, Poll Shows
content: The European Central Bank will lower borrowing costs more than previously expected this year to below 2% as inflation is seen undershooting the institution’s target in early 2026, according to economists surveyed by Bloomberg.

title: SNB’s Brief Era of Positive Rates May Be About to End
content: The Swiss National Bank will probably cut its interest rate to zero in June after less than three years in positive territory, according to a Bloomberg survey.

title: Global Stocks Climb After US, China Agree to Cut Tariffs for 90 Days
Japan’s Merchants’ Mood Hits Worst in Three Years on Tariff Woes
content: Sentiment among Japanese merchants sank to the lowest in more than three years, underscoring deepening concerns over the economic outlook at home and abroad as the impact from US tariffs begins to filter into the economy.

title: US and China Tout Progress in Trade Talks, Offer Few Details
content: The US and China both reported “substantial progress” after two days of talks in Switzerland aimed at de-escalating a trade war, marking what Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng called “an important first step” toward resolving differences.

title: Swedes’ Housing Optimism Weakens With Lower Consumer Confidence
content: Optimism among Swedes over the direction of home prices is waning as the Nordic country continues to grapple with economic headwinds and the prospect of slowing growth.

title: Africa’s Eswatini Kingdom Plans $275 Million Wealth Fund
content: The southern African Kingdom of Eswatini plans to start a sovereign wealth fund of around 5 billion emalangeni ($275 million) this year to help channel money into areas including manufacturing and agriculture, its finance minister said.

title: Japan Rules Out Trade Deal With US That Excludes Auto Tariffs
content: Japan won’t accept any initial trade agreement with the US that excludes an accord on autos, according to Prime Minister Shigeru Ishiba.

title: Americans Embrace Road Trips as Economic Fears Discourage Flying
content: Kristin Herman and her partner had been planning a European getaway with stops in Paris and Rome, but with the US economy suddenly wobbling, the couple instead drove to Oregon’s nearby redwood forests and Cannon Beach — even camping some nights to save on hotels.

title: Japan Bank Deposits Rise at Slowest Since ’07 as Inflation Bites
content: Japan’s bank deposits increased at the slowest pace since April 2007 as households seek to safeguard their assets from inflation.

title: Japan’s Sputtering Economy Likely Stalled Before Trump’s Tariffs
content: Japan’s economy likely suffered a contraction in the first three months of this year, signaling underlying fragility even before US tariff measures started hitting the country in earnest, according to economists surveyed by Bloomberg.

title: US-China Trade Talks to Boost Sentiment in Asia, Strategists Say
content: “Substantial progress” made in US-China trade relations after two days of talks in Switzerland is likely to boost sentiment in Asia, according to some strategists, while others were awaiting further details.

title: US Ambassador Says Canada Tariffs May Not Be ‘Totally Removed’
content: Some US tariffs on Canadian imports may remain in place even as the relationship between the two countries improves, Peter Hoekstra, the US ambassador to Canada, said.

title: Traders Eye Longer-Term Options to Hedge Post-Tariff Shock Rally
content: As April’s volatility storm fades into memory, traders are left balancing calmer markets and the ever-present risk of a fresh round of headline shocks.

title: Trump Hails Progress as US-China Negotiators Resume Trade Talks
content: Senior US and Chinese negotiators resumed on Sunday high-stakes talks to de-escalate their trade war, with President Donald Trump calling the hours-long discussions held a day earlier a “very good” meeting.

title: Trump Says ‘Much Agreed to’ in Meeting With Chinese Officials
content: President Donald Trump said US and Chinese negotiators in Switzerland had “a very good meeting” in an effort to de-escalate their trade war.

title: Spain Is Said to Back Sabadell Tie-Up to Counter BBVA Deal
content: The Spanish government is open to considering a tie-up for Banco Sabadell SA with another domestic bank as a way to counter the unsolicited bid from BBVA SA, according to people familiar with the matter.

title: Polestar Trims Losses on Cost Cuts, Sales of High-Margin Models
content: Polestar Automotive Holding’s losses narrowed in the first quarter as the electric-vehicle maker sold more of its newer models and cut costs.

title: Trump Vows US Drug Price Cuts of Up to 80% in Industry Blow
content: President Donald Trump said he plans to order a cut in US prescription drug costs by mandating that Americans pay no more than people in countries that have the lowest price.

title: Lilly’s Zepbound Trims More Belly Fat Than Novo’s Wegovy
content: Eli Lilly & Co.’s obesity drug Zepbound helped people trim about two inches more off their waists than Novo Nordisk A/S’s Wegovy in the first head-to-head study of the rival medicines.

title: Former StanChart Dealmaker Sets Up Abu Dhabi-Based Advisory Firm
content: A former banker at Standard Chartered Plc is launching a boutique advisory firm in Abu Dhabi, aiming to tap into the growing stream of institutional capital flowing between Asia, Europe and the Gulf.

title: UniCredit’s Profit Hits Record as CEO Orcel Pursues Deals
content: UniCredit SpA posted its highest quarterly profit ever, strengthening Chief Executive Officer Andrea Orcel’s hand as he pursues potential acquisitions.

title: EDP Says It’s Confident US Will Keep Tax Credits for Renewables
content: Portuguese utility EDP SA is confident that tax credits for renewable projects in the US will remain in place under the administration of President Donald Trump, Chief Executive Officer Miguel Stilwell d’Andrade said.

title: China’s Record Copper Ore Imports Offer Relief Amid Shortage
content: Chinese copper concentrate imports climbed to nearly 3 million tons last month, a record that’s likely to ease price pressures in the domestic market and offer relief to smelters fighting over the availability of feedstock.

title: Toyota Faces Biggest Hit From Trump Tariffs Among Automakers
content: Toyota Motor Corp. is the biggest carmaker in the world — and also the auto industry’s biggest loser when it comes to projected losses from US President Donald Trump’s trade war.

title: US Halts Cattle Imports Via Southern Border Over Screwworm Pest
content: The US said it is suspending imports of live cattle, horse, and bison via ports along the southern border because of the spread of the screwworm pest in Mexico.

title: Duffy Says ‘Several Weeks’ of Flight Cuts Needed at Newark
content: US Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said that Newark airport would see “several weeks” of reduced capacity as officials grapple with spiraling delays and safety lapses at one of the country’s busiest hubs.

title: Harvard Freeze, Funding Cuts Add to Headaches for Biotech CFOs
content: Executives fear they will have a harder time raising capital. Plus, BHP CFO Vandita Pant talks about capex, M&A and debt targets.

title: Aramco Profit Drops With Weak Oil Signaling More Strain
content: Saudi Aramco reported a decline in profit in the first quarter as lower crude prices put pressure on the finances of the world’s biggest oil exporter.

title: Crime is down in American cities. Will Trump take credit?
content: “If you’re under 55, this is probably the safest moment you’ve ever lived in.”
