content: Bloomberg’s Caroline Hyde and Ed Ludlow discuss Nvidia’s plans to sell advanced semiconductors to Humain for a massive data center project in Saudi Arabia. Plus, City Index Senior Analyst Fiona Cincotta explains why markets aren’t out of the woods yet. All this as US President Donald Trump and Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman meet in Riyadh to announce new investments.  (Source: Bloomberg)

title: S&P 500, Nasdaq 100 Erase 2025 Drop as Trade Hope Sparks Rebound
content: The S&P 500 and Nasdaq 100 indexes turned higher for the year on Tuesday, reversing multi-trillion dollar routs, as enthusiasm for US stocks grows with global trade tensions cooling after the Trump administration and China agreed to temporarily lower tariffs.

title: Google Backs Saudi AI Fund as Trump, MBS Tout New Investments
content: Saudi Arabian venture capital firm STV launched a $100 million artificial intelligence fund with backing from Google as part of a package of deals announced during US President Donald Trump’s visit to the kingdom.

title: Milei Scraps Tariffs That Put $2,000 Price Tags on iPhones
content: President Javier Milei cut tariffs that made Argentina one of the most expensive places in the world to buy iPhones after decades of protectionist policies, delivering on a campaign promise to open up the economy to trade.

title: US Warns That Using Huawei AI Chip ‘Anywhere’ Breaks Its Rules
content: The Commerce Department issued guidance stating that the use of Huawei Technologies Co.’s Ascend artificial intelligence chips “anywhere in the world” violates the government’s export controls, escalating US efforts to curb technological advances in China.

title: Microsoft Is Cutting Thousands of Employees Across the Company
content: Microsoft Corp. said it will cut 6,000 workers across the company in an effort to reduce management layers.

title: Trump to Rewrite AI Chip Curbs Reviled by Nvidia and US Allies
content: The Trump administration plans to overhaul regulations on the export of semiconductors used in artificial intelligence, tossing out a Biden-era approach that had drawn strenuous objections from US allies and companies including Nvidia Corp. and Oracle Corp.

title: Top Asia Advisers at Morgan Stanley, UBS See China Revival
content: Two senior executives from Morgan Stanley and UBS Group AG who advise Asia’s ultra-wealthy are seeing renewed investor optimism over China following a weekend truce between the two largest economies.

title: Restaurant Tech Startup Owner.com Hits $1 Billion Valuation
content: Meritech and Headline co-led a $120 million funding around for the startup.

title: US Mulls Letting UAE Buy Over a Million Leading Nvidia Chips
content: The Trump administration is weighing a deal that would allow the United Arab Emirates to import more than a million advanced Nvidia Corp. chips, people familiar with the matter said, a quantity that far exceeds limits under Biden-era AI chip regulations — and one that’s raised concerns that American hardware risks ending up in China’s hands.

title: Google Unveils Major Android Redesign Ahead of iPhone Overhaul
content: Google unveiled the biggest update to its Android mobile operating system in years, weeks before its biggest competitor in the space, Apple Inc., is expected to give a preview of its overhauled iPhone software.

title: Nvidia, AMD Sell Chips to Saudi Arabia for AI Data Centers
content: Nvidia Corp. and Advanced Micro Devices Inc. will supply semiconductors to Saudi Arabian artificial intelligence company Humain for a massive data center project, acting under a Trump administration initiative that lifts restrictions on delivering advanced technology to the region.

title: OpenAI Weighs UAE Data Center Deal as Trump Set to Visit
content: OpenAI is considering building new data center capacity in the United Arab Emirates that could significantly expand its footprint in the Middle East, according to people familiar with the matter.

title: Saudi Arabia, AMD Plan $10 Billion Deployment of AI Gear
content: Humain, Saudi Arabia’s new artificial intelligence investment company, is teaming up with chipmaker Advanced Micro Devices Inc. to spend $10 billion on AI infrastructure over the next five years.

title: Indie Music Power Broker to Depart Amid Industry Tech Reckoning
content: Jeremy Sirota, CEO of Merlin, will exit the company at the end of 2025

title: Intel’s New CEO to Focus on Executing Its Existing Strategy
content: New Intel Corp. Chief Executive Officer Lip-Bu Tan is focused on improving the execution of the chipmaker’s existing strategy rather than making sweeping changes, according to his head of finance.

title: In Trump’s World, Jets Are Key to Unlocking Political Favors
content: President Donald Trump’s long-held fascination with the world of aviation is proving a useful tool for governments and companies seeking to win his favor.

title: Merz Risks Coalition Spat With Call to Scrap EU Supply-Chain Law
content: Germany’s new chancellor, Friedrich Merz, reiterated a call for the European Union to scrap rules designed to make companies pursue sustainable policies in their supply chains, doubling down on a position that risks igniting conflict with his Social Democrat coalition partners.

title: How Australia’s Housing Market Became So Out of Reach
content: Ballooning property prices and rents are causing serious housing affordability problems in Australia. So how bad is it? And how did it get to this point?

title: Angola’s Fight Against Corruption Is Losing Momentum, IMF Says
content: Angolan President Joao Lourenco’s anti-corruption drive is losing steam, threatening the country’s economic growth outlook, according to the International Monetary Fund.

title: Wall Street Sees Higher China Growth, Less Stimulus on US Truce
content: Goldman Sachs Group Inc. and other major banks boosted their forecasts for China’s 2025 economic growth, citing a better outlook for exports following the tariff truce with the US.

title: South Korean Think Tank Halves 2025 Growth Forecast to 0.8%
content: A South Korean state-funded think tank slashed its outlook for the country’s growth this year, reflecting the fallout from Donald Trump’s tariff campaign on the trade-reliant nation as its presidential race hits full swing.

title: Japan’s Key Trade Chiefs Skip Chance to Meet Greer at APEC
content: Japan’s Trade Minister Yoji Muto will skip a gathering of trade chiefs this week, a decision that will likely lower Tokyo’s chances of holding meaningful bilateral talks with US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer on the sidelines of the meeting.

title: Peru Prime Minister Resigns After Backlash From Cabinet Reshuffle
content: Peru’s prime minister resigned on Tuesday evening after a last-ditch attempt at a cabinet reshuffle did not placate opposition lawmakers who demanded his ouster.

title: Australian Wage Growth Quickens to 3.4% on Tight Jobs Market
content: Australia’s wage growth was stronger than expected in the first three months of the year, highlighting the nation’s tight labor market that has been underpinned by a wave of public-sector hiring.

title: China Surrounded Xi’s Aide With Seasoned Experts to Seal US Deal
content: China’s surprisingly quick agreement with the US to wind back punitive tariff rates put a spotlight on a Chinese negotiating team that features decades worth of technical trade experience alongside a top aide of President Xi Jinping.

title: New Zealand Saw Record Number of People Depart in March Year
content: A record number of people left New Zealand in the year through March, reducing the net gain through immigration to the lowest in more than two years.

title: Milei Scraps Tariffs That Put $2,000 Price Tags on iPhones
content: President Javier Milei cut tariffs that made Argentina one of the most expensive places in the world to buy iPhones after decades of protectionist policies, delivering on a campaign promise to open up the economy to trade.

title: Trump’s Global Tariffs Face Key Test in US Trade Court
content: A group of small businesses urged the US trade court to block President Donald Trump’s “Liberation Day” global tariffs during a court hearing that could have a major impact on the Republican’s economic agenda.

title: Trump Says Fed Must Lower Rates After Soft Inflation Report
content: President Donald Trump cited a softer-than-expected inflation report to again pressure Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell to lower interest rates.

title: Trump and MBS Tout $1 Trillion Pledge as Details Remain Elusive
content: President Donald Trump and Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman touted a pledge for $1 trillion in commercial deals in Riyadh on Tuesday, a staggering figure that doesn’t quite stand up to scrutiny.

title: Cheaper Eggs, Pricier Car Rentals: A Look at US April Inflation
content: US inflation rose by less than expected in April, helped by steep declines in prices for sporting events, eggs and other groceries.

title: ECB’s Villeroy Says Another Rate Cut Is Likely by Summer
content: The European Central Bank will probably lower borrowing costs again by the summer as trade tensions aren’t fueling inflation in the region, Governing Council member Francois Villeroy de Galhau said.

title: Romania Raises €1.6 Billion in Local Debt Before Tight Vote
content: Romania sold more euro-denominated debt on the domestic market than planned, rushing to fill up state coffers ahead of a contentious presidential run-off that’s weighed on the the country’s assets.

title: Colombian Business Lobby Warns of Risks From a Deal With China
content: Colombia’s business lobby warned of risks to local industry from President Gustavo Petro’s plan to join the Chinese Belt and Road Initiative.

title: Student Loans Drive US Delinquency Rate to Highest Since 2020
content: The share of outstanding US consumer debt that’s in delinquency rose in the first quarter to the highest in five years, reflecting an end to the pandemic-era pause on reporting delinquent student loan payments on credit reports.

title: ECB’s Knot Sees Trade Curbing Inflation and Growth in Near Term
content: Uncertainty stemming from US trade policy is likely to curb inflation and economic growth in the near term, though its effects on prices are less clear beyond that, according to European Central Bank Governing Council member Klaas Knot.

title: UK Taxpayers to Make Money on BOE Lending to Banks, Reeves Says
content: The Bank of England is expected to make a profit on the cash it provides high street lenders, a small consolation for UK taxpayers as losses on its flagship quantitative-easing program continue to mount.

title: Bulgarian President’s Proposal for Euro Referendum Blocked
content: Bulgaria’s parliament speaker dismissed an initiative by President Rumen Radev to hold a referendum on euro adoption as the nation moves closer to joining the single currency next year.

title: Poland’s Domanski Sees EU Defense Fund Agreement This Month
content: Polish Finance Minister Andrzej Domanski said he expects the European Union to reach a deal this month on a €150 billion ($167 billion) fund to boost the bloc’s defense capabilities.

title: Softer-Than-Expected Inflation Points to Muted Tariff Fallout
content: US inflation rose by less than forecast in April amid tame prices for clothing and new cars, suggesting little urgency so far by companies to pass along the cost of higher tariffs to consumers.

title: Here Are the Key Takeaways From the US CPI Report for April
content: Here are five key takeaways from today’s April US consumer price index report:

title: US Small-Business Optimism Declines for a Fourth Straight Month
content: Sentiment among US small businesses deteriorated for a fourth straight month in April as firms grew more downbeat about the economic outlook and sales prospects amid higher tariffs.

title: Brazil Central Bank Vows Tight Monetary Policy for Prolonged Period
content: Brazil’s central bank sees the need for tighter monetary policy for a longer period due to unanchored inflation forecasts, according to the minutes to the last interest rate decision published on Tuesday.

title: Bessent Says EU Is Plagued by ‘Collective Action Problem’
content: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said the European Union suffers from a “collective action problem” that’s hampering trade negotiations, downplaying the possibility of a quick agreement with the US’s largest trading relationship.

title: Burberry to Cut Almost a Fifth of Workforce as Sales Drop
content: Burberry Group Plc plans to cut almost one-fifth of its work force as its new chief executive officer tries to turn around the British trench-coat maker, after its push into high fashion flopped amid a downturn in global demand for luxury goods.

title: Aviva’s £3.7 Billion Direct Line Deal Faces UK Merger Review
content: Aviva Plc faces a review by the UK’s merger watchdog into its plan to buy Direct Line Insurance Group Plc for roughly £3.7 billion ($4.9 billion) in a deal that would create the UK’s largest motor insurer.

title: Imperial Brands CEO to Retire After Push to Drive Tobacco Sales
content: Imperial Brands Plc Chief Executive Officer Stefan Bomhard is to retire after five years in charge of the British tobacco maker, which turned its focus back to cigarettes and boosted shareholder returns on his watch.

title: GSK to Buy Liver Disease Drug for as Much as $2 Billion
content: GSK Plc agreed to buy an experimental medicine to treat liver disease for as much as $2 billion as the UK drugmaker seeks to shore up its pipeline of new medicines.

title: Trump Favors $40-$50 Oil, Goldman Says After Sifting Posts
content: President Donald Trump appears to prefer US oil prices between $40 and $50 a barrel, according to Goldman Sachs Group Inc., citing an in-house analysis of his social-media posts on the topic.

title: Daimler Truck Cuts Guidance, Citing North America Uncertainty
content: Daimler Truck Holding AG lowered its sales and profit guidance for the year, citing increasing economic uncertainty in North America due to trade tensions in the region.

title: EON Says Grid Investments Drove First-Quarter Earnings Jump
content: EON SE’s earnings jumped in the first quarter as the German energy company continues to focus investments on power grids and benefit from the region’s energy transition.

title: Bad Trader Behavior, Short-Sale Breaches Stalk Australian Banks
content: Australia’s finance industry is beset by a raft of compliance lapses — from data reporting breaches to trader misbehavior — reigniting concerns the $541 billion sector has struggled to clean up after a litany of scandals came to light six years ago.

title: Nissan Shares Fall on Annual Loss, Withheld Profit Outlook
content: Nissan Motor Co. shares fell after the Japanese automaker posted an annual net loss of ¥670.9 billion ($4.5 billion) and decided against issuing an operating profit forecast for the current fiscal year.

title: Millennium Hires Ex-UBS Asia-Pacific Equity Derivatives Head
content: Millennium Management hired UBS Group AG’s former equity derivatives head for Asia-Pacific, the latest move by the $73 billion investment giant to tap investment bank executives for expansion.

title: VietJet Set for Financial Reckoning as Court Denies Payment Stay
content: A London High Court has refused VietJet Aviation JSC’s application for a stay and ruled the Vietnamese carrier must pay around $180 million to an aircraft leasing firm starting this week, bringing to a head a years-long legal dispute that started during the Covid-19 pandemic

title: Taiwan Opens Door to Restart Atomic Power Plants in Reversal
content: Taiwanese lawmakers revised a nuclear power bill that effectively opens the door for a restart of the island’s atomic plants, underscoring a wider policy shift as its energy demand grows and geopolitical tensions worsen.

title: Barclays Picks Avinash Thakur to Head Investment Banking in Asia Pacific
content: Barclays Plc has named Avinash Thakur as head of investment banking for Asia Pacific, replacing Vanessa Koo, who is retiring.

title: Nubank Shares Dip Post-Earnings as Funding Weighs on Margins
content: Shares of Nu Holdings Ltd. fell after reporting first quarter results that showed strong revenue growth weighed down by higher spending to attract new clients and protect against potential bad loans.

title: Harvard Expands Lawsuit Against US as Funding Feud Deepens
content: Harvard University expanded its lawsuit Tuesday against the Trump administration for freezing billions of dollars in federal funds, ratcheting up the high-stakes legal battle between the wealthiest US university and the White House.

title: UK Watchdog Set to Ease Insurance Rules for Large Companies
content: The UK markets watchdog is planning to pare its rules on how insurers can sell policies to large companies, the latest signal regulators are pivoting to a more pragmatic stance that leans heavily into the government’s growth agenda.

title: State Farm Wins 17% Emergency Rate Hike for Homes After LA Fires
content: State Farm has been approved for an emergency 17% rate increase on homeowner insurance policies in California, part of an effort to shore up the state’s largest insurer after the devastating wildfires in the Los Angeles area.

title: B. Riley Overshoots Another Deadline for Filing Results With SEC
content: B. Riley Financial Inc. added to its tally of overdue regulatory filings, this time missing the deadline for quarterly results as soured investments mounted.

title: Promoters of $100 Million NJ Deli Get Prison Time for Fraud
content: A father and son who participated in a scheme to inflate the value of a New Jersey deli to more than $100 million each received prison time for their roles in the fraud.

title: Sean ‘Diddy’ Combs’ Ex-Girlfriend Recounts ‘Freak-Offs’ and Fear
content: Sean “Diddy” Combs’ ex-girlfriend, Cassandra “Cassie” Ventura, told jurors she agreed to days-long drug-fueled sex parties during her decade-long relationship with Combs because she feared his violence, but also because she wanted to make him happy.

title: UnitedHealth Replaces CEO as Its Medicare Strategy Sputters
content: UnitedHealth Group Inc. unexpectedly replaced its chief executive and suspended earnings guidance, raising increasing questions over how the company once regarded as a safe bet by investors has got its cost predictions so wrong.

title: Arbor Realty Bundles Rental Loans in Its First CLO Deal Since 2022
content: Arbor Realty Trust Inc. is returning to securitization markets for the first time in three years as it looks to package up loans secured by apartment rental properties.

title: American Eagle Withdraws 2025 Outlook After Weak First Quarter
content: American Eagle Outfitters Inc.’s stock dropped after it pulled its guidance for the full year following a first quarter that was marred by discounting and a write-down of inventory.

title: China Birth Rate Plans Boost New Zealand’s Top-Performing Stock
content: China’s plans to lift its birth rate have helped a2 Milk Co.’s stock become the biggest gainer in New Zealand this year.

title: CFPB Drops Biden-Era Lawsuit Against Walmart, Fintech Partner
content: The Consumer Financial Protection Bureau dropped its lawsuit against Walmart Inc. and one of its financial-technology partners, the latest of the agency’s Biden-era enforcement actions to be abandoned by President Donald Trump’s administration.

title: Southwest Air Hints at International Expansion in DOT Filing
content: Southwest Airlines Co. has filed with the US Transportation Department for authority to fly to any country with which the US has an Open Skies aviation agreement, signaling the carrier intends to expand its small international route network.

title: Goldman in Talks to Expand Marcus Retail Bank Into Ireland
content: Goldman Sachs Group Inc. has held talks with regulators about an Irish launch of its retail bank Marcus, a move that could shake up the country’s heavily concentrated market and give the Wall Street giant access to tens of billions of euros in deposits.

title: Starbucks Baristas Strike Over Dress Code, Signal More Walkouts
content: Hundreds of Starbucks Corp. employees have walked off the job since Sunday to protest the company’s new dress code, according to the union representing baristas, with more strikes likely in the coming days.

title: NYC Ordered to Hand Control of Rikers Jail to Outside Manager
content: A federal judge ordered New York City to hand control of its troubled Rikers Island jail to an outside manager, capping a decade-long court-ordered monitorship that consistently found rampant violence and other ills in the city’s lockups.

title: Paul Allen’s Estate Puts NBA’s Portland Trail Blazers Up for Sale
content: The NBA has yet another team on the market, with the Portland Trail Blazers being put up for sale by the estate of Paul Allen, the Microsoft Corp. co-founder.

title: Man from Moldova accused in credit card fraud scheme
content: A man wanted in his home country of Moldova was found to be in unlawful possession of 131 credit cards that didn't match his identity following a traffic stop on the Indiana Toll Road in Porter County this past weekend.

title: “Dagestani Achilles Heel” Given Credit For Jack Della Maddalena’s Win Over Belal Muhammad at UFC 315
content: Jack Della Maddalena's coach gets huge praise from a former UFC heavyweight who labeled him the "Dagestani Achilles Heel".

title: Student loan collections resume, credit scores tumble: NY Fed
content: Millions of borrowers who are late on their student loan payments now face "grave consequences" as collection activity restarts, the New York Fed says.

title: Americans’ credit card debt falls, but past-due student loans drag on credit scores
content: Americans tidied up their household balance sheets to start 2025, cleaning up some credit card and auto loan debt, new data showed Tuesday.

title: Rain helps increase Carolina Forest wildfire containment to 93%
content: Officials with the South Carolina Forestry Commission credit recent rain for an increase in containment of the Carolina Forest wildfire.

title: Marks & Spencer confirms customers' personal data was stolen in hack
content: A ransomware gang reportedly took credit for the data breach.

content: Donald Trump has suggested that he indeed played a role in Pope Leo XIV's election. No, it's not about whether he had something to do with the papal conclave, but rather his big win among the Catholic voters in America.

content: Convenience food manufacturer Greencore Group Plc agreed to buy rival Bakkavor Group Plc for about £1.2 billion ($1.6 billion).

title: Horizons Middle East & Africa 05/15/2025
content: Horizons Middle East & Africa is your daily spotlight on one of the world's fastest-growing regions. Live from Dubai, we bring you the latest global markets and analysis, plus news-making interviews, with a special focus on MEA. All that and more, as you head to the office in the Gulf, pause for lunch in Hong Kong, or start your day in London or Johannesburg.  (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Ives: Middle East Ahead of China in Acquiring AI Chips
content: The Trump administration is clearing a path for Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates to pursue their artificial intelligence ambitions. Under new agreements with the US, the two nations will get wider access to advanced AI chips from Nvidia and AMD. Dan Ives, Managing Director and Senior Equity Analyst at Wedbush Securities, spoke to Bloomberg’s Horizons Middle East and Africa anchor Joumanna Bercetche on these deals. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: US, Chinese Trade Negotiators Meet for Talks in South Korea
content: US and Chinese officials met for trade talks in South Korea on Thursday, just days after both sides met in Switzerland and agreed to pause some tariffs for 90 days.

title: Reliance Gets $2.98 Billion Loan, India’s Biggest Since 2023
content: Billionaire Mukesh Ambani-owned Reliance Industries has obtained a $2.98 billion-equivalent loan, according to people familiar with the matter, the largest such deal for an Indian borrower in more than a year.

title: SingPost Falls Most on Record on Underlying Loss, Gloomy Outlook
content: Singapore Post Ltd.’s shares fell by a record after the company booked an underlying loss and issued a gloomy outlook on the back the of global trade tensions.

title: Aviva’s Wealth Unit Sees £2.3 Billion Inflows as Assets Rise 5%
content: UK insurer Aviva Plc said its wealth unit saw net inflows in the first quarter, with assets under management in the business rising by 5%.

title: Insight with Haslinda Amin 5/15/2025
content: Insight with Haslinda Amin, a daily news program featuring in-depth, high-profile interviews and analysis to give viewers the complete picture on the stories that matter. title: Stocks Retreat as Trade-Truce Rally Loses Steam: Markets Wrap
content: Global stocks fell on Thursday for the first time in seven sessions as the rally on Wall Street sparked by US-China trade talks showed signs of exhaustion.

title: Gold Falls as Fed Rate-Cut Bets Soften, Haven Demand Ebbs
content: Gold extended its decline after falling more than 2% Wednesday on signs there will be fewer Federal Reserve rate cuts than previously anticipated, and as easing trade tensions between the US and China sapped haven demand.

title: AllianzGI CEO Would Consider Deals to Grow Private Market Assets
content: Allianz Global Investors is open to deals as part of Chief Executive Officer Tobias C. Pross’s efforts to expand the private markets business.

title: Rakuten Group Shares Sink on Worse-Than-Expected Loss
content: Rakuten Group Inc. shares tumbled by the most in five weeks after the Japanese e-commerce firm reported a 19th straight quarterly loss.

title: Merck KGaA Lowers Outlook on Tariff Risks, Currency Headwinds
content: Merck KGaA reduced its outlook for sales and profit growth this year, citing the impact of a weak US dollar and uncertainty around tariffs.

title: Oil Falls a Second Day as Iran Signals Openness to Nuclear Deal
content: Oil fell for a second day following a report Iran is willing to forgo nuclear weapons in a deal with the US in exchange for sanctions relief.

title: Bloomberg: The China Show 05/15/2025
content: “Bloomberg: The China Show” is your definitive source for news and analysis on the world's second-biggest economy. content: The bottom line of Trump’s desired tax cuts will be greater deficits.

title: Thyssenkrupp Holds Guidance Despite Slump in Earnings, Cash
content: Thyssenkrupp AG reaffirmed its full-year guidance even as earnings slumped due to weak demand from automotive and industrial customers.

title: Why Tencent Is Investing in AI Gaming
content: Tencent has reaffirmed a commitment to keep spending on developing AI - which may crimp profit growth in the short term. But by integrating the technology across a suite of products it hopes to reap longer-term revenue and improve gaming experience. Elinor Leung, Head of Asia Telecom and Internet Research at CLSA, speaks on Bloomberg’s The Asia Trade.

title: Bloomberg: The Asia Trade 05/15/2025
content: "Bloomberg: The Asia Trade" brings you everything you need to know to get ahead as the trading day begins in Asia. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Singapore Home Sales Fall for Second Month as Demand Weakens
content: Singapore private home sales fell for a second month as demand for new projects dimmed at a time when trade tensions are fueling unease about the economic outlook.

title: Fidelity Adds US Stocks After ‘Pivotal’ Trade Truce With China
content: A Fidelity International fund manager said she has increased exposure to US stocks this week, citing renewed optimism following the trade truce with China.

title: Xero CEO on FY Results, Business Strategy
content: Sukhinder Singh Cassidy, CEO at Xero, discusses the company's full-year results and outlook for its business strategy. She speaks with Haidi Stroud-Watts and Avril Hong on "Bloomberg: The Asia Trade". (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Goldman Sachs Sees Limited Room for Asian IG Spreads Tightening
content: Goldman Sachs Group Inc. says Asian investment-grade credit spreads have limited room to tighten further after erasing the spike triggered by President Donald Trump’s early-April tariff announcement.

title: Uganda Using 'Extraordinary Measures' to Grow FX Reserves, Central Bank Governor Says
content: Bank of Uganda Governor Governor Michael Atingi-Ego says the central bank has taken "extraordinary measures" to grow the nation's foreign exchange reserves, including buying $1.5 billion from the market this fiscal year and using currency swaps. The transactions have so far amounted to $400 million, Atingi-Ego said from the capital, Kampala, in an interview with Bloomberg's Jennifer Zabasajja. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Trade Chiefs Vie for Time With Greer at APEC Meeting
content: Trade chiefs from some of major economies are vying for access to US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer at the APEC trade ministers’ meeting. Many are seeking talks with Greer to discuss tariffs affecting their economies and to try to mitigate the impact of Trump's trade policies. Stephen Engle reports from Jeju, South Korea. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Manhattan Rents at Record Highs Hint at More Increases to Come
content: Manhattan’s apartment market is heading into its most competitive months of the year with rents already at record highs. They’re only likely to continue rising through the summer.

title: US-China Trade Clash Risks Making Europe Dumping Ground for Cheap Goods
content: China’s widening trade surplus with the European Union is fueling fresh concerns that the 27-nation bloc risks becoming a dumping ground for cheap goods in the volatile tariff confrontation between Washington and Beijing.

title: US Approves $304 Million Missile Sale to Turkey as Ties Warm Up

title: Oil Falls After Spiking on Iran-US Nuclear Deal Uncertainty
content: Oil fell after a short-lived spike as Tehran cast fresh doubts about the status of US-Iran nuclear talks.

title: Gold Declines as Traders Book Profits on US-China Trade Optimism
content: Gold fell to extend its weekly loss, as investors booked profits after tensions eased between the US and China this week, cutting demand for haven assets.

title: TPG-Backed XCL Gets Private Loan From Apollo, Partners Group
content: XCL Education, a school owner and operator backed by private equity firm TPG, has obtained a $400 million private credit loan to refinance its existing debt, according to people familiar with the matter.

title: Vietnam, Thailand Lift Relationship Amid Rising Economic Ties

title: Jane Street Index Derivatives Trades Probed by India Regulator
content: India’s capital markets regulator is conducting an investigation of index derivatives trades by Jane Street Group, according to people familiar with the matter.

title: India Is Hot Trade Again as Investors Chase Trump-Era Winners
content: Global funds are pouring money back into India, driving billion-dollar corporate financing deals and sending stocks prices to near a seven-month high, as investors bet that Asia’s third-largest economy can emerge as a winner in President Donald Trump’s trade war.

title: Google VP Bhatia on Geopolitical Tensions, AI
content: Google VP Karan Bhatia discusses the impact of US-China geopolitical tensions and trade dynamics on global tech industry. He expresses strong optimism for AI adoption and growth potential in the Asia Pacific region, also emphasizing a long-term commitment even as rising trade tensions affect the tech industry. He spoke to Bloomberg's Chief North Asia Correspondent Stephen Engle on the sidelines of APEC trade ministers' meeting in Jeju, South Korea. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Japan’s Surging Yields Put Policymakers in a Tough Position
content: After years of moving at a glacial pace, yields in Japan’s $7.8 trillion government debt market are shifting higher at breakneck speed.

content: European Union Commissioner for Economy and Productivity Valdis Dombrovskis discussed the US-EU-China trade environment and how negotiations on tariffs are going. In a May 15 interview with Bloomberg’s Kriti Gupta, he also said that if the bloc was to “suddenly see that there is a strong flood of Chinese goods coming to the EU,” it will have to protect the market.

content: A wave of secondary share sales in India, driven by a rebound in local equities, is pushing the deal volume to the highest level in nearly nine months.

content: WTO Director Generral Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala says she's 'very encouraged' by the easing of US-China tensions and calls for further progress, observing that the contraction in global goods trade contraction is already lessening. content: India is reviewing a US request to lift restrictions on ethanol imports as it negotiates a wider trade deal with Washington to avoid punitive tariffs.

title: Chinese Gold Miner Chifeng Scours Globe for Takeover Targets
content: A major Chinese gold producer is scouting for acquisition opportunities around the world, although the recent price volatility driven by global trade turmoil means it’s not rushing to secure deals.

title: 'Quite Attractive' Opportunities in Asian Bonds, BlackRock's Saigal Says
content:
BlackRock's Navin Saigal says the current environment is "an exciting one" and perhaps what most investors "are not entirely used to." Saigal tells Bloomberg Television that "what is inflationary at the margin for the US could be deflationary for China and the rest of Asia." He says the disinflationary or deflationary trend is real, but it also creates a huge opportunity for bond investors to add a diversified market to their portfolios.
 (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Romania to Hold Rates With All Eyes on Leu Path
content: Romania’s central bank will probably keep interest rates unchanged on Friday, with investors looking for any clues about the outlook for the leu after political turmoil pushed the currency to record lows.

title: Trump’s Pledge to Lift Syrian Sanctions Faces a Complex Road
content: US President Donald Trump says he’s ready to ease sanctions on Syria. He won’t be able to do it quickly.

title: World Economic Forum Courts Lagarde as Its Next Leader After Founder’s Abrupt Exit
content: Klaus Schwab’s abrupt departure from the World Economic Forum, the influential organization he founded and led for more than half a century, has complicated carefully laid plans to persuade Christine Lagarde to assume the helm in a seamless transition, according to people familiar with the discussions.

title: US Treasury Warns Hong Kong Banks Over Funding Iran Oil Trades
content: A US Treasury delegation met with Hong Kong banks to warn them against facilitating Iran oil shipments to China in April, just a month before sanctioning nine non-bank entities in the city allegedly involved in such trades, according to people familiar with the matter.

title: India’s Jaishankar Discusses Kashmir in First Call With Taliban
content: India’s foreign minister discussed last month’s deadly attack in Kashmir during his first conversation with Afghanistan’s Taliban-led government, as the two sides continue efforts to improve ties.

title: India Airports End Turkish Firm’s Services Over Pakistan Row
content: India stopped a Turkish company from operating at its airports after Turkey voiced support for Pakistan during a recent conflict between the two South Asian neighbors.

content: Recent changes to immigration policy won’t do anything for people who’ve been exploited while seeking jobs in the UK. But they may worsen the care-worker shortage.

content: Romania’s track record as a reliable supporter of the European project will be put to the test Sunday as an ultranationalist Donald Trump disciple contends for the presidency against a one-time math prodigy.

title: Trump to Keep 30% China Tariffs Till Late 2025, Analysts Say
content: Donald Trump’s tariffs on China will likely remain at a level expected to severely curtail Chinese exports to the US after the 90-day truce, analysts and investors say, suggesting Beijing may have to endure further economic pain despite active talks.

title: Pakistan Says Ceasefire With India to Be Extended to May 18 as Truce Holds
content: The ceasefire between Pakistan and India will be extended to May 18, a top official in Islamabad said, indicating the respite in fighting is holding after clashes this month brought the two nuclear-armed nations close to a full-blown war.

content: In the blistering heat outside Winston Churchill’s ancestral home last summer, it began to dawn on Keir Starmer that his plan to reset Britain’s relationship with the European Union would be easier said than done.

title: Crypto Bill Poised for Resurrection After Democrats Hail Changes
content: Crypto-friendly Senate Democrats moved closer to reviving stablecoin legislation sought by the industry after bipartisan negotiators agreed to assorted revisions, including tightened restrictions on money laundering, foreign issuers and technology companies.

title: Ukraine Ceasefire Prospects Dim as Calls for New Sanctions Grow
content: Hopes faded for a Ukraine ceasefire after Vladimir Putin sent a low-level delegation to talks in Turkey, while attention shifted to bids on Capitol Hill for fresh sanctions to bring the Russian leader to the negotiating table.

content: Bloomberg’s Caroline Hyde and Ed Ludlow discuss President Trump’s call for Apple to stop moving iPhone production to India and instead shift it to the US. And CoreWeave CEO Michael Intrator discusses the expanded partnership with OpenAI and the company’s first earnings report since going public. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: EU Digital Chief Defends Bloc’s Tech Regulation
content: European Commissioner for Tech Sovereignty, Security and Democracy Henna Virkkunen talks about the EU’s efforts to shape the future of digital competition and innovation as she meets with CEOs and officials in Silicon Valley and Washington, D.C. She joins Caroline Hyde and Ed Ludlow on “Bloomberg Technology.” (Source: Bloomberg)

title: ‘Grand Theft Auto’ Delay Fails to Dent Take-Two Investor Zeal

content: The US was stripped of its last top credit rating by Moody’s Ratings, reflecting deepening concern that ballooning debt and deficits will damage America’s standing as the preeminent destination for global capital and increase the government’s borrowing costs.

title: Stocks Fall Late on US Downgrade as Yields Climb: Markets Wrap

content: Chicago is hiring Ernst & Young LLP to help the city slash costs and close budget gaps that are forecast to top $1 billion in each of the next two years.

title: Druckenmiller’s Duquesne Slashes Successful Argentina Bet by 19%
content: ARGT has paid off handsomely since the firm started building the position in early 2024

title: Europe Waits to See Where Trump Swerves to Next on Russia
content: European officials have no idea what President Donald Trump will say next about Russia’s war in Ukraine — or where that may leave them.

title: Arab League Summit in Baghdad Has Gaza Topping the Agenda
content: BAGHDAD (AP) — Regional leaders were to meet in Baghdad on Saturday at the annual summit of the Arab League, with the war in Gaza expected to once again loom large.

title: Australia Condemns Russia’s 13-Year Sentence for Citizen
content: Australia’s foreign minister condemned a 13-year prison sentence handed down by a Russian court to an Australian national who fought with Ukrainian forces, calling the process a “sham trial” and vowing to press for his release.

title: At Least Four Dead After Tornado, Storm Batters St. Louis, Mayor Says
content: ST. LOUIS (AP) — At least seven people died and authorities were searching from building to building for people who were trapped or hurt after severe storms including at least one possible tornado swept through Missouri.

title: Turkey’s Celebi Says It’s Cooperating After India Revokes Clearance
content: Turkish company Çelebi Aviation said on Saturday it’s “fully cooperating” with Indian authorities and adhering to regulations after its ground handling and cargo warehouse operations were suspended due to national security concerns.

title: Reeves Faces Call From Her Local Party to Abandon Disability Cuts
content: Rachel Reeves's local Labour party will demand that the Chancellor abandons her plans to cut disability benefits.

title: Abrego Garcia Judge Frustrated at US Not Answering Questions
content: A federal judge repeatedly expressed frustration Friday at the Trump administration’s failure to answer her questions about what it is doing to facilitate the return of a Maryland resident wrongly deported to a notorious prison in his native El Salvador.

title: Trump Expects to Meet With Putin to ‘Make a Deal’ to End War
content: President Donald Trump predicted he would probably meet with Russian leader Vladimir Putin, suggesting that he saw a potential face-to-face encounter as the only way to broker an end to the war in Ukraine.

title: White House Criticizes Moody’s Downgrade to US Credit Rating
content: The White House on Friday assailed a decision by Moody’s Ratings to lower the US credit rating, casting it as a political decision.

title: Trump Says He’s Willing to Travel to China for Xi Meeting
content: US President Donald Trump said he would be willing to travel to China to speak with Xi Jinping about foreign policy and economic issues.

title: Indian Companies, Consumers Snub Pakistan and Its Allies
content: A growing number of Indian merchants, companies, and consumers are cutting business ties with Pakistan and some of its allies after a heightened conflict between the South Asian neighbors.

title: Trump Says India Offered to Cut US Tariffs But He’s in No Rush
content: President Donald Trump said that India has offered to cut all its tariffs on US goods but downplayed any sense of urgency to reach a trade agreement with the world’s fourth-largest economy.

title: Supreme Court Extends Halt of Trump Venezuelan Deportations
content: The US Supreme Court blocked the Trump administration from using a wartime law to send about 176 Venezuelans to a notorious Salvadoran prison, faulting the government for not giving the men adequate notice about its deportation plans.

title: Why Trump Is Targeting Harvard’s Funding and Tax-Exempt Status
content: President Donald Trump has been waging a campaign to pressure elite US colleges to make a wide range of policy changes, in what his administration has framed as an initiative to fight campus antisemitism and enforce civil rights protections.

title: Chicago Taps EY to Close $1 Billion Gap as Trump Threatens Funds
content: Chicago is hiring Ernst & Young LLP to help the city slash costs and close budget gaps that are forecast to top $1 billion in each of the next two years.

title: Trump Tax Bill Fails in House Panel as GOP Splits on Cost
content: A key House committee on Friday failed to advance House Republicans’ massive tax-and-spending bill after hard-line conservatives bucked President Donald Trump and blocked the bill over cost concerns.

title: Trump’s Crypto Project Pushes Back on Senate Inquiry
content: Attorneys for Donald Trump’s World Liberty Financial crypto project pushed back against claims about potential conflicts of interest raised by the Democratic head of a Senate investigative subcommittee.

title: Trump Puts Wealth Fund on Back Burner as Ambitions Hit Limits
content: President Donald Trump has put his plan to create a sovereign wealth fund on the back burner after three months of administration deliberations failed to offer the broad investment flexibility he seeks, people familiar with the matter said.

title: CFTC to Dwindle to Two Members After Goldsmith Romero Departure
content: The five-person Commodity Futures Trading Commission will soon be down to just two members, after Commissioner Christy Goldsmith Romero announced plans to leave the agency at the end of the month.

title: Russia, Ukraine Discussed Truce, Prisoner Swap in Talks
content: The first direct talks between Russia and Ukraine in more than three years ended in Turkey with an agreement on an exchange of prisoners and discussions on a potential ceasefire, though no truce was announced.

title: SALT Republicans Signal $80,000 Cap Could Be on Table
content: Two New York Republicans signaled that the cap on the state and local tax deduction may rise to as much as $80,000 as GOP lawmakers from high-tax states demand a boost in exchange for their votes on President Donald Trump’s tax package.

title: Slovenia Calls on NATO to Expand Its Defense Spending Terms
content: Slovenia and several NATO member states are seeking ways to expand the definition of defense spending as they attempt to meet US calls to allocate more funds on security, the nation’s prime minister said.

title: Trump Threatens Iran Over Nuclear Offer Tehran Calls ‘Confusing’
content: President Donald Trump said Iran will face “something bad” if it doesn’t quickly accept a US proposal over its nuclear program, while officials in Tehran called the the US messaging “confusing and contradictory.”

title: Poland’s Presidential Vote Puts Tusk’s Reform Agenda at Stake
content: Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk’s push to undo eight years of populist rule faces a reckoning just as other parts of Europe struggle to contain rising support for more conservative, nationalist forces.

title: Energy Tax Credit Fight Splits GOP in Snag for Speaker
content: Moderate House Republicans are lobbying House Speaker Mike Johnson to lessen cuts to several clean energy tax credits in the broad tax and spending bill prior to the GOP’s plans to bring it to the floor next week.

title: Trump’s Aerospace Deals Were Big on Numbers and Slim on Details
content: US President Donald Trump ended his tour of the Middle East’s wealthiest countries touting new investments totaling a claimed $3.6 trillion — though upon closer inspection many of the deals appear inflated or recycled.

title: Gulf States Embrace Trump’s New Vision of Middle East
content: At every stop on his just-ended tour, President Donald Trump’s words were music to the ears of his Saudi, Qatari and Emirati hosts.

title: Ex-US Envoy to Ukraine Says She Resigned to Protest Trump Policy
content: The former US ambassador to Ukraine said she resigned in protest over President Donald Trump’s handling of the conflict with Russia and that she could no longer stand by while he pressured the government in Kyiv.

title: When Your Favorite Restaurant Becomes a Statistic
content: Economic trends can be tracked on charts. But when they hit home, they are life-changing.

content: Nissan Motor Co. plans to close two factories in Japan, as well as locations in four other countries as part of its restructuring and cost-cutting process, the Yomiuri newspaper and other news outlets reported, citing unidentified sources.

content: Nvidia Corp. Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang expressed confidence in his company’s trade partners and said there’s no evidence of its prized semiconductors being diverted to the Chinese market.

title: Epic Asks Court to Force Apple to Approve Fortnite on US Store
content: Epic Games Inc. asked a court to force Apple Inc. to approve access to the hit game Fortnite in the US App Store, the latest tussle in a long-running feud over Apple’s control of game distribution revenue.

content: Tesla Inc. took a step to prevent future shareholder lawsuits like the one that blocked a record-setting pay package for Chief Executive Officer Elon Musk.

title: CoreWeave Jumps to Record After Nvidia Reports Larger Stake
content: CoreWeave Inc. shares surged 22% to a record high on Friday after Nvidia Corp. reported a larger-than-anticipated stake in the cloud-computing provider.

content: Coinbase Global Inc.’s rally has been unconquerable this week, as even a one-two punch of negative headlines did little to stop the crypto exchange operator’s climb ahead of its inclusion in the S&P 500 Index.

title: Charter and Cox Combine in $34.5 Billion Cable Deal
content: Charter Communications and Cox Communications, two of the largest US cable providers, agree to combine in a deal worth $34.5 billion. Bloomberg’s Michelle Davis explains why this deal has been years in the making, speaking with Caroline Hyde and Ed Ludlow on “Bloomberg Technology.” (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Prosus CEO Defends Offer for Just Eat Takeaway
content: Prosus CEO Fabricio Bloisi explains how the company is using M&A in its ambition to become the biggest tech lifestyle company outside the US and Asia. Bloisi joins Caroline Hyde and Ed Ludlow on “Bloomberg Technology.” (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Verizon Wins FCC Nod for Frontier Deal After Ditching DEI
content: Verizon Communications Inc. won Federal Communications Commission approval for its $9.6 billion acquisition of Frontier Communications Parent Inc. after agreeing to agency demands to pare back diversity initiatives in line with President Donald Trump’s policies.

title: Airbnb Aims to Boost Revenue with New Services, Ads
content: Airbnb CEO Brian Chesky discusses why the vacation rental company overhauled its app and is refocusing on events and services. Chesky outlines the revenue opportunities for Airbnb with Caroline Hyde and Ed Ludlow on “Bloomberg Technology.” (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Amazon Removed Backup Landing Sensors Before Drone Crashes
content: Retaining the technology could have prevented the aircraft from accidentally shutting off their propellers midflight and plummeting to the ground.

title: Microsoft Will Need to Take on OpenAI to Hit AI Goals
content: Bloomberg’s Austin Carr discusses his conversation with Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella and why the tech boss says AI will remake every business. Carr joins Caroline Hyde and Ed Ludlow on “Bloomberg Technology.” (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Coinbase Hack Could Have Wide-Ranging Impact
content: Crypto trading platform Coinbase said a hacker demanded $20 million to delete illegally obtained customer data. Bloomberg’s Margi Murphy explains how the hacker gained access to Coinbase's customer information and the potential cost of the incident. She speaks with Ed Ludlow on “Bloomberg Technology.” (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Globant Suffers Record Intraday Drop as Tariffs Dent Earnings
content: Software company Globant SA suffered a record intraday decline after blaming its disappointing first-quarter results on the ripple effects of US tariffs.

title: OpenAI to Help UAE Develop One of World’s Biggest Data Centers
content: OpenAI plans to help develop a massive new data center in the United Arab Emirates that may eventually be one of the largest in the world, a major bet on the Middle East and a significant expansion of the company’s global AI infrastructure ambitions.

title: Tech Investors Digest Trump’s Week in the Middle East
content: Ipek Ozkardeskaya, Swissquote Senior Analyst, discusses how markets are reacting to tech deals announced during President Trump’s visit to the Gulf. She joins Caroline Hyde and Ed Ludlow on “Bloomberg Technology.” (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Coinbase Hack Highlights How Greed Can Overwhelm Cyber Defenses
content: Following cybersecurity best practices doesn’t always protect against human greed.

title: Cinven Taps Goldman, UBS for €6 Billion Ufinet Sale
content: Private equity firm Cinven has selected Goldman Sachs Group Inc. and UBS Group AG to arrange a sale of telecom operator Ufinet Group, according to people familiar with the matter.

title: Trump’s Week in the Gulf, Airbnb's App Redesign | Bloomberg Technology
content: Bloomberg’s Caroline Hyde and Ed Ludlow discuss President Trump’s tech-focused trip to the Middle East. Plus, Airbnb CEO Brian Chesky explains the revenue opportunity the company sees in services as it launches a redesigned app. And Prosus CEO Fabricio Bloisi says partnerships and acquisitions are part of the company’s efforts to become the biggest tech lifestyle company outside the US or China. content: Brian Armstrong, chief executive officer of Coinbase Global Inc., speaks during a "Stand With Crypto" get out the vote rally at The Bourbon Room in Los Angeles, California, US, on Monday, March 4, 2024. California's Senate race is living up to its jungle primary nickname and turning out to be one of the most competitive in the nation, featuring crypto billionaire donors and a former star baseball player.

title: European Stocks Post Fifth Week of Gains as Trade Tensions Ease
content: European stocks wrapped up a fifth straight week of gains with investors focused on US trade negotiations, while the corporate earnings season has turned out better than expected.

title: OpenAI Takes on Google, Anthropic With New AI Agent for Coders
content: OpenAI is rolling out a new artificial intelligence agent for ChatGPT users that’s designed to help streamline software development as the company pushes into a crowded market of startups and large tech firms offering AI tools for coders.

title: Applied Materials Slides After Giving Disappointing Forecast
content: Applied Materials Inc. shares fell as much as 7.3% after the chip-equipment maker gave a lackluster forecast for the current period, highlighting the potential cost of the US trade dispute with China.

title: Premier League Sponsors Exit UK After Gaming Watchdog Probe
content: Six betting websites that sponsor UK Premier League football clubs have ceased their UK operations after an investigation by the country’s gambling regulator into their licensing partner.

title: Ratos Weighs IPO of Nordic Construction Unit Sentia
content: Swedish conglomerate Ratos AB is considering listing its construction arm Sentia, according to people familiar with the matter, marking another potential initial public offering for the Nordic region.

title: Nvidia Shares Roar Back as Clouds Hanging Over Chipmaker Fade
content: After several months in the wilderness, Nvidia Corp. shares have found their way again as doubts about Big Tech spending subside, trade tensions with China ease, and new chip buyers emerge.

title: Pinterest Is in Talks to Lease Offices at NYC’s 11 Madison Tower
content: Pinterest Inc. is in talks to take office space at Manhattan’s 11 Madison Ave.

title: Lidar Maker Hesai Is Said to Confidentially File for Hong Kong Listing
content: China’s Hesai Group, the world’s largest maker of lidar sensors used in driver assistance systems, has confidentially filed for a Hong Kong listing, according to people familiar with the matter.

title: TikTok Offers to Discuss Brazil Operations With Lula Government
content: Chinese social media platform TikTok is willing to talk about its Brazil operations with the South American country’s government, according to an official with knowledge of the matter, following a recent push for regulation by President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva and his wife.

title: US Loses Last Top Credit Rating With Downgrade From Moody’s
content: The US was stripped of its last top credit rating by Moody’s Ratings, reflecting deepening concern that ballooning debt and deficits will damage America’s standing as the preeminent destination for global capital and increase the government’s borrowing costs.

title: Bank of England Forecast Shake-Up Risks Sowing Market Confusion
content: Former Bank of England ratesetters are warning that a planned shake-up of the central bank’s forecast and communications strategy risks sowing confusion in financial markets and weakening debate among policymakers.

title: Indian Companies, Consumers Snub Pakistan and Its Allies
content: A growing number of Indian merchants, companies, and consumers are cutting business ties with Pakistan and some of its allies after a heightened conflict between the South Asian neighbors.

title: Grim Outlooks Take Centerstage as Tariffs Loom: Earnings Watch
content: One thing is clear as the first-quarter earnings season draws to a close: The uncertain outlook for the global economy is superseding better-than-feared results even as stocks rally on signs of easing trade tensions.

title: Chicago Taps EY to Close $1 Billion Gap as Trump Threatens Funds
content: Chicago is hiring Ernst & Young LLP to help the city slash costs and close budget gaps that are forecast to top $1 billion in each of the next two years.

title: Fed to Shrink Staff by About 10% Over Next Several Years
content: The Federal Reserve plans to shrink its system-wide workforce by about 10% over the next couple of years, mainly through attrition.

title: Russian Inflation Steadies as Key Rate Cut Expectations Build
content: Price growth in Russia halted its acceleration in April for the first time in six months, bolstering the case for kicking off long-awaited monetary easing amid signs of a sharp economic slowdown.

title: US Consumer Sentiment Nears Record Low on Inflation Concerns
content: US consumer sentiment unexpectedly fell to the second-lowest level on record and inflation expectations climbed to multi-decade highs amid growing concerns about tariffs.

title: ECB Will Include Trade Scenarios in June Projections, Lane Says
content: The European Central Bank will publish additional scenarios for the euro-zone economy alongside next month’s quarterly outlook in an attempt to capture the possible effects of the current trade turmoil, according to Chief Economist Philip Lane.

title: Bernanke Urges Fed to Adopt ‘Alternative’ Forecast Scenarios
content: Former Federal Reserve Chair Ben S. Bernanke urged the US central bank to provide the public a fuller explanation of its interest-rate decisions and a much richer examination of potential forecast scenarios.

title: Price Hikes Are Beginning to Threaten the American Consumer
content: For all the worry about tariffs causing pain for American consumers, shoppers have so far been mostly shielded from — or shrugged off — higher prices at the checkout aisle.

title: What a Weaker US Dollar Means for the Economy
content: American exporters would benefit from the currency’s drop, but consumers could feel a pinch.

title: US Housing Starts Increase on Pickup in Multifamily Construction
content: US housing starts increased in April as a pickup in multifamily home construction more than offset a decline in single-family dwellings caused by elevated inventory.

title: Romania Holds Interest Rates Before Tight Presidential Vote
content: Romania’s central bank kept borrowing costs unchanged just days before a presidential runoff that may determine prospects for tackling a budget crisis after months of political turmoil and a market selloff.

title: Trump Says US to Set Tariff Rates for Other Nations in Weeks
content: President Donald Trump said he would set tariff rates for US trading partners “over the next two to three weeks,” saying his administration lacks the capacity to negotiate deals with all of its trading partners.

title: Swiss Had Good Exchange With US on Currency, SNB Chief Says
content: Switzerland has had productive talks with the US on the central bank’s currency interventions, Swiss National Bank President Martin Schlegel said, rejecting the suggestion that the country manipulates the franc’s exchange rate.

title: EU Economy Chief Urges China Self-Restraint on Diverting Goods
content: The European Union’s economy chief urged China to avoid flooding the European market with its goods as it seeks to avoid US tariffs.

title: APEC Trade Ministers Agree Statement Without Mentioning Tariffs
content: Trade chiefs from some of the world’s biggest economies including the US and China agreed to focus on reforming global trade rules, after reaching an unexpected agreement by ignoring one of their biggest points of difference: tariffs.

title: Treasuries, US-Made Japanese Cars Seen as Leverage
content: Holding longer-term Treasuries and importing Japanese cars manufactured in the US are among the possible bargaining chips for Tokyo in its talks with Washington over President Donald Trump’s sweeping tariffs, according to the leader of a small but influential opposition party.

title: Irish Exports to US Quadrupled in March on Tariff Threat
content: The value of exports from Ireland to the US quadrupled in March from a year earlier, on medical and pharmaceutical goods, the statistics office said.

title: Singapore Firms Up Exports During Pause in Trump’s Steep Tariffs
content: Companies in Singapore are expediting exports to take advantage of a 90-day pause in hefty tariffs proposed by the Trump administration, a top official in the city-state said.

title: EU Exports to US Surged Ahead of Trump’s Tariff Announcement
content: The European Union’s exports to the US rocketed in the month before President Donald Trump unveiled his so-called “Liberation Day” trade war with the rest of the world.

title: Atlanta Fed’s Raphael Bostic on Monetary Policy During Extreme Uncertainty
content: How to keep the Fed's goals in balance with so much in flux.

title: Odd Lots: Bostic on Fed Policy in Uncertain Times (Podcast)

And beyond that, nobody knows what the ultimate state of tariffs will be, or if they’ll ever settle into a predictable rate. So how do you conduct monetary policy in this environment? title: Fed’s Bostic Says He Sees One Rate Cut This Year, No Recession
content: Federal Reserve Bank of Atlanta President Raphael Bostic said he expects the US economy to slow this year but not fall into recession, and reiterated that he sees one interest-rate cut in 2025.

title: Chile Trade Chief Still Hopeful US Will Cut Tariffs Back to Zero
content: Chile is still expecting the US to drop all tariffs back to zero as set out in the two countries’ free-trade agreement, a senior official said, an appeal from a nation that remains vulnerable to any international downturn caused by higher duties.

title: What’s the De Minimis Tariff Loophole That Trump Closed?
content: A Latin term that used to be little-known outside the world of customs brokers has become the stuff of headlines this year. That’s thanks to a decision by US President Donald Trump to close a tariff loophole for “de minimis” merchandise from mainland China and Hong Kong from May 2.

title: Czech Rate Setters Backed ‘Moderately Restrictive’ Stance in May
content: Czech central bankers agreed monetary policy needed to remain “moderately restrictive” to address persistent domestic price pressures and uncertain global economic outlook, minutes from the May 7 meeting showed.

title: Nissan Plans to Close Plants in Japan, Mexico, Yomiuri Says
content: Nissan Motor Co. plans to close two factories in Japan, as well as locations in four other countries as part of its restructuring and cost-cutting process, the Yomiuri newspaper and other news outlets reported, citing unidentified sources.

title: Tesla Moves to Stymie Shareholder Lawsuits After Musk Pay Saga
content: Tesla Inc. took a step to prevent future shareholder lawsuits like the one that blocked a record-setting pay package for Chief Executive Officer Elon Musk.

title: FAA Seeks Cap on Newark Airport Flights After Airline Talks
content: US aviation safety regulators proposed temporarily limiting flights at Newark airport to no more than 28 arrivals per hour after a pair of radar and radio outages fueled major disruptions in recent weeks.

title: FDA Clears First Blood Test to Diagnose Alzheimer’s Disease
content: US regulators have approved the first blood test to help diagnose Alzheimer’s disease, potentially making it easier to find and treat patients with the mind-robbing disease that affects nearly 7 million Americans.

title: Progressive NYC Private School Fighting Foreclosure Files Bankruptcy
content: Manhattan Country School, an Upper West Side private school promoting social justice and a progressive academic curriculum that is battling possible foreclosure, has filed bankruptcy.

title: Driverless Trucking Firm Aurora Puts Human Back in Driver’s Seat
content: Driverless vehicle developer Aurora Innovation Inc. is putting a human back in front of the wheel of big rigs operating in Texas, reversing course less than three weeks after the company began commercial autonomous service there.

title: Weight-Loss Drug Craze Boosts $80 Billion Lilly Endowment to Largest in US
content: The endowment started by the founding family of drugmaker Eli Lilly saw its assets surge to $80 billion at the end of 2024, passing Bill Gates’ foundation for the top spot.

title: Grim Outlooks Take Centerstage as Tariffs Loom: Earnings Watch
content: One thing is clear as the first-quarter earnings season draws to a close: The uncertain outlook for the global economy is superseding better-than-feared results even as stocks rally on signs of easing trade tensions.

title: Banco do Brasil Rout Sheds $3.7 Billion as Guidance Pulled
content: Banco do Brasil SA shed 21 billion reais ($3.7 billion) in market value Friday in its worst session in five years after the Brazilian lender put parts of its 2025 forecast under review and reported rising delinquency rates on agricultural loans that took a bite out of first-quarter profit.

title: Walmart Names Company Veteran to Oversee International Growth
content: Walmart Inc. selected a company veteran to fill a newly created role that aims to spark international growth, as the world’s largest retailer looks to bolster its overseas operations.

title: Chobani Enters Ready-to-Eat Meal Market With Daily Harvest Deal
content: Chobani LLC bought ready-to-eat meal maker Daily Harvest Inc. for an undisclosed amount as it continues its expansion beyond yogurt into more areas of the grocery store.

title: Wells Fargo, BofA Lead $650 Million Refinancing for Boston Tower

title: Trump Hands Putin Win With Retreat From Ukraine Talks
content:
Eleven days ago, European leaders took heart when President Donald Trump called for a 30-day ceasefire in Ukraine and threatened new sanctions on Russia. A telephone call with Vladimir Putin on Monday revealed those hopes were misplaced. After two hours talking with Putin, Trump said on social media that Ukraine and Russia would "immediately start negotiations" toward a ceasefire — but possibly without the US. There was no sanctions threat, no demand for a time-line, and no pressure on the Russian leader. Trump followed the Putin call by reaching out to European leaders, but already several governments were airing their disappointment. 

After months of failing to move Putin closer to peace, they fear Trump is pulling back from his efforts to end the war, leaving Ukraine and its allies on their own. Our EMEA News Director Rosalind Mathieson joined Stephen Carroll and Caroline Hepker on Bloomberg radio to discuss.  (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Thoma Bravo Nears Deal for Insurance Tech Firm Itel

title: Pony AI Earnings Put Investors on Alert for Robotaxi Expansion
content: Pony AI Inc.’s report on its first full quarter as a publicly traded company will have investors and analysts homing in on how a new generation of robotaxis could put the firm on a path to profitability.

title: Google Decided Against Offering Publishers Options in AI Search
content: Company drew “hard red line” around requiring web publishers to participate in AI search, document says

title: US Battery Startup ONE Inks Production Deal With Turkey’s Pomega
content: US battery startup Our Next Energy Inc. will outsource some production of its battery cells to Turkey’s Pomega Enerji Depolama Teknolojileri AS.

title: Lyft Revives Pooled Rides at Airports in Push for Cheaper Trips
content: Lyft Inc. is bringing back cheaper shared trips at airports, reversing a decision made two years ago to discontinue the ride option as it seeks to compete with rival Uber Technologies Inc. in courting inflation-weary consumers.

title: Apple Must Resolve ‘Fortnite’ Return or Answer for It to Judge
content: Apple Inc. will have to answer to a judge for refusing to restore Fortnite to its US App Store if it hasn’t resolved its standoff with Epic Games Inc. by May 27.

title: Rio Tinto Strikes Another Lithium Deal With Codelco Venture
content: Rio Tinto Group agreed to invest in a Chilean lithium project controlled by Codelco as the world’s second-biggest miner continues its expansion into the battery metal.

title: Microsoft Is Bringing Elon Musk’s AI Models to Its Cloud
content: Microsoft Corp. is adding models from Elon Musk’s xAI to its artificial intelligence marketplace.

title: Nvidia Opens AI Ecosystem to Rival Chipmakers in Global Push
content: Nvidia Corp. Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang outlined plans to let customers deploy rival chips in data centers built around its technology, a move that acknowledges the growth of in-house semiconductor development by major clients such as Microsoft Corp. and Amazon.com Inc.

title: Aramco, Saudi Telecom Join Sequoia in Backing US-Based Startup Graphiant
content: The venture capital arms of Saudi Arabia’s oil and telecom giants have invested in US tech startup Graphiant Inc. as the kingdom seeks to drive innovation and develop its digital economy.

title: Salesforce Cuts Slack Price for US Government, Following Google
content: Salesforce Inc. will offer its Slack application to the federal government at a discounted rate, the latest software company to cut prices as the Trump administration aims to slash technology costs.

title: China Says US Chip Controls Are Undermining Trade Consensus
content: China sees the US as undermining the consensus reached between the two countries during trade talks in Geneva, a spokesperson for the Asian nation’s commerce ministry says.

title: Chipmaker AMD Agrees to Sell AI Server Assets to Sanmina
content: Sanmina Corp. is buying Advanced Micro Devices Inc.’s AI server assembly plants in a deal worth as much as $3 billion.

title: Apple Partner Hon Hai Injects $1.5 Billion Into India Unit
content: Hon Hai Precision Industry Co., the main manufacturer of Apple Inc.’s iPhones, will inject $1.5 billion into its India unit as production shifts away from China.

title: Nvidia, UAE’s MGX Plan to Build Europe’s Largest Data Center
content: Nvidia Corp. and Abu Dhabi investment vehicle MGX are partnering with French firms to establish what they say will be Europe’s largest artificial intelligence data center campus, advancing French and Emirati ambitions in the field.

title: Apple’s $100 Billion-a-Year App Store Will Never Be the Same
content: Apple’s $100 billion-a-year App Store business will never be the same again after getting upended by lawsuits. Also: Inside Apple’s artificial intelligence crisis and what comes next; new details on iOS 19, iPadOS 19 and visionOS 3; and CarPlay Ultra is finally ready — if you can afford it.

title: UK Legal Aid Hack Includes ‘Significant Amount’ of Personal Data
content: Hackers have stolen a “significant amount of personal data” from people who received legal aid across England and Wales, the UK’s Ministry of Justice said.

title: Saudi Arabia, UAE See AI Buildup as Key to Post-Oil Power
content: Welcome to Tech In Depth, our daily newsletter with reporting and analysis about the business of tech from Bloomberg’s journalists around the world. title: Telefonica’s Latin America Fire-Sale Sends Chile Unit to New Low

title: Huawei Unveils in-House Operating System to Replace Windows

title: Anthropic Is Trying to Win the AI Race Without Losing Its Soul

title: Vodacom Eyes Africa Network Sharing as Payout Beats Forecast

content: Australia’s central bank cut its key interest rate for a second time this year, highlighting mounting trade-related uncertainty and sending the currency and government bond yields tumbling.

title: Britain’s EU Reset Turns Out to Be Just the Start of Talks
