They all spoke at the Atlanta Fed's "Financial Intermediation in Transition" conference. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Japan’s Farm Minister Quits Over Rice Gaffe in Blow to Ishiba
content: Japan’s farm minister quit Wednesday after saying he’s never needed to buy rice, a comment that fueled criticism of Prime Minister Shigeru Ishiba’s minority government and its handling of rising food prices ahead of an election.

title: Pakistan Names First Field Marshal in 60 Years After India Clash
content: Pakistan promoted its army chief to field marshal for the first time in over sixty years, citing the country’s ‘success’ in this month’s military confrontation with India.

title: French Prosecutors Claim Najib Had Role in 2002 Submarine Deal Bribes
content: Allegations against former Malaysian prime minister are in 2024 court document. Prosecutors haven’t recommended that Najib stands trial.

title: Chinese Authorities Question Metals Bosses in Smuggling Probe
content: Chinese authorities have questioned the heads of some of the country’s leading metals merchants and producers as part of an intensifying effort to crack down on critical-minerals smuggling, according to people familiar with the situation.

title: Trump’s Genocide Claim Rakes Up South Africa’s Apartheid Past
content: The US president’s offer of refugee status for Afrikaners comes as his administration slashes spending that was helping Black South Africans.

title: Historic Fall in UK Migration Can’t Come Fast Enough for Starmer
content: Figures due on Thursday are likely to show Keir Starmer presiding over the biggest ever drop in net migration to the UK. For the prime minister, however, the hard part will be getting any credit from voters.

title: EU Sanctions Ships That Moved LNG From Russia’s Yamal Plant
content: The European Union imposed sanctions on three vessels that helped move gas cargoes from Russia’s Yamal LNG project, further squeezing Moscow’s energy revenues.

title: US Deports Migrants to War-Torn South Sudan, Court Records Say
content: A federal judge in Boston has ordered the Trump administration to “maintain custody” of a group of migrant men who may have been deported to South Sudan on Tuesday.

title: G-7 Finance Ministers Aim to Avoid Public Spats With US Despite Trade Turmoil
content: Finance ministers who’ve gathered in Canada for a Group of Seven meeting this week face a difficult task — trying to find common ground on trade issues while avoiding public conflict with US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent.

title: China Threatens Enforcers of US’s Huawei Curbs With Legal Action
content: China said it could take legal action against anyone enforcing US restrictions on using Huawei Technologies Co.’s AI chips, escalating a dispute that’s upset a tentative truce on tariffs.

title: Trump Loses Patience With SALT Demand as Tax Bill Faces Snag
content: President Donald Trump is growing frustrated with demands to significantly boost the cap on the state and local tax deduction, according to a senior administration official, signaling a deadlock as Republicans aim to quickly pass a giant tax-cut bill.

title: FAA Cuts Newark Flights After Air Traffic Control Issues
content: US aviation safety regulators will allow fewer flights at Newark airport after technology outages and a staffing crunch fueled a surge in delays and cancellations in recent weeks.

title: US, Philippine Coast Guards Join Navy Drills Amid China Tensions
content: The US and the Philippines held a new round of joint sails within Manila’s exclusive economic zone, with their coast guards participating for the first time, amid continuing tensions in the disputed South China Sea.

title: Chicago Suburb Plans to Seize Pope Leo’s Childhood Home
content: A Chicago-area town plans to seize control of Pope Leo XIV’s childhood home, just days after the current owner put the property up for auction.

title: Reeves to Meet Bessent as Questions Linger Over UK-US Deal
content: UK Chancellor of the Exchequer Rachel Reeves will hold talks with US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent this week, as the two countries continue to finalize the details of an agreement to cut tariffs imposed by President Donald Trump’s administration.

title: Bloody Murders in Quiet Neighborhood Shatter Mexico City’s Calm
content: In the vast swaths of Mexico controlled by drug cartels, public executions and mass graves have long been the norm. Mexico City has largely been a haven from the goriest headlines.

title: Trump Says Golden Dome Will Be Operational in Three Years
content: President Donald Trump vowed that a “Golden Dome” missile-defense shield would be “fully operational” by the end of his term, and offer the US protection from an array of threats — even though some of the technology remains unproven.

title: Mexico City Mayor’s Aides Shot Dead by Attackers on Motorbikes
content: Two senior aides to Mexico City Mayor Clara Brugada were shot dead Tuesday in the highest-profile political violence to strike the Latin American metropolis since cartel gunmen ambushed the capital’s former police chief five years ago.

title: South Africa’s Budget Gets Third Reboot With Credibility on Line
content: South African Finance Minister Enoch Godongwana’s third attempt to deliver a budget represents his sternest test yet.

title: US Clears Way for Tariffs on $13 Billion of Solar Imports
content: US duties on solar equipment from four Southeast Asian countries are set to take effect following a government agency’s conclusion the imports harm domestic manufacturers.

title: UK Sanctions British Accountant for Alleged Russia Ship Deals
content: The UK sanctioned an English accountant for allegedly helping Russia expand the fleet of tankers it uses to covertly ship crude around the globe.

title: ‘Original Sin’ Lays Out How Biden’s Decline Was Hidden by Family, Staff
content: This is Washington Edition, the newsletter about money, power and politics in the nation’s capital. Today, Bloomberg Businessweek national correspondent Joshua Green looks at the revelations in a new book about how former President Joe Biden’s family and staff hid his decline while in office. Sign up here and follow us at @bpolitics. Email our editors here.

title: Sanctions Risk Pushing Russia Away From Talks, Rubio Says
content: President Donald Trump thinks Russia will likely walk away from Ukraine peace talks if the US threatens more sanctions, according to his top diplomat, supporting the White House’s decision not to pressure Moscow despite its resistance to a ceasefire.

title: Trump Says Golden Dome System Will Be Operational in Three Years
content: President Donald Trump vowed that a “Golden Dome” missile-defense shield should be “fully operational” by the end of his term, saying it would be able to protect the US from threats including ballistic missiles, hypersonics and advanced cruise missiles.

title: Venezuela Frees American as Chevron Waiver Is Set to Be Extended
content: Venezuela released an American citizen on the same day the US was set to give Chevron Corp. another 60-day waiver to operate in the country, part of a push by President Nicolas Maduro’s government and some voices in the Trump administration to improve ties.

title: Trump Promised Record Deportations. How’s That Going?
content: President Donald Trump has vowed to carry out the largest deportation campaign in US history, a promise that mirrors one he made but failed to fulfill during his first term. This time, Trump has shown greater determination.

title: Dutch Government Needs to Spend Up to €19 Billion More to Meet NATO Target
content: The Netherlands estimates it will need to boost defense spending by as much as €19 billion ($21.4 billion) a year to meet the expected new target for the North Atlantic Treaty Organization.

title: Hegseth Starts Fresh Probe Into ‘Disastrous’ Afghanistan Pullout
content: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth announced a new probe into the 2021 Afghanistan withdrawal, vowing accountability for what he called the Biden administration’s “disastrous and embarrassing” handling of the events that led to the deaths of 13 US troops.

title: European Officials Step Up Pressure on Israel Over Gaza War
content: European and UK officials ratcheted up pressure on Israel over its latest offensive in Gaza, expanding the international outcry over the humanitarian crisis caused by the conflict.

title: EU Removes All Remaining Economic Sanctions Against Syria
content: The European Union has lifted all remaining economic sanctions against Syria, the bloc’s top diplomat Kaja Kallas told reporters after foreign ministers gathered in Brussels on Tuesday.

title: Bloomberg Daybreak: Europe 05/21/2025
content:
Bloomberg Daybreak Europe is your essential morning viewing to stay ahead. Live from London, we set the agenda for your day, catching you up with overnight markets news from the US and Asia. And we'll tell you what matters for investors in Europe, giving you insight before trading begins.

Today's Guests: Janet Mui, RBC Brewin Dolphin Head of Market Analysis (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Musk and Afrikaners Cloud the Trump-Ramaphosa Meeting Agenda
content: President Donald Trump's offer of refugee status to White Afrikaners has the potential to become a flashpoint as South African President Cyril Ramaphosa meets Trump in Washington on Wednesday. Also on the agenda: Ramaphosa's government plans to offer Elon Musk a workaround of local Black-ownership laws for his Starlink internet service to operate in the country, aiming to ease tensions with both the billionaire and Trump. Bloomberg's Anthony Sguazzin reports. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Westpac Plans to Eliminate More Than 1,500 Jobs, AFR Reports
content: Westpac Banking Corp. is planning to cut more than 1,500 jobs in the bank’s biggest redundancy in a decade as it strives to meet ambitious cost reduction targets, the Australian Financial Review reported, citing unidentified people.

title: New Fortress Energy Disqualified From Puerto Rico Power Auction
content: New Fortress Energy has been disqualified from an auction held by the Puerto Rican government to secure temporary power generation, the latest setback for billionaire Wes Edens’ troubled company.

title: Real Problem Is Medicaid Cuts: Rep. Pallone on Tax Bill
content: Rep. Frank Pallone (D) New Jersey discusses the tax bill and states the focus on SALT is "misplaced." He goes on to talk about how the tax cuts in the proposed legislation will benefit large corporations with cuts to Medicaid paying for them, what he can still do to prevent cuts to Medicaid, and shares his thoughts on the DOJ charging New Jersey Representative LaMonica McIver with assault after a confrontation outside an ICE detention facility. Rep. Pallone speaks with Kailey Leinz and Joe Mathieu on the late edition of Bloomberg's "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Kori Schake on Trump Retreats From Ukraine Peace Talks
content: Kori Schake, Senior Fellow & Director of Foreign and Defense Policy Studies at the American Enterprise Institute, shares her thoughts on talks between President Trump & President Putin and states President Putin is setting the cadence of Ukraine peace talks. She also discusses  how additional sanctions will not apply added pressure on Russia, what needs to happen to help support Ukraine, and her thoughts on Trump's announcement of a 'golden dome' missile shield. Kori Schake speaks with Kailey Leinz and Joe Mathieu on the late edition of Bloomberg's "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Apple Prepares to Open AI Models to Third-Party App Developers
content: Good morning. Apple is said to open AI models to third-party developers. Humans can’t keep up with developments in artificial intelligence. And Art Basel announces a fifth location. Listen to the day’s top stories.

title: Take-Two, QXO Launch $2 Billion Wave of Share Sales After Hours
content: A trio of companies kicked off a surge of large share sales after the close of US trading on Tuesday, in deals that could raise at least $2 billion in aggregate.

title: ICYMI: Jennifer Grancio on Volatility and Trade War

title: Marks & Spencer Says Cyberattack to Cost £300 Million
content: Marks & Spencer Group Plc is facing a £300 million ($403 million) hit to operating profit this fiscal year from a cyberattack that’s still disrupting the company’s sales and operations.

title: Nvidia CEO Urges US to Ease AI Curbs After ‘Failure’ With China
content: Nvidia Corp. chief Jensen Huang blasted the “failure” of US restrictions intended to help contain China’s technological ascent, calling on the White House to lower barriers to AI chip sales before American firms cede that market to up-and-coming rivals such as Huawei Technologies Co.

title: UAE Releases Falcon Arabic AI Model To Outcompete Mideast Rivals
content: A research arm of the Abu Dhabi government has released a powerful new Arabic-language artificial intelligence model in a bid to preserve its technological lead over rivals in the Middle East.

title: Accenture to Promote 50,000 Staff After Six-Month Delay
content: Accenture Plc will promote almost 50,000 people worldwide in June as the company tries to boost morale after a six-month delay to weather a slump in demand for consulting services.

title: Theta Capital Secures $175 Million for Crypto Fund Investments
content: Crypto investment firm Theta Capital Management closed a raise of more than $175 million for a fund-of-funds that will back institutional investors in early-stage blockchain startups.

title: Swedish Startup Einride Shuffles Management Ahead of IPO Push
content: Einride AB is shaking up its top management as the Swedish driverless truck startup lays the groundwork for a possible initial public offering.

title: SoftBank Taps Mizuho, SMBC, JPMorgan to Lead $15 Billion Loan
content: SoftBank Group Corp.’s investments in AI will be financed through a loan in which Mizuho Bank Ltd., Sumitomo Mitsui Banking Corp. and JPMorgan Chase & Co. serve as lead underwriters — a sign of the Japanese tech investor’s ability to secure financing for its outsized ambitions.

title: China AI Rally Laggard Baidu Faces Low Bar for Earnings Boost
content: The current earnings season has largely been a letdown for China’s big tech stocks, lowering the hurdle for Baidu Inc. to impress investors seeking a fresh angle on the artificial intelligence theme.

title: Inside the First Stargate AI Data Center
content: OpenAI, Oracle and SoftBank hope that the site in Texas is the first of many across the US.

title: China Threatens Enforcers of US’s Huawei Curbs With Legal Action
content: China said it could take legal action against anyone enforcing US restrictions on using Huawei Technologies Co.’s AI chips, escalating a dispute that’s upset a tentative truce on tariffs.

title: ‘Fortnite’ Returns to Apple App Store After Four-Year Battle
content: Epic Games Inc.’s hit game Fortnite has returned to Apple Inc.’s App Store in the US after more than four years, following a fierce legal battle between the two companies.

title: AI PCs Still Year or Two From Fulfilling Promise, Asus CEO Says
content: The new crop of artificial intelligence-powered PCs will take until 2026 or later to drive the market forward, according to Asustek Computer Inc. co-Chief Executive Officer Samson Hu.

title: Kalshi Pulls Announcement of xAI Tie-Up Hours After Touting Deal
content: Kalshi Inc. withdrew announcements about a collaboration with Elon Musk’s artificial-intelligence firm xAI just hours after a top executive at the prediction markets firm touted the deal.

title: Wolfspeed Put Options Surge Before Report on Bankruptcy Plans
content: Traders ramped up bearish bets Tuesday on Wolfspeed Inc., before the Wall Street Journal reported after regular market hours that the ailing chip component maker is preparing to file for bankruptcy protection within weeks.

title: Match Group Acquires ‘Her’ Dating App for Queer Women
content: Match Group has added ‘Her,’ a dating app for queer women, to its portfolio, Match Chief Executive Officer Spencer Rascoff said in a post on Linkedin.

title: Bloomberg Retracts Story on Kalshi After Firm Rescinds Statement
content: Bloomberg retracted a story published earlier Tuesday saying that Kalshi would partner with artificial-intelligence firm xAI after Kalshi rescinded its statement announcing the product integration deal. The company said details of the release, which stated that the effort would provide users with tailored information, had not been mutually confirmed between the two firms.

title: Thames Tops List of Firms Facing Criminal Probes Over Pollution
content: Thames Water tops a list of water companies under criminal investigation for pollution by the UK government, a move that could complicate efforts to turn around the beleaguered British utility.

title: What Trump’s ‘Golden Dome’ Can Learn From Israeli Air Defenses
content: An exclusive look at what Israel’s upgraded air defense system can (and can’t) do holds lessons for the US as it pushes for a missile shield.

title: WhatsApp Had No Plans to Vie With Facebook, Co-Founder Says
content: WhatsApp co-founder Brian Acton said that his messaging company had no plans to build social networking features to compete with Facebook before he sold the company to Mark Zuckerberg, a claim that bolsters Meta’s defense as it faces federal antitrust allegations.

title: Dell Tech World, Musk Commits to Staying at Tesla | Bloomberg Technology
content: Bloomberg’s Ed Ludlow, live from Dell Technologies World, discusses developments in AI infrastructure. Plus, Elon Musk says he is committed to running Tesla for the next five years. And Cohere CEO Aidan Gomez says the competitor to OpenAI has doubled its revenue since the start of the year. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Take-Two Dips as Video-Game Maker Preps $1 Billion Stock Sale
content: Take-Two Interactive Software Inc. shares fell as much as 5% in extended trading after the company announced plans to sell $1 billion of new stock to investors.

title: Amazon Gives Refunds for Years-Old Returns
content: Amazon.com Inc. customers are suddenly getting refunds for products they purchased and returned as far back as 2018, along with apologies from the online retailer after it discovered “unresolved” issues.

title: Uber Squeezes More From Aurora Stake With $1.2 Billion Bond Sale
content: Uber Technologies Inc.’s $1.2 billion exchangeable bond deal, linked to its shares in a self-driving truck firm, shows why the unusual financial maneuver can be more attractive than a typical stake sale, according to observers.

title: Xreal and Google Debut Aura AR Glasses to Rival Meta’s Orion Plan
content: Alphabet Inc.’s Google has entered the glasses race by partnering with Xreal Inc. on the first spectacles to run an augmented-reality version of its operating system.

title: Jimmy Fallon Offered $1 Million Air-Taxi Bet by Short Seller
content: Air taxi company Archer Aviation Inc. has been targeted by short sellers before, but the latest attack has an unusual twist: A proposed $1 million “friendly wager” with the TV show host Jimmy Fallon.

title: Alphabet’s Google Bringing AI Mode to Search for US
content: Alphabet Inc.’s Google will offer “AI mode” in search to all US users, part of an effort to bring products to market faster and keep pace with new rivals in the artificial intelligence age.

title: Microsoft-Backed Builder.ai Set for Bankruptcy After Cash Seized
content: Builder.ai, the British artificial intelligence startup backed by Microsoft Corp. and the Qatar Investment Authority, is filing for bankruptcy after the chief executive officer said a major creditor had seized most of its cash.

title: Google Bringing Products to Market Faster: Alphabet CEO
content: Alphabet Inc.’s Chief Executive Officer Sundar Pichai said Google will bring products to market faster to keep pace with new rivals in the artificial intelligence age. “We want to get our best models into your hands,” Pichai said Tuesday at the company’s developer conference in Mountain View, California, “so we are shipping faster than ever.”

title: Musk Commits to Tesla CEO Role and Plans Political Pullback
content: Elon Musk said he’s committed to still leading Tesla Inc. five years from now and expects to pare back his political spending, assuaging some investors’ concerns about the future of his most valuable company.

title: DoorDash Ends AI Voice-Ordering Product for Restaurants
content: DoorDash Inc. ended a pilot of its voice-ordering product for restaurant clients, a year after it poached talent from an artificial intelligence startup to bolster the product.

title: Traders Pare Bets on BOE Cuts, Pound Climbs After UK Inflation
content: Traders pared bets on further interest-rate cuts from the Bank of England, sending the pound to a three-year high versus the dollar, after data showed UK inflation rose more than expected in April.

title: UK Inflation Surge Prompts Traders to Rein In Bets on BOE Cuts
content: UK inflation jumped more than forecast to its highest rate in over a year as households were hit by a raft of price increases, prompting investors to pare bets on rate cuts from the Bank of England.

content: Japan’s farm minister quit Wednesday after saying he’s never needed to buy rice, a comment that fueled criticism of Prime Minister Shigeru Ishiba’s minority government and its handling of rising food prices ahead of an election.

title: Chinese Authorities Question Metals Bosses in Smuggling Probe
content: Chinese authorities have questioned the heads of some of the country’s leading metals merchants and producers as part of an intensifying effort to crack down on critical-minerals smuggling, according to people familiar with the situation.

title: Bank Indonesia Poised to Resume Rate Cuts as Growth Falters
content: Indonesia’s central bank is expected to resume lowering interest rates as the US-China trade truce and the rupiah’s ensuing rebound open up a window of opportunity for policymakers to spur economic growth.

title: G-7 Countries Discuss Tariffs on Low-Value Chinese Products
content: Canadian Finance Minister Francois-Philippe Champagne said Group of Seven countries have started discussing tariffs on oversupplied, low-value Chinese products.

title: US Sets the Stage for Duties on Battery Materials From China
content: The US Commerce Department set the stage for anti-subsidy duties on imports of key battery components from China, after concluding materials had been unfairly subsidized.

title: G-7 Finance Ministers Aim to Avoid Public Spats With US Despite Trade Turmoil
content: Finance ministers who’ve gathered in Canada for a Group of Seven meeting this week face a difficult task — trying to find common ground on trade issues while avoiding public conflict with US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent.

title: China-US Trade Soars as Exporters Race to Hit Trade Truce Window
content: A temporary trade truce between the world’s two largest economies has sparked a knee-jerk bounce across China’s ports and factory floors.

title: China Ran Record Budget Deficit With Spending Blitz Amid Tariffs
content: China’s fiscal stimulus pushed its four-month budget deficit to a record high, as the government ramped up support for the economy during an escalation in its trade conflict with the US.

title: Japan’s Exports Slow as US Tariffs Bite, Risking Recession
content: Growth in Japan’s exports slowed as the US ramped up its tariff measures, highlighting the risks the country faces after its economy already contracted before the levies began hitting in earnest.

title: South Korean Early May Exports Fall as Shipments to US Slump
content: South Korea’s early trade data showed exports falling again this month especially to the US as negotiations between Seoul and Washington continue over tariffs on shipments from the Asian nation.

title: Fed’s Daly, Hammack Stress Wait-And-See Policy Approach
content: Two Federal Reserve officials underscored the US central bank can be patient and assess incoming data before adjusting policy as the economy navigates heightened uncertainty.

title: Reeves to Meet Bessent as Questions Linger Over UK-US Deal
content: UK Chancellor of the Exchequer Rachel Reeves will hold talks with US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent this week, as the two countries continue to finalize the details of an agreement to cut tariffs imposed by President Donald Trump’s administration.

title: South Africa’s Budget Gets Third Reboot With Credibility on Line
content: South African Finance Minister Enoch Godongwana’s third attempt to deliver a budget represents his sternest test yet.

title: Sanctions Risk Pushing Russia Away From Talks, Rubio Says
content: President Donald Trump thinks Russia will likely walk away from Ukraine peace talks if the US threatens more sanctions, according to his top diplomat, supporting the White House’s decision not to pressure Moscow despite its resistance to a ceasefire.

title: Fed’s Musalem Says Tariffs Will Likely Weigh on Growth, Jobs
content: Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis President Alberto Musalem said tariffs will likely weigh on the US economy and weaken the labor market.

title: Australia's Rare Feat on Inflation, Jobs May Hold Lessons for Other Economies
content: Through the post-Covid cost-of-living crisis, Australia’s central bank took a gentler approach than global peers to reining in inflation, managing to keep the economy close to full employment throughout — a rare feat that’s sparked debate about its viability as a model to tackle future crises.

title: Brazil Finance Chief Pivots as Lula Lingers in the Limelight
content: Not long ago, Brazil’s finance chief was a rising star in the government of President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva. Now, factors beyond Fernando Haddad’s control have put his political ambitions on hold.

title: Influx of Foreign-Born Workers Drove 2024 US Labor Force Growth
content: Foreign-born workers drove US labor force growth for another year in 2024, providing a last boost for the job market before President Donald Trump’s immigration crackdown was set in motion.

title: New Zealand Set to Deliver Tight Budget as Economic Outlook Dims
content: New Zealand Finance Minister Nicola Willis will keep a tight rein on spending in this week’s budget as uncertainty about global growth holds back a domestic recovery and restrains government revenue.

title: Romania to Weigh Rate Cuts When Politics and Markets Calm
content: Romania will weigh further interest-rate cuts only after a return to market and political stability, the central bank chief said, as the election of a centrist candidate to the presidency on Sunday spurred preparations to form a new government.

title: ECB’s Wunsch Says Economy May Need Some Support From Rates
content: European Central Bank Governing Council member Pierre Wunsch said the euro-zone economy may need interest rates at “mildly supportive” levels to ensure inflation doesn’t fall below target after a series of shocks.

title: Nigeria Holds Key Rate Again Amid ‘Heightened Uncertainty’
content: The Central Bank of Nigeria left interest rates unchanged as it awaits more data to determine the inflation outlook and for the turbulence spawned by US President Donald Trump’s trade war to settle.

title: Canada Inflation Slows on Carbon Tax End, But Core Rises
content: Canadian inflation eased to its slowest pace since September on the elimination of the consumer carbon tax and lower oil prices, but core measures accelerated.

title: White House’s Miran Dismisses Inflation Risk From Tariff Hikes
content: The White House’s chief economist dismissed the idea that tariff increases will have a lasting impact on US inflation, and cited the potential for interest rates to get back down to pre-Covid levels.

title: Singapore Central Bank Chief Says US Dollar Assets Irreplaceable
content: Dollar-based assets have “enduring advantages” and remain virtually irreplaceable in the global financial system despite the US losing its top triple-A credit rating, according to Singapore’s central bank chief.

title: A Spendthrift Saudi Arabia Can’t Finance the World Anymore
content: Hello from Doha. I’m Erik Schatzker, editorial director of Bloomberg New Economy, bringing you a special edition of the newsletter from this year’s Qatar Economic Forum. title: Toyota Goes All-Hybrid With Its Best-Selling US Vehicle
content: Toyota Motor Corp. is scrapping the gas-powered version of its best-selling vehicle in the US as the Japanese carmaker doubles down on its push into hybrids.

title: SSE Cuts Spending Plan by £3 Billion Amid Slowing Growth
content: SSE Plc cut its five-year spending plan by £3 billion ($4 billion) as projects slow amid planning delays.

title: Critical Minerals at Higher Risk of Painful Disruption, Says IEA
content: Critical minerals are at increasing risk of “painful disruption” due to their higher concentration in a handful of countries and the spread of export restrictions, according to a report from the International Energy Agency.

title: SocGen CEO Krupa Says He Has Completed ‘Bulk’ of Unit Sales
content: Societe Generale SA is largely done selling units, Chief Executive Officer Slawomir Krupa told shareholders, as the French lender is setting its sights on growth again.

title: Global Investment, Crypto and AI Top Agenda at Qatar Economic Forum
Julius Baer Faces $156 Million Loan Loss Charge
content: Julius Baer Group Ltd. said it’s booking another large loss from property developments it helped finance, just as the Swiss wealth manager is emerging from a crisis triggered by its exposure to Rene Benko’s Signa real estate empire.

title: Rio Tinto Defends Pilbara After Forrest Voices ‘Wasteland’ Fears
content: A Rio Tinto Group executive has defended the future of Australia’s iron ore hub, after mining billionaire Andrew Forrest delivered a downbeat message on its prospects unless it gets more green investment.

title: Chinese Authorities Question Metals Bosses in Smuggling Probe
content: Chinese authorities have questioned the heads of some of the country’s leading metals merchants and producers as part of an intensifying effort to crack down on critical-minerals smuggling, according to people familiar with the situation.

title: Global LNG Suppliers Wager That China’s Demand Slump Is Fleeting
content: Global gas giants are betting the current lull in Chinese demand is temporary, and that the country will underpin their multibillion-dollar investments for years to come.

title: China-US Trade Soars as Exporters Race to Hit Trade Truce Window
content: A temporary trade truce between the world’s two largest economies has sparked a knee-jerk bounce across China’s ports and factory floors.

title: FAA Cuts Newark Flights After Air Traffic Control Issues
content: US aviation safety regulators will allow fewer flights at Newark airport after technology outages and a staffing crunch fueled a surge in delays and cancellations in recent weeks.

title: First Alzheimer’s Blood Test Available in US in June
content: The first blood test to help diagnose Alzheimer’s disease will be available from late June in the US following regulatory clearance for its use last week, according to the Japanese company behind the innovation.

title: Chicago Suburb Plans to Seize Pope Leo’s Childhood Home
content: A Chicago-area town plans to seize control of Pope Leo XIV’s childhood home, just days after the current owner put the property up for auction.

title: Former Citi Traders Drop Hong Kong Lawsuit on Cost Concerns
content: Two former Citigroup Inc. traders in Hong Kong abandoned their employment lawsuits after weighing costs and difficulties of taking it to a higher court, people familiar with the matter said.

title: Westpac Plans to Eliminate More Than 1,500 Jobs, AFR Reports
content: Westpac Banking Corp. is planning to cut more than 1,500 jobs in the bank’s biggest redundancy in a decade as it strives to meet ambitious cost reduction targets, the Australian Financial Review reported, citing unidentified people.

title: New Fortress Energy Disqualified From Puerto Rico Power Auction
content: New Fortress Energy has been disqualified from an auction held by the Puerto Rican government to secure temporary power generation, the latest setback for billionaire Wes Edens’ troubled company.

title: Jefferies Fraud Suit Against Ex-Fund Manager Tossed by Judge
content: A Jefferies Financial Group Inc. hedge fund’s lawsuit claiming it was defrauded by a former portfolio manager who invested $100 million of its money in a Ponzi-like scheme was dismissed by a federal judge.

title: Blackstone, CVC Split From Group Set to Invest in NFL Teams
content: Blackstone Inc. and CVC Capital Partners are no longer part of a private equity group that had won preliminary approval to invest in NFL teams, according to people familiar with the matter.

title: Nu COO Lahrech Steps Down, Adding to Turnover Atop Fintech
content: Nu Holdings Ltd. said Chief Operating Officer Youssef Lahrech is stepping down after more than five years, adding to a string of management changes in the upper ranks of Latin America’s standout financial technology firm.

title: Roche Needs More US Data on Key Cancer Drug, FDA Advisers Say
content: A group of advisers to the Food and Drug Administration said Roche Holding AG needs to study its blood cancer treatment in more American patients before its use can be expanded.

title: GPIF to Invest $500 Million in a Fund Managed by Thoma Bravo
content: Japan’s Government Pension Investment Fund said it’s investing $500 million in a fund managed by US private equity firm Thoma Bravo, as part of its effort to boost alternative assets.

title: PNC Agrees to Acquire Alternatives Fundraiser Aqueduct Capital
content: PNC Financial Services Group said its bank will acquire Aqueduct Capital Group, a move that expands PNC’s services for alternative asset managers.

title: Kraft Heinz Mulls Deals After Berkshire Hathaway Exits Board
content: Kraft Heinz Co. said it is evaluating potential “strategic transactions” in an effort to boost its stock price, and announced that Berkshire Hathaway Inc. is giving up its seats on the board.

title: What Trump’s ‘Golden Dome’ Can Learn From Israeli Air Defenses
content: An exclusive look at what Israel’s upgraded air defense system can (and can’t) do holds lessons for the US as it pushes for a missile shield.

title: Congo Gambles on Cobalt as US-China Metals Fight Heats Up
content: In the middle of a global trade war, Congo is trying to woo Trump’s White House without risking critical investment from Beijing.

title: Toll Maintains Home Sales Forecast as Luxury Demand Holds Up
content: Luxury builder Toll Brothers Inc. reaffirmed expectations for home sales in its full fiscal year, citing resilience among its affluent buyers.

title: Victoria’s Secret Adopts Poison Pill to Thwart Investor BBRC (3)
content: Victoria’s Secret & Co. announced a shareholder rights plan after an investor began acquiring a substantial amount of stock in the lingerie retailer.

title: NFL Owners Approve 49ers, Chargers’ Sale of Minority Stakes
content: NFL owners approved the sale of a 6.2% stake in the San Francisco 49ers to three investor groups at an $8.5 billion valuation, the highest ever for a sports team.

title: Mary Barra de GM apostó por los autos eléctricos. Ahora, con Trump, debe probar su éxito
content: El fabricante de autos estadounidense se enfrenta a aranceles, a un presidente amante del petróleo y a Elon Musk en la Casa Blanca

title: US Will No Longer Approve Covid Boosters for Healthy Kids, Adults Without New Trials
content: US regulators will no longer approve Covid booster shots for healthy adults and children without new studies, adding a costly requirement for drugmakers, though they will still be available for millions of high-risk Americans.

title: BOJ Shouldn’t Act on Surging Super-Long Yields, Noguchi Says
content: The Bank of Japan doesn’t need to step into the bond market to take action against a recent spike in super-long yields, as it’s hard to say there’s anything abnormal about the moves, according to a member of the central bank’s board.

title: Insight with Haslinda Amin 5/22/2025
content: Insight with Haslinda Amin, a daily news program featuring in-depth, high-profile interviews and analysis to give viewers the complete picture on the stories that matter. The show features prominent leaders spanning the worlds of business, finance, politics and culture. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Singapore DPM Says Holding Geopolitical Neutrality Not Possible
content: Singapore’s Deputy Prime Minister Gan Kim Yong said neutrality is not possible, highlighting the rising challenges for the city-state that has long sought to tread a diplomatic tightrope amid US-China trade tensions.

title: Gold Rally Could Be Past Its Peak by Year End: StanChart
content: Standard Chartered Precious Metal Analyst Suki Cooper discusses the factors that led to the gold rally and its relationship to the inflow of ETFs. "If we start to see tax stimulus measures in the US and we start to see some of the uncertainty around geopolitical risks starting to unwind, we could actually see gold starting to stabilize the elevated levels," Cooper tells Bloomberg Television. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Diversification Trade May Only Just Be Starting: Citi
content: There are signs that the diversification of equity flows away from the US may only be in its infancy, according to Beata Manthey, strategist at Citigroup. Manthey, who called the European stocks rally in October, says the latest inflows into Europe have offset only 10% of the previous outflows, which occurred when investors took flight after Russia invaded Ukraine. She speaks on Bloomberg Television.

title: Trump Clashes with Ramaphosa; QEF Underway in Doha | Horizons Middle East & Africa 05/22/2025
content: US President Donald Trump's meeting with South Africa's Cyril Ramaphosa was seen as a chance to mend relations, but the exchange did not go as planned. Also on the show: two staff members of the Israeli embassy in Washington have been shot and killed; JPMorgan's Jamie Dimon says he's holding off on evaluating the impact of Trump's recent trip to the Middle East; 25 startups to watch in Africa; Citigroup says it remains optimistic about the prospects for countries across the Middle East. Guests include: Ozan Tarman, Deutsche Bank, Vice Chair Global Macro; Omeed Malik, 1789 Capital, Founder & President; Hendrik du Toit, Ninety One, CEO; Jamie Dimon, JPMorgan, Chairman & CEO; Chilufya Mutale-Mwila, Eshandi Financial Services, Co-Founder & Chief Visionary Officer; Owusu Akoto, Freezelink, Founder & CEO; Carmen Haddad, Citi Private Bank, Vice Chair. (Source: Bloomberg)

content: Omeed Malik, Founder & President 1789 Capital says their firm is "providing another option for investors" who agree with their views on ESG and DEI, which he believes "destroys shareholder value". Speaking in an interview with Bloomberg's Joumanna Bercetche at the Qatar Economic Forum in Doha off the back of a panel discussion yesterday alongside Donald Trump Junior, Malik reiterated that their main goal is to "help the president's agenda in the private sector." (Source: Bloomberg)

China Shows Off Its Tech Advances Amid Huawei Tensions
content: Some of China's tech advances are on display at Macau's Beyond Expo, including humanoid robots. The show unfolds against a backdrop of simmering tensions between the US and China over access to semiconductors. The Chinese government has accused the Trump administration of undermining recent trade talks in Geneva after the US issued warnings against the use of Huawei's AI chips. Meanwhile, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has urged the US to ease restrictions on exporting AI technology to China. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Stocks Decline, Treasuries Steady After Selloff: Markets Wrap
content: Asian stocks fell as risk mood soured and Treasuries steadied after a selloff sparked by concerns about a proposed tax-cut bill that threatened to enlarge the US deficit.

content: Speaking at the Qatar Economic Forum in Doha, Ozan Tarman, Deutsche Bank Vice Chair of Global Macro tells Bloomberg's Joumanna Bercetche he remains optimistic about Europe's fiscal potential despite external factors such Germany's Chancellor, Merz initially struggling to form a government coupled with the US markets making a comeback, potentially dampening European optimism. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Southern Greek Islands Hit by 6.1-Magnitude Earthquake
content: ATHENS, Greece (AP) — An undersea 6.1-magnitude earthquake scale struck off the Greek island of Crete early Thursday and was felt across the Aegean Sea, but there were no immediate reports of injuries or significant damage.

title: Goldman Combines APAC Investment Banking Business
content: Goldman Sachs Group Inc. is combining its investment banking businesses across Asia Pacific into one entity in a move to help bolster advisory and capital markets execution.

title: Trump Tax Bill Holdouts Lured With SALT Hike, Medicaid Cuts

content: Finance ministers from the Group of Seven industrialized nations have agreed to continue backing Ukraine in its defense against Russia’s invasion, German Finance Minister Lars Klingbeil said on the sidelines of a G-7 meeting in Canada.

content: Two members of the Israeli embassy’s staff were shot dead outside the Capital Jewish Museum in Washington on Wednesday night, Homeland Security Secretary Kristi Noem said.

title: Northvolt to Stop Production in June With No Buyers In Sight
content: Northvolt AB will stop making cells at its last remaining factory in northern Sweden at the end of June, marking the demise of what was once Europe’s best hope of a homegrown battery champion.

title: BOE Wants Banks to Hold More Capital Against Weak Foreign Debt
content: The Bank of England has proposed raising capital charges for banks’ holdings of lower-rated overseas debt, as it pushes to close a regulatory loophole that allows UK lenders to underestimate potential losses from securities backed by weaker sovereigns.

title: EU Set to Delay Implementation of New Trading Rule for Banks
content: The European Commission is set to recommend a fresh delay to the adoption of new trading book rules that govern the trading activities of banks, according to people familiar with the matter.

title: Tom Cruise Really Did Get a US Aircraft Carrier for This Mission
content:
For fans of Tom Cruise’s Mission: Impossible series, the Pentagon can answer the incredulous question at the climax of its latest trailer: “You gave him an aircraft carrier?”
Yes, the US Navy and Air Force Special Operations decided to accept the mission: help Cruise’s secret agent Ethan Hunt save the world. Or, at least make a movie about it.
For Paramount Global’s The Final Reckoning, released Friday in the US, Cruise and the crew spent three days in the Adriatic Sea filming aboard the USS George H.W. Bush, a nuclear powered Nimitz-class carrier commissioned in 2009. 
It’s the latest cinematic incarnation of Cruise’s career-long affinity for the US military and its aircraft (as well as doing his own stunts). It’s also an example of the Pentagon’s willingness to showcase its hardware and martial might through a classic piece of American soft power, the Hollywood blockbuster. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Vietnam Takes Steps to Block Telegram Over Illegal Content
content: Vietnam authorities have instructed local telecoms and internet service providers to block the Telegram messaging app in the country for allegedly failing to prevent illegal content and anti-government activities being carried out by its users.

title: CoreWeave Bulls Face Off Against Short Sellers as Shares Spike
content: CoreWeave Inc. shares have been on a tear as investors snap up the stock despite widespread concerns about elevated debt levels, the rate of cash-burn and the long-term demand for the cloud-computing services it provides.

title: Surge of Successful Tech IPOs Gives Hope to Silicon Valley Startups
content: Welcome to Tech In Depth, our daily newsletter with reporting and analysis about the business of tech from Bloomberg’s journalists around the world. Today, Katie Roof and Kate Clark report on the light at the end of the tunnel for Silicon Valley tech startups after a few recent successful debuts in the public markets.

title: Tiger-Backed Robinhood Rival Launches DIY Indexing With a Twist
content: What if you wanted to build an index betting on companies traveling to Mars, firms with the most social-media followers, or those with CEOs over six feet tall?

title: South Africa Pushes Policy Directive to Smooth Way for Starlink
content: South Africa’s government plans to push ahead with a policy directive that provides a workaround to Black-ownership requirements in the telecommunications industry, aiming to encourage Elon Musk’s Starlink and other satellite services to operate in the country.

title: A $20,000 ‘Home Companion’ Robot From China to Debut This Year
content: China’s UBTech Robotics Corp. is planning to unveil a $20,000 humanoid robot that can serve as a household companion this year, seeking to expand beyond factories.

title: OnlyFans Owner Exploring Sale at $8 Billion Valuation
content: OnlyFans Ltd. owner Leonid Radvinsky is exploring a sale of the adult-content social network that would value it at about $8 billion, according to a person familiar with the matter.

title: EngineAI Targets $1 Billion Valuation as Chinese Robots Heat Up
content: EngineAI is targeting a round of financing later this year at a $1 billion valuation, seeking capital to join a global race to develop humanoid robots.

title: China Asks Dutch to Ease Chips Export Curbs, Minister Says
content: China has asked the Netherlands to relax export restrictions related to semiconductors, Dutch Foreign Affairs Minister Caspar Veldkamp said following a meeting with officials in Beijing.

title: How Britain’s Stats Geeks Lost Track of the Economy
content: Just before midday on May 9, employees of the Office for National Statistics were summoned to an urgent call.

title: Trump Forces Switzerland to Question Its Love for Farmers
content: Switzerland’s bid for a US trade deal risks sparking a showdown with one political force at least as feisty as President Donald Trump: its own farmers.

title: Japan Signals Intent to Reach US Tariff Deal by G-7 in June
content: Japan’s chief trade negotiator Ryosei Akazawa indicated his aim to resolve tariff talks in time for a June meeting between US President Donald Trump and Japan’s Prime Minister Shigeru Ishiba following Trump’s surprise pivot to allow a partnership between two of the countries’ steelmakers.

title: Meloni Wins Hope of Moody’s Italy Upgrade From Brink of Junk
content: Italy’s credit score is skewed toward a potential upgrade at Moody’s Ratings, which has just joined rivals in rewarding Premier Giorgia Meloni’s push for fiscal restraint.

title: Trump Threatens EU, Smartphones as Tariff Rhetoric Escalates
content: President Donald Trump dug in on his threat to impose a 50% tariff on the European Union and said a potential 25% charge on smartphones would apply to all foreign-made devices, in the latest escalation of a trade war that is rattling markets and confusing businesses.

title: Paraguay Holds Key Rate at 6% Amid Steady Inflation Expectations
content: Paraguay’s central bank kept its benchmark interest rate steady at 6%, citing stable long-term inflation expectations congruent with its target.

title: Chile Finance Chief Wants to Unlock Billions in New Investments
content: Chile’s government is readying legislation to unlock billions of dollars of investments by speeding up the approval process, following years of complaints over excessive red tape, Finance Minister Mario Marcel said.

title: Bessent Says Trump Paused Sovereign Wealth Fund to Focus on Debt
content: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said the Trump administration paused plans to create a sovereign wealth fund as the president prioritizes paying down the national debt.

title: Bessent Sees Easing Capital Rule on Treasuries This Summer
content: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said that US regulators this summer may ease a rule that’s served as a constraint on banks’ trading in the $29 trillion Treasuries market.

title: Ghana Holds Key Rate as Cedi Rally Seen Taming Inflation
content: Ghana’s central bank kept its key interest rate on hold to maintain downward pressure on inflation, which is expected to get a boost from the West African nation’s world-beating currency.

title: Bessent Sees ‘Several Large’ Trade Deals in Next Few Weeks
content: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said there could be “several large” trade deals announced in the next couple of weeks, adding that he expects Trump administration officials will meet with their Chinese counterparts again in-person to negotiate those tariffs.

title: European Officials Urge ‘Calm’ Facing Trump 50% Tariff Threat
content: European officials sought to portray a unified calm after US President Donald Trump threatened to impose a 50% tariff on the bloc’s imports, a potential escalation that sent stocks tumbling on both sides of the Atlantic on concerns a trade war will disrupt the world’s largest commercial and investment relationship.

title: Euro-Zone’s Top Economies May Now Have Inflation at or Under 2%
content: Inflation in all of the euro zone’s four biggest economies is at or below the European Central Bank’s 2% target, according to economists.

title: Tracking Every Trump Tariff and Its Economic Effect
content: For the full experience visit: Tracking Every Trump Tariff and Its Economic Effect

title: US New-Home Sales Jump to Highest Since 2022 as Prices Fall
content: US new-home sales rose unexpectedly in April to the highest level since February 2022, likely helped by builder incentives aimed at alleviating affordability challenges.

title: Fed Must Contain Long-Term Inflation Expectations, Musalem Says
content: Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis President Alberto Musalem said officials are focused on keeping long-run inflation expectations stable as businesses and consumers anticipate prices to rise in the near term.

title: Economists Say Canada Recession Has Already Begun as Trade War Rages On
content: Canada’s economy is likely in the early stages of a recession, according to forecasters, as unemployment rises and exports fall because of a trade war with the US.

title: RBI to Make a Record Transfer of $32 Billion to Government
content: India’s central bank will give a record dividend to the government, shoring up finances to bolster growth in Asia’s third largest economy.

title: US Inflation, Recession Forecasts Ease on Trade Truce With China
content: Latest Bloomberg survey still suggests economy is shifting into a lower gear

title: Ghana’s Debt Burden Falls to IMF Threshold Ahead of 2028 Target
content: Ghana’s debt burden fell to a threshold required by the International Monetary Fund’s $3 billion program three years ahead of schedule, as the the new government curbed borrowing.

title: European Bonds Rally as Trump Tariff Threat Fuels Rate-Cut Bets
content: European bonds rallied after US President Donald Trump threatened to apply levies of 50% on the region starting June 1, fueling bets policymakers will have to lower interest rates further to support the economy.

title: ECB’s Lane Says US Price Jump Wouldn’t Necessarily Reach Europe
content: Faster US inflation triggered by President Donald Trump’s tariffs wouldn’t necessarily spill over into the euro zone, according to European Central Bank Chief Economist Philip Lane.

title: ECB’s Kazimir to Receive Verdict in Bribery Case Next Week
content: The bribery trial of European Central Bank Governing Council member Peter Kazimir is expected to deliver a verdict next week.

title: EU Agrees to Reinstate Trade Quotas on Ukraine as War Drags on
content: The European Union has agreed to reinstate quotas on imports of several agricultural goods from Ukraine, adding to the challenges faced by its war-hit economy.

title: Sickly Animals Remind the World of Fragile Food Trade
content: Lethargic chickens with swollen heads or cattle with maggots burrowing into their flesh — these are effects of diseases that have been disrupting global trade.

title: The $3 Trillion in Capital Needed to Bring Back US Factory Jobs
content: I’m Mark Niquette, a US economy reporter in Columbus, Ohio. Today we’re looking at bringing back manufacturing jobs to the US. Send us feedback and tips to ecodaily@bloomberg.net. And if you aren’t yet signed up to receive this newsletter, you can do so here.

title: Euro-Zone Wage Growth Sinks, Supporting Further ECB Easing
content: A key measure of euro-area pay growth plunged, supporting the European Central Bank’s claim that inflation will soon hit the 2% target and backing calls to lower interest rates further.

title: US Aid Retreat Opens Door for Bigger Islamic Development Bank Role in Africa
content: The Islamic world’s premier lending institution said it’s prepared to step up support for some of its neediest members, as the US and others slash aid programs for Africa and beyond.

title: Bulgaria Is on Track to Win EU Approval to Join the Euro Next Year
content: Bulgaria is close to clearing a major hurdle toward euro adoption, putting the Black Sea nation on course to join the currency area next year.

title: Zambia Halts Rate Hikes as Corn Boom Seen Cooling Inflation
content: Zambia’s central bank held its key interest rate as it expects the disinflation process to continue.

title: Andrew Left’s Lawyer Says Case Doesn’t Fit Trump Priorities
content: Short seller Andrew Left is making a new push to sway the US Justice Department to drop fraud charges filed against him last year, hiring a former federal prosecutor to make fresh arguments directly to the Trump administration.

title: Cenovus Executive Downplays Chance of MEG Bid Amid Organic Growth Push
content: A Cenovus Energy Inc. executive downplayed the chance the oil sands producer would offer to buy MEG Energy Corp., saying the company is more focused on expanding existing assets than making acquisitions.

title: Cobalto del Congo: el nuevo campo de batalla en la lucha entre China y EE.UU.
content: En medio de una guerra comercial global, el Congo intenta cortejar a la Casa Blanca de Trump sin arriesgar inversiones cruciales de Pekín.

title: Carney’s Energy Chief Pushes Oil Sands to Build Carbon-Capture Systems
content: Canada’s new energy minister said it’s critical to build carbon-capture systems for the oil sands and identified crude and natural gas exports as a major priority for Prime Minister Mark Carney’s government.

title: McDonald’s to Close Beverage-Focused Concept Stores, Test New Drinks
content: McDonald’s Corp. plans to close standalone CosMc’s stores, winding down its experiment with the beverage-focused concept.

title: Harvard Wins Temporary Block of Trump’s Foreign Student Ban
content: Harvard University won a temporary court order blocking the Trump administration from enforcing a ban on international students at the school, giving it a win in a high-stakes legal fight with broad implications for higher education in the US.

title: Rio Tinto Board Looks for a New CEO Who Knows Mining Better
content: When Jakob Stausholm took the top job at Rio Tinto Group, his task was to repair the reputation of a company that had just blasted through a 46,000-year-old sacred Aboriginal site and bungled its response. Now the world’s second-largest miner has decided it needs a boss that can lead it into the future.

title: Lauder, L’Oreal Suffer as China Duty-Free Spend Falls
content: Unable to travel overseas during the Covid-19 pandemic, Chinese consumers sparked a shopping boom in the southernmost province of Hainan, lured by the tropical island’s plethora of duty-free shopping malls.

title: What Happens When an Italian Racing Team Meets the Indy 500
content: Prema sets sights on making history this weekend after the Italian team took pole position.

title: Volvo Car CEO Rejects Worries Over R&D Shifting to China
content: Upcoming job cuts at Volvo Car AB are not a sign that the carmaker’s Chinese owner is taking more control over product development, Chief Executive Officer Hakan Samuelsson said.

title: Italy Plans to Stick With Its Tough Terms on UniCredit’s BPM Bid
content: Italy is set to keep the strict conditions it imposed on UniCredit SpA to take over rival lender Banco BPM SpA, even if the bidder starts a legal battle to ease those terms.

title: Travel Anxiety Swells as Airports Face Busiest Memorial Day Ever
content: Flyers heading out for the Memorial Day holiday in the US are bracing for stress as record numbers of travelers place fresh strain on an outmoded and undermanned air traffic system.

title: Visa, Mastercard Fees Hit by New Round of EU Antitrust Scrutiny
content: Visa Inc. and Mastercard Inc. fees are under fresh scrutiny from European Union antitrust enforcers, less than a decade after a series of probes ended with hefty fines and an agreement to cut some of their controversial levies.

title: Musk Backer to Join New Ownership at Reading Football Club
content: Aliya Capital Partners, a Miami-based investment firm, is joining the ownership group that bought out 154-year-old Reading Football Club from Chinese businessman Dai Yongge.

title: Nigerian Manufacturers ‘Harassed’ Over FX Contracts, Lobby Says
content: Nigerian manufacturers say they’re being “harassed” by lenders over outstanding forward foreign exchange contracts with the central bank.

title: UniCredit Escalates BPM Fight With Italy by Going to Court
content: UniCredit SpA is escalating the standoff with the Italian government over its bid for rival Banco BPM SpA as the firm plans to take the matter to court.

title: Hensoldt Said to Weigh Sale of South African Optronics Unit
content: German radar maker Hensoldt AG is exploring options for its South African optronics business, including a potential sale, according to people familiar with the matter.

title: EU Set to Delay Implementation of Bank Trading Rule
content: The European Commission is set to recommend a fresh delay to the adoption of new trading book rules that govern the trading activities of banks, according to people familiar with the matter.

title: US Firms Face Biggest Hit on Trump Tariffs, HSBC Survey Says
content: US businesses are the most worried about the impact of President Donald Trump’s shifting tariff policies on their revenues, with more than half projecting a hit of at least 25% to their revenue, according to a survey by HSBC Holdings Plc.

title: US Approves GSK Lung Disease Drug, Fueling Sanofi Rivalry
content: GSK Plc won US approval for its drug to treat a deadly lung disease, ramping up competition with rival Sanofi.

title: House Republican bill boosts maximum child tax credit to $2,500
content: The House Republican multi-trillion-dollar tax package includes a bigger child tax credit. If enacted, here's who could benefit from the changes.

title: The U.S. credit downgrade is not the problem. Our reckless spending is
content: Habitual deficit financing — the very disease Alexander Hamilton warned against — has become business as usual.

title: Google Wallet users in the US get another upgrade this week
content: The digital wallet now supports over 5,000 banks and credit unions, making it the most popular mobile payment service.

title: European Stocks Rally as Trump Extends Deadline for EU Tariffs
content: European stocks gained after President Donald Trump said he would extend the deadline for the region to face higher tariffs, as investors weigh the prospects for a longer-term trade deal.

content: Chinese stocks are expected to benefit from further gains in the yuan, which has been showing resilience amid the country’s trade spat with the US, according to strategists at Goldman Sachs Group Inc.

content: Federal Reserve Bank of Minneapolis President Neel Kashkari says "there's no question the shock of tariffs is stagflationary," adding that the magnitude depends on the rate of the trade levies and time period involved. title: Bloomberg Daybreak: Europe 05/26/2025

Bloomberg Daybreak Europe is your essential morning viewing to stay ahead. Live from London, we set the agenda for your day, catching you up with overnight markets news from the US and Asia. And we'll tell you what matters for investors in Europe, giving you insight before trading begins.

On today's show, US President Trump says he will pause his 50% tariffs on the European Union until July 9th after speaking with Commission President Ursula von der Leyen. The move allows for more time to negotiate a trade deal between Washington and Brussels.

Meanwhile, President Trump says he is considering new sanctions against Russia, after Moscow launched a second night of deadly missile and drone strikes across much of Ukraine. Trump's comments come as he appears to grow frustrated with Russian President Vladimir Putin, with ceasefire efforts losing momentum. (Source: Bloomberg)

content: Good morning. Japan is keen on reaching a US tariff deal by the G-7 summit next month. Nvidia plans a cheaper Blackwell AI chip for China, Reuters says. And Japan’s travel industry wobbles as a viral manga prophecy sparks fears of an earthquake. Listen to the day’s top stories.

title: Portugal Continues Easing Limits on Power Imports From Spain
content: Portugal will continue to ease limits on the electricity interconnection capacity for imports from Spain after trading between the two countries was halted last month due to a blackout.

content: Source: Bloomberg, 4:06

title: In Qatar, CFOs Talk Regional Risks and Opportunities
content: Executives focus on rising costs, consumer spending and the dollar. Plus, Qatar Airways’ Duncan Naysmith talks about the airline’s latest plane purchases and the benefits of lower oil prices.

content: Source: Bloomberg, 4:14

title: GMO Group Scraps $2 Billion Share Sale Plan of Internet Unit
content: The Japanese conglomerate GMO Internet Group Inc. canceled a planned share offering of one of its listed arms after the stock surged in recent months, pushing up the unit’s valuation.

title: OpenAI to Set Up Shop in South Korea to Spur Further Growth
content: OpenAI has established a legal entity in South Korea, seeking to propel further adoption of its artificial intelligence technologies.

title: China’s Meituan, Xiaomi See Long-Term Expansion Efforts in Spotlight
content: Meituan and Xiaomi Corp.’s long-term ambitions and investment plans will dominate this week’s earnings releases, continuing to shape sentiment for China’s tech sector.

title: Nvidia Plans Cheaper Blackwell AI Chip for China, Reuters Says
content: Nvidia Corp. plans to launch a new artificial intelligence chip for China with its latest Blackwell architecture at a lower price than the H20 model, Reuters reported on Saturday, citing people familiar with the matter who weren’t identified.

title: Japan’s Stocks Solid as Trump Rhetoric Cools; Nippon Steel Gains
content: Japanese shares gained for a second day on hopes of softer trade policies from US President Donald Trump, after he extended the deadline for higher duties on European Union goods and backed a deal between Nippon Steel Corp. and US Steel Corp.

title: African Central Banks to Join EM Peers Easing Rates
content: Central banks in key African economies are getting set to line up with other emerging-markets in coming weeks and cut interest rates where inflation pressures are seen abating, or stay on guard where the path is less clear.

title: Shipping Bottlenecks in Europe Send a Warning to US, Asia
content: Port congestion is worsening at key gateways in northern Europe and other hubs, according to a new report which suggests trade wars could spread maritime disruptions to Asia and the US and push up shipping rates.

title: Japan to Sell Rice Stockpiles With Aim to Halve Soaring Prices
content: Japan will sell additional stockpiles of rice at a fixed price with an aim to halve soaring costs, newly-appointed agriculture minister Shinjiro Koizumi said as the country heads toward a summer election.

title: Israel Set to Hold Rates as Inflation Spikes, Gaza War Escalates
content: Israel’s central bank is set to keep interest rates on hold for the 11th time in a row, amid increased military operations in Gaza and an uptick in inflation.

title: Japan Touts Ships Expertise, LNG Project as Tariff Talks Key
content: Japan may offer financial and technical contributions ranging from investment in an Alaskan LNG pipeline project to shipbuilding expertise as it seeks to smooth the path toward a tariff deal with the US by mid-June.

title: Asean Must Keep Joining Global Supply Chains, Thailand Says
content: Southeast Asian nations should look at ways to further integrate their supply chains regionally and around the world to reap the benefits of economies of scale and gain access to larger markets, Thailand’s foreign minister said.

title: Kashkari Says ‘Not Sure’ on Interest Rate Moves by September
content: Federal Reserve Bank of Minneapolis President Neel Kashkari said major shifts in US trade and immigration policy are creating uncertainty for Fed officials to move on interest rates before September, as the Trump administration continues tariff talks with numerous governments.

title: Malaysia’s Anwar Writes Trump Seeking Summit With Southeast Asia
content: Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim said he personally wrote to Donald Trump seeking to organize a meeting with Southeast Asian nations amid concerns over the US president’s proposed tariff hikes.

title: Trump Extends Deadline for 50% Tariffs on EU Goods to July 9
content: President Donald Trump said he would extend the deadline for the European Union to face 50% tariffs until July 9 after a phone call with Commission President Ursula von der Leyen.

title: Chinese EV Stocks Tumble After BYD Slashes Prices Up to 35%
content: BYD Co. led Chinese electric vehicle stocks lower in Hong Kong on Monday, as investors digested the auto giant’s sweeping price cuts of as much as 34% late last week.

title: Shipping Bottlenecks in Europe Send a Warning to US, Asia
content: Port congestion is worsening at key gateways in northern Europe and other hubs, according to a new report which suggests trade wars could spread maritime disruptions to Asia and the US and push up shipping rates.

title: Healthscope Receives Funding From CBA to Keep Hospitals Running
content: Australia’s biggest bank has stepped in to provide funding to hospital operator Healthscope Ltd. as the government said it wouldn’t provide a bailout.

title: VietJet, Airbus Sign New Order for 20 A330neo Widebody Aircraft
content: VietJet Aviation JSC has doubled its order for Airbus SE widebody aircraft, ordering 20 more A330neos, to bolster its expansion plans over the next decade.

title: Stirling Square Sells French Perfume Bottle Maker Verescence
content: Stirling Square Capital Partners has sold Verescence, a French glass packaging maker for the perfumery and cosmetics industry, to Movendo Capital and asset manager Draycott.

title: China’s Ambassador Warns Australia Over Port of Darwin Lease
content: China’s ambassador to Australia has warned Canberra to be careful in its handling of the lease of a strategically important port, after Prime Minister Anthony Albanese pledged to bring it back into his country’s hands.

title: Racer Kyle Larson Crashes at Coca-Cola 600 and Indy 500
content: CONCORD, N.C. (AP) — Kyle Larson’s day went from bad to worse Sunday night at the Charlotte Motor Speedway, leaving the talented young driver unsure if he will attempt to run “The Double” again.

title: Chinese Steel Exports to Drop as Barriers Mount, Says Goldman
content: The blowout in Chinese steel exports has likely peaked, as trade barriers mount and domestic production falls, according to Goldman Sachs Group Inc.

title: Trump Backing for a Nippon Steel Deal Leaves Big Questions
content: After more than 17 months of lobbying and close-fought negotiations to secure control of United States Steel Corp., Japan’s Nippon Steel Corp. appeared on Friday to have received a presidential blessing.

title: Country Garden Gets More Time for $14.1 Billion Restructuring
content: Chinese developer Country Garden Holdings Co. was given more time by a Hong Kong court to work on its $14.1 billion offshore restructuring after amassing additional creditor support for the plan.

title: Taiwan to Hold Referendum on Restarting Closed Nuclear Reactor
content: Taiwan will hold a national referendum on restarting a nuclear reactor that it shut down just last week, potentially opening up a pathway to reverse the government’s anti-nuclear policy.

title: WiseTech Buys E2Open for $2.1 Billion in Its Biggest Deal
content: Australian shipping software company WiseTech Global Ltd. made its biggest ever acquisition, agreeing to buy E2open Parent Holdings Inc. in a deal that values the US firm at $2.1 billion.

title: US Wins First World Hockey Title Since 1933 With Victory Over Switzerland
content: STOCKHOLM (AP) — Tage Thompson scored at 2:02 of overtime to the give the United States a 1-0 victory over Switzerland on Sunday for its second world hockey championship and first since 1933.

title: US’s Cerberus Floated Bid For Chinese-Owned Port of Darwin
content: US private equity firm Cerberus Capital Management LP expressed interest in purchasing the lease for Australia’s strategically important Port of Darwin from Landbridge Group, despite the Chinese firm insisting it has no interest in selling the asset.

title: Zimbabwe Sees $2.6 Billion Bridge Finance Secured in 2026
content: Zimbabwe expects $2.6 billion in bridge finance — needed to repay debt owed to international financial institutions and regain access to capital markets — to be in place by the first quarter of next year, Finance Minister Mthuli Ncube said.

title: What's Zuckerberg Getting From His Shift Toward Trump?
content: Mark Zuckerberg, the chief executive officer of Meta Platforms Inc., seems to have taken actions to make the company more Trump-friendly. Since November, Zuckerberg has already had a string of postelection get-togethers with Donald Trump and made multiple trips to Mar-a-Lago in Florida. Meta also donated $1 million to the inauguration, and Zuckerberg co-hosted a black-tie reception that evening in Trump’s honor. Bloomberg's Charlie Wells discuss this and what this means for Zuckerberg and Meta. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Treasuries Rally With Japan Bonds as MOF News Boosts Sentiment

title: Lagarde Touts Euro’s Global Role During Speech in Berlin
content: European Central Bank President Christine Lagarde said there is an opportunity to strengthen the euro’s international role and allow the currency bloc to enjoy more of the privileges so far reserved for the US. “Europe has many of the key ingredients for success, but they need to be brought together,” Lagarde said May 26 during a speech in Berlin. content:
