content: Thailand’s second-richest person Charoen Sirivadhanabhakdi transferred ownership of two major listed companies to his five children as the octogenarian businessman pulls back from day-to-day management of his beer-to-property conglomerate.

title: Hedge Funds Bet on Korean Won to Mirror Taiwan Dollar Surge
content: Hedge funds are ramping up bets in the options market that the South Korean won will mirror the Taiwan dollar’s recent rally against the greenback.

title: HK's Gaw Capital New Fund to Invest in China, Japan
content: Real estate-focused private equity firm Gaw Capital is looking use its new fund that could be worth $2 billion to invest in China, Japan, Australia and Vietnam. Gaw Capital Managing Principal and Global Head of Capital Markets, Christina Gaw, discusses her outlook for commercial property in Hong Kong and mainland China with David Ingles and Yvonne Man on "Bloomberg: The China Show."  (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Macron Courts Southeast Asia Nations Trapped by US-China Dispute
content: French President Emmanuel Macron is spearheading the latest effort by European leaders to woo Southeast Asian nations worried about becoming collateral damage in the US trade war and security disputes between Washington and Beijing.

title: US’s Cerberus Floated Bid For Chinese-Owned Port of Darwin
content: US private equity firm Cerberus Capital Management LP expressed interest in purchasing the lease for Australia’s strategically important Port of Darwin from Landbridge Group, despite the Chinese firm insisting it has no interest in selling the asset.

title: Japan Government Panel Warns on Rising Yields’ Hit on Finances
content: A Japanese government advisory panel urged authorities to step up fiscal consolidation efforts, as the Bank of Japan’s ongoing monetary tightening efforts raise the risk of higher debt-servicing costs for the world’s most indebted developed nation.

title: Malaysia Sees Reducing the US’s Proposed Tariff to 10% as a Good Outcome
content: The US reducing its proposed tariffs on Malaysia to a 10% baseline would be seen as a positive move, Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Zafrul Aziz said, conceding that a previously hoped for levy of zero may not be possible.

title: North Korea Says Trump’s Golden Dome Risks ‘Space Nuclear War’
content: North Korea sharply criticized President Donald Trump’s plan for a Golden Dome missile-defense system, a shield intended to counter threats from rivals including Pyongyang.

title: Why This River in India and Pakistan Is Causing So Much Angst
content: The suspension of a water-sharing agreement in place for 65 years signals a new low in relations between the nations.

title: Bolsonaro’s Son Investigated Over Alleged Court Intimidation
content: A Brazilian Supreme Court justice has authorized the federal police to investigate one of the sons of former President Jair Bolsonaro over allegations that he sought to intimidate members of the court while in the US.

title: UK to Train 120,000 Builders, Carers to Cut Reliance on Migrants
content: The UK government plans to train 120,000 British builders, engineers and care workers as it tries to curb migration without worsening skill shortages.

title: Milei Beefs With Netflix Star Over Price of a Dozen Empanadas
content: President Javier Milei and his finance chief criticized a globally known Argentine actor for complaining that the country’s staple food was overpriced, stirring debate about how expensive Argentina has become in dollar terms.

title: Israel-Backed Gaza Food Plan Starts Amid Dissent, Delay
content: The Gaza Humanitarian Foundation, a new Swiss-based nonprofit, said it began distributing food to Palestinians in the war-ravaged Gaza Strip and appointed a new executive director following earlier setbacks.

title: Mark Zuckerberg Loves MAGA Now. Will MAGA Ever Love Him Back?
content: Meta’s CEO has done everything he can to win over Trump, and it’s not clear how much he has to show for it.

title: Trump to Pardon Sheriff Found Guilty of ‘Cash-for-Badges’ Scheme
content: President Donald Trump said he would be pardoning a former Virginia sheriff facing a 10-year prison sentence after being convicted of bribery and fraud charges.

title: King Charles Visits Canada as Country Rattled by Trump Taunts
content: King Charles III arrived in Canada to open a new parliamentary session at the invitation of Prime Minister Mark Carney, a move designed in part to send a message to US President Donald Trump about the northern country’s sovereignty.

title: Multiple People Taken to Hospitals After Shooting Incident in South Carolina Beach Town
content: LITTLE RIVER, S.C. (AP) — Ten people were shot during a fight that started after a private boat hosting a holiday weekend party arrived at a dock Sunday night on the South Carolina coast, authorities said.

title: US Money Managers Put on Notice by $65 Billion Dutch Investor
content: Dutch pension fund PME is issuing a blanket warning to US money managers, amid concerns America’s investment industry is caving in to pressure from the Trump administration to abandon basic principles of stewardship.

title: South Korean Election: Can a New President Bring Back Stability?
content: South Koreans are set to finally choose a new president after the nation’s worst constitutional crisis in decades.

title: Charles Rangel, a Voice for the Poor in Tax Debates, Dies at 94
content: Charles Rangel, the dapper, voluble US congressman from New York’s Harlem district who for four decades used his perch on the House tax-writing committee to advocate for inner cities and the people who live there, has died. He was 94.

title: Macron Says Shoving Incident on Plane Was Him and Wife ‘Joking’
content: PARIS (AP) — They were just playfighting.

title: Chile’s Leftist Presidential Hopefuls Spar Over SQM-Codelco Deal
content: Chile’s left-leaning presidential contenders clashed over a landmark deal signed last year between lithium supplier SQM and state-owned Codelco, highlighting differences ahead of the sector’s primary vote.

title: NATO Chief Rutte Says Members Moving Toward 5% Spending Target
content: NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte confirmed the alliance will seek to adopt a new defense spending target of 5% of GDP at a June summit, meeting a demand by US President Donald Trump that had originally seemed unrealistic.

title: Suriname Election Deadlocks With Newfound Oil Bonanza at Stake
content: Suriname’s political future hangs in the balance after the two main parties were virtually tied in Sunday’s election, triggering intense coalition talks to determine who will get to manage the upcoming oil bonanza.

title: Merz Gives Ukraine Green Light to Strike Deep Inside Russia
content: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz said Ukraine has been given permission to use weapons supplied by its allies to launch strikes deep inside Russia.

title: Trump Threatens to Send Harvard Grant Money to Trade Schools
content: President Donald Trump on Monday threatened to divert billions in grant dollars away from Harvard University and give those funds to trade schools across the US, escalating his clash with the elite institution.

title: EU Plans to ‘Fast Track’ Trade Talks With US Amid Tariff Fight
content: The European Union said it agreed to accelerate negotiations with the US to avoid a transatlantic trade war, signaling a more amicable approach just days after President Donald Trump criticized the bloc for taking advantage of the US and slow-walking talks.

title: Ukraine’s Zelenskiy Said to Meet With Merz in Berlin Wednesday
content: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy is set to travel to Berlin Wednesday for talks with Chancellor Friedrich Merz, according to a person familiar with his plans.

title: Germany’s Merz Floats Cutting Off EU Funds to Fico’s Slovakia
content: Germany would consider suspending European Union funding to Slovakia if the country continues to diverge from the bloc’s shared direction, according to Chancellor Friedrich Merz.

title: Germany Calls Ugandan Claims of Subversive Activities ‘Absurd’
content: Germany said allegations that its ambassador to Uganda was involved in subversive activities were “absurd,” after the East African nation said it was suspending military cooperation.

title: ‘Revenge Tax’: US Bill Hits Allies That Have Tax Rules Trump Doesn’t Like
content: Investors in nations with tax regimes that the US deems unfair would face higher tax rates on income earned in the US if the tax bill that’s making its way to the Senate becomes law.

title: Germany’s Merz Says US Tech Perks Could Be Target in Trade War
content: The European Union could retaliate against US technology companies if the trade conflict with Donald Trump’s administration escalates, German Chancellor Friedrich Merz said.

content: Malaysia is seeking to expand its palm oil market in China by offering a plant-based alternative for use in mala hotpot, a popular spicy dish that’s cooked with raw meats and vegetables in a simmering pot.

title: OPEC+ to Decide July Oil Production Levels on May 31
content: OPEC+ brought forward a video-conference that will decide July oil production levels by one day to May 31, delegates said. The eight-nation sub-group led by Saudi Arabia and Russia held preliminary talks last week on making another bumper output increase of about 411,000 barrels a day for a third consecutive month. Bloomberg’s Dan Murtaugh reports.

title: China’s Air Conditioning Use Poised to Skyrocket This Summer
content: A surge in electricity demand could require a lot more coal to be burnt, fueling the cycle for even hotter summers in the years ahead.

title: Samsung Is Said in Talks to Invest in California-Based Exo
content: Samsung Electronics Co.’s investment arm is among a group of firms seeking to invest in US health-care software and device company Exo Imaging Inc., according to people familiar with the matter.

title: Meituan, JD.com’s Food Delivery War Worsens $100 Billion Rout
content: Shares of Meituan and JD.com have lost a combined $100 billion in market value since late last year, highlighting the fallout of a costly battle to win a bigger slice of the Chinese food delivery business.

title: HKBN’s CEO Says China Mobile Takeover Offer Undervalues Firm
content: China Mobile Ltd.’s takeover offer for HKBN Ltd. undervalues the company, according to the Hong Kong broadband provider’s top executive.

title: Meituan Warns Local Rivalry, Global Push to Hurt Profits
content: Meituan warned its profitability may suffer as the Chinese food delivery leader faces intensifying competition at home and is aggressively expanding into new markets.

title: ALS to Raise Up to A$390 Million to Grow Laboratory Network
content: Australia’s ALS Ltd. is seeking to raise up to A$390 million ($253 million) as the testing services company looks to expand its laboratory network.

title: Mark Zuckerberg Loves MAGA Now. Will MAGA Ever Love Him Back?
content: Meta’s CEO has done everything he can to win over Trump, and it’s not clear how much he has to show for it.

title: US Prosecutors Sought Builder.ai Data After Sales Overstated
content: US prosecutors demanded that Builder.ai hand over financial statements and other documents, signaling that the artificial intelligence company was facing legal scrutiny in the weeks before it went bust.

title: EU Tells Shein to Tackle Consumer Law Breaches or Face Fines
content: Shein Group Ltd., the Singapore-based e-commerce firm, was warned by European Union regulators it could face fines unless it clamps down on consumer protection violations on its platform.

title: ChatGPT’s Improved Memory Points Toward a More Personal AI
content: Welcome to Tech In Depth, our daily newsletter with reporting and analysis about the business of tech from Bloomberg’s journalists around the world. Today, Austin Carr reports on the improvements recently announced to the major consumer chatbots that have made it easier for them to know more about their users.

title: French Inflation Eases to Lowest Rate Since 2020 on Energy
content: France’s inflation rate dropped further below the European Central Bank’s 2% target, reaching a more than four-year low and adding to arguments that borrowing costs can be cut further.

title: Swiss Exports to US Plummet in First Month of Trump Tariffs
content: Swiss exports to the US plummeted in April, showing the fallout from President Donald Trump’s tariff policy.

title: Zimbabwe Sees $2.6 Billion Bridge Finance Secured in 2026
content: Zimbabwe expects $2.6 billion in bridge finance — needed to repay debt owed to international financial institutions and regain access to capital markets — to be in place by the first quarter of next year, Finance Minister Mthuli Ncube said.

title: Japan Government Panel Warns on Rising Yields’ Hit on Finances
content: A Japanese government advisory panel urged authorities to step up fiscal consolidation efforts, as the Bank of Japan’s ongoing monetary tightening efforts raise the risk of higher debt-servicing costs for the world’s most indebted developed nation.

title: Japan Loses Top Creditor Status for First Time in 34 Years
content: Japan lost its position as the world’s largest creditor nation for the first time in 34 years, despite posting a record amount of overseas assets.

title: Hungary to Hold Rates With Price Risks in Focus: Decision Guide
content: Hungary’s central bank will probably keep interest rates unchanged as policymakers focus on curbing inflation risks even as the government signals a worsening outlook for growth.

title: Malaysia Sees Reducing the US’s Proposed Tariff to 10% as a Good Outcome
content: The US reducing its proposed tariffs on Malaysia to a 10% baseline would be seen as a positive move, Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Zafrul Aziz said, conceding that a previously hoped for levy of zero may not be possible.

title: Ueda Indicates BOJ Is Still Eyeing More Rate Hikes, Boosting Yen
content: Bank of Japan Governor Kazuo Ueda gave the yen a boost by clearly indicating his intention to continue raising the benchmark interest rate if the economy improves as expected.

title: UK Food Inflation Highest in a Year as Grocers Face More Costs
content: UK food inflation nudged up in May to the highest level in a year, as British supermarkets battle higher operating costs stemming from the UK government’s revenue-raising budget.

title: Milei Beefs With Netflix Star Over Price of a Dozen Empanadas
content: President Javier Milei and his finance chief criticized a globally known Argentine actor for complaining that the country’s staple food was overpriced, stirring debate about how expensive Argentina has become in dollar terms.

title: Argentina Claims Return to Global Markets With Peso Bond Sale
content: Argentina’s government will issue a five-year bond denominated in pesos that’s aimed at international investors who are allowed to purchase it in US dollars, a move the government hailed as its return to global markets after a sovereign restructuring during the pandemic.

title: King Charles Visits Canada as Country Rattled by Trump Taunts
content: King Charles III arrived in Canada to open a new parliamentary session at the invitation of Prime Minister Mark Carney, a move designed in part to send a message to US President Donald Trump about the northern country’s sovereignty.

title: Brazil Keeps Bungling Its Budget and Worrying Investors
content: An unmistakable sense of deja vu hit Brazil last week when an announcement of measures meant to shore up the nation’s budget sparked a market selloff instead.

title: RBNZ Set to Make Sixth Rate Cut and Signal Bias to More Easing
content: New Zealand’s central bank is set to cut interest rates for a sixth straight meeting and signal it’s open to further easing as US trade barriers dim the economic outlook.

title: South Africa Can Entice Investors With New Budget, Minister Says
content: South Africa can focus on rebuilding the economy and resuscitating investor interest now that the third iteration of the budget has the support of the nation’s coalition government, the infrastructure minister said.

title: Chile’s Leftist Presidential Hopefuls Spar Over SQM-Codelco Deal
content: Chile’s left-leaning presidential contenders clashed over a landmark deal signed last year between lithium supplier SQM and state-owned Codelco, highlighting differences ahead of the sector’s primary vote.

title: Israel Holds Rates as Inflation Spikes, Gaza War Escalates
content: Israel’s central bank kept interest rates on hold for the 11th time in a row, maintaining a wait-and-see stance amid increased military operations in Gaza and an uptick in inflation.

title: Lagarde Sees Opportunities to Raise Euro’s Global Profile
content: President Donald Trump’s erratic policies offer a “prime opportunity” to strengthen the euro’s international role and allow the currency bloc to enjoy more of the privileges so far reserved for the US, European Central Bank President Christine Lagarde said.

title: Chinese, EU Trade Heads to Meet as Trump Tariff Tensions Rise
content: Top trade officials from the European Union and China are planning to meet again early next month, another sign that both sides are stepping up engagements as they try to push back against tariff pressure from Donald Trump.

title: Moody’s Rethinks Its Rating Spectrum on the G-7
content: I’m Craig Stirling, a senior editor in Frankfurt. Today we’re looking the shift in view by Moody’s on Italy. Send us feedback and tips to ecodaily@bloomberg.net. And if you aren’t yet signed up to receive this newsletter, you can do so here.

title: Swiss Desire for a Trump Trade Deal Tests Its Love for Farmers
content: The UK may have been first to clinch some sort of trade accord with the US, but Switzerland has reason to hope it’s not far behind. Earlier this month, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said both countries were “at the front of  the queue” for a deal.

title: Romania Boosts Liquidity to Calm Markets After Rates Spike
content: Romania’s central bank injected the highest amount of liquidity to the domestic market in almost seven years as it sought to bring down short-term interest rates that spiked because of recent political turmoil.

title: Hungary Warns Wage-Hike Plan at Risk From Weak Economy
content: Hungary’s government warned it may need to renegotiate minimum wage hikes planned for 2026 due to weaker-than-expected growth, in the latest downbeat economic outlook from officials.

title: ECB Faces Greater Risk Inflation Will Undershoot 2%, Simkus Says
content: There’s a growing danger that inflation will fall short of the European Central Bank’s 2% target, according to Governing Council member Gediminas Simkus.

title: BYD Shares Extend Losses as Price Cuts Throw Spotlight on Sales
content: BYD Co. shares extended losses in Hong Kong trading Tuesday — taking their two-day slide to more than 10% — as last week’s sweeping price cuts stoked concern of another wave of discounting in China’s cutthroat electric car market.

title: Europe Car Sales Slip as Economic Woes Hold Back Consumers
content: European car sales dipped in April as weaker economic growth and uncertainty due to global trade tensions prompted consumers to hold off on larger purchases.

title: China’s Industrial Profit Growth Picks Up Despite US Tariffs
content: China’s industrial firms saw their profits increase at a faster pace in April, as a government trade-in program drove demand for manufactured products in the face of pressure from higher US tariffs.

title: Chinese Solar Giant Longi Founder Li Steps Back as Losses Deepen
content: The founder of one of China’s biggest solar manufacturers, Longi Green Energy Technology Co., will stand down from his role overseeing day-to-day operations, as deepening losses plague the company and its peers across the sector.

title: Chinese Plastics Buyers Resist Switch Back to US Propane Despite Pause in Trade War
content: Chinese plastics factories left without US raw material when trade relations collapsed earlier this year are holding back from returning to many of those suppliers despite a pause in hostilities, underscoring the difficulty in restoring commercial ties between the world’s two largest economies.

title: Ivanhoe Slumps After Withdrawing Congo Copper Mine Guidance
content: Ivanhoe Mines Ltd. shares slumped the most in 12 years after it withdrew cost and production guidance for Africa’s largest copper mine, where further seismic activity has halted some underground operations.

title: Wildfires Erupt Near Alberta Oil Well Sites Amid Hot Weather
content: Hot weather sparked a string of wildfires around Alberta over the weekend, including some near oil and gas wells operated by Canadian Natural Resources Ltd. and others.

title: Luxury Tokyo Penthouse Sold for Over $65 Million in Booming Market
content: A Tokyo penthouse developed by Swedish buyout firm EQT AB has sold for about ¥9.5 billion ($67 million), shedding light on the cost of buying into the city’s booming high-end property market.

title: Charterhouse Sells Gelato Maker Casa Optima to Terlos
content: Charterhouse Capital Partners has agreed to sell Casa Optima, a gelato and pastry ingredient maker, to a group of investors led by consumer-focused private equity firm Terlos, according to people familiar with the matter.

title: ‘Lilo & Stitch,’ ‘Mission: Impossible’ Fuel Memorial Day Record
content: The twin releases of Walt Disney Co.’s Lilo & Stitch and Paramount Global’s Mission: Impossible — The Final Reckoning lifted US and Canadian theater ticket sales to $326.7 million through Monday, setting a box office record for the Memorial Day holiday weekend.

title: Italy’s Banco BPM Appeals UniCredit Bid Delay in Escalation
content: Banco BPM SpA is seeking to reverse a decision to suspend UniCredit SpA’s tender offer for the smaller rival, further escalating the tensions around the deal.

title: CaixaBank Pushes Back on Opposition to Spanish Banks in Portugal
content: The head of CaixaBank SA’s Portuguese unit sought to refute criticism that Spanish banks have too much influence in the country, saying their investment was vital in strengthening Portugal’s finance industry when others pulled back.

title: South Africa Has Too Many Retail Stores, Pick n Pay CEO Says
content: South African retailers are opening too many new stores, putting their financial viability at risk, according to Pick n Pay Stores Ltd. Chief Executive Officer Sean Summers.

title: Four Ex-VW Managers Convicted in Germany Over Diesel Scandal
content: Four former Volkswagen AG managers were convicted by a German court for their roles in the diesel-emission scandal, involving the manipulation of millions of cars and causing €2.1 billion ($2.4 billion) in damages to drivers.

title: Greece Hooks Up Undersea Power Link to Crete as Part of Mediterranean Grid Plans
content: ATHENS, Greece (AP) — Greece announced Monday it has completed the work on an undersea power cable link connecting the mainland to the island of Crete, a key step in its ambitious plan for a wider expansion of the grid in the Eastern Mediterranean that will eventually include Cyprus and Israel.

title: Thyssenkrupp Plans to End Conglomerate Era in Bid for Turnaround
content: Thyssenkrupp AG plans to transform itself into a holding company with majority stakes in standalone business units, marking the end of its era as a fully integrated industrial conglomerate.

title: Volvo Car Plans to Cut 3,000 Jobs After Profit Plunge
content: Volvo Car AB plans to eliminate around 7% of its global workforce as the Swedish carmaker cuts costs to counter muted demand and protect profits.

title: Indian Steel Tycoon’s Pathway to Mozambique Coal Deal Reopens
content: India’s largest steelmaker can proceed with the acquisition of a coal deposit in Mozambique after the seller recovered the concession rights from the country’s new government.

title: Malaysia, Singapore Explore Importing Wind Energy from Vietnam
content: Major power companies in Singapore, Malaysia and Vietnam have agreed to explore renewable energy links across their borders, as Southeast Asia takes steps to realize its long-held vision of a regional supergrid.

title: Lombard Odier, Hong Leong Team Up for Southeast Asia Wealth
content: Lombard Odier struck its seventh partnership in Asia as the Swiss wealth manager tied up with Hong Leong Bank Bhd., a move that underscores how financial firms are expanding to cater to the rising wealth in the region.

title: Indonesia Trims Gas, Backs Renewables in National Power Plan
content: Indonesia aims to boost the buildout of renewable energy in its latest national power plan, scaling back gas additions to the grid.

title: AfDB Presidential Hopeful Eyes $4.5 Trillion in Private Capital
content: Africa should tap domestic private capital to fund development and reduce reliance on costly international borrowing, said a contender for the African Development Bank presidency.

title: Chinese EV Stocks Tumble After BYD Slashes Prices as Much as 34%
content: BYD Co. led Chinese electric vehicle stocks lower in Hong Kong on Monday, as investors digested the auto giant’s sweeping price cuts of as much as 34% late last week.

content: Chinese developer Country Garden Holdings Co.’s efforts to win backing for a $14.1 billion offshore restructuring are running into resistance as key bank creditors say failure to accept some of their demands would be a “deal breaker.”

title: At Least 21 Palestinians Killed Heading to Gaza Aid Hub, Hospital Says
content: RAFAH, Gaza Strip (AP) — At least 31 people were killed and over 170 were wounded Sunday as large crowds were on their way to receive food in the Gaza Strip, health officials and witnesses said. Witnesses said Israeli forces fired toward the crowds just before dawn around a kilometer (about 1,100 yards) from an aid site run by an Israeli-backed foundation.

title: Matthei Gives Chile Vote Pledges a Reality Check on Fiscal Woes

title: Trump Wants to Sell US’s 1 Million Barrel Reserve of Diesel Fuel
content: The Trump administration wants to put a 1 million barrel cache of diesel fuel on the market, saying the reserve meant to provide an emergency supply of home heating oil for the Northeast has never been used for its intended purpose.

title: What Trump’s 50% Tariffs Mean for the Steel Industry
content: President Donald Trump said he will double tariffs on aluminum and steel, sending futures for the metals surging higher. Steel Manufacturers Association Government Affairs Vice President Brandon Farris discusses the impact of the tariffs and an expected deal between US Steel and Japan’s Nippon Steel Corp.

title: Supreme Court Lets Finra Case Proceed in Test of Wall Street’s Self Regulation
content: The US Supreme Court let the Financial Industry Regulatory Authority proceed with disciplinary proceedings against a brokerage accused of stealing from customers in a case testing Wall Street’s longstanding reliance on self-regulatory organizations.

title: France Scraps Bank Capital Rule for Indebted Firms as Risks Ease
content: France will ease some capital requirements for its largest banks on exposure to highly-indebted companies, after regulators said lenders face lower risk than they did two years ago.

title: Philippines Aims to Cut Reliance on Vietnam for Rice
content: The Philippines, the world’s top rice importer, plans to look beyond its dominant supplier, Vietnam, to ensure steady supplies and competitive prices at home.

title: New World’s Distress Worsens After Delay on Bond Interest
content: Hong Kong developer New World Development Co. is sliding deeper into distress after jolting investors by delaying interest payments on some bonds, marking the latest flashpoint in a years-long crisis in China’s property market.

title: China Says US Is Violating Trade Deal

title: Morgan Stanley Sees Dollar Falling 9% Over Next Year
content: Matthew Hornbach, global head of macro strategy at Morgan Stanley, explains why interest rate cuts and slowing growth will cause the US dollar to tumble around 9% from current levels by the middle of next year.

title: France Amends Offshore Wind Farm Contracts to Ease Power Glut

title: Ukraine's Audacious Drone Strike Ahead Of Russia Talks
content:
Ukraine staged a dramatic series of strikes across Russia, deploying drones hidden in trucks deep inside the country to hit strategic airfields as far away as eastern Siberia. More than 40 Russian aircraft, including the Tu-95 and Tu-22 M3 long-range bombers capable of deploying conventional and nuclear weapons as well as the A-50, were reportedly damaged in Sunday's operation, an official in Ukraine's Security Service said on condition of anonymity as the details are not public. Ukraine's Security Service chief Vasyl Malyuk led the operation and losses are assessed to be at least $2 billion, the person said. 

Bloomberg's EMEA News Director Rosalind Mathieson joins Stephen Carroll and Lizzy Burden to discuss.  (Source: Bloomberg)

content: Hello and welcome to the newsletter, a grab bag of daily content from the Odd Lots universe. Sometimes it's us, Joe Weisenthal and Tracy Alloway, bringing you our thoughts on the most recent developments in markets, finance and the economy. And sometimes it's contributions from our network of expert guests and sources. Whatever it is, we promise it will always be interesting.

title: Treasuries Fall as Tariff Concerns Cloud Outlook, ISM Weaker
content: Treasuries remained lower amid broad weakness in US assets on Monday, as worries over President Donald Trump’s tariff policy swirl at the start of a busy week for data on the health of the world’s largest economy.

title: Wall Street Sees Deeper Rout as Dollar Nears 2023 Low
content: Wall Street banks are reinforcing their calls that the dollar will weaken further, hit by interest-rate cuts, slowing economic growth and President Donald Trump’s trade and tax policies.

title: Alberta Wildfires Shut Down About 7% of Canada’s Oil Production
content: Wildfires in Canada’s energy heartland of Alberta have shut down almost 350,000 barrels of daily heavy crude production — about 7% of the country’s output — as a major blaze near the province’s eastern border menaces oil sands operations.

title: US Stocks Slip as Trade Friction, Weak Data Dent Sentiment
content: US equities edged lower Monday as reemerging tensions around global trade and a weak manufacturing report sapped investor confidence.

title: The Ratings Underdog Making Waves in Private Credit
content: Egan-Jones is a small but significant player in the private credit market,  grading over three thousand investments last year with a team of just 20 analysts. The firm's fast growth and optimistic ratings, however, are raising concerns about the risks in the private credit market, with some major investors excluding them from their lists of acceptable credit graders. Bloomberg Private Credit Reporter Silas Brown joined Wall Street Beat on Bloomberg Open Interest with the details. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Gold Surges With Rising Global Tensions Boosting Haven Demand
content: Gold surged on revived demand for safer assets as the US and China traded accusations, while a dramatic series of attacks clouded the prospects of peace between Russia and Ukraine.

title: Bloomberg Surveillance 6/2/2025
content: Jonathan Ferro, Lisa Abramowicz and Annmarie Hordern speak daily with leaders and decision makers from Wall Street to Washington and beyond. No other program better positions investors and executives for the trading day. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Diamond Wars: The Future of Lab Grown vs. Natural Diamonds
content: Lab Grown diamonds continue to put pressure on the $370 billion dollar global jewelry market. For the first time ever, more than half of engagement rings are made with lab grown diamonds. Despite the boom, De Beers says it will be closing its lab-grown diamond jewelry brand Lightbox. Ankur Daga, the Co-Founder and CEO of Angara, an online jeweler. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Some Retailers Can Get Away With Raising Prices, Widlitz Says
content: Stacey Widlitz, SW Retail Advisors president, says many consumers are still willing to pay higher prices, despite tariffs. She says many brands are getting away with raising prices if their products are in demand. She is on "Bloomberg Surveillance" talking about the impact of tariffs on retailers and says there could be fewer deals for customers in the electronic and footwear space. (Source: Bloomberg)

content: Helaba and other German lenders have paid millions of euros in recent weeks to settle claims by the administrator of former real estate tycoon Rene Benko’s Signa Prime Selection AG.

content: A Malian court has for the third time postponed a ruling on whether Barrick Gold Corp.’s Loulo-Gounkoto mine should be placed under state administration.

title: Eramet Drops as Gabon Aims to End Manganese Ore Exports
content: Eramet SA shares fell as much as 5.7% after Gabon decided to ban the export of manganese ore from 2029, jeopardizing the French miner’s biggest source of profit.

content: The Trump administration wants to put a 1 million barrel cache of diesel fuel on the market, saying the reserve meant to provide an emergency supply of home heating oil for the Northeast has never been used for its intended purpose.

title: Trump’s Tariffs Plunge US and Global Economy Into Slowdown
content: Donald Trump’s combative trade policies have tipped the world economy into a downturn clouded in heightened uncertainty, with the US among the hardest hit, the OECD said.

title: Bloomberg Daybreak: Daybreak Europe 06/03/2025
content:
Bloomberg Daybreak Europe is your essential morning viewing to stay ahead. Live from London, we set the agenda for your day, catching you up with overnight markets news from the US and Asia. And we'll tell you what matters for investors in Europe, giving you insight before trading begins.

Today's Guests: Alexandra Ivanova, Fund Manager at Invesco.  (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Toyota Industries Receives Buyout Offer From Group Companies
content: Toyota Industries Corp. said it received a $33 billion offer to take the company private in a move that could lead to the founding family strengthening its grip over Japan’s biggest business empire.

title: Rheinmetall to Replace Kering in Euro Stoxx 50, JPMorgan Says
content: Rheinmetall AG’s surging stock price has earned the tank and munitions maker a place in the euro area’s main stock benchmark.

title: Japan’s Bonds Pass 10-Year Supply Test as 30-Year Sale Looms
content: Stronger demand at Japan’s 10-year bond sale brought some temporary relief as traders position for another auction in less than 48 hours that will test appetite for longer-dated debt.

title: MJ Gleeson Cuts Outlook on Slow UK Recovery, Planning Hurdles
content: MJ Gleeson Plc slashed guidance, citing a slow housing market recovery in the UK and planning delays.

title: Swiss Inflation Turns Negative for First Time in Four Years
content: The inflation rate in Switzerland turned negative for the first time since early 2021, adding to pressure on policymakers to lower borrowing costs later this month.

title: Gold Edges Lower on Stronger Dollar Ahead of US Labor Figures
content: Gold dipped as the dollar strengthened ahead of US labor data later this week that will help steer the Federal Reserve’s monetary policy.

title: China’s Private Factory Gauge Plunges to Weakest Since 2022
content: China’s manufacturing sector had its worst slump since September 2022, according to a private survey, as higher tariffs took a toll on smaller exporters despite a truce in the trade war with the US.

title: UK’s Ofwat Set for Supervisory Role in Regulatory Overhaul
content: The UK water regulator needs to take a more supervisory role akin to the banking sector in order to help stem the industry’s worst crisis in decades.

title: Global Stocks Near Record High Sets Stage for Further Gains
content: Global equities are edging close to an all-time high, with some analysts forecasting further upside supported by dip-buying activity.

title: US Stock Futures Drop, Dollar Gains After Selloff: Markets Wrap
content: US equity-index futures retreated after a rally in the S&P 500 late Monday as investors awaited news on any trade talks between President Donald Trump and China’s Xi Jinping.

title: Tilton: China Very Competitive Gaining Shares vs US
content: The US is extending the tariff pause on some Chinese goods until August 31 as President Donald Trump is expected to speak with Chinese leader, Xi Jinping. Meanwhile the Caixin manufacturing PMI fell to 48.3 last month, experiencing its worst slump since September 2022. Andrew Tilton, Chief APAC Economist at Goldman Sachs spoke to Bloomberg’s Horizons Middle East and Africa anchor Joumanna Bercetche on the Chinese economy performance. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Harling: Biggest EM Challenge is Currency Stability
content: Bonds in Australia and Singapore gained as questions about the appeal of US Treasuries sent investors toward top-rated alternatives. But Emerging-market stocks fell to their lowest level since May 9 as fresh trade tensions between the US and China clouded the global outlook. Victoria Harling, Co-Head of Emerging Market Corporate Debt at Ninety One spoke to Bloomberg’s Horizons Middle East and Africa anchor Joumanna Bercetche on the mood in emerging markets. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Qatar-Backed Kasada Targets First North Africa Hotel Deal
content: Kasada Capital Management, a private equity firm backed by Qatar’s $524 billion sovereign wealth fund, expects to strike a hotel deal in Morocco in the first half of 2026, marking its entry into North Africa’s booming hospitality and tourism industry.

content: “Bloomberg: The China Show” is your definitive source for news and analysis on the world's second-biggest economy. From politics and policy to tech and trends, Yvonne Man and David Ingles give global investors unique insight, delivering in-depth discussions with the newsmakers who matter. (Source: Bloomberg)

content: Insight with Haslinda Amin, a daily news program featuring in-depth, high-profile interviews and analysis to give viewers the complete picture on the stories that matter. The show features prominent leaders spanning the worlds of business, finance, politics and culture. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Klarna CEO Attracts Sweden’s Elite in Flat Capital Share Sale
content: Flat Capital AB, the investment firm of Klarna co-founder Sebastian Siemiatkowski and his wife Nina Siemiatkowski, has broadened its shareholder base via a rights issue that included some of Sweden’s most prominent business families.

title: Palm Oil Jumps on Demand Prospects After India Cuts Import Duty
content: Palm oil climbed to the highest level in almost three weeks on expectations for higher demand after top buyer India cut import duties.

title: Oil Extends Gains on Weaker Dollar, Geopolitical Uncertainty
content: Oil rose for a second day as a weakener dollar boosted the appeal of commodities priced in the currency and geopolitical ructions limited the chance of more supply from Russia and Iran.

title: Most Adani Stocks Fall on Report of US Probe Into Iran Shipments
content: Most Adani Group units’ shares fell Tuesday following a report by The Wall Street Journal that said US prosecutors are probing the Indian conglomerate’s possible dealings with sanctions-hit Iran.

title: Swedish Steelmaker Alleima Sees Pricing as Counter to US Tariffs
content: The chief executive officer of Swedish steelmaker Alleima AB says the company will not absorb any potential costs from tariffs and will instead focus its efforts on raising prices, as well as targeting specific industries.

title: Iron Ore Falls as China PMI Slips to Lowest Level Since 2022
content: Iron ore and base metals dropped on concerns about China’s economic outlook, as a gauge of the country’s manufacturing activity fell to its lowest level in more than two years.

title: US Dollar Will Go Lower But Not in Disorderly Fashion, Nomura's Koo Says
content: Richard Koo, chief economist at Nomura Research Institute, shares his outlook for the US dollar, trade relations and bond yields. He speaks to Bloomberg's Haslinda Amin at the Nomura Investment Forum Asia in Singapore. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: America's 'Smartest Minds' Will Be Beckoned to Australia: Jagadish
content: The Australian Academy of Science says the country has an unparalleled opportunity to attract talent leaving the United States amid Trump's foreign student visa crackdown. The academy's president, Chennupati Jagadish talks about the opportunities for Australia on "Bloomberg: The Asia Trade." (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Bloomberg: The Asia Trade 6/3/25
content: "Bloomberg: The Asia Trade" brings you everything you need to know to get ahead as the trading day begins in Asia. Bloomberg TV is live from Seoul and Sydney with Shery Ahn and Haidi Stroud-Watts, getting insight and analysis from newsmakers and industry leaders on the biggest stories shaping global markets. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: RBA’s Hunter Sees US Tariffs Dragging on Australian Growth, Jobs
content: Australia’s central bank expects global trade uncertainty will weigh on the domestic economy and employment, according to a senior official, helping explain policymakers’ surprise switch to a dovish stance last month.

title: Mongolia’s Main Party to Form New Government After PM Ousted
content: Mongolia’s main political party will form a new government after lawmakers rejected a confidence vote, ousting Prime Minister Oyun-Erdene Luvsannamsrai and exacerbating uncertainty for the nation’s economy as it struggles with China’s weakening demand for raw materials.

title: Lutnick Sees US-India Trade Deal in ‘Not-Too-Distant Future’
content: Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick said he’s “very optimistic” about prospects for a trade deal between the US and India, suggesting an agreement could come before a July deadline for higher tariffs.

title: Swiss Inflation Turns Negative for First Time in Four Years
content: The inflation rate in Switzerland turned negative for the first time since early 2021, adding to pressure on policymakers to lower borrowing costs later this month.

title: Dutch Parties Hold Emergency Talks to Avoid Government Collapse
content: The ruling coalition in the Netherlands will hold a second day of emergency meetings Tuesday in a bid to avoid a government collapse over the country’s migration policy.

title: UK Threatens to Sue Roman Abramovich Over Chelsea Sale Proceeds
content: The UK government said it may take billionaire Russian businessman Roman Abramovich to court in order to release £2.34 billion ($3.2 billion) from the proceeds of his sale of Chelsea football club for humanitarian purposes in Ukraine.

title: Starmer Torn Between Trump and Labour on UK Defense Overhaul
content: Keir Starmer’s revamp of defense policy intended to show both Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin that Britain is serious about maintaining its role as a key power in Europe and NATO.

title: Trump’s Dealmaking Style Won’t Sway Xi, Ex-White House Aide Says
content: A potential trade deal between the world’s top two economies hinges on Donald Trump and Xi Jinping overcoming core differences in their negotiation styles, former acting White House Chief of Staff Mick Mulvaney said.

title: Israel’s Gaza Attacks Spur European Leaders to Criticize Netanyahu
content: Some of Israel’s most loyal supporters in Europe are increasingly speaking out against the war in Gaza, with several nations, including Germany, considering curbs on trade and arms sales.

title: Trump Says US Won’t Agree to Any Uranium Enrichment by Iran
content: The US won’t allow any uranium enrichment as part of a potential nuclear deal with Iran, President Donald Trump said.

title: South Korea Votes for New Leader to Heal Nation, Spur Growth
content: South Koreans head to the polls Tuesday to elect a new president after an attempt to impose martial law at the end of last year triggered its worst constitutional crisis in decades.

title: How Ukraine’s Drone Arsenal Shocked Russia and Changed Modern Warfare
content: Costing as little as $400 apiece, Kyiv’s flying machines are successfully neutralizing sophisticated Russian equipment worth thousands of times more.

title: UK Eyes Greater Nuclear Role in Europe Amid Doubts About US
content: The UK envisages taking an enhanced role in NATO’s nuclear deterrence amid doubts surrounding the US commitment to the alliance, as Prime Minister Keir Starmer pledges to make Britain “war-ready” to counter Russian aggression in Europe.

title: Nigeria Attacks Surge as Islamic-State Affiliate Hits Army Bases
content: Islamist militants have ramped up an insurgency in northeastern Nigeria and attacked dozens of fortified army bases since the start of the year, setting back President Bola Tinubu’s efforts to restore security in Africa’s most-populous nation.

title: Macron and Meloni Aim to Reconcile as Europe Seeks United Front
content: French President Emmanuel Macron and Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni will look to patch up difficult relations during a bilateral meeting in Rome on Tuesday, as Europe grapples with the seismic geopolitical shifts caused by the Trump administration.

title: BOJ’s Ueda Hints at Chance of Continuing to Cut Bond Purchases
content: Bank of Japan Governor Kazuo Ueda hinted that the central bank could continue to slow the pace of government bond purchases next fiscal year, as the board’s decision over bond buying approaches.

title: Chinese Firms Warn EU Procurement Curb Could Hurt Trade Ties
content: A Chinese business lobby group warned that EU actions to curb access of the country’s medical device makers to government contracts in the bloc will hurt trade ties.

title: Prabowo Slams Corrupt Indonesian Officials, Warns Foreign NGOs
content: Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto used a national holiday address to deliver a sharp warning to the country’s political elite, urging underperforming public officials to step down or face removal.

title: Media Groups Probed by FTC Over Allegedly Coordinating Boycotts
content: The US Federal Trade Commission is investigating whether more than a dozen media and advertising groups have illegally colluded to boycott online content alleged to be hateful, false or misleading, according to people familiar with the matter and a document seen by Bloomberg News.

title: Trump Presses Reluctant GOP Senators to Embrace House Tax Bill
content: President Donald Trump worked the phones Monday and took to social media to try to sway Republican holdouts on his multi-trillion dollar tax bill, encountering conflicting demands from GOP senators even as he urged them to move swiftly.

title: Carney Open to New Canada Oil Pipeline Tied to Carbon Capture
content: Mark Carney said he sees opportunity for Canada to build a new pipeline to ship more oil to foreign markets, if it’s tied to billions in green investments to reduce the industry’s environmental footprint.

title: Doritos, M&Ms Could Be Forced to Include Warning Labels in Texas
content: A Texas bill on the verge of becoming law would require labels on packaged food from Skittles to Mountain Dew that warn about ingredients “not recommended for human consumption” by other countries.

title: Korean Air Chairman Calls for Political Stability, Tariff Cuts
content: South Korea’s next government should prioritize making a trade deal with Washington that shields the aviation industry from tariffs, the head of the country’s largest airline said.

title: Federal Retirement Process Goes Digital, Targeting Paper Pileup
content: The federal personnel agency has launched an online system for processing retirement applications, ending a paper-based method that had remained largely unchanged for decades.

title: For Volatile Trump, Trade Pacts With China, Europe Prove Elusive
content: US President Donald Trump is eager to land more trade deals, but talks with China and Europe continue to languish amid communications breakdowns and fresh tariff threats.

title: Saudi Arabia’s Hurdles at Home Are Reshaping the Mideast Financial Order
content: Bankers and business leaders are shifting more attention toward the kingdom’s neighbors in the Gulf as it grapples with lower oil prices and weakening finances.

content: This is Washington Edition, the newsletter about money, power and politics in the nation’s capital. title: Mexico Remittances Plunge as Trump Cracks Down on Migrants
content: Remittances sent to Mexico fell 12% in April from a year prior, registering the largest annual drop in more than a decade as US lawmakers mull taxing the transfers and Donald Trump’s administration toughens its rhetoric against migrants.

title: Senate to Review Trump ‘Revenge’ Tax Worrying Wall Street
content: Senate Republicans will examine the potential impact of a so-called “revenge” tax buried in President Donald Trump’s massive fiscal package before passing the measure, Majority Leader John Thune said Monday.

content: Toyota Industries Corp. said it received a $33 billion offer to take the company private in a move that could lead to the founding family strengthening its grip over Japan’s biggest business empire.

title: Poland: Tusk Calls for Confidence Vote in His Government
content: Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk will seek a vote of confidence to bolster support for his coalition government following last weekend’s presidential election, which saw nationalist Karol Nawrocki defeat the candidate backed by Tusk’s party, potentially jeopardizing the premier’s legislative agenda. Bloomberg’s Oliver Crook reports.

title: Russia, Ukraine Talks Result in Prisoner Swap Agreement
content: Russia and Ukraine held a second round of talks in Istanbul, but failed to reach an agreement to end the war. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said that the delegations agreed on another prisoner swap of 1,000 from each side. Kyiv demanded an unconditional truce, Moscow in turn proposed a ceasefire for two-to-three days along certain parts of the front to allow the evacuation of war dead. Bloomberg’s Greg Sullivan reports.

content: Bloomberg’s Caroline Hyde discusses the latest trade tensions between the US and China and the impact they are having on tech. title: Clearlake Overhauls Debt, Gets Fresh Capital for Quest Software

title: Korean Stocks Rise to Enter Bull Market, Bonds Sink After Vote
content: South Korea’s equity benchmark climbed to enter a bull market, after Lee Jae-myung’s widely-expected win in the presidential election ended a months-long political leadership vacuum.

title: Norway Seafood Exports Snap 10-Month Streak on Salmon Retreat
content: A slump in salmon prices in May contributed to the first annual drop in Norwegian seafood exports after 10 months of growth as production of the pink-fleshed fish rose.

title: Horizons Middle East & Africa 6/4/2025
content: Horizons Middle East & Africa is your daily spotlight on one of the world's fastest-growing regions. Live from Dubai, we bring you the latest global markets and analysis, plus news-making interviews, with a special focus on MEA. All that and more, as you head to the office in the Gulf, pause for lunch in Hong Kong, or start your day in London or Johannesburg.  (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Trump to Attend NATO Summit Later This Month
content: Donald Trump will attend the upcoming NATO summit in The Hague, Netherlands, the White House said, as the US president seeks to rally the alliance’s members to step up defense spending to 5% of GDP. Bloomberg’s Oliver Crook reports.

title: Bankers, Economists Vie for Governor’s Role at Bank of Thailand
content: The race to be Bank of Thailand governor is heating up, with multiple bankers and economists applying ahead of Wednesday’s deadline for a pivotal role in Southeast Asia’s second-biggest economy.

title: Stocks, European Futures Rise on US Jobs Surprise: Markets Wrap
content: Asian stocks rose for the first time in four days after data showed the US labor market is holding up, easing concerns President Donald Trump’s tariff war is pushing the world economy into a downturn.

title: Bloomberg: The China Show 06/04/2025
content: “Bloomberg: The China Show” is your definitive source for news and analysis on the world's second-biggest economy. From politics and policy to tech and trends, Yvonne Man and David Ingles give global investors unique insight, delivering in-depth discussions with the newsmakers who matter. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Gower: Aluminum Tariff Hike Unlikely to Impact US Short-Term Imports
content: President Trump has signed a directive, doubling steel and aluminum tariffs to 50-percent, with the higher levies coming into force on Wednesday. Morgan Stanley Metals and Mining Commodities Strategist Amy Gower spoke to Joumanna Bercetche on Horizons Middle East and Africa, and says the higher tariff is unlikely to impact US imports in the short term. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Trivium China Sees Beijing With Rare Earths Advantage
content: As tensions rise between the US and China, one of the main sticking points looks to be around the issue of rare earths. And Trivium China says Beijing still has significant leverage when it comes to the critical minerals. Cory Combs, Head of Critical Mineral and Supply Chain Research made the comments during "Bloomberg's The China Show." (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Insight with Haslinda Amin 6/4/2025
content: Insight with Haslinda Amin, a daily news program featuring in-depth, high-profile interviews and analysis to give viewers the complete picture on the stories that matter. The show features prominent leaders spanning the worlds of business, finance, politics and culture. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Miniso Is Said to Hire JPMorgan, UBS for Top Toy’s Hong Kong IPO
content: Miniso Group Holding Ltd. has hired JPMorgan Chase & Co. and UBS Group AG for the planned initial public offering of unit Top Toy in Hong Kong, according to people familiar with the development.

title: South Korea’s Lee Kicks Off Presidency
content: South Korea’s newly elected President Lee Jae-myung took office with a pledge to revive the nation’s tariff-hit economy and seek dialogue with North Korea to diffuse tensions on the Korean Peninsula. Bloomberg TV's Shery Ahn speaks on Insight with Haslinda Amin about the newly elected leader. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Action in Hong Kong Equity Markets Stirs Most Excitement in Years
content: Hong Kong’s equity capital markets are seeing the most action in years, with multibillion dollar deals lifting the mood and fueling anticipation about more transactions to come.

title: Oil Steadies With Focus on Canada Wildfires, US Crude Stockpiles
content: Oil steadied after a two-day gain as rains slowed the growth of some blazes which had disrupted Canadian crude production.

title: Toyota Industries Shares Slide on Buyout Discount Blowback
content: Toyota Industries Corp. shares fell the most in nine months after the Toyota group unveiled a ¥4.7 trillion ($33 billion) plan to privatize Toyota Industries Corp., drawing sharp criticism from investors and analysts who say the proposal significantly undervalues the company.

title: Lagarde’s ECB Future Set for Scrutiny After WEF Job Speculation
content: Christine Lagarde is about to face scrutiny on her commitment to keep leading the European Central Bank, not least as she nears the milestone of having just about tamed inflation.

title: Poland to Hold Rates, Focus on Glapinski’s Tone
content: Poland is set to keep interest rates on hold, with investors focusing on central bank Governor Adam Glapinski’s outlook for borrowing costs following a pivotal presidential election.

title: Former S.Korean Trade Minister Yeo on Trade Outlook
content: Han-koo Yeo, Peterson Institute for International Economics Senior Fellow and Former South Korean Trade Minister, discusses the economic and trade outlook for the country after South Koreans elected Lee Jae-myung as their new President, following months of political turmoil after a martial law declaration late 2024. He speaks with Shery Ahn and Paul Allen on "Bloomberg: The Asia Trade". (Source: Bloomberg)

title: China Consumers Get Thrifty During Holidays as Spending Stumbles
content: Chinese consumer spending faltered during a major holiday even as more people hit the road, suggesting a trade truce with the US is failing to turn around sentiment in an economy reeling from Donald Trump’s tariffs.

title: China Bond Futures Trade Dwindles as Market Awaits Xi-Trump Call
content: Transactions in China’s long-term sovereign bond futures are cooling as traders hold off making bets in the market given continued tariff disputes with the US.

title: Vietnam Orders Action to Avert Power Crunch as Heat Lifts Demand
content: Vietnamese Prime Minister Pham Minh Chinh has ordered government agencies to ensure uninterrupted power supplies for households and businesses as heat waves boost electricity demand to a record.

title: Gold Edges Up on Dip-Buying, Persistent Trade War Worries
content: Gold edged higher after falling in the previous session, buoyed by Asian bargain-hunters as concerns resurfaced over the impact of US President Donald Trump’s trade war.

title: Bloomberg: The Asia Trade 6/4/25
content: "Bloomberg: The Asia Trade" brings you everything you need to know to get ahead as the trading day begins in Asia. Bloomberg TV is live from Seoul and Sydney with Shery Ahn and Paul Allen, getting insight and analysis from newsmakers and industry leaders on the biggest stories shaping global markets. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Iran Oil Flows to China Fall on Sanctions, Refinery Maintenance
content: Iran is shipping less oil to China, as toughening sanctions snarl the OPEC producer’s shipments and refinery demand falls in the world’s biggest fossil fuel importer.

title: Overweight US and Asia Equities, HSBC’s Sels Says
content: Willem Sels, Global CIO at HSBC Global Private Banking & Premier Wealth, says “we’re rebuilding our equity exposure with overweights in the US and in Asia.” Sels also discusses his outlook for the US economy and opportunities in fixed income. He speaks on Bloomberg Television.

title: Indian Stocks Bullish Momentum Takes a Pause
content: Before the trading day starts we bring you a digest of the key news and events that are likely to move markets. Today we look at:

title: Petronas Is Said to Weigh Sale of $7 Billion Canada Business
content: Petroliam Nasional Bhd. is considering options for its Canadian company formerly known as Progress Energy Resources Corp., including a sale, according to people familiar with the matter.

title: China’s Wheat Harvest Risks 7-Year Low as Farmers Battle Drought
content: China’s wheat output could drop as much as 5% this year to the lowest since 2018, after recent drought in key growing regions stressed the crop.

title: Iran’s Khamenei Spurns ‘Arrogant’ US Nuclear-Deal Proposal
content: Iran’s Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei criticized a US proposal for a nuclear deal and called American officials “arrogant” for expecting the Islamic Republic to cease uranium enrichment.

title: Korean Stocks Rise to Enter Bull Market, Bonds Sink After Vote
content: South Korea’s equity benchmark climbed to enter a bull market, after Lee Jae-myung’s widely-expected win in the presidential election ended a months-long political leadership vacuum.

title: Trump Gives UK Five-Week Deadline After Reprieve on Steel Tariff
content: The UK is contending with a new five-week deadline to finalize its trade agreement with the US after President Donald Trump spared the country’s steel and aluminum exports from a doubling of existing tariffs.

title: Korean Air Chairman Calls for Stability, Tariff Cuts
content: South Korea’s next government should prioritize making a trade deal with Washington that shields the aviation industry from tariffs, the head of the country’s largest airline said.

title: Trump Says China’s Xi Is ‘Extremely Hard to Make a Deal With’
content: President Donald Trump in a late-night social media post called Xi Jinping very tough to make a deal with, dimming the prospect of an immediate call between the two men.

title: Netherlands Faces Months in Limbo After Government Collapses
content: The Netherlands faces months of uncertainty after far-right politician Geert Wilders pulled the plug on the coalition, toppling the government.

title: Tariffs, North Korea Cast Shadow Over Lee’s First Day in Office
content: South Korea’s newly elected President Lee Jae-myung took office with a pledge to revive a national economy threatened by Donald Trump’s tariffs just as the US president doubled duties on steel and aluminum, highlighting the pressing challenges facing the Asian leader.

title: Democrats Lose Challenge to Trump’s Order on Election Commission
content: The Democratic Party’s governing body lost its legal challenge to an executive order by President Donald Trump that it said would eliminate the bipartisan nature of the Federal Elections Commission and shift authority to the White House.

title: Trump Signs Order Doubling US Steel, Aluminum Tariffs to 50%
content: President Donald Trump has raised steel and aluminum tariffs to 50% from 25%, following through on a pledge to boost US import taxes to help domestic manufacturers.

title: Merz Has Courted and Criticized Trump From Afar. Now They Meet
content: After weeks of preparation, the new German chancellor faces his biggest test yet.

title: UK Confronts Hard Reality of Rebuilding Its Military Prowess
content: Years of underinvestment, botched contracts and poor recruitment have hollowed out what was once a superpower.

title: Pentagon Wants to Delay Navy’s Next-Gen Fighter to Focus on F-47
content: The Pentagon wants to give priority to the Air Force’s F-47 stealth fighter over Navy plans to develop its own next-generation jet, arguing that pursuing the two programs at the same time could delay them both.

title: Lagarde’s ECB Future Set for Scrutiny After WEF Job Speculation
content: Christine Lagarde is about to face scrutiny on her commitment to keep leading the European Central Bank, not least as she nears the milestone of having just about tamed inflation.

title: Philippine Vice President Duterte Questions Impeachment Trial Under New Congress
content: Philippine Vice President Sara Duterte has questioned whether her impeachment trial on charges that include a suspected plot to assassinate President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. can go forward when a new set of lawmakers takes office next month.

title: Rubio Eulogizes Tiananmen Protesters as Tariffs Test Ties
content: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio praised pro-democracy protesters who were killed in Beijing’s bloody Tiananmen Square crackdown 36 years ago, carrying on Washington’s criticism of China’s human rights record as tariff disputes further test already frayed ties.

title: University of Florida President Pick Santa Ono Rejected After Republican DEI Backlash
content: Florida state university leaders voted to reject Santo Ono as president of the University of Florida, following Republican backlash over the former University of Michigan president’s previous support for diversity programs.

title: Mexico Will Ask US Government for Steel Tariff Exemption
content: Mexico will ask Donald Trump’s administration this week to be exempted from an increase in steel tariffs to 50%, the country’s economy minister said on Tuesday.

title: South Korea Elects Lee President, Capping Six Months of Chaos
content: Left-leaning challenger Lee Jae-myung won South Korea’s presidential election, ending three years of conservative rule in a race that was largely a verdict on his ousted predecessor’s botched attempt to revive martial law in the longstanding US ally.

title: Trump Taps Former Small Business Chief for Role Overseeing CFIUS
content: President Donald Trump has nominated Chris Pilkerton, the acting head of the Small Business Administration during his first term, to oversee a committee charged with screening foreign investments into the US as well as outbound investments in foreign countries, with a close eye on competition with China.

title: House SALT Deal Will Have to Change, Senate Leader Thune Says
content: Senate Majority Leader John Thune believes the deal that led the US House to increase the maximum deduction for state and local taxes to $40,000 will have to be changed in his chamber, according to his office.

title: Walmart Cuts Some Florida Jobs After Immigration Rulings
content: Walmart Inc. is terminating some jobs in Florida after recent Supreme Court rulings about the legal residency of migrants, the latest sign that such orders are hitting US workplaces.

title: China’s Top Diplomat Urges US to Put Relations on ‘Right Track’
content: Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi used his first meeting with new US Ambassador David Perdue to complain about recent actions by Washington, underscoring a downturn in relations between the world’s two biggest economies.

title: Penn Wins Dismissal of Antisemitism Suit by Jewish Students
content: A federal judge dismissed a lawsuit against University of Pennsylvania filed by Jewish students over antisemitism, ruling they failed to show the Ivy League school engaged in intentional discrimination.

title: UK Could Miss 2030 Clean Power Goal, Parliament Committee Warns
content: The UK’s goal of a clean power grid by 2030 is in danger of slipping out of reach as planning delays and infrastructure bottlenecks challenge the government.

title: Reeves Fights Back Against Cuts Narrative With UK Building Blitz
content: Chancellor of the Exchequer Rachel Reeves will detail hundreds of billions of pounds worth of projects to fix Britain’s creaking infrastructure during next week’s spending review, a crunch moment for Keir Starmer’s administration as it struggles to regain momentum after a faltering first year in power.

title: Outspoken South Korea Leftist Survived Stabbing on Path to Power
content: Lee Jae-myung, the tenacious left-leaning maverick who became South Korea’s new president Wednesday, has spent a lifetime picking himself off the canvas to fight again.

title: Trump Revokes Biden-Era Rule on Emergency Abortions in Hospitals
content: The Trump administration rescinded guidance put in place by former President Joe Biden that directed US hospitals to provide abortions on an emergency basis when they’re medically necessary to stabilize patients.

title: US Farm Sentiment at 4-Year High as Trump Seeks Trade Deals
content: American farmer sentiment jumped to a four-year high, with growers betting on rising crop exports as the Trump administration pushes for more trade deals from Vietnam to Italy.

title: Mexico Vote for Top Court Shows Majority With Morena Ties
content: Mexico’s new Supreme Court will feature a clear majority of justices with direct ties to the country’s former leftist president or the ruling Morena party he founded, according to preliminary election results with nearly all votes counted.

title: Trump Asks Congress to Slash Funds for NPR, PBS and Foreign Aid
content: President Donald Trump asked lawmakers to cut more than $9 billion in funding for the Public Broadcasting Service, National Public Radio and foreign aid from this year’s budget, an attempt to write into law some of the so-called “DOGE cuts” initiated by Elon Musk’s Department of Government Efficiency.

content: Remy Cointreau SA withdrew its long-term sales guidance, blaming tariff policies in America and China and a stunted recovery in the US market.

The government’s latest defense review set out plans to rebuild stockpiles, expand the nation’s nuclear deterrence and submarine fleet as well as invest more heavily in long-range weapons and advanced tech like drones and lasers. title: Climate Investor Energize Raises $430 Million for New VC Fund
content: The climate tech investment firm Energize Capital has raised $430 million for a new fund targeting early-stage startups working on projects like new batteries and software for the electric grid.

title: Marathon’s Richards Raises Caution on Direct Lending to Software Firms
content: Handing out private loans to software technology companies is not “intelligent,” said Marathon Asset Management Chief Executive Officer and founder Bruce Richards.

title: Mark Zuckerberg’s AI Slop Will Make Ads Creepier and Worse
content: As Meta grabs for more control over how companies talk to customers, the rest of us may be left flooded in more algorithmic mediocrity.

title: Microsoft Cuts Hundreds of Jobs After Firing 6,000 in May
content: Microsoft Corp. cut hundreds more jobs just weeks after its largest layoff in years, underscoring the tech industry’s efforts to trim costs even as it plows billions of dollars into artificial intelligence.

title: Meta’s Deal for Nuclear Power Is Likely Cheaper Than Microsoft’s, Jefferies Says
content: Surging demand for power to run artificial intelligence just prompted Meta Platforms Inc. to enter a 20-year contract with the biggest US nuclear operator, penning a deal that’s likely to be priced at a cheaper rate than a similar agreement rival Microsoft Corp. entered last year.

title: Kuwait Wealth Fund Joins Microsoft, MGX’s $30 Billion AI Venture
content: Kuwait’s sovereign wealth fund is joining a Microsoft Corp.-backed initiative to bankroll $30 billion in artificial intelligence infrastructure globally, as the oil-rich Gulf nation looks to tap into the booming sector.

title: Broadcom Ships New Gear Meant to Improve AI Chip Performance
content: Data center switch will let customers get more from their Nvidia processors

title: Chinese EV Maker Nio to Reduce R&D Costs to Hit Break-Even Goal
content: Nio Inc. aims to reduce research and development spending by as much as 25% as it seeks to reach its break-even target by the fourth quarter.

title: Musk’s X Aims to Soothe EU Regulators With Blue Check Disclaimer
content: Elon Musk’s social network X is showing users a prominent disclaimer about the platform’s blue checkmark program in a bid to appease concerns from the European Union’s content regulators that it’s deceptive and should be overhauled.

title: Meta to Buy Nuclear Power From Constellation as AI Demand Soars
content: Constellation Energy Corp. agreed to sell power from an Illinois nuclear plant to Meta Platforms Inc. as artificial intelligence sends power demand soaring.

title: Victoria’s Secret Says Security Incident That Shut Down Website May Hurt Results
content: Victoria’s Secret & Co. said a security incident that caused it to shut down its e-commerce site may hurt results for the current quarter.

title: Prosus President and Chief Investment Officer Tu to Resign
content: Prosus NV’s President and Chief Investment Officer Ervin Tu will step down from his role after a nearly four-year tenure during which the South African-Dutch tech investment company restructured itself and appointed a new chief executive officer.

title: Cracking the Code of Making Old Clothes New Again
content: Discarded clothing is an environmental scourge. But across Europe, companies are joining forces to build new technologies that could make recycling scalable.

title: Huawei’s Pura X Is An Intriguing New Foldable — If You’re Outside the US
content: Review: The clamshell device is the company’s first flagship phone to launch with its new operating system to challenge iOS and Android.

title: Former Key SpaceX Engineer’s Impulse Space Raises $300 Million
content: Impulse Space raised $300 million in its latest funding round as the US-based startup looks to cash in on demand for its highly agile spacecraft.

title: Ex-Lebanese PM Sets Up Abu Dhabi Investment Firm Targeting AI
content: Former Lebanese Prime Minister Saad Hariri is launching an investment firm in Abu Dhabi, deepening his ties to the capital of the United Arab Emirates.

title: China’s Manus Shows the Promise of AI Agents: Review
content: Welcome to Tech In Depth, our daily newsletter with reporting and analysis about the business of tech from Bloomberg’s journalists around the world. Today, Newley Purnell tests out the Manus AI agent.

title: AI Drug Startup Touts Promising Advance in Treating Lung Disease

title: Putin’s War Economy Roars Ahead and the Rest of Russia Struggles
content: The rift in Russia’s two-track economy is becoming wider as businesses tied to President Vladimir Putin’s invasion of Ukraine thrive and the rest are struggling for resources.

title: Trump Gives UK Five-Week Deadline After Reprieve on Steel Tariff

title: Tariffs, North Korea Cast Shadow Over Lee’s First Day in Office

Pan says clients are now looking at markets such as Japan, Singapore and Europe to diversify. It's a change from high net worth individuals who were previously more focused on China and the US. content: A US judge ruled that the Trump administration violated the due-process rights of more than 100 Venezuelans deported to a notorious prison in El Salvador, and they must now get a chance to challenge their removal.
