title: Romanian Inflation Climbs to One-Year High as Leu Hit Record Low
content: Romanian inflation accelerated in May after the leu’s decline to a record low during a recent political crisis boosted costs of goods and services.

title: China Found World’s Pain Point on Trade — and Will Use It Again
content: For months Donald Trump pushed tariffs and trade restrictions on China to unprecedented levels, part of a strategy to force Xi Jinping into talks the US president expected would help cut the trade deficit and boost American manufacturing.

title: Trump Open to Dialogue With Kim Jong Un, White House Says
content: President Donald Trump remains open to communications with North Korean leader Kim Jong Un, the White House said in its latest comments expressing willingness to resume dialogue with the nuclear-armed North, despite little signal from Kim seeking engagement.

title: India Central Bank Sends Conflicting Signs With Policy Moves
content: India’s central bank under new Governor Sanjay Malhotra is giving market participants conflicting signals about monetary policy as it takes aggressive steps to spur economic growth and lending.

title: Bulgarians Are Getting the Euro, But Half of Them Don’t Want It
content: People are growing more concerned about the potential impact on prices.

title: Serbia Seen Resuming Rate Cuts After Long Pause: Decision Guide
content: Serbia is poised to cut borrowing costs for the first time since September as inflation approaches the central bank’s target and economic growth slows.

title: East African Finance Chiefs Face Fiscal Tightrope in Budgets
content: East African finance ministers will be walking a tightrope when they reveal their spending plans on Thursday, with ballooning debt, underperforming revenue and geopolitics challenging planned fiscal consolidation.

title: CDPQ Looks to Trim US Assets as CEO Worries About Stagflation
content: The head of Caisse de Dépôt et Placement du Québec said it’s time for the fund to scale back on US investments after years of growth and great returns.

title: Japan’s Firms See Business Climate Worsen on Tariff Hits
content: Japan’s largest businesses turned pessimistic for the first time in more than a year as Donald Trump’s sweeping tariffs upended key sectors, a development that could complicate the Bank of Japan’s policy path.

title: NZ’s Willis Criticizes RBNZ Handling of Orr Resignation
content: New Zealand Finance Minister Nicola Willis has criticized the Reserve Bank for its handling of former Governor Adrian Orr’s resignation, saying it should have been more transparent about his reason for quitting.

title: Sperling Sees Enduring US-China Trade Tensions, Volatility Ahead
content: Trade tensions between the U.S. and China are unlikely to ease soon despite a recent thaw on tariffs, according to Gene Sperling of Pacific Investment Management Co., who warns market volatility is likely to persist.

title: Australia Inflation Expectations Rise to Highest Since 2023
content: Australia’s expected inflation rate rose to 5.0% in June, the highest level since July 2023, according to a survey released by the Melbourne Institute.

title: Trump’s Auto Tariffs Strike at the Heart of Japan’s Economy
content: Toyota, Honda, Subaru and other Japanese carmakers brace for a profit hit of more than $19 billion as economists flag the risk of a recession and a setback for key wage cycle

title: Asia’s Easing Prices Pave Path for Rate Cuts and US Divergence
content: Inflation is easing across Asia as lower food and fuel prices and stronger local currencies against the dollar push down costs. That’s giving the region’s central bank chiefs scope to support their trade-reliant economies as the risk of US tariffs and related uncertainty weigh on the outlook.

title: Trump Says Again He’ll Set Unilateral Tariffs in Two Weeks
content: President Donald Trump said he intended to send letters to trading partners in the next one to two weeks setting unilateral tariff rates, ahead of a July 9 deadline to reimpose higher duties on dozens of economies.

title: UK House Price Indicator Slides to 10-Month Low as Market Cools
content: A closely watched index of UK property prices declined to its lowest in almost a year, suggesting the housing market remains under pressure after a tax break for buyers expired.

title: RBNZ Policymaker’s Closed-Door Talk Raises Transparency Concerns
content: An external member of the Reserve Bank of New Zealand’s Monetary Policy Committee will give a rare presentation today, but it will be behind closed doors.

title: US Tariff Revenue Hits Fresh Record, Helping Shrink May Deficit
content: US customs duties climbed to a record in May, helping shrink the budget deficit for the month, while doubts remain about the persistence of the inflows as the Trump administration negotiates with trading partners and faces a judicial challenge over its levies.

title: Bessent Says $2 Trillion Reasonable for Dollar Stablecoin Market
content: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said that dollar-linked stablecoins could hit $2 trillion or even more as he reiterated the potential for these digital assets to strengthen the greenback’s position in the global financial system.

title: Why China Can Afford to Wait for a Deal, and the US Can’t
content: On this episode of Trumponomics, we discuss the status of Washington’s trade war negotiations with Beijing, and why Xi Jinping still has the upper hand.

title: US Tariffs Threaten to Derail Vietnam’s Historic Industrial Boom
content: An economic boom lifted the country of 100 million out of poverty. Then came the Trump rug-pull.

title: Trump Says China Will Ship Rare Earths in ‘Done’ Trade Deal
content: President Donald Trump said a trade framework with China has been completed, with Beijing supplying rare earths and magnets “UP FRONT” and the US allowing Chinese students into its colleges and universities.

title: Bank of France Cuts Growth Forecasts as Trade Tensions Hit
content: The Bank of France cut its economic-growth and inflation forecasts through 2027 as the fallout from US tariffs dulls activity in Europe.

title: US Makes Export Controls Negotiable as Part of China Trade Talks
content: Trade talks between the US and China this week cemented a seismic change in Washington’s approach to the countries’ economic relationship: US export curbs, meant to keep sensitive technologies out of Beijing’s hands, are now explicitly up for negotiation.

title: Canada and US Exchange Working Document on Trade Deal, CBC Says
content: US and Canadian officials are exchanging a document outlining potential trade deal terms, CBC News reported on Wednesday, citing anonymous sources, who said the paper is seen as a step toward a new trade pact.

title: Bessent Says ‘Remains to Be Seen’ Whether Tax Bill Adds to Debt
content: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent refrained from arguing that the tax legislation Republicans are working to finalize in Congress will avoid adding to the debt burden.

title: EU Likely to Be at ‘Very End’ of US Trade Deals, Lutnick Says
content: Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick said the European Union is likely to be among the last deals that the US completes, as the administration rushes to secure tariff agreements with other trading partners.

title: Tesco Private-Label Foods Fueled Sales Gain Last Quarter
content: Tesco Plc’s sales increased more than expected as the supermarket chain sold more premium and own-brand products.

title: Sumitomo Realty Seeks Office Sale After Elliott Takes Stake
content: Sumitomo Realty & Development Co., the Japanese developer facing pressure from Elliott Investment Management to boost its value, is seeking to sell a group of office properties in Tokyo for at least ¥100 billion ($700 million), according to people with knowledge of the matter.

title: Thai Exporters Face $600 Million in Added Costs as Port Congestion Worsens

title: DHL to Invest €500 Million on Africa, Middle East Expansion
content: Logistics giant DHL Group plans to invest about €500 million ($575 million) in health-care services in Africa and the Middle East over the next five years to capitalize on China‘s push into the regions.

title: China Gets First Private Builder Dollar Bond Offering Since 2023

title: Toyota Shareholders Vote to Reappoint Chairman Akio Toyoda

title: China Likely to Ditch Low-Grade Coal From Indonesia Due to Glut

content: A senior Trump administration official said that Huawei Technologies Co.’s ability to produce AI semiconductors will be very limited this year, responding to US lawmakers’ concerns that China is gaining ground in production of advanced semiconductors.

title: Trump Says US Will Have ‘Golden Share’ in US Steel
content: President Donald Trump says the US government will retain a “golden share” in United States Steel after its purchase by Japan’s Nippon Steel.

title: Trump Calls California’s EV Mandate a ‘Disaster’
content: President Donald Trump signed mandates that revoke California clean air policies, including requirements that carmakers sell electric vehicles in greater numbers each year in the state.

title: Tesla Sues Ex-Optimus Engineer Alleging Theft of Robotic Trade Secrets
content: Tesla Inc. sued a former engineer with the company’s highly secretive Optimus program, accusing him of stealing confidential information about the humanoid robot and setting up a rival startup in Silicon Valley.

title: UK Pension Intervention Will Unlock Capital, Tech Minister Says
content: The London Stock Exchange is under-capitalized and the UK government’s plan to intervene in pension funds — forcing them to invest in private companies — will boost the amount of money being pumped into the economy, Technology Secretary Peter Kyle said.

title: Arm CEO Sides With Nvidia on US Export Limits on China
content: Arm Holdings Plc CEO Rene Haas aligned himself with Nvidia Corp. Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang in saying that US export controls on China threaten to slow overall technological advances and are ultimately bad for consumers and companies. Haas spoke Thursday in an interview with Bloomberg at the Founders Forum Global conference in Oxford.

title: Synthesia CEO Riparbelli on Tech Opportunities in Europe
content: Synthesia CEO Victor Riparbelli says ongoing political tension has created better opportunities for entrepreneurs to build companies as focus shifts away from regulation and into the technology and defense sectors. He speaks with Bloomberg's Tom Mackenzie at the Founders Forum in Oxfordshire. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Why Voyager Shares Are Jumping After Upsized IPO
content: Voyager Technologies shares ended their debut trading day up 82% after the company raised $383 million in an upsized US initial public offering. Norah Mulinda reports on “Bloomberg Open Interest.”

title: Micron Pledges $200 Billion Investment in US Manufacturing
content: Chipmaker Micron Technology Inc. said it will spend about $200 billion on US manufacturing, research and development, the latest company to pledge large-scale investments in the country since President Donald Trump won election.

title: Micron to Invest About $200B in US Chip Manufacturing
content: Micron Technology said it will spend about $200 billion on US manufacturing, research and development. The spending will include roughly $150 billion for domestic manufacturing capacity and another $50 billion for R&D. Jake Silverman has more on “Bloomberg The Open.”

title: Mattel Taps OpenAI to Help It Design Toys, Other Products
content: The first release from the collaboration is expected later this year.

title: CoreWeave Shorts Face 150% Borrow Costs After $1.6 Billion Loss
content: CoreWeave Inc.’s soaring share price is torching short sellers who are paying high prices to bet that the stock will soon fall back to earth.

title: Yahoo Adds New AI Features to Mail App in Attempt to Up Usage
content: Yahoo is rolling out new artificial intelligence features for its email platform in an effort to better engage one of its fast-growing subset of users: Gen Z and millennials.

title: Arm CEO Sides With Nvidia Against US Export Limits on China
content: Arm Holdings Plc Chief Executive Officer Rene Haas said Thursday that US export controls on China threaten to slow overall technological advances and are ultimately bad for consumers and companies, aligning himself with Nvidia Corp. title: China’s Economy Withstood Trade Chaos But Momentum Likely Slowed
content: The Chinese economy rode out the tariff rollercoaster in May even as domestic consumption likely weakened again, after the government’s massive fiscal stimulus and frontloading by exporters offset shocks from abroad.

title: India, US Harden Trade Stance as July Tariff Deadline Nears
content: Trade officials from India and the US have hardened their stance on some key issues as they race to conclude an interim deal before higher US tariffs take effect in July, people familiar with the matter said.

title: Israeli Attack on Iran Raises Risk of Wider Conflict, Bloomberg Economics Says
content: Israel’s attack on the Iranian nuclear program and its ballistic missile sites threatens to spark wider fighting in the Middle East that risks drawing in the US, according to Bloomberg Economics.

title: Caller ID Is Destroying Our Understanding of the Jobs Market
content: Britain’s statistics crisis is not unique — modern technology and changing habits are causing problems in many countries

title: BOJ Is Said to See Inflation Running Stronger Than Expected

title: A $115 Billion Fund Manager Bets on Shortest Maturity India Debt
content: India’s economic growth is set to accelerate sharply, making the ultra short-end of the debt market the most attractive segment, according to one of the country’s top money managers.

title: Akazawa Sees a Deal With US Sparing Japan From Higher Car Levies
content: Japan’s top trade negotiator expects a trade deal with the US to spare Tokyo from higher auto tariffs, even if US President Donald Trump decides to increase them against other nations.

title: South Korea’s Lee to Meet Chaebol Heads in Bid to Revive Economy
content: South Korean President Lee Jae-myung will meet the heads of the country’s biggest conglomerates Friday, as he seeks to jumpstart a flagging economy while navigating tensions over his reform agenda aimed at curbing the dominance that chaebols wield over the corporate landscape.

title: Peru Holds Key Rate as Policymakers Weigh Risks to Growth
content: Peru held interest rates unchanged as the central bank gauges whether US tariff policy will jeopardize its combination of the fastest growth and the lowest inflation among Latin America’s major economies.

title: Taxes and Tariffs Prompt UK Firms to Slow Hiring, Recruiters Say
content: British employers scaled back hiring further in May in the wake of the sharp tax increases imposed by the Labour government and US President Donald Trump’s trade war, according to a closely watched survey.

title: Xi Plays Long Game on US-China Trade as Trump Seeks Quick Wins
content: While Donald Trump hailed the outcome of trade talks in London, Xi Jinping walked away with an understated strategic gain: a negotiating process that buys China time and helps defuse the threat of more harmful tariffs and technology curbs.

title: Wealthy Australians Brace for a New Tax on Retirement Savings
content: Australia is forging ahead with a new tax on its richest retirement savers amid concerns that the country’s A$4.1 trillion ($2.7 trillion) pensions system is becoming a high-wealth accumulation vehicle.

title: China Forced to Keep Unprofitable Firms Alive to Save Jobs and Avoid Unrest
content: Saddled with the most loss-making industrial companies since 2001, Xi Jinping is trying to clean up his economy without triggering mass layoffs.

title: Argentina Inflation Hits Lowest Since Covid in Win for Milei
content: Argentina’s monthly inflation slowed to the lowest level since the height of the pandemic, scoring a major victory for President Javier Milei ahead of a crucial midterm vote.

title: Key Senator Looks to Slow Ted Cruz Plan on Fed Interest to Banks

title: IMF Sees Unwinding of Global Trade Surge Ahead of Trump Tariffs

content: The co-founder of bankrupt genetic analysis company 23andMe won an auction for the firm’s assets, agreeing, along with a California research institute, to pay $305 million for a cache of customer DNA data

content: JPMorgan Chase & Co. plans to kick off a $6.5 billion debt offering to support private equity firm 3G Capital’s purchase of footwear maker Skechers as soon as next week, according to a person with knowledge of the matter.

title: Belgium’s Credit Rating Cut by Fitch as Budget Concerns Linger
content: Belgium’s sovereign credit was cut by Fitch Ratings, signaling an increase in uncertainty about the country’s ability to rein in years of substantial debt accumulation.

title: Columbia Graduate Still in Custody After Frantic Day of Appeals
content: A Columbia University graduate who participated in pro-Palestinian protests will remain in custody at an immigration facility after a federal judge said the government could detain him over alleged problems with his green card application.

title: Rational Moves in the Market: Nuveen's Persson
content: The conflict between Iran and Israel sent volatility through the global markets, Nuveen CIO for Global Fixed Income Anders Persson says the moves though have been "rational”. He speaks with Sonali Basak on "Real Yield." (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Wall Street’s Momentum Machine Faces a Middle East Stress Test
content: It’s the kind of geopolitical flashpoint that might once have triggered a full-blown market meltdown: Israeli warplanes struck Iranian nuclear sites, Tehran vowed revenge — then followed through. Oil spiked.

title: Dollar’s Tepid Rebound Reinforces Questions Around Haven Role
content: The dollar’s muted rally against major peers after Israel’s strikes on Iran reinforced the impression that the greenback’s role as a global haven currency is fading.

title: Dye & Durham’s Ex-CFO Urges Sale After Stock Drops, Debt Mounts
content: A former senior executive and shareholder of Canadian technology firm Dye & Durham Ltd. is asking the board to consider a full sale of the company, citing a plunge in shareholder value and growing competitive pressures.

title: Travel Stocks Sink, Energy Soars as Israel Strikes Iran
content: Israel’s strikes on Iran rippled through the US stock market on Friday, sinking shares of travel companies and lifting energy and defense stocks as traders braced for the possibility of a wider Middle East conflict.

title: Stocks Sink, Oil Jumps as Mideast Tensions Build: Markets Wrap
content: Wall Street buckled as reports of Iran’s retaliation for Israel’s attack on its nuclear facilities deepened concerns that the conflict is escalating, with oil jumping and stocks taking a hit.

title: S&P 500 Suffers Weekly Loss as Middle East Conflict Intensifies
content: The US stock market snapped a two-week winning streak as investors piled into safe haven assets after Israel launched military strikes on Iran, followed by retaliation from Tehran, with traders fearing the clash may spiral into a wider global and economic conflict.

title: Trump Plans Biofuel Quota Boost, Seeks to Crimp Imports
content: The Trump administration is proposing oil refiners blend more biofuels into gasoline and diesel next year, while seeking to discourage the use of imported supplies.

title: Felicis Ventures Raises Its Largest Fund
content: Felicis Ventures Managing Partner Sundeep Peechu discusses how the firm plans to target AI investments with its latest $900 million fundraise. Peechu joins Caroline Hyde on “Bloomberg Tech.” (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Hedge Funds Ramped Up Bullish Oil Bets Ahead of Israel’s Attack
content: Hedge funds took the most bullish stance on US crude since January in the week before Israel launched strikes against Iran’s nuclear program, putting them in a position to profit from this week’s jump in oil prices.

title: Europe Set to Move a Step Closer to Halting Russian Gas Imports
content: The European Union is expected to take a major step next week toward curbing Russian gas imports starting next year with aims to sever ties with its former top supplier by the end of 2027.

title: Addressing AI’s Impact on the Gender Gap
content: Artificial intelligence data sets need to better represent women, says Shubhi Rao, Founder and CEO of Uplevyl, a platform designed to accelerate women in the workplace. Rao speaks with Caroline Hyde on “Bloomberg Tech.” (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu Addresses The People of Iran
content: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu addressed the people of Iran directly after an early morning military strike. He warned "more is on the way." (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Iran Says Talks With US Now ‘Meaningless’ After Israeli Strikes
content: Iran said further nuclear talks with the US are now “meaningless” after Israel’s strikes, Tehran Times reported, citing Esmaeil Baghaei, a spokesman for the foreign ministry.

title: Keir Starmer: ‘We Are Gravely Concerned’
content: The UK’s prime minister is focused on de-escalating the Israel-Iran conflict, and sees a path forward for Ukraine and a US-UK trade deal.

title: Iran Launches New Attack Wave on Israel as Conflict Widens
content: Iran fired hundreds of ballistic missiles against Israel following an unprecedented direct attack on its nuclear facilities, ramping up a conflict between sworn enemies that threatens to engulf the Middle East and disrupt global oil supplies.

title: Marines Move Into Los Angeles as Newsom Fights Deployment
content: US Marines who are part of a military deployment ordered by President Donald Trump have arrived at the Wilshire Federal Building in Los Angeles, positioning them miles away from the areas where protests spurred by immigration raids have taken place.

title: US Steel Sale to Nippon Steel Poised To Close After Trump Deal
content: Nippon Steel Corp. won conditional US approval for its $14.1 billion purchase of United States Steel Corp., capping a lengthy saga in a tie-up that will create one of the world’s largest steel companies.

title: Colombia Activates Fiscal ‘Escape Clause’ and Plans Tax Hike
content: Colombia activated an “escape clause” to suspend borrowing limits as the finance ministry forecasts the widest fiscal deficit since the pandemic.

title: Key Iran Nuclear Enrichment Site of Natanz Shows No Sign of Breach
content: The United Nations atomic watchdog said Israeli strikes destroyed several facilities at Iran’s main uranium-enrichment site of Natanz but not the underground area where uranium enrichment takes place.

title: Trump Urged Ergen, Carr to Cut a Deal on EchoStar Spectrum
content: President Donald Trump has intervened to push EchoStar Corp. and Federal Communications Commission Chairman Brendan Carr to resolve a dispute over the satellite communications company’s valuable spectrum licenses.

title: US Opposes European Push to Lower G-7 Price Cap on Russian Oil
content: The US isn’t budging from its opposition to a lower price cap on Russian oil sales, people familiar with the matter said, dampening European hopes that leaders meeting for a Group of Seven summit in Canada will agree to a cut.

title: Trump Eyes Nominating FTC Commissioner for Utah US Attorney

content: Missouri Governor Mike Kehoe is activating National Guard troops to support local law enforcement, joining Texas in turning to military personnel ahead of nationwide protests on Saturday against President Donald Trump.

title: Netanyahu Pulls Trigger on Iran Attack After 30-Year Wait
content: Benjamin Netanyahu has said for three decades that the central threat to Israel’s existence is Iran’s nuclear program. At least twice over that period, he came within inches of carrying out an attack on it.

title: Israel Attacks Iran’s Nuclear Sites, Kills Senior Commanders
content: Israel launched strikes across Iran on Friday morning, targeting nuclear facilities and killing top military commanders in a major escalation against its chief adversary that risks sparking a broad war in the Middle East.

title: US, Vietnam Move Closer to Trade Framework as Deadline Nears
content: The US and Vietnam are closing in on a framework trade agreement, despite ongoing concerns about Chinese goods being rerouted through the Southeast Asian nation to avoid tariffs, according to people familiar with the talks.

title: US to Ease Rules Hindering Tesla’s Self-Driving Cybercab
content: The Trump administration is taking steps that would make it easier for automakers to deploy-self driving cars without driver controls, a potential boon to the ambitions of Tesla Inc. and rivals looking to put robotaxis on US roads in the near future.

title: Dutch Cabinet Approves NATO’s 5% Defense Spending Target
content: Dutch Prime Minister Dick Schoof’s caretaker cabinet agreed to increase defense and security spending to 5% of gross domestic product by 2032 in line with the North Atlantic Treaty Organization’s proposed target.

title: Four Men Escape From ICE-Contracted Detention Facility in Newark
content: Four people detained by US Immigration and Customs Enforcement escaped from a privately operated detention facility in Newark, New Jersey, a senior Homeland Security official told Bloomberg News.

title: Starmer Signals Support for 3.5% NATO Aim With Talks on Date
content: Prime Minister Keir Starmer indicated that the UK was prepared to endorse a new NATO target committing 3.5% of members’ economic output to core defense spending, although he emphasized that key details such as the timeline were still being negotiated.

title: Germany’s Klingbeil to Support Push to End EU Capital-Markets Impasse
content: German Finance Minister and Vice Chancellor Lars Klingbeil said he’ll support a push to try to break a deadlock on a decade-old European Union effort to deepen the bloc’s capital markets.

title: NY Lawmakers Near Deadline to Pass Bill Targeting Emerging Market ‘Vulture Funds’
content: New York state lawmakers are within days of a deadline to pass legislation targeting so-called vulture funds that has languished in the local legislature for the past two years.

title: Battle Over Sports Betting Threatens Lula’s New Fiscal Plan
content: A fierce lobbying push by sports betting companies is threatening to bring down the Brazilian government’s plan to raise revenues and hit fiscal goals after the lower house speaker backed off support for a deal he helped broker.

title: Oil Tanker Market Roiled by Israeli Airstrikes Against Iran
content: Israel’s overnight airstrikes on Iran drove up freight rates and tanker stocks Friday as traders and investors priced in the prospect of disruption to a large swath of the global oil-shipping fleet.

title: Keir Starmer Says UK Is Luring Top Talent Even as Non-Doms Leave
content: UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer said he wants to attract more investors to Britain, even as the nation contends with an exodus of wealthy individuals because of tax hikes.

title: India and Canada Reach Deal to Share Intelligence on Terrorism, Crime
content: The governments of Canada and India are set to establish a new structure to share information about cross-border crimes, their latest step toward rebuilding ties nearly two years after Canadian officials accused India of orchestrating the murder of a Sikh activist near Vancouver.

title: Starmer Says UK Has ‘Grave Concerns’ on Iran Nuclear Program
content: Prime Minister Keir Starmer said the UK has “grave concerns” about Iran’s nuclear program and backed Israel’s right to self-defense, while calling for de-escalation in a conflict that risks engulfing the Middle East.

title: Trump Wants to Make It More Expensive to Sue Over His Policies
content: President Donald Trump and his allies are pursuing an alternative strategy to defend against mounting court orders blocking his policies: Raise the financial stakes for those suing the administration.

content: Flooding and thunderstorms are threatening disruption for large parts of the UK on Saturday, hot on the heels of the warmest day of the year to date.

content: Wayne Sanders, Bloomberg Intelligence senior defense analyst, reacts to retaliatory strikes on Tel Aviv as Israel continues its attacks on Iran's nuclear program. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Balance of Power: Israel Attacks Iran’s Nuclear Sites (Podcast)
content: Source: Bloomberg, 40:32

title: Ramp Hits $16 Billion Valuation in New Funding Round
content: Financial technology startup Ramp is now valued at $16 billion following a $200 million funding round, according to a person familiar with the matter.

title: Relativity Space Said to Reverse Stock Split After Schmidt Deal
content: Relativity Space Inc., a maker of 3D-printed rockets, enacted a reverse stock split that has significantly diluted existing shareholders and staff, according to people familiar with the matter.

title: Neuralink Device Helps Monkey See Something That’s Not There
content: Elon Musk’s Neuralink Corp. used a brain implant to enable a monkey to see something that wasn’t physically there, according to an engineer, as it moves toward its goal of helping blind people see.

title: Meta's $14.3B Scale Investment, Apple's New Siri Launch | Bloomberg Tech 6/13/2025
content: Bloomberg’s Caroline Hyde breaks down Meta’s plans to take a 49% stake in Scale AI and hire the startup's CEO, Alexandr Wang. Plus, the CEO of stablecoin network Circle discusses how the passing of the GENIUS Act could impact the payments space. And Apple targets the spring of 2026 for the launch of its revamped voice assistant Siri, as the iPhone maker plays catch-up in the AI race. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Adobe Slips After Revenue Outlook Fails to Sway AI Skeptics
content: Adobe Inc. shares fell the most in three months after the creative-software company gave a sales outlook for the current quarter that failed to calm investors who have been skeptical it can hold its own against AI-focused upstarts.

title: Drone Maker Airo Jumps 140% in Latest Post-IPO Debut Pop
content: Airo Group Holdings Inc. shares climbed 140% in their public trading debut on Friday after the company raised $60 million in an initial public offering, becoming the third company this month to more than double during its opening session.

title: Google’s Plan to Buy Security Firm Wiz Gets Antitrust Review
content: Justice Department antitrust enforcers are reviewing whether Google’s planned $32 billion acquisition of cybersecurity company Wiz Inc. would illegally limit competition in the marketplace, according to people with knowledge of the matter.

title: Scale AI Backer Accel Set for $2.5 Billion Windfall on Meta Deal
content: Accel is among a handful of VC firms poised to see big returns from early bets on Scale AI.

title: A $60 Billion Visa, Mastercard Slump Seen as Buying Opportunity
content: A report that large multinational merchants are exploring ways to bypass traditional credit-card fees presents investors with an opportunity to buy shares of Mastercard Inc. and Visa Inc., according to Wall Street analysts.

title: Trump Seeks to Register His Name for Mobile Phone Service
content: DTTM Operations LLC, the entity that manages trademarks on behalf of President Donald Trump, has applied to use his name and the term T1 for telecom services.

title: Centerview Is Sole Bank on Meta’s $14 Billion AI Bet
content: One of the largest-ever investments in a private US company has minted just one investment banking winner: Centerview Partners.

title: Indie Music’s Growing Backlash Against the State of Streaming
content: As the streaming model evolves, tensions are building throughout the music industry

title: How ‘Hitman’ Developer Became One of the Largest Independent Game Companies
content: Eight years ago, IO Interactive was bleeding money. Now it’s one of the biggest privately owned video-game companies in the world.

title: Ransomware Plague Targeting Hospitals Comes to Ohio
content: Demonstrators drive trucks down interstate 70 as part of a Peoples Convoy 'Freedom and Accountability' caravan in Dayton, Ohio, U.S., on Thursday, March 3, 2022. The People's Convoy have called on President Joe Biden to end vaccine and other pandemic mandates while modeling themselves after Canadian drivers who had occupied the center of Ottawa in a similar protest.

title: Ships’ Electronics Increasingly Jammed Since Israel Struck Iran
content: Israel’s airstrikes on Iran have led to increased jamming of the signals of vessels operating in the Middle East, the world’s largest oil producing region, a multinational naval force protecting maritime trade said.

title: Micron Plans $200 Billion US Chip Spend, Chime IPO | Bloomberg Tech 6/12/2025
content: Bloomberg’s Caroline Hyde and Ed Ludlow discuss Micron’s plans to spend $200 billion on U.S. chip manufacturing and R&D. Plus, Chime CEO Chris Britt discusses the company’s growth strategy as the company goes public. And Oracle’s earnings impress investors with its rising cloud sales. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: OpenAI to Continue Working With Scale After Meta Deal, CFO Says
content: OpenAI said it will continue working with Scale AI after Meta Platforms Inc. made a multibillion-dollar investment in the startup, as it seeks to maintain a broad ecosystem of data sources.

title: How the Clippers Engineered the NBA’s Best Home Court Advantage
content: Reward the loudest fans and make sure there are lots and lots of bathrooms.

title: China Boosts Tesla Self-Driving Plan With Car-Data Export Rules
content: Chinese authorities released draft guidelines on transmitting data from automobiles overseas, a move that could pave the way for the wider rollout of Tesla Inc.’s most advanced driver-assistance functions in the world’s largest car market.

title: Abu Dhabi’s G42 Opens Europe Hub in Sign of Growing AI Ambition
content: Abu Dhabi’s main artificial intelligence company, G42, is launching a European unit as part of the emirate’s broader push into the continent, where the government has pledged billions of dollars in investment.

title: Meta Risks Regulatory Scrutiny in Pursuit of Scale AI
content: Welcome to Tech In Depth, our daily newsletter with reporting and analysis about the business of tech from Bloomberg’s journalists around the world. Today, Jackie Davalos reports on Big Tech’s “acqui-hire” strategy for artificial intelligence that is drawing scrutiny from regulators.

title: Big Tech Is Dealing Flat Design a Death Blow
content: From Airbnb’s new app icons to Apple’s “Liquid Glass” design, skeuomorphism is back and everything in the digital world has dimensionality again.

title: Taiyo to Decide on Delisting as Early as August, President Says
content: Taiyo Holdings Co. will decide on proposals from several private equity funds to delist it after a shareholder meeting this month, where its president is likely to face a vote on his ouster.

title: Tencent Studies Deal for ‘Dungeon & Fighter’ Developer Nexon
content: Tencent Holdings Ltd. is studying a potential deal for Nexon Co., as the Chinese internet giant looks for ways to bolster its lucrative gaming operations, people with knowledge of the matter said.

title: ECB Within Reach of 2% Inflation Goal, Lagarde Tells Xinhua
content: The European Central Bank is approaching its goal for consumer-price growth, President Christine Lagarde said, warning of uncertainty emanating from US tariffs.

title: Switzerland’s Likely Rate Cut to Zero Threatens to Test Banks
content: The Swiss National Bank’s next cut in borrowing costs may be about to cause a headache for banks, if officials end up experimenting with their first-ever interest rate of zero.

title: Japan Seeks Possibility of Trade Deal With US as G-7 Looms
content: Japan and the US held another round of trade talks in Washington as officials try to reach an agreement ahead of a Group of Seven summit in Canada and a meeting between President Donald Trump and Prime Minister Shigeru Ishiba.

title: Belgium’s Credit Rating Cut by Fitch as Budget Concerns Linger
content: Belgium’s sovereign credit was cut by Fitch Ratings, signaling an increase in uncertainty about the country’s ability to rein in years of substantial debt accumulation.

title: Port of LA Imports Drop 19% in May as Tariffs Hit US Businesses
content: Import volumes through the busiest trade hub in the US fell 19% from the month before, a fallout from President Donald Trump’s tariffs.

title: Bets Emerge That End to Powell’s Term Means More Fed Rate Cuts
content: The prospect of a shift in US monetary policy when President Donald Trump replaces Jerome Powell at the end of his term as Federal Reserve chair in May 2026 has interest-rate traders looking for pay dirt.

title: Dutch Cabinet Approves NATO’s 5% Defense Spending Target
content: Dutch Prime Minister Dick Schoof’s caretaker cabinet agreed to increase defense and security spending to 5% of gross domestic product by 2032 in line with the North Atlantic Treaty Organization’s proposed target.

title: Israel-Iran Conflict Risks More Inflation, Delayed Fed Rate Cuts
content: Israel’s attacks on Iran’s nuclear facilities risk pushing back the timeline for Federal Reserve interest-rate cuts as the US central bank waits to assess any potential impact on inflation, economists said.

title: Starmer Signals Support for 3.5% NATO Aim With Talks on Date
content: Prime Minister Keir Starmer indicated that the UK was prepared to endorse a new NATO target committing 3.5% of members’ economic output to core defense spending, although he emphasized that key details such as the timeline were still being negotiated.

title: Germany’s Klingbeil to Support Push to End EU Capital-Markets Impasse
content: German Finance Minister and Vice Chancellor Lars Klingbeil said he’ll support a push to try to break a deadlock on a decade-old European Union effort to deepen the bloc’s capital markets.

title: Indian Tax Authorities Chasing Unreported Crypto Transactions
content: Indian tax authorities are investigating tax evasion and money laundering by “high-risk persons” through cryptocurrency, a government official said Friday.

title: Oil Tanker Market Roiled by Israeli Airstrikes Against Iran
content: Israel’s overnight airstrikes on Iran drove up freight rates and tanker stocks Friday as traders and investors priced in the prospect of disruption to a large swath of the global oil-shipping fleet.

title: Keir Starmer Says UK Is Luring Top Talent Even as Non-Doms Leave
content: UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer said he wants to attract more investors to Britain, even as the nation contends with an exodus of wealthy individuals because of tax hikes.

title: Starmer Says UK Has ‘Grave Concerns’ on Iran Nuclear Program
content: Prime Minister Keir Starmer said the UK has “grave concerns” about Iran’s nuclear program and backed Israel’s right to self-defense, while calling for de-escalation in a conflict that risks engulfing the Middle East.

title: Starmer Says No Obstacles Left in Finishing US-UK Trade Deal
content: UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer said there are no “hiccups or obstacles” remaining in the way of finalizing a trade deal with the US and indicated that an agreement would likely come soon.

title: US Consumer Sentiment Jumps as Inflation Expectations Improve
content: US consumer sentiment rose by the most since January 2024 as concerns about the economy eased and short-term inflation expectations showed a marked improvement.

title: Netherlands Picks Sleijpen to Succeed Knot at Central Bank
content: The Dutch government appointed Olaf Sleijpen to head the central bank, sticking with an insider for the traditionally hawkish institution.

title: Trump Ripping Up the Free Trade Playbook Comes With $1 Trillion Cost
content: The ominous trajectory of the US president’s tariff overhaul looms over the G-7 gathering.

title: Japan’s Kato Says Talks With Markets Key for Bond Issuance
content: Japan’s Finance Minister said that discussions with market participants is a key factor in making sure that government bonds are bought and sold stably, as the ministry neared a closely watched gathering with investors.

title: US Corporate Profit Fat Offers Cushion for Absorbing Tariffs
content: I’m Ben Holland, an economics editor in Washington. Today we’re looking at the implications for inflation from US corporate profit margins. Send us feedback and tips to ecodaily@bloomberg.net. And if you aren’t yet signed up to receive this newsletter, you can do so here.

title: Wrecking Ball Trump Makes the G-7 More Necessary
content: The upcoming conclave in Canada may be the rare space to find common ground, even as the forum itself is looking increasingly outmoded.

title: UK Household Inflation Expectations Fell Before April CPI Spike
content: UK households had been expecting inflation to slow over the coming year, according to a Bank of England survey that was conducted before the sudden jump in consumer prices reported last month.

title: PSP Hunts for More Canada Deals as Assets Surge to $220 Billion
content: Canada’s Public Sector Pension Investment Board is looking to deploy more capital in its home country after years of global expansion that has pushed its investment portfolio to C$300 billion ($220 billion).

title: No Clarity for Fed Until at Least September, Economists Say
content: It will take months yet before the Federal Reserve can get a clear idea of how Trump administration policy changes will shape the US economy, making officials unlikely to consider a change to interest rates before September, according to economists surveyed by Bloomberg News.

title: South Africa Rail Firm Averts Strike as Unions Accept Deal
content: South Africa’s state-owned ports and freight-rail company reached a pay deal with its two recognized labor unions, averting a strike that threatened to disrupt mineral and agricultural exports.

title: Trump’s Chief Economist Downplays Fears of Investment Fallout From ‘Revenge Tax’
content: The White House’s chief economist dismissed concerns that a controversial provision in President Donald Trump’s tax-and-spending bill would drive away foreign bond investors, calling such fears a “misinterpretation.”

title: Korea’s Lee Urges Chaebols to Quell Distrust, Hears Trade Fears
content: South Korean President Lee Jae-myung called on the heads of the country’s largest conglomerates to help restore market trust while hearing out their concerns over the impact of Donald Trump’s tariffs on global trade.

title: HSBC Hastens Search to Find Next Chairman as Tucker’s Exit Nears
content: With the clock ticking in the hunt for HSBC Holdings Plc’s next chairman, Europe’s largest bank is speeding its efforts to assemble a list of candidates for the role.

title: US Steel Sale to Nippon Steel Poised To Close After Trump Deal
content: Nippon Steel Corp. won conditional US approval for its $14.1 billion purchase of United States Steel Corp., capping a lengthy saga in a tie-up that will create one of the world’s largest steel companies.

title: Grupo Mexico Will Sell Highway Business for $406 Million
content: Grupo Mexico, the copper mining conglomerate controlled by Mexican billionaire German Larrea, will sell its highway business for 7.7 billion pesos ($406 million) to local investment trusts FIBRAeMX and FEXI in the latest move to restructure the company.

title: Neuralink Device Helps Monkey See Something That’s Not There
content: Elon Musk’s Neuralink Corp. used a brain implant to enable a monkey to see something that wasn’t physically there, according to an engineer, as it moves toward its goal of helping blind people see.

title: FDA Tells Drugmaker ‘Heavy Workload’ to Delay Approval Decision
content: US regulators delayed their decision on whether to approve the first pill taken on demand for a rare, inherited swelling disorder due to a “heavy workload and limited resources,” a biotech company said.

title: Blackstone Said to Be in Talks to Buy Embattled Allegiant Resort
content: Blackstone Inc. is in talks to purchase Allegiant Travel Co.’s Sunseeker Resort, moving the parent of Allegiant Airlines closer to shedding the beleaguered retreat that had been a drag on earnings, according to people with knowledge of the matter.

title: Key Iran Nuclear Enrichment Site of Natanz Shows No Sign of Breach
content: The United Nations atomic watchdog said Israeli strikes destroyed several facilities at Iran’s main uranium-enrichment site of Natanz but not the underground area where uranium enrichment takes place.

title: Lilly’s Experimental Obesity Drug Shows Promise in Early Study
content: An experimental weight-loss drug from Eli Lilly & Co. helped patients lose weight with few side effects, according to the summary of a small study that suggests the company has another foothold in the obesity market.

title: Trump Plans Biofuel Quota Boost, Seeks to Crimp Imports
content: The Trump administration is proposing oil refiners blend more biofuels into gasoline and diesel next year, while seeking to discourage the use of imported supplies.

title: Hedge Funds Ramped Up Bullish Oil Bets Ahead of Israel’s Attack
content: Hedge funds took the most bullish stance on US crude since January in the week before Israel launched strikes against Iran’s nuclear program, putting them in a position to profit from this week’s jump in oil prices.

title: Europe Set to Move a Step Closer to Halting Russian Gas Imports
content: The European Union is expected to take a major step next week toward curbing Russian gas imports starting next year with aims to sever ties with its former top supplier by the end of 2027.

title: British Virgin Islands, Bolivia Put on Watchdog ‘Gray List’
content: The British Virgin Islands and Bolivia were added to a global financial watchdog’s “gray list” for shortcomings in combating illicit flows, a move that may hamper investor confidence and heighten bank scrutiny.

title: Boeing Delivers First Jet to China in Tariff War Reprieve
content: Boeing Co. delivered its first aircraft to a Chinese airline customer since President Donald Trump unleashed a wave of tariffs in early April, a sign of rapprochement as Washington and Beijing look to ease tensions.

title: Swiss Industrials Company Sika Sees Big India Opportunity
content: Sika AG Chief Executive Officer Thomas Hasler views the Indian market as being one of the biggest opportunities for the Swiss building products company over the next few years.

title: Kohl’s CEO Tries to Reverse Record-Low Morale in Latest Address
content: Kohl’s Corp.’s interim Chief Executive Officer Michael Bender tried to quell employee unrest during one of his first all-hands calls since replacing Ashley Buchanan last month.

title: Airbus Says Air India Accident Is Learning Moment for Industry
content: Airbus SE said the fatal accident on Thursday in India involving a Boeing Co. airliner should spur the industry as a whole to advance its safety culture, dismissing the notion that the crash could bring a competitive edge to one planemaker over the other in the global duopoly.

title: Key Oil Market Trades Are Lighting Up After Israel’s Attack
content: Israel’s extensive strikes against Iran’s nuclear facilities, a dramatic new turn in the conflict in the Middle East, are rippling across the energy market.

title: Chevron to Name Van Dyke Commodities Lead in Trading Revamp
content: Chevron Corp. is promoting some of its traders and offered voluntary severance to others as part of a restructuring of its trading division aimed at cutting costs and boosting performance.

title: Centerview Is Sole Bank on Meta’s $14 Billion AI Bet
content: One of the largest-ever investments in a private US company has minted just one investment banking winner: Centerview Partners.

title: Delta, United Suspend Flights to Tel Aviv After Iran Bombing
content: Delta Air Lines Inc. and United Airlines Holdings Inc. suspended flights to Tel Aviv following Israel’s bombing of Iran and the closure of Israel’s airspace.

title: FIFA to Splash $1 Billion of Prize Money on First Club World Cup
content: FIFA, the global governing body of international soccer, has lured some of the world’s top teams to the US for an inaugural Club World Cup with a record $1 billion to be distributed over the next month.

title: US to Ease Rules Hindering Tesla’s Self-Driving Cybercab
content: The Trump administration is taking steps that would make it easier for automakers to deploy-self driving cars without driver controls, a potential boon to the ambitions of Tesla Inc. and rivals looking to put robotaxis on US roads in the near future.

title: Oil Tanker Market Roiled by Israeli Airstrikes Against Iran
content: Israel’s overnight airstrikes on Iran drove up freight rates and tanker stocks Friday as traders and investors priced in the prospect of disruption to a large swath of the global oil-shipping fleet.

title: Banca Akros Says Monte Paschi Stake Sale Was in Full Compliance
content: Banco BPM SpA’s unit Banca Akros said it fully complied with the law and best practices as coordinator for the sale of an Italian government stake in Banca Monte dei Paschi di Siena SpA in November.

title: Lone Star’s Banking Bet Pays Off as BPCE Buys Novo Banco
content: Lone Star will sell its majority stake in Portugal’s Novo Banco SA to French banking group BPCE, earning the private equity firm a huge windfall from the bet it made on the sector’s recovery almost a decade ago.

title: From Hustling on Wall Street to Helping Turn Around the Florida Panthers
content: We’ve gone Q&A heavy this week. Normally we like to use this newsletter as a rare chance to pontificate, but sometimes we have to put our hands up and admit other people know a lot more than we do. We chat to the CEO of the Florida Panthers about how they’ve turned the team around, and what comes next now that college athletes are paid-up professionals. And we take a quick look at the Club World Cup again.

title: Boeing Returns to Crisis-Mode as India Crash Poses New Test
content: Boeing Co. Chief Executive Officer Kelly Ortberg finds himself in a painfully familiar role as he faces another crisis, this time over a crash involving the company’s marquee 787 Dreamliner jet in India that killed more than 240 people.

title: Trump Aid Pullback Spurs East African Nations to Action
content: Finance ministers across East Africa have boosted health spending after US President Donald Trump abruptly ended billions of dollars of aid to the continent earlier this year, sending a wake-up call for countries to be more self-reliant.

title: South Africa’s Ramaphosa to Lead Global Fund’s HIV Replenishment
content: South Africa will lead the next refunding exercise for the Global Fund, raising money for the international partnership fighting AIDS after the US cut healthcare support to the continent.

title: Very Possible This Iranian Regime Could Collapse, NUFDI's Khansarinia Says
content:
Israel and Iran continued intense bombardments of one another for a third day. The worst military assault on the Islamic Republic since it was invaded by Iraq in 1980 underscores how Tehran’s regional might has bean dealt a serious blow along with its inability to protect some of its most sensitive national assets and its 90 million citizens.

Cameron Khansarinia, Vice President for the National Union for Democracy in Iran, says the Islamic Republic is "probably at its weakest moment that it's ever been." He says with the head of Iran's armed forced killed, the psychological toll of the regime is very significant. 

"I think it's very possible that this regime collapses and we're looking at a entirely new Iran again, for policymakers, but also for investors," he adds.

Khansarinia joins Bloomeberg's Tom Mackenzie on "Daybreak: Europe." (Source: Bloomberg)

content: A planned meeting between President Donald Trump and Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese at the G-7 summit in Canada has been scrapped, following Trump's abrupt exit due to the escalating crisis in the Middle East. title: Auterion Strikes Deal With Taiwan for Unmanned Drone Software

title: SoftBank Sells T-Mobile Stake for $4.8 Billion to Fund AI Push

title: China Joins US in Brain Implant Race With Clinical Trial
content: China’s first clinical trial of a technology that allows signals from the brain to control an external device has shown early signs of success, making it only the second country after the US to reach this stage, according to the Global Times.

title: OpenAI Snags $200 Million Contract With US Defense Department
content: OpenAI has won a $200 million contract for a pilot program aimed at helping the US Defense Department determine how it could use artificial intelligence for a range of administrative and security tasks.

title: Hedge Fund Up 42% Last Year Offloads Its Biggest Winner Nvidia
content: Hedge fund founder Jonah Cheng calls Nvidia Corp. the best pick of his career. But he has now sold the last of his shares in the company, expressing doubts about the outlook for the $3.5 trillion chipmaker.

title: Washington Post Probes Hack of Journalist Email Accounts
content: The Washington Post is investigating a cyberattack on the email accounts of some journalists, prompting the newspaper to beef up its online security.

title: Trump To Launch Mobile Services, New Training for Robots | Bloomberg Tech 6/16/2025
content: Bloomberg’s Caroline Hyde and Ed Ludlow discuss the Trump family’s plan for a self-branded mobile phone service. Plus, Meta launches ads on the privacy-focused messaging service WhatsApp. And robotics firm 1X Technologies announces a new “World Model” to train robots on the physical world using data-driven simulations.  (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Warner Bros. Wins Support From Bondholders for Debt Overhaul
content: Warner Bros. Discovery Inc. said it won enough support from creditors to overhaul its debt as part of a plan to split into two separate companies, a significant victory for the entertainment giant as it tries to turn itself around.

title: Scale AI’s Wang Brings to Meta Knowledge of What Everyone Else is Doing
content: Scale AI co-founder Alexandr Wang is such an enthusiastic networker that his former roommate — OpenAI Chief Executive Officer Sam Altman — once jokingly told him to tone it down a bit.

title: SFR Working to Restore Wireless Service Across France With Fix
content: Phone carrier SFR said it’s working on restoring mobile service after an issue caused a widespread mobile network outage across France.

title: Nintendo Switch 2 Review: Bigger and Mostly Better
content: The second-generation Switch brings design improvements and faster performance, but the battery life and game selection underwhelm.

title: BC Partners-Backed Telco United Group Names KPN Alum as CEO
content: United Group, the southeastern European telecom operator owned by BC Partners, appointed former Royal KPN NV executive Stan Miller as chief executive officer.

title: Trump Family Launches Branded Mobile Phone Service in US
content: President Donald Trump’s family is getting into the mobile phone business with a Trump-branded service that will rely on pre-existing wireless networks and hardware that is “made in America.”

title: CoreWeave Downgraded But Gets Street-High Price Target at Bank of America
content: CoreWeave Inc. was downgraded at Bank of America, with the firm citing valuation after shares of the cloud-computing provider quadrupled in recent months.

title: Entain Jumps Most Since 2021 on BetMGM Guidance Upgrade
content: Entain Plc shares jumped the most in more than three-and-a-half years after the sports betting and gaming group upgraded its full-year revenue guidance for BetMGM, the US-based joint venture it shares with MGM Resorts International.

title: Air Taxi Firm Archer Sees More Defense Demand in Near Term

title: Unicorn Juniper Square Sells Picks and Shovels of Private Market Boom

title: Samsung Is Building a Hub for Patients to Share Data with Doctors

title: WhatsApp to Show Ads, Offer Paid Subscriptions for First Time
content: Meta Platforms Inc. will begin showing ads inside of its WhatsApp messaging service, opening a new potential revenue stream while the company invests heavily in artificial intelligence and other long-term projects.

title: Picton Plans More AI, Technology Hiring in Canadian Firm’s Growth Push
content: Canadian hedge fund manager David Picton says artificial intelligence will be a disruptive force for the money management industry, and his firm is looking to expand its technology capabilities as part of its growth plan.

title: Roku Shares Jump on Amazon-Connected TV Advertising Partnership

title: Humanoid Robot Development Seen as Vital to the Future of Manufacturing

title: How a Tiny Middleman Could Access Two-Factor Login Codes From Tech Giants

title: Irish State Exits AIB, Putting Bank Into Private Ownership

title: BOJ to Slow Bond Market Withdrawal After Standing Pat on Rates

content: Star Capital is considering an initial public offering of German defense technology firm Vincorion, people familiar with the matter said, as rising investor interest lifts the value in European aerospace and defense assets.

content: In a year that’s all about Europe, there’s one key market missing out on all the investor love: France.

content: “Bloomberg: The China Show” is your definitive source for news and analysis on the world's second-biggest economy. title: Kamel: Trump Riding The Wave of Israel Campaign in Iran
content: US President Donald Trump met with his national security team in Washington on Tuesday to discuss the escalating Middle East conflict and any US involvement in the war between Israel and Iran.  Ayham Kamel, Edelman Public and Government Affairs Middle East President told Joumanna Bercetche on Horizons Middle East and Africa that the president is acting on the basis of his own convictions and examining political opportunities. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Blackstone-Backed Casino Operator Cirsa Announces IPO in Spain
content: Cirsa Enterprises, the casino operator owned by Blackstone Inc., announced plans for an initial public offering in Spain.

title: The World’s First Mass-Market Electric Car Gets a Facelift
content: Nissan Motor Co.’s push to breathe new life into its lineup will yield an updated version of the Leaf, the struggling brand’s compact family car that was the world’s first mass-market electric vehicle.

title: Mali to Control Loulo-Gounkoto Gold Mine for Six Months
content: Barrick Mining Corp.’s Loulo-Gounkoto gold mining complex should be placed under provisional administration for six months, handing control of one of the company’s biggest operations to state-appointed management, a Malian court ruled. Bloomberg’s William Clowes breaks down the situation.

title: KKR, GIC Are Among Final Bidders for MasOrange, Zegona  Joint Venture
content: KKR & Co. and GIC Pte. are among the final bidders for a stake in a fiber-optic broadband network venture owned by MasOrange and Zegona Communications Plc, according to people familiar with the matter.

title: PBOC Chief Envisions New World Currency Order After Dollar Era
content: People’s Bank of China Governor Pan Gongsheng laid out in the clearest terms yet his vision for the future of a new global currency order after decades of dollar dominance, predicting a more competitive system will take root in the years to come.

title: Oil Swings in Volatile Market as Trump Spurs War Escalation Fear
content: Oil fluctuated after rallying around 10% since Israel started its attacks on Iran last week, as speculation the US may join the conflict stoked concerns about supply disruptions in the Middle East.

title: Oil Near Five-Month High on Middle-East Tensions: Markets Wrap
content: Oil traded near a five-month high on concern escalating tensions in the Middle East will trigger more direct US involvement. Equities were mixed before a Federal Reserve monetary policy decision.

title: BSE Shares Fall as Options Expiry Day Shift Raises Earnings Risk
content: Shares of BSE Ltd. extended a five-day drop Wednesday after the bourse announced plans to switch its expiry day for equity derivatives contracts to Thursday, marking the latest shake-up in the world’s largest market for the contracts.

BBVA in Talks With Cerberus, One William Street on Loan Sales
content: BBVA SA is in advanced talks to sell two loan portfolios totaling around €650 million ($754 million) to funds including Cerberus Capital Management’s Spanish unit and One William Street Capital Fund, according to people familiar with the matter.

title: How China Is Building a Powerful Army of Hackers
content: On today’s Big Take Asia podcast, how China’s domestic hacking competitions are helping boost the country’s cyber-espionage capabilities.

title: The Asia Trade: 6/18/2025
content: "Bloomberg: The Asia Trade" brings you everything you need to know to get ahead as the trading day begins in Asia. Bloomberg TV is live from Singapore and Sydney with Avril Hong and Haidi Stroud-Watts, getting insight and analysis from newsmakers and industry leaders on the biggest stories shaping global markets. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: China’s Rare Earth Exports Slump in May as Magnet Sales Curbed
content: China’s exports of rare earth products — including powerful magnets now at the heart of tensions with the US — slumped to a fresh five-year low in May as Beijing’s export curbs choked flows.

title: Making Oil Gyrate Again, One Post at a Time
content: Raising the stakes to direct intervention and regime change is driving the price higher.

title: Goldman, JPMorgan Bet Strong Franc Will Shrug Off SNB Rate at 0%
content: Wall Street’s biggest banks are betting the Swiss franc’s strength and haven appeal will cope with the potential return of subzero interest rates in Europe.

title: China Will Hike Quota for Investors Buying Overseas Assets
content: China will allow some local investors to put more of their money into overseas assets, a sign Beijing is opening up its financial market as the yuan steadies.

title: Hedge Fund Traders Are Pushing Their Firms Into Dubai and Abu Dhabi
content: The rush of hedge funds heading to the UAE has been driven by the need to keep star traders happy. Escalating conflict in the region hasn’t deterred them so far.

title: EQT Founder Backs Startup Swebal With Plans to Build TNT Factory
content: Swedish defense startup Swebal has raised €3 million ($3.5 million) from investors including Thomas von Koch, the co-founder of private equity firm EQT AB, to help it construct a factory manufacturing the explosive material TNT.

title: Iron Ore Extends Downward Trend on Weaker Chinese Steel Market
content: Iron ore edged down for the fifth day, continuing a downward trajectory as China’s steel market weakens.

title: Energy CEOs Comment on Impact of Escalating Middle East Tensions
content: While speaking at a conference in Tokyo, the chief executives of Woodside Energy, JERA Co. and TotalEnergies commented on the impact of rising tensions in the Middle East on oil and gas markets.  (Source: Bloomberg)

title: TotalEnergies Says It Can Replace Russian Gas With Growing LNG Supply
content: TotalEnergies SE sees abundant alternatives to Russian gas as the European Union proposes a ban on all deliveries from the country by the end of 2027. "The good news is that the LNG market will be well supplied from 2027, 2028 and 2029,” the company’s Chief Executive Officer Patrick Pouyanne says at an energy conference in Tokyo. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Israel Begins Repatriation of Citizens Stranded By Iran Strikes
content: Israel is repatriating tens of thousands of its citizens stranded abroad after a flare-up in fighting with Iran, deploying emergency airlifts and ferries.

title: Thai Cabinet Rift Over Key Post Risks Shaking Ruling Bloc
content: Thailand’s ruling party and its top coalition partner are clashing over a key ministerial post, as a looming cabinet shakeup by Prime Minister Paetongtarn Shinawatra threatens to shift alliances and unsettle the conservative establishment.

title: India’s Goyal to Visit UK to Discuss Trade Deal Implementation
content: India’s Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal will visit the United Kingdom on June 18 to discuss the progress on the implementation of the trade deal announced last month.

title: Indonesia to Summon BI Deputy as Witness in Graft Case: Technoz
content: Indonesia’s anti graft agency has sent a letter summoning Bank Indonesia Deputy Governor Filianingsih Hendarta for questioning as a witness in a graft case related to a social program, local news outlet Technoz reported on Wednesday.

title: Pakistan’s Army Chief Set to Meet Trump Amid Iran Tensions
content: President Donald Trump is expected to meet Pakistan’s army chief for talks as the US considers supporting Israeli airstrikes on Iran — a partner of the government in Islamabad.

title: Israel-Iran Conflict Enters Sixth Day as Trump Weighs Options
content: Iran and Israel exchanged fire for a sixth day after US President Donald Trump met with his national security team to discuss the escalating conflict, fueling fresh speculation that Washington is on the verge of joining the attacks.

title: Modi Pushes Back Against Trump’s Claim on Pakistan Ceasefire
content: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi disputed President Donald Trump’s claims that trade deals were used to clinch a ceasefire with Pakistan during last month’s military conflict.

title: A UK Wealth Exodus? Why ‘Non-Dom’ Crackdown Risks Backfiring for Reeves
content: The debate over the UK’s “non-dom” status has taken center stage yet again. The decision by Chancellor of the Exchequer Rachel Reeves to end a two-century old tax break for wealthy foreigners has triggered the exit of many well-heeled residents from the country.

title: Once-Mighty Hezbollah Stays Out of Iran’s War Against Israel
content: One of Israel’s most feared scenarios has long been that Iran would unleash an attack on it in coordination with its powerful network of proxy militias.

title: US-China Tech Fight Widens After Taiwan Blacklists Huawei
content: Taiwan joined a yearslong US campaign to curtail China’s technological ascent when it blacklisted the country’s AI and chipmaking champions, an unprecedented step that may signal a resurgent effort to isolate its powerful neighbor’s semiconductor sector.

title: Trump Flexes Security Powers to Keep Global Tariff Goal Alive
content: The Trump administration is pressing ahead with another tariff barrage that some trade experts say is more legally sound than the president’s country-by-country duties and may end up having an equally broad effect on imports.

title: China Consumer Rush for Subsidies Overloads Stimulus Program
content: China is testing the limits of what its consumer stimulus can accomplish by subsidizing purchases of select goods, fueling a shopping spree that boosted retail sales growth to the strongest in more than a year but threatening to overwhelm authorities even in the richest regions.

title: US Lawmakers’ Talks With Top Taiwan Official Risk Irking China
content: A group of US lawmakers held a rare publicly disclosed meeting with Taiwan’s top defense official, a discussion that risks spurring China to step up its military intimidation of the democracy.

title: Canada, India Agree to Name New Ambassadors After Expulsions
content: Canada and India agreed to appoint new chief diplomats in a major step toward moving past a feud that last year saw them expel each other’s officials over accusations of transnational repression and crime.

title: Japan to Protect Trade Interests And Not Rush Deal, Ishiba Says
content: Japan will prioritize protecting its national interests in trade talks without rushing into a deal with the US, Japanese Prime Minister Shigeru Ishiba said as he wrapped up two days of meetings at the Group of Seven gathering.

title: Putin Aide Shoigu Meets Kim as Pyongyang Plans More Military Aid
content: Kim Jong Un discussed ongoing cooperation with Moscow in talks with President Vladimir Putin’s top security aide Sergei Shoigu, North Korea’s state media said Wednesday, after reports that Pyongyang plans to send more military personnel to support Russia.

title: Australian PM Says EU Trade Deal Is ‘Symbolically Important’
content: Expanding trade ties between Australia and the European Union would be “symbolically important” in an environment of rising protectionism, Prime Minister Anthony Albanese said Wednesday, as the two sides also plan talks on a defense agreement.

title: Petro Seizes Colombia Labor Reform Victory, Worrying Businesses
content: The Colombian Senate approved one of President Gustavo Petro’s key reforms to boost workers’ benefits, creating concerns among businesses that it would raise labor costs.

title: Stefanik Asks SEC to Investigate Harvard Bond Offering
content: Representative Elise Stefanik called on the US Securities and Exchange Commission to investigate Harvard University’s recent bond sale, alleging the school may have withheld material information from investors about its standoff with the federal government.

title: Warren Slams Hegseth Decision to Slash Pentagon Weapons Testing Office
content: A Pentagon plan to slash staffing at its weapons testing office threatens the safety and effectiveness of every weapons program it oversees and “will cost service members’ lives and waste taxpayer dollars,” Senator Elizabeth Warren said.

title: Meloni Pushes for Gaza Ceasefire at G-7 Amid Israel-Iran Crisis
content: Italian Premier Giorgia Meloni sought to rally the Group of Seven leaders to support a ceasefire in Gaza, renewing the push amid an escalation of hostilities between Iran and Israel.

title: Colombia High Court Returns Petro’s Pension Bill to Congress
content: Colombia’s Constitutional Court returned the government-backed pension reform to Congress, citing a procedural error in a move that offers a glimmer of hope for President Gustavo Petro, whose ambitious social reforms have faced significant hurdles in the legislature.

title: Trump Weighs Iran Options as Israel Ratchets Up Airstrikes
content: President Donald Trump met with his national security team in Washington for more than an hour on Tuesday to discuss the escalating Middle East conflict, according to people familiar with the matter, fueling fresh speculation that the US is on the verge of joining Israel’s attack on Iran.

title: G-7 Confronts New Reality After Trump Spoils Hopes for Unity
content: On Sunday evening, Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney took to a comfy sofa to chew the fat over glasses of wine with European Group of Seven leaders at their hotel bar in Kananaskis, the Rocky Mountain resort hosting this year’s summit.

title: US Embassy in Jerusalem to Close for Three Days as Tensions Rise
content: The US Embassy in Jerusalem will remain closed for the next three days, the State Department said, as speculation grows that the Trump administration may be on the verge of joining Israel’s attack against Iran.

title: Key Takeaways From Summit of G-7 Leaders in Canada
content: Below are the key takeaways from our blog coverage of the Group of Seven leaders’ summit in Kananaskis, Canada. For more, click here for our TOPLive blog.

title: Senate Passes Stablecoin Bill in Win for Crypto, Trump
content: The US Senate passed stablecoin legislation setting up regulatory rules for cryptocurrencies pegged to the dollar, in a landmark win for the ascendant crypto industry and President Donald Trump.

title: Viasat Identified as Victim in Sweeping Phone Hack Tied to China
content: Viasat Inc. is the latest US communications company identified as a victim of the sweeping surveillance hack blamed on the Chinese government that emerged during last year’s presidential campaign, according to people familiar with the matter.

title: Iran-Israel Conflict Spills to Digital World, Inflaming Rivalry
content: The conflict between Israel and Iran is spilling over into the digital world, inflaming a decades-long campaign of hacks and espionage between two nations renowned for their cyber prowess.

title: Trump Again Pushes TikTok Sale Deadline With 90-Day Extension
content: President Donald Trump is extending for a third time the deadline for Chinese company ByteDance Ltd. to divest the American operations of TikTok, allowing the social media app to keep running in the US while negotiations proceed.

content: Airbus SE said it would target higher dividend payments, raising the upper range of its payout to shareholders, as earnings remain resilient despite uncertainty from tariffs and supply chain snags that have slowed down deliveries of its aircraft to customers.

title: Hedge Fund Traders Are Pushing Their Firms Into Dubai and Abu Dhabi
content: The rush of hedge funds heading to the UAE has been driven by the need to keep star traders happy. Escalating conflict in the region hasn’t deterred them so far.
