title: Star Capital Weighs IPO of Defense Tech Firm Vincorion
content: Star Capital is considering an initial public offering of German defense technology firm Vincorion, people familiar with the matter said, as rising investor interest lifts the value in European aerospace and defense assets.

title: KKR, GIC Are Among Final Bidders for MasOrange, Zegona  Joint Venture
content: KKR & Co. and GIC Pte. are among the final bidders for a stake in a fiber-optic broadband network venture owned by MasOrange and Zegona Communications Plc, according to people familiar with the matter.

title: How China Is Building a Powerful Army of Hackers
content: On today’s Big Take Asia podcast, how China’s domestic hacking competitions are helping boost the country’s cyber-espionage capabilities.

title: JD.com Billionaire Unveils Turnaround Plan After Five-Year Slump
content: JD.com Inc. founder Richard Liu vowed to speed an overseas foray and compete with Meituan in new arenas from food delivery to travel, describing his boldest attempt yet to revive an online retailer that’s languished since a 2020 government crackdown.

title: US-China Tech Fight Widens After Taiwan Blacklists Huawei
content: Taiwan joined a yearslong US campaign to curtail China’s technological ascent when it blacklisted the country’s AI and chipmaking champions, an unprecedented step that may signal a resurgent effort to isolate its powerful neighbor’s semiconductor sector.

title: Nintendo Extends Gains to Record on Booming Sales of Switch 2
content: Nintendo Co. shares rallied the most in two months to a fresh record as investors increased their focus on the firm’s strong sales growth as a shelter from global volatility.

title: AI Startup Anysphere Fields VC Offers at Over $18 Billion Valuation
content: Silicon Valley investors are anxious to back the startup they say is the fastest growing of all time.

title: Altman Says Meta Offered OpenAI Staffers $100 Million Bonuses
content: OpenAI Chief Executive Officer Sam Altman said Meta Platforms Inc. has offered his employees signing bonuses as high as $100 million, with even larger annual compensation packages, as it seeks to build a top artificial intelligence team.

title: Iran-Israel Conflict Spills to Digital World, Inflaming Rivalry
content: The conflict between Israel and Iran is spilling over into the digital world, inflaming a decades-long campaign of hacks and espionage between two nations renowned for their cyber prowess.

title: Trump Again Pushes TikTok Sale Deadline With 90-Day Extension
content: President Donald Trump is extending for a third time the deadline for Chinese company ByteDance Ltd. to divest the American operations of TikTok, allowing the social media app to keep running in the US while negotiations proceed.

title: Chip Tax Credits Get Boost in Trump Tax Bill | Bloomberg Tech 6/17/2025
content: Bloomberg’s Caroline Hyde and Ed Ludlow discuss how President Trump’s tax bill could boost investment credit for semiconductors to 30%. Plus, the CEO of Applied Intuition talks about how the startup plans to use its latest $600 million fundraising to make more moving machines self-driving. And the CEO of Purism says the company has spoken to the Trump family about supplying its made-in-the-USA smartphones to the new Trump mobile phone service. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Musk’s xAI Burns Through $1 Billion a Month as Costs Pile Up
content: Elon Musk’s artificial intelligence startup xAI is burning through $1 billion a month as the cost of building its advanced AI models races ahead of the limited revenues, according to people briefed on the company’s financials.

title: JPMorgan to Pilot Deposit Token JPMD on Coinbase-Linked Blockchain
content: JPMorgan Chase & Co. will launch a pilot for a token called JPMD that represents dollar deposits at the world’s biggest bank, as financial institutions deepen their push into the digital-asset sector.

title: Amazon’s Jassy Says AI Will Reduce Company’s Corporate Ranks
content: Amazon.com Inc. Chief Executive Officer Andy Jassy says he expects the company’s workforce to decline in the next few years as the retail and cloud-computing giant uses artificial intelligence to handle more tasks.

title: A Lithium Startup Is Building a US Battery Plant That Will Skirt Trump’s Tariffs
content: US startup Pure Lithium Corp. is working on a testing facility to build a new type of lithium battery that’s completely manufactured domestically.

title: Musk’s X Sues New York Over Law Requiring Hate-Speech Data
content: Elon Musk’s X Corp. sued the state of New York claiming a law requiring social media companies to disclose how they deal with hate speech, extremism and disinformation violates the US Constitution.

title: Revolut Will Soon Launch Its AI Financial Assistant, UK CEO Says
content: Revolut will be launching its AI financial assistant soon, according to one of the fintech’s top executives.

title: Adobe Debuts Standalone App for Generating AI Videos, Images
content: Adobe Inc. on Tuesday released a standalone Firefly mobile application for Android and iOS in an attempt to put a larger spotlight on its artificial intelligence-powered image generation and editing tools.

title: Meta Just Bet Big Bucks on AI Talent
content: Mark Zuckerberg’s investment in Scale AI and its founder, Alexandr Wang, shows how AI startups have become farm teams for the big-spending giants, explains Bloomberg Opinion columnist Dave Lee. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: SoftBank Sells T-Mobile Stake for $4.8 Billion to Bet on AI
content: SoftBank Group Corp. raised around $4.8 billion through a sale of T-Mobile US Inc. shares, a move that helps fund the Japanese company’s grandiose plans for artificial intelligence.

title: Musk’s xAI in Talks to Raise $4.3 Billion in Equity Funding
content: Elon Musk’s artificial intelligence startup xAI is in talks to raise $4.3 billion through an equity investment on top of the $5 billion it has recently been trying to borrow from debt investors, according to information the company shared with investors who asked not to be identified because it is private.

title: Salesforce Increases Prices as it Promotes New AI Features
content: Salesforce Inc. is increasing the price for many products, becoming the latest software maker to adjust its cost structure as it integrates artificial intelligence.

title: 23andMe Fined £2.31 Million by UK Over Genetic Data Leak
content: 23andMe was fined £2.31 million ($3.1 million) by UK regulators after a 2023 cyber attack exposed users’ genetic data in yet another privacy crisis surrounding the troubled DNA data bank.

title: Oracle’s $116 Billion Surge Leaves Little Room for Error on AI
content: Oracle Corp. investors find themselves at a pivotal crossroads. Either heed the warning from a growing list of indicators that suggest the stock has run up too far, too fast — or continue to chase another rally that’s been supercharged by lofty artificial intelligence expectations.

title: Applied Intuition Hits $15 Billion Valuation for AI Vehicle Tech
content: The company raised $600 million from investors as it prepares for an eventual IPO.

title: Ramp Investors Add Funding as Company Expands, Plans AI Agents
content: Spend-management platform Ramp gave existing investors an opportunity to double down on the six-year-old upstart with a recently closed $200 million funding round that boosted the company’s valuation to $16 billion.

title: Tiny Startup Brings Homegrown AI to Mongolia, Avoiding China-US Dominance
content: Welcome to Tech In Depth, our daily newsletter with reporting and analysis about the business of tech from Bloomberg’s journalists around the world. Today, Saritha Rai looks at an AI startup in tiny Mongolia and its surprising development of a homegrown large language model.

title: China’s MiniMax Says Its New AI Reasoning Model Beats DeepSeek
content: Chinese AI upstart MiniMax released a new large language model, joining a slew of domestic peers inspired to surpass DeepSeek in the field of reasoning AI.

title: Thiel-Backed Fund Invests in Ex-Citi Banker’s Stablecoin Startup
content: A startup run by two-decade Citigroup Inc. veteran Tony McLaughlin raised $10 million from investors including Peter Thiel’s Founders Fund to address an issue it says is holding back adoption of stablecoins.

title: UK Inflation Holds at Highest in Over a Year Before BOE Vote
content: UK inflation remained at its highest in over a year, keeping price pressures uncomfortably strong as the Bank of England weighs how much energy market turmoil will affect its path to cutting interest rates.

title: China Car Subsidy Halted in Some Areas as Funds Run Low
content: China’s trade-in subsidy to boost sales of electric and fuel-efficient vehicles has been suspended in key cities across at least six provinces as funds run short and officials scrutinize the prevalence of ‘zero-mileage’ used cars.

title: Nomura Says US to Set High Asia Tariffs to Stop China Rerouting
content: The US may keep elevated tariffs on Southeast Asian countries amid data suggesting that China is diverting goods through the region to avoid higher levies, according to Nomura Holdings Inc.

title: Indonesia to Summon BI Deputy as Witness in Graft Case: Technoz
content: Indonesia’s anti graft agency has sent a letter summoning Bank Indonesia Deputy Governor Filianingsih Hendarta for questioning as a witness in a graft case related to a social program, local news outlet Technoz reported on Wednesday.

title: PBOC Chief Envisions New World Currency Order After Dollar Era
content: People’s Bank of China Governor Pan Gongsheng laid out in the clearest terms yet his vision for the future of a new global currency order after decades of dollar dominance, predicting a more competitive system will take root in the years to come.

title: Thai Exports Soar Most in Three Years as Tariff Talks Begin
content: Thailand’s exports surged the most since early 2022 as companies rushed to stockpile goods while the Trump administration’s planned tariffs are still on hold.

title: Modi Pushes Back Against Trump’s Claim on Pakistan Ceasefire
content: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi disputed President Donald Trump’s claims that trade deals were used to clinch a ceasefire with Pakistan during last month’s military conflict.

title: Goldman, JPMorgan Bet Strong Franc Will Shrug Off SNB Rate at 0%
content: Wall Street’s biggest banks are betting the Swiss franc’s strength and haven appeal will cope with the potential return of subzero interest rates in Europe.

title: London’s Sky-High Prices Thin the Ranks of Room-to-Rent Seekers
content: The number of people looking for a room to rent in London has continued to slide, data from a property search website show, in a sign that high rents are pushing even that modest goal out of reach for many residents.

title: BOK Warns of Inflation Risks From US Tariffs, Israel-Iran Crisis
content: While South Korea’s inflation has stabilized near the central bank’s 2% target, US tariffs and the Israel-Iran conflict are adding uncertainty to the outlook, according to the Bank of Korea.

title: Japan to Protect Trade Interests And Not Rush Deal, Ishiba Says
content: Japan will prioritize protecting its national interests in trade talks without rushing into a deal with the US, Japanese Prime Minister Shigeru Ishiba said as he wrapped up two days of meetings at the Group of Seven gathering.

title: Australian PM Says EU Trade Deal Is ‘Symbolically Important’
content: Expanding trade ties between Australia and the European Union would be “symbolically important” in an environment of rising protectionism, Prime Minister Anthony Albanese said Wednesday, as the two sides also plan talks on a defense agreement.

title: Japan, South Korea Pledge Closer Ties After Lee-Ishiba Meeting
content: South Korean President Lee Jae Myung and Japan’s Prime Minister Shigeru Ishiba agreed to step up cooperation in their first in-person talks, in an early indication of the direction of future relations between the two countries after Lee took office.

title: Japan’s Exports Drop Raises Recession Risks as US Tariffs Bite
content: Japan’s exports fell for the first time in eight months as the US tariff campaign weighed on global trade, raising the risk of a technical recession after the economy contracted at the start of the year.

title: Biggest Free Food Program Hobbled by India’s Dated Census Data
content: The government relies on old figures to shape budgets and policies.

title: Chile Holds Rates at 5%, Leaving Timing Open on Future Cuts
content: Chile’s central bank kept its interest rate unchanged and signaled it will resume cuts in coming months as long as the economic impact from global uncertainty — including the Middle East conflict — remains limited.

title: Fed to Hold Rates Steady Again as Officials Wait for More Clarity on Economy
content: Federal Reserve officials are widely expected to leave interest rates unchanged for a fourth straight meeting on Wednesday, reiterating they want more clarity on the economic impact of a wide array of government policy changes before adjusting borrowing costs.

title: New Zealand Plans Switch to Annual Data-Driven Census From 2030
content: New Zealand will drop its five-yearly census and adopt a new approach using administrative data collected across a range of government agencies from 2030.

title: Milei Cools Argentina Wholesale Inflation to Lowest Since 2020
content: Argentine President Javier Milei notched another economic victory Tuesday after data showed wholesale prices declined in May for the first time since the height of the pandemic, adding to his momentum before October midterm elections.

title: Supreme Court Asked to Hear Challenge to Trump’s Global Tariffs
content: Two family-owned toy companies are asking the US Supreme Court to consider striking down many of President Donald Trump’s sweeping tariffs, putting a high-stakes fight with worldwide economic implications before the justices for the first time.

title: Harder to Cut With Core Inflation Firm, Bank of Canada Says
content: Bank of Canada officials said it would be tough to cut the policy interest rate further if core inflation remains firm, but acknowledged more easing may be needed if the economy continues to weaken.

title: Tax Bill Lacks Votes as Senate Aims for SALT, Medicaid Deals
content: Republican leaders are aiming for quick negotiations over needed changes to the newly unveiled Senate tax bill which lacks the votes to secure majorities in both chambers as written.

title: G-7 Leaders Won't Reach Agreement on Ukraine Statement
content: World leaders meet during the Group of Seven (G7) Summit at the Pomeroy Kananaskis Mountain Lodge in Kananaskis, Alberta, Canada on June 17, 2025.

title: Europe Pitches Stability to Bond Investors Wary of US Turbulence
content: Finance officials from across Europe are touting their bond markets as a haven from US volatility in a bid to attract global investors rethinking their dollar allocations.

title: IMF Met With Emerging-Market Creditors on Debt Rework Strategies
content: A group of International Monetary Fund officials met private creditors last week in London, as part of the multilateral lender’s work to publish a new report on sovereign debt restructurings in emerging markets, according to people familiar with the matter.

title: ECB Should Watch Oil Price, Euro in Setting Rates, Villeroy Says
content: The European Central Bank needs to assess fluctuations in oil prices and the euro as it sets borrowing costs, according to Governing Council member Francois Villeroy de Galhau.

title: Nassim Taleb Says Trump’s Approach to Tariffs ‘Makes No Sense’
content: The Black Swan author Nassim Taleb said President Donald Trump’s approach to tariffs will depress US gross domestic product and could soon lead to labor shortages.

title: US Homebuilder Sentiment Drops to Lowest Level Since End of 2022
content: Confidence among US homebuilders fell in June to the lowest level since December 2022, with potential buyers deterred by high mortgage rates and anxiety about tariffs and the economy.

title: US Retail Sales Drop for Second Month as Tariff Anxiety Sets In
content: US retail sales fell for a second straight month in May, suggesting anxiety over tariffs and personal finances prompted consumers to pull back after an early-year spending rush.

title: Ireland Removes Pay Caps for AIB and PTSB Executives
content: Salary caps for executives at AIB Group Plc and Permanent TSB Group Plc will be removed, Ireland’s Minister for Finance Paschal Donohoe said.

title: Germany’s Defense Firms Need Steelmakers to Help Fuel Boom

title: German Property Lender PBB Leaves US, Issues Profit Warning

It was the first time a senior US executive from the bank had stepped foot in China in five years, and came days after a rare board meeting in Tokyo near the Imperial Palace.

content: General Mills Inc., the maker of Lucky Charms and Trix cereals, will remove synthetic dyes from its products by the end of 2027, according to the Minnesota Star Tribune.

title: Caris Life Sciences Shares Climb After $494 Million IPO

content: A panel of key government advisers appointed by Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. will weigh in on an infrequently used vaccine preservative that has been wrongly linked to autism in the past.

title: Trump Activates 2,000 National Guard Soldiers in Los Angeles
content: The Trump administration has deployed into duty 2,000 National Guard soldiers in California, even as the state’s governor clashes with the White House over using troops to quell protests over the federal immigration crackdown.

title: Spanish Grid Denies Network Mismanagement on Day of Blackout
content: Spanish power grid operator Red Electrica said it managed the network properly on the day of the nationwide blackout in April, clashing with the government’s opinion about the causes of the incident.

title: Iran’s Missile Attacks Wane, Allowing Israel to Start Reopening
content: Iran’s missile and drone attacks on Israel appear to be subsiding, prompting Israeli authorities to relax some safety restrictions.

title: Police Have Right to Ban Budapest Pride Event, Minister Says
content: A senior minister said Hungary’s police have the right to ban a Pride parade scheduled later this month, in response to an attempt by Budapest’s mayor to organize it under the capital’s auspices.

title: Colleges Face Major Tax Blow in Trump’s Proposed IRS Rules on Race
content: The Trump administration is privately considering unleashing what advocates and critics agree would be one of its biggest cudgels yet to pressure colleges to end slews of programs and practices benefiting students who are racial minorities.

title: Republican Who Flip-Flopped on Energy Credits Risks Voters’ Ire

title: Fertilizer Plant Set to Lose License as Trump Squeezes Venezuela

title: UN Says It Has Lost Track of Iran’s Near-Bomb-Grade Uranium
content: The United Nations nuclear watchdog said the location of Iran’s near-bomb-grade stockpile of enriched uranium cannot currently be verified, as Israel’s ongoing military assault is preventing inspectors from doing their work.

title: Iran’s Leader Stays Defiant as Trump Weighs War Intervention
content: Iran’s Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei rejected President Donald Trump’s demands for complete capitulation and predicted “irreparable damage” if the US joins Israel in bombarding his country.

title: Orban Confronts Strongest Opposition Poll Surge of His Rule
content: Hungary’s opposition Tisza Party surged to an unprecedented 15 percentage point lead over Prime Minister Viktor Orban’s Fidesz in an opinion poll, with more voters now expecting the strongman premier to face defeat in the next elections.

title: Khamenei Tells US That Iran Won’t Surrender to Israel
content: Iran’s Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei said his country won’t surrender to Israel after US President Donald Trump called for the Islamic Republic’s capitulation amid growing speculation that Washington could enter the conflict.

title: South Africa, US to Resume Trade Talks as Tariff Deadline Looms
content: South Africa will resume trade talks with the Trump administration on the sidelines of the US-Africa Business Summit next week, with less than a month to go before Washington’s reciprocal tariffs are set to come into effect.

title: Thai PM Sparks Turmoil After Criticizing Army in Leaked Audio
content: Thailand’s prime minister blamed her own military for escalating a border dispute with Cambodia, according to a leaked audio recording, sparking fresh political turmoil in the country as opposition groups called on her to resign.

content: Portuguese Prime Minister Luis Montenegro’s minority government got backing from the two biggest opposition parties in a vote in parliament after his center-right coalition won a snap election in May.

title: Amazon’s Zoox Opens Robotaxi Production Site in California
content: Amazon.com Inc.’s Zoox autonomous driving unit opened a robotaxi production facility in California in the latest move by a deep-pocketed tech company to expand the nascent industry.

title: Waymo Applies for NYC Testing Permit, Sending Uber and Lyft Shares Lower
content: Alphabet Inc.’s Waymo has applied for a permit to test its robotaxis in New York City, underscoring its intent to operate in one of the largest ride-hailing markets in the US despite an absence of local regulations supporting commercially operated autonomous vehicles.

title: Nvidia Joins $650 Million Funding for Gates-Backed Nuke Firm
content: TerraPower LLC, a nuclear startup founded by billionaire Bill Gates, raised $650 million to help continue development of an advanced reactor project under construction in Wyoming.

title: Trump Again Pushes TikTok Sale Deadline With 90-Day Reprieve
content: President Donald Trump plans to extend for a third time the deadline for Chinese company ByteDance Ltd. to divest the American operations of TikTok, allowing the social media app to keep running in the US while negotiations proceed.

title: Intel Brings in New Engineering Leaders to Help AI Comeback
content: Intel Corp. named new engineering leadership as part of a turnaround effort under Chief Executive Officer Lip-Bu Tan, tapping veterans of Cadence Design Systems Inc., Apple Inc. and Google.

title: Justices Back Temporary Texas Nuclear Waste Storage Site
content: The US Supreme Court left intact a federal plan to store as much as 40,000 tons of highly radioactive waste at a temporary site in west Texas over the objections of local landowners and oil and gas operators.

title: OpenAI Is Phasing Out Scale AI Work Following Startup’s Meta Deal
content: OpenAI is phasing out the work it does with data-labeling startup Scale AI, cutting ties with the company days after Meta Platforms Inc. invested billions of dollars in it and hired its founder.

title: Lab-Grown Meat Soon on Australia’s Menus After Approval
content: Australia has approved the sale of slaughter-free Japanese quail, becoming only the third country in the world to permit the sale of meat cultivated from animal cells.

title: Chipmaker Wolfspeed Nears Bankruptcy Deal With Lenders Including Apollo
content: Struggling chipmaker Wolfspeed Inc. will be taken over by creditors including Apollo Global Management Inc. under a proposal that would put it into bankruptcy just long enough to slash billions in debt, according to people familiar with the plan.

title: Broadcom’s 340% Rally Has Wall Street Debating If It's Magnificent Seven Material
content: For more than two years, conversations about the biggest, most important technology companies have revolved around the same seven stocks. Now, some on Wall Street are making the case that Broadcom Inc. should be part of that discussion.

title: Xreal’s One Pro Are a Stopgap Ahead of True AR Smart Glasses
content: Review: The company’s latest augmented-reality glasses excel as an external display for phones, PCs and gaming devices.

title: Tencent-Backed MiniMax Releasing AI Tools to Take On Manus
content: Chinese upstart MiniMax is slated to roll out a pair of AI products that autonomously perform tasks on behalf of users, upping its game in the realm of agentic AI against the likes of OpenAI and Manus.

title: Texas Instruments Touts Plans to Invest $60 Billion in the US
content: Texas Instruments Inc. touted plans to spend more than $60 billion on semiconductor plants in the US, making it the latest chipmaker to promote its domestic manufacturing ambitions as the Trump administration urges investments and threatens to upend the sector with tariffs.

title: Road to a $3.7 Trillion Stablecoin Market Is Full of Obstacles
content: The passage of stablecoin legislation in the US Senate marks a huge leap forward for the potential mainstreaming of cryptocurrencies that track the US dollar one-to-one.

title: SoftBank-Backed Startup Misses Financial Goals, Slashes Staff
content: Just a couple years ago, Spotter Inc. was one of the most valuable startups in the booming business of YouTube celebrity. The company, which boasted a new way for social media stars to fund their operations, fronted millions of dollars to creators like MrBeast and Dude Perfect in exchange for a share of the revenue their videos generated.

title: Italy’s Brembo to Provide Brakes for US Bike Brand Specialized
content: Brembo NV will supply a braking system for US bicycle brand Specialized as part of a partnership the two companies are setting up, people familiar with the matter said.

title: Ad Industry Parties at Cannes in Face of Looming AI Upheaval
content: Welcome to Tech In Depth, our daily newsletter with reporting and analysis about the business of tech from Bloomberg’s journalists around the world. Today, Benoit Berthelot reports that the ad industry continues to party as usual at the annual Cannes Lions festival in France despite underlying anxiety about the coming effects of artificial intelligence.

title: Ex-SpaceX Staffers Raise Cash for Defense Manufacturing Startup
content: Senra Systems joins a growing list of startups aiming to accelerate American manufacturing of drones, rockets and more.

title: UBS Confirms Data Stolen After Hack at External Supplier
content: UBS Group AG said that information about the company had been stolen in a cyber attack on one of its suppliers, following a report a Swiss newspaper that data on more than 130,000 employees had been subject to a hack.

title: Alibaba-Backed ‘AI Dragon’ MiniMax Is Said to Plan Hong Kong IPO
content: MiniMax is considering an initial public offering in Hong Kong, people familiar with the situation said, in what would be a landmark industry debut for a Chinese AI startup valued at about $3 billion.

title: SAP and IBM Unit Ensnared in $800 Million Quebec IT Fiasco
content: Software company SAP SE and an IBM Corp. subsidiary are embroiled in a C$1.1 billion ($810 million) technology boondoggle that triggered both a public inquiry and an anti-corruption investigation in Quebec.

title: Netflix Adds Live TV Broadcasts, Sports From France’s TF1
content: Netflix Inc. will add live television channels and shows from French broadcaster TF1, expanding the streaming platform’s live offer for customers in the country.

title: EU Says AliExpress Failed to Stop Illegal Sales in DSA Probe
content: The European Union escalated a probe against Alibaba Group Holding Ltd.’s e-commerce service AliExpress, accusing it of failing to tackle the spread of illegal products on its platform.

title: Big Spenders Have Banks Raising Prices, Perks on Premium Cards
content: Sweeter benefits — and higher fees — on travel cards from Chase and Amex reflect a new US economic reality, with the richest households driving half of all consumer spending.

title: IMF Says Zimbabwe’s Economy Has Made ‘Significant Progress’
content: The International Monetary Fund said Zimbabwe’s economic progress represents a “regime change,” but declined to say if or when the Washington-based lender would grant it a staff-monitored program.

title: ECB’s Panetta Says Economic Outlook Faces Substantial Risks
content: The euro-zone’s economic prospects face “substantial” dangers that officials are struggling to assess, according to European Central Bank Governing Council member Fabio Panetta.

title: Modi Disputes Trump’s Version of India-Pakistan Ceasefire
content: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi disputed President Donald Trump’s claims that trade deals were used to clinch a recent ceasefire with Pakistan, the latest sign of possible strain in the relationship between New Delhi and Washington.

title: Macklem Warns of Firmer Inflation, Uncertainty About Impact of Tariffs
content: Bank of Canada Governor Tiff Macklem reiterated that he sees inflation running hotter than expected, while saying employment appears to be holding up outside of trade-intensive sectors.

title: France’s Economy Is Falling Behind as Europe Gradually Recovers
content: France’s economy is falling behind the rest of Europe with weakness across the board — just as uncertainty over budget cuts looks set to return, according to the statistics office.

title: UK Inheritance Tax Surge on Rich Was Mistake, Policy Author Says
content: One of the architects of the UK Labour government’s flagship crackdown on the wealthy said it was a “mistake” to expose non-doms to an immediate 40% inheritance tax on their overseas assets.

title: New Home Construction Falls to Five-Year Low
content: New US residential construction declined in May to the slowest pace since the onset of the pandemic as an elevated inventory of homes for sale and high mortgage rates sapped the motivation to build.

title: Zimbabwe Asks South Africa to Back G-20 Debt Overhaul
content: Zimbabwe has asked South Africa to help garner support for its debt to be revamped under the Group of 20’s Common Framework, a step that could restore its access to international capital markets for the first time in more than 25 years.

title: US Jobless Claims Stabilize Near Highest Levels This Year
content: Applications for US unemployment benefits ticked down last week, stabilizing near the highest levels in eight months.

title: Euro Zone Is Still Held Back by Rising Mortgage Rates, ECB Finds
content: Household consumption in the euro area will remain restrained for some time as past interest-rate hikes continue to feed through to mortgages, according to research by the European Central Bank.

title: South Africa, US to Resume Trade Talks as Tariff Deadline Looms
content: South Africa will resume trade talks with the Trump administration on the sidelines of the US-Africa Business Summit next week, with less than a month to go before Washington’s reciprocal tariffs are set to come into effect.

title: UK Home Prices See Biggest Drop Since 2021 as Tax Hike Kicks In
content: UK home prices fell in April by most since 2021, government data show, as a tax increase drove some buyers out of the market.

title: Trump Taps Tariff Toolkit to Hit Consumer Goods
content: With President Donald Trump’s universal tariffs possibly headed for a Supreme Court showdown, his administration is pressing ahead with another strategy that could hit an equally broad swath of imports.

title: Riksbank Cuts Key Rate and Signals Potential for More Easing
content: Sweden’s central bank lowered borrowing costs by a quarter point, resuming attempts to jump-start growth in the biggest Nordic economy, and raised the prospect of one more cut this year.

title: Norway Will Keep Waiting Before First Rate Cut
content: Norway’s central bank is poised to stick with one of the most hawkish policy stances among advanced economies, holding off on any start to post-pandemic easing until later this year.

title: Bank Indonesia Official Summoned as Witness in Graft Case
content: A Bank Indonesia deputy governor will testify this week as a witness in a graft case related to the use of corporate social responsibility funds.

title: Brazil Economists’ Shifting Calls Presage Thriller Rate Decision
content: On the eve of Brazil’s interest rate decision this week, XP’s Chief Economist Caio Megale agonized over data and policymaker speeches before switching his forecast to a hold from a quarter-point rise. Poring over the same details, ASA economist Leonardo Costa went the opposite way, ditching his bet on steady borrowing costs and calling for a hike instead.

title: Philippine Central Bank Chief Calls Peso Intervention Futile
content: The Philippines will tolerate the slide in its currency to a two-month low, with the central bank governor flagging that interventions won’t be effective in the face of global risk aversion.

title: PBOC Head Imagines New World Currency Order After Dollar Era
content: People’s Bank of China Governor Pan Gongsheng laid out in the clearest terms yet his vision for the future of a new global currency order after decades of dollar dominance, predicting a more competitive system will take root in the years to come.

title: South African Inflation Holds Steady as Conflict Clouds Outlook
content: South African inflation rate held steady in May as uncertainty around the outlook for price-growth mounts, complicating the task for the central bank when it meets to discuss its monetary policy stance next month.

title: IMF Met Emerging-Market Creditors on Debt Rework Strategies
content: A group of International Monetary Fund officials met with private creditors last week in London, as part of the multilateral lender’s work to publish a new report on sovereign debt restructurings in emerging markets, according to people familiar with the matter.

title: The US Has More Copper Than China But No Way to Refine All of It
content: The industry will need to overcome high energy and labor costs, environmental regulations and a glut of cheap Chinese competition to make US copper smelting great again.

title: Yellen, Bernanke Oppose GOP-Backed Cuts to Financial Research
content: Former Federal Reserve Chairs Janet Yellen and Ben Bernanke, along with several other academics, market participants and former Treasury officials, urged congressional leadership to oppose cuts to an office charged with gathering data aimed at preventing another financial crisis.

title: Czech Central Banker Kubicek Sees Rate Cuts Ending on Inflation
content: The Czech central bank may have to refrain from lowering interest rates any further because sticky inflation requires restrictive monetary conditions, according to board member Jan Kubicek.

title: Amazon’s Zoox Opens Robotaxi Production Site in California
content: Amazon.com Inc.’s Zoox autonomous driving unit opened a robotaxi production facility in California in the latest move by a deep-pocketed tech company to expand the nascent industry.

title: Brookfield’s Insurer Trims Private Credit, Citing Crowded Trade
content: Brookfield Corp.’s insurance unit has pulled back from investments in private credit as surging demand from rival bidders pushes yields down.

title: Biggest US Oil Stockpile Drop in a Year Shows Tightening Market
content: US crude stockpiles declined the most in almost a year last week, signaling a tighter market for American oil just as the Israel-Iran conflict threatens supplies from the Middle East.

title: RFK Jr.’s New Panel Takes on Vaccine Ingredients, Shots for Kids
content: Robert F. Kennedy Jr.’s plan for America’s vaccines is coming into focus, with his revamped immunization advisory panel set to discuss the use of measles shots in kids next week and vote on an ingredient that’s been wrongly linked to autism.

title: US Plans to Ease Capital Rule Limiting Banks Treasury Trades
content: The top US bank regulators plan to reduce a key capital buffer by up to 1.5 percentage points for the biggest lenders after concerns that it constrained their trading in the $29 trillion Treasuries market.

title: UAW President Retaliated Against Union Official, Monitor Alleges

title: Zimbabwe Asks South Africa to Back G-20 Debt Overhaul

content: Australia’s world-first social media ban for under-16s moved closer to implementation after a key trial found that checking a user’s age is technologically possible and can be integrated into existing services.

title: JD.com Billionaire’s Viral Stunt Reignites China’s Food-Delivery Feud
content: One unusually warm evening in April, Richard Liu revved his scooter through Beijing’s traffic-snarled streets alongside other delivery workers, and then personally handed food orders to surprised customers. Later that night, over spicy hotpot and ice-cold beer, the JD.com Inc. founder welcomed a pair of riders from two rival delivery firms to his company.

content: Elon Musk’s $33 billion xAI buyout of social media platform X has sparked new scrutiny from the European Union as regulators size up a penalty under the Digital Services Act.

title: Top Thai Billionaires-Backed Groups Win Digital Bank Permits

content: President Donald Trump has long criticized Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell for not lowering interest rates.

content: Oil prices reacted after Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu ordered Israel's military to intensify attacks against Iran.

content: India’s top government adviser said rising oil prices are likely to have a limited impact on inflation for now and Asia’s third-largest economy remains in a relatively favorable position to weather global risks.

content: Elon Musk’s artificial intelligence startup xAI Corp. lured enough investors to its $5 billion debt deal by offering sweeter pricing on Friday.

content:
A memo titled "Abolishing FEMA" outlines ways for Trump to scrap the agency. 

 Zahra Hirji explains how the administration aims to create a re-branded, radically smaller disaster response organization. (Source: Bloomberg)

content: "Bloomberg Markets" follows the market moves across every global asset class and discusses the biggest issues for Wall Street. Today's guests; Bloomberg's Nir Kaissar, David Welch, Michelle Cortez, and Rachel Phua. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: US Refining Capacity Declines Amid Uncertain Fuel Demand Outlook
content: US refiners’ operating capacity edged lower in 2024 as an uncertain outlook for gasoline and diesel prompted fuelmakers to pull back after a period of expansion.

title: S&P 500 Trading Volume Spikes at Wall Street Close: Markets Wrap
content: A jittery week ended with losses in stocks as investors weighed geopolitical and trade developments, chipmakers sank while a $6.5 trillion options expiration spurred a surge in volume. Short-dated yields fell as Federal Reserve’s Christopher Waller said rates could drop as early as July.

title: Hedge Funds Rush Into Oil Long Bets as Mideast Conflict Grows
content: Hedge funds boosted their bullish position in Brent crude by the most since early October as Israel’s strikes against Iran’s nuclear program imperiled a region that produces around a third of the world’s oil.

title: Trump Says Iran Wants to Speak With US, Not Europe
content: President Donald Trump says two weeks is the maximum amount of time he will allow to pursue diplomacy with Iran while speaking with reporters. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Equities Finish Choppy Session Lower | Closing Bell
content: Comprehensive cross-platform coverage of the U.S. market close on Bloomberg Television, Bloomberg Radio, and YouTube with Romaine Bostick, Scarlet Fu, Carol Massar and Tim Stenovec. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Wall Street’s First-Half Whiplash Rewards All-Weather Portfolios
content: Somehow, for all its drama — tariffs, fiscal brinkmanship, inflation fears, and geopolitical flare-ups — the first half of 2025 may be remembered by diversified investors for something else entirely: the strongest stretch of synchronized market gains in years.

title: Fed’s Daly Says Next Rate Cut More Likely in the Fall
content: Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco President Mary Daly said an interest-rate cut this fall looks more appropriate than moving when policymakers gather in July.

title: Bitcoin Network Activity Slows While Price Lingers Near Highs
content: Once institutional investors are finally onboard has long been a rallying cry for Bitcoin enthusiasts projecting sky-high price forecasts.

title: US Stocks Extend Losing Run as Geopolitics Dampens Investor Mood
content: US stocks ended the week with losses as investors assessed the latest geopolitical developments and tried to determine the Federal Reserve’s interest-rate path.

title: Circle Gets Buy Rating After Senate Passes Stablecoin Bill
content: Circle Internet Group Inc.’s shares jumped 20% on Friday after Seaport Global gave the stablecoin issuer its first buy rating in the wake of the US Senate’s move this week to pass legislation setting up regulatory rules for cryptocurrencies pegged to the dollar.

title: Oil Drops as Trump Eases Concerns About Imminent Strike on Iran
content: Oil fell after President Donald Trump signaled a decision on whether to strike Iran will be made within two weeks, easing concerns about an imminent attack from the US.

title: LME Sets New Rule Forcing Traders to Reduce Big Metals Bets
content: The London Metal Exchange has imposed a new rule to force traders to reduce large positions, after the market was rocked in recent months by the arrival of some of the world’s biggest energy traders.

title: AQR’s Cliff Asness Sides With Jim Chanos in Critique of Michael Saylor’s Strategy
content: AQR Capital Management’s Cliff Asness says he’s in agreement with famed short seller Jim Chanos when it comes to his criticism of Strategy founder Michael Saylor’s claim that the use of convertible debt affords the leveraged Bitcoin proxy downside protection while continuing to accumulate the cryptocurrency.

title: Government Contractors Recruit Fewer Prospects
content: Thousands of private government consultants laid off during the Trump administration’s cost-cutting crusade are increasingly flooding a shrinking labor market. Bloomberg's Rachel Phua has more on the story.  (Source: Bloomberg)

title: September Is Live Meeting for Fed, Says Guggenheim's Brown
content: Guggenheim Fixed Income CIO Steven Brown says September will be a "live meeting" for the Federal Reserve when it decides on interest rates. He speaks on "Bloomberg Real Yield." (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Fed's Next Move, Narrowing Labor Market, Inflation
content: Guggenheim’s Fixed Income CIO Steven Brown and Columbia Threadneedle’s Global Rates Strategist Ed Al-Hussainy discussed what and when will be Fed's next move. They flagged a slowing job market and narrowing labor cushion, warning that even slight rises in unemployment could shift the Fed’s tone — especially as more inflation and tariff data come in. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Robot Delivery Service Plans US and Europe Expansion
content: Coco Robotics, the maker of cooler-sized delivery robots, has raised $80 million in its latest funding round to improve the technology and expand to new cities. CEO Zach Rash discusses how the service has been performing in L.A., Helsinki, and other cities with Caroline Hyde on “Bloomberg Tech.” (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Israel-Iran War Reaches Second Week as Trump Sends Mixed Signals
content: Israel and Iran launched new strikes in a second week of hostilities, as Donald Trump deepened uncertainty about his readiness to join the conflict and dismissed European efforts to find a diplomatic solution.

title: Starmer Faces Brewing Rebellion Over £5 Billion Benefit Cut
content: UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer is less than 10 days away from the biggest parliamentary challenge to his authority in his not-yet year-long tenure.

title: China’s Top HK Official Says Security Will Ensure City’s Success
content: China’s top official for Hong Kong affairs said the city needs to prioritize national security to ensure prosperity.

title: Judge Says He Will Order Ex-Columbia Student Khalil Freed From Detention
content: JENA, La. (AP) — Palestinian activist Mahmoud Khalil was released Friday from federal immigration detention, freed after 104 days by a judge’s ruling after becoming a symbol of President Donald Trump ’s clampdown on campus protests.

title: India to See Limited Inflation Fallout From Oil, Government Adviser Says
content: India’s top government adviser said rising oil prices are likely to have a limited impact on inflation for now and Asia’s third-largest economy remains in a relatively favorable position to weather global risks.

title: Dr. Phil’s Media Company Cuts 40 More Jobs, Pauses Evening News
content: Merit Street Media, the company founded by celebrity psychologist Phil McGraw, has cut jobs and paused some programming, according to a spokesperson.

title: Universities Win Order Voiding Agency’s 15% Research Cost Cap
content: Brown and Cornell universities, the Massachusetts Institute of Technology and several other US schools won a federal court order striking down a National Science Foundation cap on indirect cost rates for government-funded research.

title: China, Philippines Report Encounter in South China Sea
content: China’s coast guard said it drove away a Philippine ship around Scarborough Shoal in the South China Sea, the latest friction in a longstanding rivalry in the strategic waterway.

title: Carney Bill to Speed Projects Passes Vote Despite Indigenous Opposition
content: Canada’s House of Commons cleared a bill to accelerate the building of major projects such as pipelines, but Indigenous groups are threatening to force a legal battle over it.

title: Deal, Not Bombs, Seen as Only Way to End Iranian Nuclear Threat
content: While President Donald Trump weighs whether to join Israel’s assault on Iran, foreign policy veterans and analysts argue that a negotiated settlement, not bombs nor commandos, is the only way to eliminate the threat of Tehran gaining a nuclear weapon.

title: Harvard Nears ‘Mindbogglingly’ Historic US Deal, Trump Says
content: President Donald Trump said his administration has been holding talks with Harvard University and may announce a deal over the next week, potentially ending a standoff that has jeopardized billions of dollars of the school’s funding and ignited a rollicking legal fight.

title: Trump Says Spain Has to Pay as NATO Seeks Deal on Spending
content: NATO allies are pressing Spain to sign on to a stepped-up defense spending target and end a holdout that US President Donald Trump portrayed as unacceptable.

title: Trump Sends Mixed Signals on Iran Strikes With Ceasefire Hint
content: Donald Trump deepened uncertainty about his readiness to join Israel’s week-old war with Iran, signaling he might consider backing a ceasefire but also warning that he could order military action sooner than the deadline he flagged just a day earlier.

title: Trump Keeps the World Waiting With Deadlines and Deferrals
content: This is Washington Edition, the newsletter about money, power and politics in the nation’s capital. Every Friday, White House correspondent Akayla Gardner delivers a roundup of the key news and events in politics, policy and economics that you need to know.  Sign up here and follow us at @bpolitics. Email our editors here.

title: America the Avoidable: Why Trump’s Policies Could Cost US Tourism Billions
content: On today’s Big Take podcast: How President Trump’s “American First” policies have kept international tourists away, forecasted to cost the US travel industry billions.

title: Harvard Gets Longer Reprieve From Trump Foreign Student Ban
content: A federal judge issued a new order that allows Harvard University to continue enrolling foreign students while the school fights the Trump administration’s efforts to prevent it from doing so.

title: EU Finds Israel May Have Broken Human Rights Terms in Accord
content: A report commissioned by the European Union found that Israel may have broken the humanitarian terms of the accord that dictates their bilateral relations.

title: Under New Leadership, OAS Is Determined to Show Progress on Haiti
content: Amid pressure from Washington to resolve the crisis in Haiti, the new head of the Western Hemisphere’s top multilateral organization pledged to work with the United Nations and international donors to chart a roadmap for peace in the violence-torn island nation.

title: NYC Sets Smaller Driver Pay Bump After Uber, Lyft Pushback
content: New York City on Friday announced new minimum-pay rules for rideshare drivers, settling on a smaller-than-proposed 5% increase following pushback from Uber Technologies Inc. and Lyft Inc.

title: Niger Junta Seizes French Nuclear Giant Orano’s Uranium Mine
content: Niger’s military government took control of Orano SA’s uranium mine, escalating a standoff with the French nuclear-power company.

title: Trump Allowed to Keep Using National Guard in LA for Now
content: President Donald Trump can continue to use California National Guard troops to respond to protests in Los Angeles as a legal challenge over the deployment proceeds, a federal appeals court ruled.

title: No Urgent Need for Key Producers to Aid Oil Market, Putin Says
content: The global oil market so far does not call for any additional steps from producers amid the conflict between Israel and Iran as the tensions have had only a limited effect on prices, according to Russia’s President Vladimir Putin.

title: Why a Remote UK Base Makes the US-Iran Standoff So Difficult for Starmer
content: UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer will be relieved by US President Donald Trump’s move to delay a decision for now on striking Iran, giving the British leader more time to address the vexing issue of providing military support.

title: US Sanctions Target Iran Defense Industry, Houthis
content: The US escalated pressure on Iran with sanctions targeting individuals and companies allegedly involved in obtaining machinery for its defense industry, as well as those backing a militant group with ties to the regime.

title: Russia Says Israel, US Pledge Staff Safety at Iran Nuclear Plant
content: President Vladimir Putin said Russia sought and received assurances from Israel and the US that they’d ensure the safety of Russian staff working at Iran’s nuclear power plant at Bushehr.

title: Supreme Court Refuses to Expedite Challenge to Trump’s Tariffs
content: The US Supreme Court refused to put a challenge to President Donald Trump’s sweeping tariffs on an ultra-fast track.

title: Putin Says He Isn’t Seeking Ukraine’s ‘Capitulation’ to End War
content: President Vladimir Putin said he isn’t seeking Ukraine’s “capitulation” as a way to end the war, even as he reiterated his claim that the two countries are one people.

title: UN Chief Calls for Diplomacy as Israel-Iran War Rages
content: UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres called for a return to negotiations to resolve the conflict between Israel and Iran, warning that the world is “on course to potential chaos” if it expands.

title: Bezos Wedding Draws Protests, Soul-Searching Over Tourism in Venice
content: The $10 million bash has called attention to whether the city needs to take stronger actions to stop a deluge of visitors.

content: Silicon Valley dominates artificial intelligence headlines, but a quiet AI revolution is unfolding across Europe -- from billion-dollar startups to a growing push for sovereignty in the tech of tomorrow. Bloomberg's Tom Mackenzie explains. (Source: Bloomberg)

content: Continental AG intends to become the latest German manufacturing stalwart to dismantle itself, highlighting the pressure to become more agile to weather structural issues at home and respond to mounting competition abroad.

She speaks with Joe Mathieu and Tyler Kendall on the late edition of Bloomberg's "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

content: Kenneth Pollack, Vice President for Policy at the Middle East Institute, discusses President Trump's two week delay on deciding whether or not the US will strike Iran, and what factors must be considered. title: Andreessen Horowitz Backs AI Startup With Slogan ‘Cheat at Everything’
content: Andreessen Horowitz led a $15 million funding round for an artificial intelligence startup called Cluely Inc., famous on social platforms like X for controversial viral marketing stunts and the slogan “cheat on everything.”

title: Apple Executives Have Held Internal Talks About Buying AI Startup Perplexity
content: Apple Inc. executives have held internal discussions about potentially bidding for artificial intelligence startup Perplexity AI, seeking to address the need for more AI talent and technology.

title: Circle Gets Buy Rating After Senate Passes Stablecoin Bill
content: Circle Internet Group Inc.’s shares jumped 20% on Friday after Seaport Global gave the stablecoin issuer its first buy rating in the wake of the US Senate’s move this week to pass legislation setting up regulatory rules for cryptocurrencies pegged to the dollar.

title: SoftBank’s Son Pitches $1 Trillion US AI Hub | Bloomberg Tech 6/20/2025
content: Bloomberg’s Caroline Hyde discusses SoftBank founder Masayoshi Son’s pitch to build a trillion-dollar AI industrial complex with TSMC in Arizona. Plus, the global robotaxi market heats up as Baidu looks to expand internationally and Tesla prepares to launch its service in Austin. And Meta rolls out new smart-glasses in a partnership with Oakley.  (Source: Bloomberg)

title: NYC Sets Smaller Driver Pay Bump After Uber, Lyft Pushback
content: New York City on Friday announced new minimum-pay rules for rideshare drivers, settling on a smaller-than-proposed 5% increase following pushback from Uber Technologies Inc. and Lyft Inc.

title: LinkedIn’s CEO Has Advice to Help AI-Proof Your Career
content: LinkedIn’s CEO offers his thoughts on how AI is changing the way people work, himself included. But first…

title: Meta Discussed Buying Perplexity Before Investing in Scale
content: Meta Platforms Inc. held discussions with artificial intelligence search startup Perplexity AI Inc. about a possible takeover before moving ahead with a multibillion-dollar investment in Scale AI, according to people familiar with the matter.

title: Meta Launches $399 Oakley AI Glasses With 3K Video Recording
content: Meta Platforms Inc. is going up-market with its surprise hit smart glasses, rolling out new models with Oakley that are aimed at athletes and include improved video recording.

title: Aflac Reports Potential Leak of Personal Data in Breach
content: Aflac Inc. said a recent cybersecurity breach could have given intruders unauthorized access to customers’ personal information, including Social Security numbers, as well as health and claims data.

title: Israel Says Iran Is Hacking Private Security Cameras
content: Iran is tapping into private security cameras in Israel to gather real-time intelligence about its adversary, exposing a recurrent problem with the devices that has emerged in other global conflicts. Bloomberg's Michael Shepard reports.  (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Dark Web Forum Tried to Hide by Shifting to Privacy-Focused Crypto
Startup Too Good To Go Weighs €300 Million Funding Round
content: Too Good To Go, which operates an app that allows users to buy near-expired food at a discount, is considering raising €200 million ($231 million) to €300 million in a new funding round to support its business expansion, people familiar with the matter said.

title: Amazon Ends Speedy Delivery by Kia Soul in Favor of Gig Workers
content: Amazon.com Inc. is ending an experiment that saw drivers in Kia Souls make same-day deliveries and will rely on its network of gig-economy workers instead.

title: How Telegram Became a Magnet for Extremists, Crime
content: Messaging service Telegram is one of the most downloaded apps worldwide. Its private chat setting has made it a free space for open discussion in countries with authoritarian regimes. But a relatively light-touch approach to content moderation on Telegram is frustrating governments trying to stop criminal activities and the spread of misinformation that can destabilize societies.

title: Chip Stocks Slide on Report of New Possible Limits on China
content: Shares of Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. and other chipmakers slid on Friday after the Wall Street Journal reported that the Trump administration is considering further restrictions on China.

title: Trump Pledge of Quick China Magnet Flows Has Yet to Materialize
content: Almost 10 days since President Donald Trump declared a “done” trade deal with Beijing, US companies remain largely in the dark on when they’ll receive crucial magnets from China — and whether Washington, in turn, will allow a host of other exports to resume.

title: German Startup Neura Robotics Eyes Up to €1 Billion Round
content: German startup Neura Robotics is targeting to raise as much as €1 billion ($1.2 billion) in new funding as the company prepares to debut a humanoid robot, according to people familiar with the matter.

title: Trust in AI Strongest in China, Low-Income Nations, Study Shows
content: A United Nations study found a sharp global divide on attitudes toward artificial intelligence, with trust strongest in low-income countries and skepticism high in wealthier ones.

title: One in Four Indians Uses Only a Mobile for Content, Ditching TV
content: Nearly one in four Indians said in a survey they use only mobile phones to consume media content, as TVs stay unaffordable for many, prompting companies from Meta Platforms Inc. to Netflix Inc. to boost digital strategies in the world’s largest consumer market.

title: Nidec CEO Stresses Compliance in Shift From Fixation on Growth
content: Nidec Corp. founder Shigenobu Nagamori said the Japanese maker of precision motors is prioritizing compliance, stepping away from a half-century-long focus on profit and growth.

title: ICG Targets €10 Billion for Flagship Flexible Capital Fund
content: Intermediate Capital Group Plc. is looking to raise €10 billion ($11.5 billion) for its flagship flexible capital strategy, according to people familiar with the matter.

title: HBO’s ‘Mountainhead’ Depicts Hollywood’s Sinister View of Tech Titans
content: Welcome to Tech In Depth, our daily newsletter with reporting and analysis about the business of tech from Bloomberg’s journalists around the world. Today, Ellen Huet looks at how HBO’s movie Mountainhead shows the changing cultural view of tech’s rich and powerful.

title: Masa Son Pitches $1 Trillion US AI Hub to TSMC, Trump Team
content: SoftBank Group Corp. founder Masayoshi Son is seeking to team up with Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. to realize what could be his biggest bet yet — a trillion-dollar industrial complex in Arizona to build robots and artificial intelligence.

title: Pignataro’s ION Plans to Invest in Azimut-Backed Fintech
content: Andrea Pignataro’s ION Group plans to buy a minority stake in a new Italian digital bank backed by private equity firm FSI SGR SpA and asset manager Azimut Holding SpA, according to people familiar with the matter.

title: Israeli Officials Warn Iran Is Hijacking Security Cameras to Spy
content: Iran is tapping into private security cameras in Israel to gather real-time intelligence about its adversary, exposing a recurrent problem with the devices that has emerged in other global conflicts.

title: Surging UK Grocery Bills Threaten to Rekindle Inflation Fears
content: Surging grocery bills are threatening to slow the pace of the Bank of England’s interest-rate cuts by raising the risk that inflation will stay elevated even as the UK economy shows signs of sputtering.

title: India to See Limited Inflation Fallout From Oil, Government Adviser Says
content: India’s top government adviser said rising oil prices are likely to have a limited impact on inflation for now and Asia’s third-largest economy remains in a relatively favorable position to weather global risks.

title: Waller Says Fed Could Cut Interest Rates as Soon as July
content: Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller said the central bank can lower interest rates as soon as next month, reiterating his view that the inflation hit from tariffs is likely to be short-lived.

title: Fed’s Daly Says Next Rate Cut More Likely in the Fall
content: Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco President Mary Daly said an interest-rate cut this fall looks more appropriate than moving when policymakers gather in July.

title: America the Avoidable: Why Trump’s Policies Could Cost US Tourism Billions
content: On today’s Big Take podcast: How President Trump’s “American First” policies have kept international tourists away, forecasted to cost the US travel industry billions.

title: Fed’s Musalem Reports Multiple Real Estate Transactions
content: A new set of financial disclosures for Federal Reserve regional bank heads released Friday show that St. Louis Fed President Alberto Musalem and his spouse sold and purchased several residential real estate holdings last year.

title: The Two New Tensions at the Federal Reserve
content: Hello and welcome to the newsletter, a grab bag of daily content from the Odd Lots universe. Sometimes it's us, Joe Weisenthal and Tracy Alloway, bringing you our thoughts on the most recent developments in markets, finance and the economy. And sometimes it's contributions from our network of expert guests and sources. Whatever it is, we promise it will always be interesting.

title: Trump Pledge of Quick China Magnet Flows Has Yet to Materialize
content: Almost 10 days since President Donald Trump declared a “done” trade deal with Beijing, US companies remain largely in the dark on when they’ll receive crucial magnets from China — and whether Washington, in turn, will allow a host of other exports to resume.

title: Fed Says Labor Market Balanced, Points to Immigration Slowdown
content: A sharp stepdown in immigration has led the supply of workers to grow more slowly, helping to keep the labor market in balance as job growth cools, the Federal Reserve said Friday.

title: Canada Retail Sales Fell 1.1% in May, Largest Drop in a Year
content: The strain on Canadian consumers became more evident last month after a rush to buy cars ahead of price increases from tariffs appeared to come to an end.

title: Thousands of Laid-Off Government Workers Are Flooding a Shrinking Job Market
content: Thousands of private government consultants laid off during the Trump administration’s cost-cutting crusade are increasingly flooding a shrinking labor market.

title: RBI Front-Loaded Rate Action to Spur Demand, Minutes Show
content: India’s rate-setters opted for a larger-than-expected interest rate cut to spur demand, while adjusting the policy stance to retain flexibility amid global uncertainty, minutes of the central bank’s policy meeting showed Friday.

title: Banks Offer Higher Rates on Deposits as BOE Drains Liquidity
content: UK banks are offering unusually high interest rates to clients in order to attract cash, the latest sign of how the Bank of England’s balance-sheet reduction is shrinking liquidity in the system.

title: Plunging UK Retail Sales Deepen Concern About Broader Slowdown
content: A dramatic drop in UK retail sales is raising fresh questions about the sustainability of Britain’s recent growth spurt and Prime Minister Keir Starmer’s plans to use it to restore controversial benefit cuts.

title: Thriving Southern Cities Face Economic Threat From Funding Cuts
content: North Carolina's Research Triangle shows how federal efforts to curb spending are unleashing economic uncertainty in communities across the US.

title: China Shrugs Off Tariffs But Not its Property Slump
content: I’m Malcolm Scott, international economics editor in Sydney. Today we’re looking at China’s property drag. Send us feedback and tips to ecodaily@bloomberg.net. And if you aren’t yet signed up to receive this newsletter, you can do so here.

title: Japan Surprises With Bigger Cut to Super-Long Bond Issuance
content: Japan is planning to cut the issuance of super-long bonds this year by more than earlier reported as it tries to restore calm to a market spooked by recent record highs in yields.

title: Political Woes Could Sink Thai Economy Deeper Into Malaise
content: Thailand’s sudden descent into a new political crisis threatens an economy that’s already on the brink of a technical recession and bracing for the impact of the global trade war.

title: BOE’s Bailey Raises Doubts Over Digital Pound for Consumers
content: Bank of England Governor Andrew Bailey cast doubt on the need for a digital pound for consumers, calling into question whether the UK will push ahead with its plans.

title: A Guide to Trade Talks, Trump-Style: Is His Unorthodox Approach Working?
content: The president is trying force rather than persuasion to secure improved access to foreign markets for US companies. The quick wins he promised are yet to materialize.

title: Zichen Wang's Exit Interview From America
content: The popular Substacker returns home to China.

title: Odd Lots: Zichen Wang’s Exit Interview from America (Podcast)
content: Zichen Wang is the writer of the Pekingnology newsletter, which translates important speeches and articles from China into English, and contextualizes them for Western readers. Over the past year, he’s been a master’s degree student at Princeton University, although he’s recently returned home to resume his career at a think tank in China. His stint in the US obviously came at a very interesting time, both due to the rising US-China tensions, and also the growing restrictions on Chinese students

title: French Manufacturing Confidence Unexpectedly Dips in June
content: French manufacturing confidence fell unexpectedly in June, adding to warning signs for an economy already struggling to keep pace with European peers.

title: Trump Administration’s New Rule Will Limit Obamacare Enrollments
content: Trump administration officials on Friday finalized regulations aimed at making it more difficult to enroll in health insurance through the Affordable Care Act.

title: Hedge Funds Rush Into Oil Long Bets as Mideast Conflict Grows
content: Hedge funds boosted their bullish position in Brent crude by the most since early October as Israel’s strikes against Iran’s nuclear program imperiled a region that produces around a third of the world’s oil.

title: America the Avoidable: Why Trump’s Policies Could Cost US Tourism Billions
content: On today’s Big Take podcast: How President Trump’s “American First” policies have kept international tourists away, forecasted to cost the US travel industry billions.

title: Third Point, Arb Funds Reap Big Gains as US Steel Bet Pays Out
content: US hedge funds including Third Point LLC and Pentwater Capital Management are reaping a windfall from bets that political noise wouldn’t keep United States Steel Corp. from completing its $14.1 billion deal with its Japanese suitor.

title: How Long Before We Get a $6 Trillion Sports Team?
content: The LA Lakers being acquired for $10 billion smashes the record for a pro franchise.

title: CareerBuilder and Monster Venture Said to Consider Bankruptcy
content: A joint venture involving CareerBuilder and Monster, the early pioneers of online job hunting, is working with advisers on a potential bankruptcy filing, according to people familiar with the situation.

title: Alberta Pension Looks For New CIO Amid Push to Expand Calgary Office
content: Alberta Investment Management Corp. is hunting for a new chief investment officer as it carries out an overhaul that began last year when the provincial government fired the board and its top executive.

title: Kroger Sales Beat Expectations on Steady Grocery Spending
content: Kroger Co.’s sales surpassed expectations during the latest quarter, a sign that consumers are still spending on groceries and other essentials despite economic turbulence.

title: Mark Walter Is Creating a Sports Empire With $10 Billion Lakers
content: For just under $10 billion, private equity firm 3G Capital recently bought Skechers — an ascendant global footwear brand with $9 billion in annual sales and 20,000 employees spread across 5,300 stores.

title: Not All Ritalin Is Created Equal: Why Some Generics Fail to Work
content: Stanford University researchers have discovered why some people with attention deficit hyperactivity disorder may do well on their medicine for a while but struggle down the road.

title: Weight-Loss Drugs Should Be First Step to Prevent Heart Disease, Top Cardiology Group Says
content: Millions more Americans should be taking weight-loss drugs to prevent heart disease, according to the American College of Cardiology.

title: QXO Won’t Raise Its Offer for GMS After Report of Home Depot Bid
content: QXO Inc. won’t raise its $5 billion offer for building products distributor GMS Inc. after Home Depot Inc. reportedly made its own bid.

title: Citigroup Hires JPMorgan Tech Veteran Rajkovic as M&A Co-Head
content: Citigroup Inc. is hiring veteran JPMorgan Chase & Co. banker Drago Rajkovic as global co-head of mergers and acquisitions, as the US lender continues poaching senior dealmakers from its rivals to bolster its investment banking franchise.

title: Freeport CEO Says Tariffs Threaten US Copper Mining
content: The threat of US levies on copper imports has been a boon for Freeport-McMoRan Inc., with North America’s top producer cashing in on selling the metal at a premium. Still, the firm’s top boss warns that broader tariffs could hurt an industry President Donald Trump is trying to help.

title: Citadel’s Fixed Income Head Edwin Lin Is Taking a Sabbatical
content: Edwin Lin, Citadel’s head of fixed income and macro, is taking a sabbatical from the firm after 14 years.

title: Darden Weighs Sale of Bahama Breeze Restaurant Chain
content: Darden Restaurants Inc. is considering “strategic alternatives” for its Bahama Breeze chain, Chief Executive Officer Rick Cardenas said.

title: Mulberry Seeks Fresh Cash for Turnaround as Losses Set to Widen
content: Mulberry Group Plc warned on profit and said it needs to raise £20 million ($27 million) to fund the British handbag maker’s turnaround plan.

title: UniCredit Taps Adviser for BPM Bid Branch Sales Amid Deal Doubts
content: UniCredit SpA has tapped an investment bank to manage the possible sale of branches it needs to carry out if it buys Banco BPM SpA, according to people familiar with the matter.

title: Banks Face €5 Billion French Dividend Tax Bill, Senator Says
content: Banks in France are facing a combined tax bill of as much as €5 billion ($5.8 billion) over contentious trades allegedly designed to escape levies on dividend payments, according to a lawmaker who dubbed the process a “fraud.”

title: US Banks That Fueled Ireland’s Finance Rebound Face Tariff Angst
content: When the US launched sweeping tariffs against trade partners in April, BlackRock Inc. Chief Executive Officer Larry Fink found himself in Ireland, one of the countries with most to lose if US multinationals were forced to curtail their operations overseas.

title: Greenland Awards Permit for Metal Critical to Defense Industry
content: Greenland has given permission to a Canadian mining company to explore for molybdenum, a metal critical to the production of steel, amid growing demand from the defense industry.

title: Can Saudi Arabia’s Aramco Fuel a New Era?
content: Saudi Arabia’s Aramco has been synonymous with oil, but its next generation extends far beyond petrochemicals. The company is evolving into a tech-driven energy giant, investing heavily in AI, renewables, and low-carbon initiatives like hydrogen and carbon capture. Despite geopolitical tensions, Aramco remains the backbone of Saudi government revenue. We travel to Dhahran to get a first-hand look at the parallel stories of the Kingdom and Aramco. (Source: Bloomberg)

Summers agrees but warns that rising inflation and unemployment make the Fed’s job harder. He also highlights the potential economic fallout from U.S.-Iran tensions. Summers criticizes New York mayoral candidate Zohran Mamdani’s platform as “profoundly dangerous” for not only the city, but also for the country. (Source: Bloomberg)

How a Cornered Iran Could Wreak Havoc on Global Oil Trade
content: US airstrikes on Iranian nuclear facilities are sharpening the focus on one option Iran has yet to really deploy in the conflict: disrupting regional oil trade, especially through the critical Strait of Hormuz.

title: Options Traders Wrestle With Stocks’ Muted Reaction to War Risk
content: The stock market’s recent calm in the face of rising geopolitical threats had left options traders with a conundrum: sell volatility and risk being blindsided should the Middle East conflict escalate; or buy it and bleed away premiums as actual moves stay subdued. That tension is set to ratchet even higher after the US attacked Iranian nuclear sites.

title: Investors Set to Flock to Safety as World Awaits Iran’s Response
content: Traders are forecasting a drop in stocks, a jump in crude prices and possibly a strengthening of the dollar as investors head for safety in the wake of the US attack on Iran’s three main nuclear sites.

title: Billions of Fans Anticipate Netflix’s New Adventure
content: As the $76 billion industry evolves, everyone is racing to capture attention and market share through immersive experiences in a space dominated by traditional media players, Disney and NBCUniversal. While legacy parks rely on decades-old IP and massive capital investments, Netflix is tapping into fan obsession with shows like Stranger Things and Squid Game to launch live experiences in malls and cities worldwide. At the same time, family-owned Herschend is betting that old is gold to keep visitors coming back to parks like Silver Dollar City. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: How Will Iran Respond to Trump's Air Strikes?
content: The US carried out airstrikes on three nuclear sites in Iran, directly entering Israel's war with Tehran, despite President Donald Trump's promises to avoid new foreign conflicts. Trump says Iran's nuclear capabilities have been obliterated. Iran says the attacks were "outrageous." Bloomberg's Joumanna Bercetche reports on how Iran could respond and the reaction from the Middle East.  (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Hegseth and Gen. Caine Detail Air Strikes Against Iran
content: US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth and General Dan Caine, the chairman of the US Joint Chiefs of Staff, detail the strike against three Iranian nuclear facilities. Dubbed "Operation Midnight Hammer," it involved B-2 bombers,  a submarine that launched Tomahawk cruise missiles and bunker-buster bombs. Hegseth says the mission was not about a regime change in Iran. They speak at the Pentagon. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Israeli Stocks Rise as Traders See US Hastening End to Conflict
content: Middle Eastern stocks rose on Sunday, led by Israel and Egypt, as the region’s traders bet the US strikes on Iran may accelerate the end of the conflict between the country and Israel.

title: Central Banks in Asia Are Becoming Wary of Currency Intervention
content: Some of emerging Asia’s biggest central banks look to be dialing back their interventions in the currency market.

title: Trump’s Airstrikes on Iran Leave Oil Market Braced for Surge
content: Oil traders are preparing for an oil-price surge when trading reopens, with the focus on whether Tehran’s retaliation to US airstrikes will lead to a disruption in crude flows that have been largely unaffected so far.

title: NATO Offers to Tweak 5% Spending Goal to Win Spanish Approval
content: NATO has offered to tweak key language on ambitious defense spending targets to help win support from holdout Spain, before leaders of the military alliance gather on Tuesday.

title: Robinhood CEO Vlad Tenev Wants to Change the Future of AI
content: The race to creating the most efficient and most intelligent AI programs has some unlikely contenders who are hoping to redefine specific industries through more advanced models. Robinhood’s Vlad Tenev is developing “mathematical superintelligence” for provable accuracy in math and science, while SandboxAQ’s Jack Hidary backs “large quantitative models” trained on numbers, not words. As billions flow into AI, the future may not be one-size-fits-all models like ChatGPT. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: China Condemns Trump’s Iran Attack in First Comment Since US Hit
content: China criticized the US strike on Iranian nuclear facilities and again said it’s willing to join international efforts to restore peace in the Middle East.

title: British, Singapore Airlines Halt Gulf Flights After Iran Strike
content: British Airways and Singapore Airlines canceled flights to the Persian Gulf, increasing aviation disruptions in the region after the US struck three nuclear sites in Iran and Tehran vowed to retaliate.

title: Congo Adds Three Months to Cobalt Export Ban to Curb Supply
content: The Democratic Republic of Congo extended a temporary ban on cobalt exports by three months, according to a statement from a regulatory agency, prolonging its efforts to rein in a glut on the international market.

title: Euro-Area Economy Needs More ECB Stimulus, Centeno Tells Stampa
content: The European Central Bank needs to provide the euro-area economy with “further stimulus,” Governing Council member Mario Centeno told Italy’s La Stampa.

title: US Attack Against Iran Hinged on Misdirection and Decoys
content: The US strikes that targeted Iran’s nuclear sites involved a decoy mission aimed at drawing attention from flight trackers while the largest-ever deployment of B-2 stealth bombers delivered 30,000-pound bunker-buster bombs for the first time in combat.

title: Shipping on High Alert in Mideast After US Strikes on Iran
content: The shipping industry was placed on high alert on Sunday with warnings that Tehran could retaliate against commercial vessels following after US airstrikes against Iran’s nuclear facilities.

title: Ivory Coast’s Ouattara Delays Decision on Fourth Term Bid
content: Ivory Coast President Alassane Ouattara surprised delegates as he shelved his decision to accept the party’s nomination as the presidential candidate for October elections to a later date.

title: Trump Stakes His Legacy on Iran Attack
content: It remains unclear if this is the end of the military campaign, or whether the confrontation could spiral into a push for regime change in Tehran
