content: The US carried out airstrikes on three nuclear sites in Iran overnight, directly entering Israel’s war with Tehran despite President Donald Trump’s longtime promises to avoid new foreign conflicts.

title: How the US Dropped Bunker-Busting Bombs on Iran’s Nuclear Sites
content: In the first American military strike ever on Iran, dubbed Operation Midnight Hammer, the US on June 21 dropped 14 of the largest conventional bombs in its arsenal on the country’s facilities for producing enriched uranium.

title: Bombing Iran’s Nuclear Sites Complicates Hunt for What’s Left
content: The task of ensuring Iran doesn’t build a weapon might just have got tougher.

title: What If Iran Tries to Close the Strait of Hormuz?
content: The US bombed Iran’s three main nuclear sites in a major escalation of this month’s conflict in the Middle East. Tehran said it will reserve all options to defend itself.

title: Thailand, Cambodia Shut Land Crossings as Border Row Worsens
content: Thailand and Cambodia shut several border crossings in tit-for-tat moves, ratcheting up tensions between the two Southeast Asian neighbors as Prime Minister Paetongtarn Shinawatra fights to save her government from a political crisis triggered by a leaked phone call over the weekslong standoff.

title: UK Says Not Involved in Strikes on Iran, But Supports Outcome
content: The UK said its military wasn’t involved in American air strikes on Iran, although a cabinet minister expressed support for their results.

title: Ukraine Commander Says Russia Shows No Sign of Winding Down War
content: Russia shows no signs it plans to wind down its war in Ukraine, with an estimated 695,000 troops deployed across an expanded front line and another 121,000 in strategic reserve, according to Ukraine’s commander-in-chief Oleksandr Syrskyi.

title: Gulf States Fear Escalation as US Iran Strikes Rattle Region
content: Iran’s Arab neighbors urged restraint and warned of potentially devastating implications for the region after US strikes on Tehran’s nuclear program raised the prospects for all-out war in the Middle East.

title: Iran Says ‘All Options’ Open After US Strikes on Atomic Sites
content: Iran warned that US strikes on three Iranian nuclear sites early Sunday will trigger “everlasting consequences” and said it “reserves all options” to respond.

content: Novo Nordisk A/S’s next-generation obesity shot CagriSema helped patients lose weight in large studies despite only about three-quarters of the patients ever making it to the highest dose. Surprisingly, patients who chose to stick with a lower dose lost more weight on average.

content: South African contractors jailed in Equatorial Guinea after working in the country’s offshore oil fields returned home on Saturday following more than two years of detention.

content: “The US administration holds the sole and full responsibility for the consequences of its actions, including the Islamic Republic of Iran’s right to self-defense under the principles of the United Charter,” Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said on Sunday. “Iran reserves all options to defend its security interests and people,” he added. (Source: Associated Press)

content: “The Islamic Republic of Iran condemns in the strongest terms the United States’ brutal military aggression against Iran’s peaceful nuclear facilities, Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said on Sunday. “The warmongering and lawless administration in Washington is solely and fully responsible for the dangerous consequences and far-reaching implications of its act of aggression,” Araghchi added. (Source: Associated Press)

content: Japanese equities snapped a three-day losing streak after US President Donald Trump announced a tentative ceasefire between Iran and Israel that soothed market sentiment.

content: Gold fell as haven demand ebbed after US President Donald Trump announced that Israel and Iran had agreed to a ceasefire.

title: Horizons Middle East & Africa 06/24/2025
content: Horizons Middle East & Africa is your daily spotlight on one of the world's fastest-growing regions. Live from Dubai, we bring you the latest global markets and analysis, plus news-making interviews, with a special focus on MEA. All that and more, as you head to the office in the Gulf, pause for lunch in Hong Kong, or start your day in London or Johannesburg.  (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Oil Extends Drop as Trump Forges Middle East Ceasefire Agreement
content: Oil extended a slump as US President Donald Trump announced a ceasefire between Iran and Israel.

title: Virgin Australia CEO Downplays Mideast Fears as Shares Debut
content: Virgin Australia Holdings Ltd. Chief Executive Officer Dave Emerson brushed away concerns the Middle East conflict will disrupt demand for travel as the airline surged on its return to the stock exchange in Sydney.

title: Bain’s Virgin Australia Rises 11% in Sydney After Relisting
content: Bain Capital’s Virgin Australia rose in Sydney trading after raising A$685 million ($444 million) in one of the country’s biggest initial public offerings of the year.

title: Issuers Offer Rare Bond Safeguards as Japan Seeks Bigger Market
content: Two Japanese companies sold bonds that offer protection for investors against events like corporate takeovers, in rare moves that reflect the desire of policymakers to broaden the market to include riskier borrowers.

title: China On Target to Launch National Power Market by End of Year
content: China is on target to launch a unified national power trading market by the end of this year, according to its main electricity grid operator.

title: Japan Bourse CEO Reappointed With Slimmer Vote as Rating Falls
content: Japan Exchange Group Inc. chief executive officer Hiromi Yamaji was re-elected with a smaller majority as his approval rating slid to the lowest ever and the bourse operator’s shares underperformed the market benchmark.

title: CBA’s Market Cap Tops $200 Billion in Unswerving Stock Rally
content: Commonwealth Bank of Australia’s market value hit a fresh milestone, with the stock seemingly undeterred by recent geopolitical tensions that have rattled equity markets.

title: PhonePe Is Said to Seek $1.5 Billion for India IPO
content: Walmart Inc.’s PhonePe, India’s largest provider of digital payments, is preparing to file preliminary documents for an initial public offering that may raise as much as $1.5 billion, according to people familiar with the matter.

title: The Asia Trade 06/26/2025
content: "Bloomberg: The Asia Trade" brings you everything you need to know to get ahead as the trading day begins in Asia. title: Australia’s Top Iron Ore Export Hub Has Busiest May on Record
content: Iron ore shipments from the largest bulk-export terminal set a record for the month of May, putting flows at the biggest year-to-date volumes even after weather issues curbed exports earlier in 2025.

title: Handjani: Israel Started War During Iran-US Negotiations
content: Iran and Israel may be nearing a pause in their 12-day war. The proposed ceasefire deal follows a measured Iranian attack on a US base in Qatar, that caused no casualties. Amir Handjani, Non-resident fellow at the Quincy Institute for Responsible Statecraft spoke to Bloomberg's Horizons Middle East and Africa anchor Joumanna Bercetche about the path ahead for US Israel and Iran. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: What Deals to Expect at the US-Africa Business Summit
content: The US-Africa Business Summit started in Luanda, Angola. At the opening of the event, Angolan President Joao Lourenco called on US companies to expand their investments in Africa beyond traditional oil and mineral extraction to industries such as automobiles, shipbuilding, tourism, cement and steel. Bloomberg’s Jennifer Zabasajja reports on what deals can be expected.

title: Ex-CIA: Iran's Nuclear Facilities Far From 'Obliterated'
content:
Former CIA official Paul Pillar says he thinks Iran's nuclear facilities are far from obliterated.
He also told us that President Trump's ceasefire declaration could be nothing more than "inertia selling."
He appeared on Bloomberg's Insight with Haslinda Amin. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: China’s Oil Refiners Hold Off Buying as Weak Demand Hits Profits
content: China’s oil refiners are keeping to the sidelines of global crude markets, as geopolitical developments roil prices and weaker domestic demand eats into their profitability.

title: Japan’s 20-Year Sale Shows Market Still Wary on Longer Bonds
content: Demand at Japan’s 20-year bond sale was slightly lower than the average over the past year, indicating that investors are still cautious even after the government adjusted its borrowing plans to calm a surge in yields.

title: Tata Capital Is Said to Get SEBI Approval for $2 Billion IPO
content: Tata Capital Ltd. received the approval of India’s markets regulator to proceed with its plans for an initial public offering that may fetch about $2 billion, according to people familiar with the matter, in what is expected to be the country’s biggest listing this year.

title: ECB Can Still Cut Rates in Next Six Months, Villeroy Tells FT
content: The European Central Bank could still cut interest rates in the next half year, Governing Council member Francois Villeroy de Galhau told the Financial Times.

title: Is It Over When Trump Says It’s Over? We’ll See
content: Oil prices couldn’t wait to fall again, but it’s unclear what Iran has really agreed to.

title: Standard Bank Chairman on Managing Uncertainties
content: Nonkululeko Nyembezi, Chairman at Africa's Standard Bank Group, says the Africa continent is facing uncertainty that is at a "level that is hard to cope with." She speaks with Stephen Engle on the sidelines at the World Economic Forum’s Annual Meeting of the New Champions in Tianjin. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: SNB Rate Seen Stuck at Zero This Year After Last Week’s Cut
content: The Swiss National Bank probably won’t act this year on its threat of cutting borrowing costs to below zero, according to a majority of economists.

title: Germany Reaches Deal With States on Sharing Burden From Tax Cuts
content: Germany’s ruling coalition reached an agreement with the country’s state premiers on how to share the financial burden from planned corporate tax cuts meant to boost economic growth.

title: Israel Agrees to Truce With Iran After Trump Push to End War
content: US President Donald Trump said a ceasefire is now in place between Iran and Israel, moments after Israeli emergency services said at least three people were killed by Iranian strikes.

title: Singapore’s Premier Vows Closer China Cooperation in Xi Meeting
content: Singapore’s Prime Minister Lawrence Wong pledged to deepen bilateral cooperation in a meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping, as the trade-dependent city-state confronts intensifying tensions between Beijing and Washington.

title: Spain and Rutte Locked in a Showdown on Eve of NATO Summit
content: By refusing to agree spending increases to appease US President Donald Trump, Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez threatens to derail a NATO summit that Secretary General Mark Rutte needs to run smoothly for the sake of the military alliance’s future survival.

title: French Government Under Pressure as Pension Talks Stumble
content: Negotiations over France’s contentious retirement reform ended in deadlock late Monday, raising the chances of government collapse should opposition parties unite in a no-confidence vote.

title: Seoul Foreign Minister Pick to Prioritize US-North Korea Talks
content: South Korea’s foreign minister nominee Cho Hyun pledged to make resuming the US-North Korea dialogue a top priority, underscoring new President Lee Jae Myung’s vision of building lasting peace on the Korean Peninsula.

title: China Slams Taiwan’s Lai for Speech Mentioning Independence
content: China harshly condemned Taiwanese President Lai Ching-te for a speech aimed at rallying the democracy’s 23 million people to stand up to its larger neighbor — a back-and-forth that illustrates a deepening cross-strait divide.

title: Thai PM Faces Legal Challenges After Averting Coalition Collapse
content: Thailand’s anti-graft agency will probe Prime Minister Paetongtarn Shinawatra’s controversial phone call with ex-Cambodian leader Hun Sen, according to local media reports, as her rivals seek legal recourse to force her ouster.

title: Japan’s Akazawa Says Still Working on Date for Next Trade Talks
content: Japan and the US are still working on setting the timing for the next round of cabinet-level trade talks, Japan’s point person for the negotiations said, as the deadline for a deal to avert another hike in tariffs nears.

title: Iran-Israel War Heads Toward Pause After Trump Claims Ceasefire
content: Iran and Israel appeared to be nearing a pause in their 12-day war after President Donald Trump announced a surprise ceasefire in a conflict that saw key Iranian military leaders and scientists killed, US bombing of Iranian nuclear sites and a salvo of missiles launched at Qatar.

title: Kospi Surges to Lead Stock Gains in Asia After Mideast Ceasefire
content: Asia’s stock benchmark climbed the most in seven weeks, led by technology shares, as risk sentiment improved after US President Donald Trump announced a tentative ceasefire between Israel and Iran.

title: YouTube Exemption From Australian Teen Social Media Ban Opposed by Regulator
content: Australia’s online regulator called on the government to reverse its controversial exemption for YouTube from a social media ban for under-16s, an unusual intervention that echoes similar pleas from rival platforms including Facebook and TikTok.

title: Australia Must Choose Defense or Social Spending, Rabobank Says
Thailand Targets Cambodian Scam Centers Amid Border Dispute
content: Thailand announced a raft of security and trade measures to cripple transnational crime syndicates in Cambodia, as Prime Minister Paetongtarn Shinawatra seeks an upper hand in a simmering border dispute with its neighbor.

title: Harvard Wins Longer Block on Trump’s Foreign Student Ban
content: A federal judge issued another court order letting Harvard University keep hosting foreign students, this one in its fight to overturn President Donald Trump’s proclamation barring their entry to the US.

title: UK Urges Iran to Grasp Opportunity to Return to Talks
content: The UK has urged Iran to de-escalate and return to talks with the international community following the announcement of a ceasefire in its conflict with Israel.

title: Korean Consumer Confidence Jumps to 4-Year High on Stimulus Hope
content: South Korea’s consumer confidence rose to the highest in four years as easing domestic political uncertainty, fresh fiscal stimulus and hopes for pro-growth policies under the new administration buoyed sentiment.

title: Senate GOP to Offer $40,000 SALT Cap With Lower Income Threshold
content: Senate Republicans are coming around to the $40,000 cap on state and local tax deduction key House lawmakers demand in President Donald Trump’s massive tax package, but they want to lower the income threshold.

title: Key Senator Calls to Delay Meeting of New RFK Jr. Vaccine Panel
content: Republican Senator Bill Cassidy is seeking to delay a scheduled meeting of vaccine advisers selected by Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. out of concern they’re not sufficiently qualified.

title: Putin Going to War With NATO Would Cost World $1.5 Trillion
content: The NATO chief says Russia may be ready for an attack on eastern Europe within five years. Bloomberg Economics ran the numbers on what that would mean.

title: UK Welcomes £40 Billion Amazon Investment Plan in Warehouses
content: UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer welcomed a three-year program by Amazon.com Inc. to invest £40 billion ($54 billion) in the British economy over the next three years, including opening four new warehouses.

title: Trump Thanks Iran After Attack Choreographed to De-Escalate
content: The Qataris knew the missile barrage was coming. So did the Americans. The Iranians had told them.

title: Supreme Court Backs Trump on Deportations With Short Notice
content: A sharply divided US Supreme Court let the Trump administration resume quickly deporting migrants to countries other than their own, lifting a judge’s order that gave people 10 days notice and a chance to argue they would be at risk of torture.

title: Gulf States Reopen Airspace and Resume Flight Operations
content: Several Persian Gulf states, including Qatar and the United Arab Emirates, have reopened their airspace and resumed operations at some of the world’s busiest airports after halting flights as Iran launched air strikes at a US base in Qatar.

title: UK Vows to Spend 5% of GDP on Security by 2035 to Hit NATO Goal
content: UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer will vow to spend 5% of British economic output on security by 2035, embracing an ambitious NATO target sought by President Donald Trump without providing a path on how to get there.

title: EU and Canada Sign Security Pact as Carney Pivots From US
content: The European Union and Canada have signed a security partnership that moves them closer to cooperation on military purchases, as Prime Minister Mark Carney aims to reduce his country’s dependence on the US for defense.

title: FTC Clears Omnicom Deal After Barring Advertising Boycotts Over Politics
content: Omnicom Group Inc., the third-largest US advertising agency, agreed to stop withholding online ads for political reasons to clear the way for federal antitrust regulators to approve the company’s $13.5 billion buyout of rival Interpublic Group.

Earlier, US President Donald Trump had shared a post on Truth Social saying a ceasefire “is now in effect” and urging parties not to violate it. Bloomberg’s Joumanna Bercetche reports.

title: The Impact of Airspace Closures on Flights, Aviation
content: Israel reopened its airspace, the Airport Authority said. Several Persian Gulf states, including Qatar and the United Arab Emirates, also reopened their airspace and resumed operations at some of the world’s busiest airports. Bloomberg’s Benedikt Kammel breaks down the situation and discusses what impacts airspace closures have on the broader aviation industry.

title: NATO Summit: What to Expect, Defense Spending Goals
content: The NATO summit is being held in The Hague against the backdrop of conflicts in the Middle East and Russia’s ongoing invasion of Ukraine. Meanwhile, Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez is refusing to agree to defense spending increases. Bloomberg’s Oliver Crook breaks down the situation and what to expect from the gathering in the Netherlands.

content: In a post on Truth Social, US President Donald Trump said a ceasefire “is now in effect.” He added: “Please do not violate it!” Bloomberg’s Joumanna Bercetche reports.

content: Iran and Israel may be nearing a pause in their war after US President Donald Trump announced a ceasefire. The specific timing of the pause and Israel’s response to Trump’s announcement remain uncertain. Meanwhile, attacks were reported by both sides in the early hours of Tuesday. Bloomberg’s Paul Wallace reports.

content: Project A, a German venture capital firm that has placed early bets on defense startups, raised a €325 million ($373 million) fund to back European companies.

content: Thailand’s richest man Charoen Sirivadhanabhakdi distributed stakes in holding firms which control about 66% of Thai Beverage Pcl to his five children, though stopped short of handing over full control of the drinks giant.

title: Google Faces UK Pressure Over AI Search Summary, Advertising
content: Alphabet Inc.’s Google is set to face more scrutiny from the UK’s antitrust watchdog over its online search and advertising business.

title: China on Cusp of Seeing Over 100 DeepSeeks, Ex-Top Official Says
content: China’s advantages in developing artificial intelligence are about to unleash a wave of innovation that will generate more than 100 DeepSeek-like breakthroughs in the coming 18 months, according to a former top official.

title: VC Firm Project A Raises €325 Million Fund for European Startups
content: Project A, a German venture capital firm that has placed early bets on defense startups, raised a €325 million ($373 million) fund to back European companies.

title: JPMorgan Sees Asian Tech Stocks Gaining Another 15-20% This Year
content: Asian technology stocks may rally another 15%-20% this year, driven mainly by the strong momentum in the artificial intelligence space, according to JPMorgan Chase & Co.

title: YouTube Exemption From Australian Teen Social Media Ban Opposed by Regulator
content: Australia’s online regulator called on the government to reverse its controversial exemption for YouTube from a social media ban for under-16s, an unusual intervention that echoes similar pleas from rival platforms including Facebook and TikTok.

title: Jensen Huang Starts Selling Nvidia Stock Under $865 Million Plan
content: Nvidia Corp. Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang has started selling the chipmaker’s stock, his first transactions under a plan that allows him to offload up to $865 million worth by year’s end.

title: Chinese Investors Trim Exposure to Tencent After April Peak
content: Chinese investors have steadily reduced their exposure to Tencent Holdings Ltd. over the past two months as the tech giant struggles to maintain market enthusiasm.

title: Samsung Is Poised to Unveil Latest Folding Smartphones on July 9
content: Company announces will introduce new Galaxy devices and AI features at Unpacked summer event

title: Tesla Shares Jump Most in Two Months on Robotaxi Rollout
content: Tesla Inc. shares climbed after the automaker rolled out its long-promised driverless taxi service to a handful of riders, a modest debut for what Elon Musk sees as a transformative new business line.

title: Defense Tech Sector Reacts to US-Iran Strike | Bloomberg Tech 6/23/2025
content: Bloomberg’s Caroline Hyde discusses the US strike on Iranian nuclear sites and the market impact. Plus, defense tech investors look for startups addressing asymmetric threats. And Tesla’s robotaxi service gets underway with a modest launch. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Meta Held Deal Talks With Startup Runway in AI Recruiting Push
content: Meta Platforms Inc. Chief Executive Officer Mark Zuckerberg discussed a possible acquisition with video startup Runway AI Inc., as part of his deal-making drive in artificial intelligence.

title: House Bans WhatsApp From Staffers’ Government-Issued Devices
content: Meta’s WhatsApp messaging platform has been added to a list of apps banned from government-issued devices for congressional staffers in the US House of Representatives, a move driven by concerns about the app’s data security.

title: VSCO Debuts Standalone iPhone Camera App With Popular Photo Filters
content: Capture joins a growing group of apps positioned as alternatives to Apple’s iPhone camera software.

title: Murati’s Thinking Machines Raises Cash at $10 Billion Valuation
content: Andreessen Horowitz, Accel and Conviction Partners have invested in the former OpenAI executive’s startup.

title: Super Micro Seeks $2 Billion Convertible Bond as Deals Ramp Up
content: Super Micro Computer Inc. is raising $2 billion from the sale of convertible bonds, extending a dramatic run of companies tapping the resurgent market to secure cheap capital.

title: CityFibre Set to Secure Close to £2 Billion for Fiber Rollout
content: CityFibre is nearing an agreement for about £2 billion ($2.7 billion) in fresh capital in a round that will help the fiber company continue operating and expand its reach, according to people familiar with the matter.

title: Tesla Rolls Out Robotaxi in Austin to Handful of Users
content: Tesla Inc. rolled out its long-awaited robotaxi service to a handful of users following almost a decade of hype from Elon Musk, kicking off a precarious new era for the carmaker. Some online influencers were invited to take a ride. A human "safety monitor" rode in the front passenger seat. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Wolfspeed Plans Bankruptcy After Clinching Deal With Creditors
content: Wolfspeed Inc. is planning to file for bankruptcy by July 1 with a deal to slash its debt by about $4.6 billion and hand over control to convertible noteholders.

title: Robo-adviser Wealthfront Files Confidentially for an IPO
content: The robo-advisory firm Wealthfront filed confidentially for a US initial public offering, a signal that more financial-technology firms are set to go public after a protracted lull.

title: Strategy Makes Second-Smallest Bitcoin Purchase Since November
content: Strategy bought $26 million of Bitcoin over the past seven days, the second-smallest weekly acquisition announced by the Michael Saylor-led digital-asset treasury company since he ramped up its cryptocurrency purchases more than six months ago.

title: Military Satellite Maker Iceye Explores IPO as Sales on Track to Double
content: A Finnish satellite startup that’s benefiting from Europe’s military spending boom expects to double sales this year and is exploring an initial public offering.

title: Huawei’s New Laptop Adds to Evidence of Stalled Chip Advance
content: Huawei Technologies Co.’s latest computer product is powered by a chip manufactured using years-old technology, suggesting US sanctions are still preventing China from developing cutting-edge semiconductor technologies.

title: Hedge Fund Executives Eye $100 Million to Accumulate BNB Token
content: A team of crypto hedge fund executives are in advanced talks to raise $100 million for investing in a token linked to Binance Holdings Ltd. through a publicly listed company they control, in the latest spin on the Bitcoin treasury blueprint pioneered by Michael Saylor’s Strategy.

title: US Braces for ‘Low-Level’ Cyberattacks by Iran After Airstrikes
content: US officials are warning businesses to brace for potential Iranian cyberattacks following American airstrikes on the country’s nuclear sites, an event that experts say could draw a relatively small response from hackers.

title: Apple Crashes Tech’s Formula One Party as Money Behind ‘F1’
content: Welcome to Tech In Depth, our daily newsletter with reporting and analysis about the business of tech from Bloomberg’s journalists around the world. Today, Austin Carr reports on the tech industry’s branding effort with Formula One racing, including Apple’s backing for a new movie to be released later this week.

title: US Clean-Energy Project Cancellations Hit GOP Districts Hardest
content: Clean energy investments in the US are shrinking fast amid the rollback of tax incentives and policy uncertainties under President Donald Trump’s administration, with Republican districts hardest hit.

title: Sanhua Slips in Hong Kong Debut After $1.2 Billion Listing
content: Zhejiang Sanhua Intelligent Controls Co., the Chinese maker of fridge parts that’s working on becoming a cutting-edge robotics company, edged lower during its Hong Kong trading debut after its HK$9.3 billion ($1.2 billion) stock offering.

But there is one particular company that is clearly on the mind of CEO Jensen Huang, and that is Huawei. title: Germany Reaches Deal With States on Sharing Burden From Tax Cuts
content: Germany’s ruling coalition reached an agreement with the country’s state premiers on how to share the financial burden from planned corporate tax cuts meant to boost economic growth.

title: Powell Headed for Congressional Grilling Over Fed’s Rate Hold
content: Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell will have two chances this week to explain to lawmakers why he and most of his fellow policymakers seem resolved to continue holding interest rates steady at least until September, ignoring President Donald Trump’s persistent calls to lower borrowing costs.

title: US Finalizing $500 Million for African Critical Minerals Railway
content: The US International Development Finance Corp. is finalizing more than $500 million in financing for the Lobito corridor, a railway project that will haul critical minerals from central Africa’s copper belt to an Atlantic port in Angola.

title: French Government Under Pressure as Pension Talks Stumble
content: Negotiations over France’s contentious retirement reform ended in deadlock late Monday, raising the chances of government collapse should opposition parties unite in a no-confidence vote.

title: ECB Can Still Cut Rates in Next Six Months, Villeroy Tells FT
content: The European Central Bank could still cut interest rates in the next half year, Governing Council member Francois Villeroy de Galhau told the Financial Times.

title: India Eyes US Trade Deal by July Though Challenges Remain
content: India and the US are keen to clinch an early trade deal before a July 9 deadline when higher US tariffs are set to kick in, but challenges remain, an Indian official familiar with the matter said.

title: SNB Rate Seen Stuck at Zero This Year After Last Week’s Cut
content: The Swiss National Bank probably won’t act this year on its threat of cutting borrowing costs to below zero, according to a majority of economists.

title: Hungary Is Set to Hold Interest Rates as Price Curbs Fall Short
content: Hungary’s central bank is likely to keep its key interest rate unchanged for a ninth month, holding steady amid mounting geopolitical risks and persistently high inflation expectations.

title: Japan’s Akazawa Says Still Working on Date for Next Trade Talks
content: Japan and the US are still working on setting the timing for the next round of cabinet-level trade talks, Japan’s point person for the negotiations said, as the deadline for a deal to avert another hike in tariffs nears.

title: South Korea’s Trade Chief Seeks Tariff Relief in First US Talks
content: South Korea reiterated its call to be exempted from US tariffs including duties affecting key industries such as cars and steel, Trade Minister Yeo Han-koo said after his first meeting with US counterparts since taking up his position.

title: Australia Must Choose Defense or Social Spending, Rabobank Says
Malaysia to Boost Venture Capital With Tax Incentives
content: Malaysia is dangling new tax incentives to investors to boost its venture capital industry, according to Second Finance Minister Amir Hamzah Azizan.

title: China Expands Its Coal Exports and Shrinks Imports Due to Glut
content: China’s coal glut is resulting in an increasing number of unwanted cargoes being offered abroad.

title: Korean Consumer Confidence Jumps to 4-Year High on Stimulus Hope
content: South Korea’s consumer confidence rose to the highest in four years as easing domestic political uncertainty, fresh fiscal stimulus and hopes for pro-growth policies under the new administration buoyed sentiment.

title: Canada’s Defense Pledges Mean More Borrowing, Watchdog Says
content: Prime Minister Mark Carney’s surprise announcement that Canada would spend 2% of gross domestic product on defense this fiscal year is a recipe for even deeper deficits, the parliamentary budget officer said.

title: UK Welcomes £40 Billion Amazon Investment Plan in Warehouses
content: UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer welcomed a three-year program by Amazon.com Inc. to invest £40 billion ($54 billion) in the British economy over the next three years, including opening four new warehouses.

title: Trump Tariff Deadline Spurs Asia Export Surge, Wider Trade Gaps
content: The US trade deficit with Asia is widening as importers stock up ahead of President Donald Trump’s “reciprocal” tariffs deadline.

title: Federal Reserve to Eliminate Reputation Risk in Bank Exams
content: The Federal Reserve said Monday it will no longer consider reputation risk as part of its bank exams, following calls from some bank groups and Republican lawmakers to end a practice critics have viewed as unfair.

title: IMF Approves $1.3 Billion for Bangladesh as Reforms Advance
content: The International Monetary Fund’s executive board has approved a total of $1.3 billion in funding for Bangladesh as part of the ongoing loan program, as the South Asian country pushes ahead with currency and tax reforms.

title: Angola Gets Budget Relief From Oil Gains on Middle East Tension
content: Angola may meet its 2025 budget goals without major spending cuts if the oil price remains around $70 where it was benchmarked at, Minister of State for Economic Coordination Jose de Lima Massano said.

title: Argentina Economy Grows Less Than Expected as Imports Surge
content: Argentina’s economy grew less than expected in the first quarter of 2025 as a pickup in imports along with declines in exports and government spending tempered the South American nation’s recovery.

title: Goolsbee Says Fed Can Cut Rates If Tariff Inflation Doesn’t Come
content: Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago President Austan Goolsbee said the central bank could resume interest-rate cuts if the inflation hit from tariffs remains subdued, without weighing in on the exact timing of such a move.

title: Ireland Warns Thousands of Jobs at Risk From Pharma Tariffs
content: Ireland plans to use its budget cushion to pump money into infrastructure to protect competitiveness as global trade turmoil and tariffs threaten thousands of jobs in the multinational hub.

title: Fed’s Bowman Says ‘Time Has Come’ to Reform Key Capital Rule
content: Federal Reserve Vice Chair for Supervision Michelle Bowman warned the current approach to leverage ratio requirements has led to unintended consequences in the market while adding she could support lowering interest rates as soon as July.

title: BOE Chief Rejects Reform UK’s Plan to End Interest on Reserves
content: Bank of England Governor Andrew Bailey said Reform UK’s plans to end interest payments on central bank reserves would do little to raise revenue and potentially slow down the pace of lending.

title: Nagel Says ECB Can’t Commit on Rates Given High Uncertainty
content: The European Central Bank shouldn’t commit to a certain interest-rate path, given how US trade policy and the situation in the Middle East are clouding the outlook, according to Governing Council member Joachim Nagel.

title: US Home Resales Stay Sluggish on Affordability Constraints
content: US previously owned home sales rose slightly in May to a still-sluggish pace that continues to show a housing market constrained by poor affordability.

title: Lagarde Reiterates ECB Well Placed But Monitoring Oil Swings
content: The European Central Bank is well placed to tackle “exceptionally high” uncertainty but will closely watch gyrations in commodities markets as tensions in the Middle East flare, President Christine Lagarde said.

title: US Manufacturing Expands While Inflation Measures Accelerate
content: US manufacturing grew at a steady pace so far in June, partly reflecting stronger employment growth, while two measures of inflation accelerated to the highest levels since July 2022.

title: Global Economy, Resilient to Tariffs, Faces New Mideast Storm
content: I’m Chris Anstey, an economics editor in Boston. Today we’re looking at the latest threat to wreck the global economic expansion. Send us feedback and tips to ecodaily@bloomberg.net. And if you aren’t yet signed up to receive this newsletter, you can do so here.

title: Spain to Add Hurdles to BBVA’s Sabadell Bid, Vanguardia Says
content: Spain’s government is set to impose additional conditions on BBVA SA’s planned takeover of Banco Sabadell SA, La Vanguardia reported, in a further setback for the €14 billion ($16 billion) deal more than a year after it was first proposed.

title: Qantas Jet Takes 15-Hour Flight to Nowhere Due to Mideast Crisis
content: Passengers aboard a Paris-bound Qantas Airways Ltd. flight spent more than 15 hours in the air only to find themselves back where they started from in Australia after an Iranian missile attack shut down swathes of Middle East airspace.

title: Private Equity Firm Jadwa Said to Put Saudi Pharma Unit on Sale
content: Jadwa Investment Co. is looking to sell its stake in one of Saudi Arabia’s largest pharmaceutical groups, according to people familiar with the matter, offering buyers an opportunity to tap into a fast-growing segment of the kingdom’s economy.

title: Virgin Australia CEO Downplays Mideast Fears as Shares Debut
content: Virgin Australia Holdings Ltd. Chief Executive Officer Dave Emerson brushed away concerns the Middle East conflict will disrupt demand for travel as the airline surged on its return to the stock exchange in Sydney.

title: Bain’s Virgin Australia Rises 11% in Sydney After Relisting
content: Bain Capital’s Virgin Australia rose in Sydney trading after raising A$685 million ($444 million) in one of the country’s biggest initial public offerings of the year.

title: China On Target to Launch National Power Market by End of Year
content: China is on target to launch a unified national power trading market by the end of this year, according to its main electricity grid operator.

title: Apollo-Led Funds Invest $750 Million in Adani’s Mumbai Airport
content: Adani Group has raised around $750 million from global investors led by Apollo Global Management Inc. to refinance existing debt for India’s second largest airport.

title: Japan Bourse CEO Reappointed With Slimmer Vote as Rating Falls
content: Japan Exchange Group Inc. chief executive officer Hiromi Yamaji was re-elected with a smaller majority as his approval rating slid to the lowest ever and the bourse operator’s shares underperformed the market benchmark.

title: Nissan’s New CEO Faces Investor Grilling Over Job Cuts, Losses and Mounting Debt
content: Ivan Espinosa’s first annual meeting as Nissan Motor Co.’s chief executive officer was a baptism by fire, as shareholders questioned the feasibility of his turnaround plan and the carmaker’s failed tie-up with Honda Motor Co.

title: Chinese Port Activity Surges to Record After Trade Truce With US
content: Chinese ports just had their busiest week on record, likely due to exporters racing to get goods into the US as quickly as possible ahead of tariffs that may be imposed early next month.

title: South African Auto Firms Bracing for Tariffs Face Pay-Talks Test
content: A potential deadlock over pay increases for South Africa’s automotive sector workers risks shutting down an industry that accounts for more than a fifth of the nation’s manufacturing output, weighing on an already moribund economy.

title: Germany’s LNG Rush Benefits Neighbors as Storage Levels Lag
content: Germany’s liquefied natural gas terminals are busier than ever, but much of the fuel they import is flowing abroad — leaving domestic storage levels stubbornly low.

title: Nomura Shareholders Reject Proposal to Change Company Name
content: Nomura Holdings Inc. shareholders voted against a proposal to change the company’s name following a pair of scandals at Japan’s biggest brokerage.

title: Air India Cancels Europe, US East Coast Flights on Iran Crisis
content: Air India Ltd. suspended flights across major parts of its international network as the carrier, still reeling from a deadly plane crash earlier this month, joins major global airlines in grappling with extensive disruptions from the Middle East conflict.

title: China Expands Its Coal Exports and Shrinks Imports Due to Glut
content: China’s coal glut is resulting in an increasing number of unwanted cargoes being offered abroad.

title: Penfolds Maker Treasury Says Asia Leads Wine Consumption Growth
content: Treasury Wine Estates Ltd. said it’s seeing strong sales in Asia thanks to the reestablishment of its China market, and announced an imminent share buyback.

title: Starbucks Denies Plans of Full China Sale as Business Stalls

title: Marubeni Boosts Power Role in Singapore by Raising Senoko Stake
content: Japan’s Marubeni Corp. has raised its stake in Senoko Energy Pte to 50%, after acquiring shares in the Singaporean power generator’s holding company.

title: Chinese Copper Smelters Ramp Up Exports to Escape Squeeze on LME
content: An historic squeeze in the copper market has put pressure on some Chinese smelters, prompting them to ramp up exports in a bid to cover their positions on the London Metal Exchange.

title: Singapore Air CEO’s Pay Slipped 14% to $5.5 Million Last Year
content: Singapore Airlines Ltd. awarded Chief Executive Officer Goh Choon Phong S$7.01 million ($5.5 million) last financial year, a drop of almost 14%.

title: NTSB Casts Blame on Boeing, FAA for 2024 Midair Blowout
content: Boeing Co.’s failure to provide adequate training and oversight to its factory workers led to a door-sized panel blowing off a 737 Max aircraft shortly after takeoff last year, the US National Transportation Safety Board said.

title: Ping An Builds $23 Billion Stake in China Banks on Dividend Bet
content: Ping An Insurance Group Co., as well as other Chinese insurers, have ramped up investments in the nation’s biggest banks on a bet the dividend yields will outweigh headwinds of narrower margins and earnings pressure.

title: FedEx Guidance Disappoints With Tariffs Weighing on Demand
content: FedEx Corp. forecast a worse-than-expected profit for the current quarter in a sign that soft parcel demand and uncertainty over global trade are unlikely to abate in the near term.

title: Daiwa Plans $690 Million Real Estate Fund as Japan Market Booms

title: Hong Kong Developer Sought Loans Backed by Picasso, Warhol Art
content: A Hong Kong property dynasty that became one of the city’s most prolific collectors is discovering the limits of the burgeoning world of art-backed lending.

title: Hims ‘Won’t Cave’ to Novo Demands Over Copycat Weight-Loss Shots, CEO Says

title: Citadel Securities Seeks to Stop Launch of IEX Options Venue

title: Spirit Air Says United-JetBlue Venture Would Hurt Competition

title: Best Buy Divests Home Care Unit Bought for $400 Million in 2021

title: Starbucks Is Changing How It Charges for Extra Syrups, Matcha Powder

title: Target Explores Factory-Direct Shipping Model Used by Temu

title: Viruses Related to Deadly Human Diseases Found in Chinese Bats
content: Scientists have discovered 20 previously unknown viruses in bats from China’s Yunnan province, including two closely related to the deadly Nipah and Hendra viruses, raising fresh concerns about the risk of animal pathogens infecting people.

title: Oil Traders Piled Into Leveraged Bearish Oil ETF Before Rout

content: Families are not holding back on back-to-school spending this year, despite growing economic pressure, according to a new PwC consumer survey.

China LNG Imports Set to Fall for Eighth Month, Kpler Data Show
content: China’s imports of liquefied natural gas are poised to decline for an eighth month on a year-on-year basis, according to data from Kpler, as piped and domestically produced supplies remain robust.

title: Copper Extends Gains as Goldman Sees 2025 Price Peak in August
content: Copper extended gains for a fifth day, after Goldman Sachs Group Inc. said it expected prices to rise to a 2025 peak of around $10,050 a ton in August, as supplies outside the US tighten.

title: Taiwan’s Central Bank Wards Off FX Speculators Piling Into ETFs
content: Taiwan told foreign investors to exit bets on the local dollar, taken through exchange-traded funds, as a 12% gain in its currency threatens its economy and companies.

title: Mousavian: Full Damage To Iran Nuclear Sites Unknown
content: President Trump says the US will meet with Iran next week, while casting doubt on the need for a diplomatic agreement on Tehran's nuclear program. President Trump continues to insist that US strikes on Iranian nuclear facilities had obliterated them. Seyed Hossein Mousavian, Former Iranian Ambassador to Germany spoke to Bloomberg's Horizons Middle East and Africa anchor Joumanna Bercetche on the extent of damage to these sites. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Convenience Store Retailer Trolley Plans Rare IPO in Kuwait
content: Kuwaiti convenience store Trolley is planning an initial public offering, according to people familiar with the matter, a rare transaction in one of the Gulf’s quietest markets for new share sales.

title: Hong Kong Intervenes to Defend FX Peg as Local Currency Drops
content: Hong Kong’s de-facto central bank spent more than a billion dollars propping up the city’s currency, as it sought to defend a peg that has been strained by volatility in the greenback.

title: The Real Threat To the Labubu Economy
content:
Labubu has become a global pop-culture sensation but other Chinese companies are looking to give Pop Mart's famous dolls a run for their money.
Bloomberg Opinion columnist Shuli Ren told Insight with Haslinda Amin how the company can hold on to its monstrous market lead. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Oil Climbs as Trump Maintains Iran Pressure, Stockpiles Fall
content: Oil extended gains after US President Donald Trump said his maximum pressure campaign on Iranian oil will continue, and a government report showed another large decline in American crude stockpiles.

title: Horizons Middle East & Africa 06/26/2025
content: Horizons Middle East & Africa is your daily spotlight on one of the world's fastest-growing regions. Live from Dubai, we bring you the latest global markets and analysis, plus news-making interviews, with a special focus on MEA. All that and more, as you head to the office in the Gulf, pause for lunch in Hong Kong, or start your day in London or Johannesburg.  (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Clashes in Kenya Leave Eight Protesters Dead
content: Protests in at least a dozen towns across Kenya left at least eight people dead in clashes with police. Thousands took to the streets to commemorate the more than 60 who died in June 2024 during protests against planned tax increases and government corruption. Bloomberg’s Ondiro Oganga reports from Kigali.

title: Guotai Junan Surges 300% This Week on Crypto-Trading Approval
content: Guotai Junan International Holdings Ltd. shares are headed for their best week on record after the broker obtained regulatory approval to offer trading services of cryptocurrencies in Hong Kong.

title: Insight with Haslinda Amin 6/26/2025
content: Insight with Haslinda Amin, a daily news program featuring in-depth, high-profile interviews and analysis to give viewers the complete picture on the stories that matter. The show features prominent leaders spanning the worlds of business, finance, politics and culture. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Shifting Rate Bets Push Dollar, Bond Yields Lower: Markets Wrap
content: The dollar declined and Treasury yields edged lower on bets that US rate cuts could come sooner than expected, after a report that President Donald Trump is considering an early appointment for the next Federal Reserve chairman.

title: FTSE 100 Live: Pound Rallies to January 2022 High Against Dollar
Hesai: Lidar is the Future of Airbags
content: Hesai Technology's CEO, David Li, thinks Lidar, or light detection and ranging, could be the future of airbags despite criticism from Elon Musk. Hesai is one of the world's largest maker of lidar sensors, used in driver assistance systems. Li spoke with Bloomberg's Chief North Asia Correspondent Stephen Engle, from the sidelines of the WEF Annual Meetings in the Chinese city of Tianjin. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Platinum Jumps to Highest Since 2014 on Robust Jewelry Demand
content: Platinum rose to the highest since 2014 on solid demand from Chinese jewelry buyers who are favoring the metal over gold.

title: Bloomberg: The China Show 6/26/2025
content: “Bloomberg: The China Show” is your definitive source for news and analysis on the world's second-biggest economy. From politics and policy to tech and trends, Yvonne Man and David Ingles give global investors unique insight, delivering in-depth discussions with the newsmakers who matter. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: ADB on APAC's Geopolitical Risks
content: Asian Development Bank's Scott Morris thinks the geopolitical and economic outlook for the Asia Pacific region remains challenging due to an ongoing trade war and recent developments in the Middle East. Morris spoke to The China Show out of the AIIB annual meeting in Beijing. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Tokyo Gas in Talks to Seal Long-Term US LNG Purchase Deals
content: Tokyo Gas Co. is in discussions with multiple US liquefied natural gas suppliers to secure a long-term purchase agreement, as rising energy demand leaves Japan increasingly dependent on the fuel source.

title: Taiwan Dollar Hits Three-Year High on Fund Inflows, Repatriation
content: Taiwan’s dollar rallied to its strongest in three years amid inflows to its stock market and broad-based weakness in the greenback.

title: The Market Is Getting Back to Ignoring Iran
content: But it’s too soon to Make America Exceptional Again.

title: Greenland Miner Eyes US, EU Deals After Trump Boosted Interest
content: Greenland’s biggest miner Amaroq Minerals Ltd is in talks with several state-backed agencies as Donald Trump’s political spotlight translates into concrete investor interest, the company’s chief executive officer said.

title: Hong Kong May Need Further FX Intervention, OCBC Bank Says
content: OCBC Bank's Frances Cheung shares her views on the Hong Kong dollar (HKD) after the city's monetary authority intervened to defend the peg to the US dollar (USD). She tells Bloomberg Television that the amount of local currency the HKMA bought "was actually quite small" and that she suspects "further or additional FX intervention will be needed." (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Last Qantas Bear Finally Surrenders After Stock Dips From Record
content: The sole bearish Qantas Airways Ltd. analyst has finally yielded, giving Chief Executive Officer Vanessa Hudson unanimous support from the market as she pushes through the biggest fleet overhaul in the Australian airline’s 105-year history.

title: Indian Tech Stocks Rally Has Legs as Earnings Outlook Improves
content: Before the trading day starts we bring you a digest of the key news and events that are likely to move markets. Today we look at:

title: China Opens First Offshore Gold Vault in Hong Kong
content: The Shanghai Gold Exchange has expanded outside mainland China for the first time, with the roll out of two new contracts and a bullion vault in Hong Kong.

title: JC Flowers-Backed Jefferson Capital’s IPO Raises $150 Million
content: Jefferson Capital Inc. and some of its backers raised $150 million in an initial public offering, pricing shares at the bottom of the range.

title: Richard Li’s FWD Group Seeks $442 Million in Hong Kong IPO
content: Billionaire Richard Li’s FWD Group Holdings Ltd. is seeking to raise HK$3.5 billion ($442 million) in a Hong Kong initial public offering, seizing on a hot market to finally launch a share sale initially planned four years ago.

title: AT&T Finds Efficiencies in Fiber Push
content: AT&T has begun to decommission its legacy copper networks, with the intention of completely retiring them by the end of the decade. On Bloomberg Chief Future Officer, CFO Pascal Desroches takes Lisa Abramowicz to one of the company's connectivity hubs and explains how fiber isn't just less costly to operate and maintain -- it also takes up less space, allowing AT&T to generate capital from underutilized facilities. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: How AT&T Found Its Focus
content: Since John Stankey became AT&T CEO in 2020, the company has streamlined its focus around connectivity and concentrated on developing fiber broadband and 5G wireless networks. On Bloomberg Chief Future Office, Stankey and CFO Pascal Desroches tell Lisa Abramowicz why they're confident that AT&T is positioned to turn this technological foundation into profitable growth. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Starmer in Talks With Labour Rebels About Easing Welfare Cuts
content: Prime Minister Keir Starmer looks ready to water down another of the UK government’s key policies, offering concessions to stop Labour party colleagues derailing his reforms to Britain’s expensive welfare payments.

title: Trump Says US and Iran Will Talk Next Week, Mideast War Over for Now
content: President Donald Trump said the US would hold a meeting with Iran next week but cast doubt on the need for a diplomatic agreement on the country’s nuclear program, citing the damage that American bombing had done to key sites.

title: UK’s Labour Needs to Contain Non-Dom Exodus, Lord Mayor Says
content: The UK government should act to stem an exodus of wealthy foreigners from the country following a major tax crackdown, said Alastair King, Lord Mayor of the City of London.

title: Is the Anti-Immigrant Reform UK Ready to Take Charge?
content: According to new polling, the far-right party led by Nigel Farage now stands at 34% support, nine points ahead of Labour and well ahead of the Conservatives.

title: Japan Reiterates It Cannot Accept 25% Car Tariffs From US
content: Japan’s chief trade negotiator Ryosei Akazawa said the country can’t accept the US’s 25% tariffs on cars, adding that the Asian nation’s automakers produce far more cars in the US than they export to America.

title: US Accuses Three Mexican Financial Firms of Aiding Fentanyl Trafficking
content: The US government identified three Mexican financial firms for potentially laundering proceeds from illicit drug trafficking, effectively choking them off from the US financial system as it seeks to clamp down on cartels.

title: US Allows Ethane Cargoes to Sail to China But Not Discharge
content: The Trump administration has eased recent export limits on a critical petroleum product that’s used to make plastics — a shift that represents a modest pullback on curbs used as leverage in trade negotiations with China.

title: Malaysian Agency to Forfeit $41.8M Linked to Ex-PM Probe: NST
content: The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission plans to seek forfeiture of 177 million ringgit ($41.8 million) in assets and cash it seized in its probe into former prime minister Ismail Sabri Yaakob, the New Straits Times reported.

title: Brazil’s Congress Blocks Tax Decree in Fiscal Blow to Lula
content: Brazil’s Congress voted to block President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva’s proposed tax increases on some financial transactions, dealing a major blow to the government’s efforts to shore up its budget.

title: Abrego Garcia Remains in Jail Amid Dispute Over Release
content: Kilmar Abrego Garcia, the Maryland man who the Trump administration mistakenly deported to a prison in El Salvador, remains in legal limbo after defeating a bid by the government to keep him locked up on criminal charges.

title: Trump Says Three or Four People on List to Replace Fed’s Powell
content: President Donald Trump said he has three or four people in mind to succeed Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell when his term expires next year.

title: Pentagon Posts Document With Fiscal Year 2026 Weapons Requests
content: The Defense Department’s proposed $961 billion budget for the fiscal year beginning Oct. 1 includes funding to purchase 24 F-35 fighters, 21 new model F-15 jets and two Virginia-class submarines, according to budget documents posted on the website of the department’s comptroller Wednesday evening.

title: China’s Maritime Structures Near Japan and Korea Raise Tensions
content: China has stepped up construction of drilling rigs and other platforms off its east coast to tap into maritime resources such as natural gas and fish, raising the ire of Japan and South Korea and fanning fresh concerns about Beijing’s regional ambitions.

title: Treasury Close to Deal That Would Make ‘Revenge Tax’ Irrelevant
content: The Treasury Department is nearing a deal that would make the so-called “revenge tax” irrelevant, the agency’s second-in-command said, a development that could bring great relief to Wall Street investors worried about punitive tax measures on foreigners.

title: US Extends Debt-Limit Special-Measures Period Through July 24
content: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent told US lawmakers he’s extending the latest period for deploying special accounting measures to keep within the debt limit through July 24, 2025.

title: Top UK Business Leader Warns Rachel Reeves Not to Hike Corporate Taxes
content: Chancellor of the Exchequer Rachel Reeves should resist the temptation to raise levies on UK companies further because of the risk of strangling economic growth, one of the country’s biggest business lobbies said.

title: New Zealand Māori Party MP Takutai Kemp Dies Aged 50
content: New Zealand member of parliament Takutai Moana Natasha Kemp, of the small opposition Māori Party, has died at the age of 50.

title: Vance to Headline $250,000 Nantucket Dinner Hosted by Putnam CEO
content: Vice President JD Vance is scheduled to headline a political fundraiser in Nantucket in July, according to a person familiar with the matter, courting the Massachusetts island’s wealthy summer crowd to bolster Republicans before the midterm elections.

title: Republicans ‘Far From’ Deal on SALT Limit, New Yorker Says
content: House Republicans from high-tax states remain at loggerheads with the Senate GOP over limits on the state and local tax deduction despite a meeting with Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent to try to resolve differences, a New York lawmaker said.

title: Starmer Seeks to Expand Service Exports in UK Trade Strategy
content: The UK is seeking to increase the recognition of British professional certifications abroad, a move aimed at boosting the nation’s service-sector exports by making it easier for highly skilled employees to work for clients overseas.

title: Treasury’s Faulkender Sees Sub-April 2 Tariff Rates After Talks
content: Deputy Treasury Secretary Michael Faulkender said the expectation is that, following negotiations with US trading partners, tariffs won’t go back as high as the reciprocal levies that President Donald Trump announced on April 2.

title: California Reaches $321 Billion Budget Deal Boosting Hollywood
content: California Governor Gavin Newsom and state lawmakers struck a budget agreement that provides $750 million in tax credits for Hollywood while scaling back free health care for undocumented immigrants.

title: Trump’s Tax Cut Bill Progress May Hinge on SALT Content
content: This is Washington Edition, the newsletter about money, power and politics in the nation’s capital. Today, Capitol influence reporter Emily Birnbaum looks at the status of the Republican tax-cut and spending bill with a deadline coming up. Sign up here and follow us at @bpolitics. Email our editors here.

title: Mamdani’s Rent-Freeze Agenda Sparks Slide in NYC-Linked REITs
content: Shares of companies linked to New York City real estate fell Wednesday as Zohran Mamdani, a state Assembly member who has vowed to freeze rents, looks all but certain to become the Democratic nominee for mayor.

title: Mamdani’s Shock Win Has Wall Street Fretting Over ‘Hot Commie Summer’
content: Even Zohran Mamdani’s detractors recognize that the vibes are with the 33-year-old democratic socialist.

title: MIT Sued by Student, Instructor Claiming Campus Antisemitism
content: The Massachusetts Institute of Technology was sued by an instructor and a former student who claim the school’s administration failed to address a “hostile anti-Semitic environment” on campus following the Oct. 7, 2023, attacks in Israel by Hamas.

title: HUD Plans to Move Operations From Washington to Virginia
content: The US Department of Housing and Urban Development is relocating its headquarters to a federal building in Virginia, months after the agency’s existing space downtown in Washington was put up for sale as part of a broader effort by President Donald Trump’s administration to consolidate its real estate.

title: Trump Slams NYC Mayoral Candidate Mamdani as ‘Communist Lunatic’
content: President Donald Trump described Zohran Mamdani, the expected Democratic nominee for New York City mayor, as a “Communist Lunatic,” signaling how Republicans will seek to portray the upstart politician as representative of the party.

title: California Schools Risk DC Funding Cuts on Transgender Athlete Debate
content: Public school funding in California is at risk after the US Education Department found that the state is violating rules protecting female athletes from unfair competition and unsafe situations “by allowing males in girls’ sports and intimate spaces.”

title: What We Know About a Hong Kong TCM Stock That Spiked 82,000%
content: In this week’s Hong Kong Edition, we break down what we know about a TCM company and its dizzying stock surge, take a look at the HKMA’s dollar defense and check in with Bloomberg’s Mishal Husain. We also review a buzzy new Thai restaurant by the team behind Trattoria Felino.

title: BCC Warns Reeves Not to Hike Corporate Taxes
content: The head of the British Chambers of Commerce, Shevaun Haviland, is warning the UK government not to hike corporate taxes. The show features prominent leaders spanning the worlds of business, finance, politics and culture. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Indian REITs May Stretch Gains on Rate Cuts, Strong Leasing
content: Units of Indian real estate investment trusts are poised to extend gains on the back of falling interest rates and a buoyant commercial property market, analysts tracking the sector said.

title: Zambian Economy Expected to Grow 6% in 2025
content: Zambia's economy is expected to expand at least 6% this year, driven by improving rainfall, increased copper production, and a debt restructuring with low interest rates.  Bloomberg News Editor-In-Chief Emeritus Matthew Winkler spoke to Lizzy Burden on Horizons Middle East and Africa about how the nation's economic recovery is the unlikely surprise of 2025. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Gold Heads for Weekly Loss as Middle East Truce Saps Demand
content: Gold headed for its second consecutive weekly loss, after a ceasefire between Israel and Iran dented demand for havens.

title: McGonegal: The Fed Is Always Behind The Curve
content: President Donald Trump says he has three or four people in mind to succeed Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell when his term expires next year. The US President and The Fed have been at loggerheads over rate cuts. Capital Link CEO, Brett McGonegal told Bloomberg’s Lizzy Burden on Horizons Middle East and Africa that the Fed has remained behind the curve with their print reads and decisions. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Surge in Euro Options Trading Adds to Chances of Hitting $1.20
content: Blockbuster euro trading volumes in the $300 billion-plus foreign exchange options market are another sign investors are betting the currency’s gains may have room to run.

title: Vietnam Passes Law to Support Troubled Banks, Tackle Bad Debt
content: Vietnam’s parliament passed a revised law on credit institutions, bolstering the central bank’s authority to ensure the safety of the banking system while offering long-awaited legal clarity for commercial lenders to resolve non-performing loans.

title: Germany's Plans Are Big, But Not Big Enough, KKR's Vincent Policard Says
content: The German cabinet has approved plans to spend €500B on infrastructure over the next 12 years, but KKR's Vincent Policard says it's not enough. KKR has invested billions in Germany over the past few years, and Policard says private capital will be key. He spoke to Bloomberg's Tom Mackenzie on "Daybreak Europe" on June 25. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: JSW Agrees to Buy Akzo Nobel India Unit in $1.6 Billion Deal
content: JSW Group agreed to buy up to 75% of Akzo Nobel NV’s Indian business as the conglomerate seeks to expand its presence in areas such as paints.

title: ‘Revenge Tax’ Shift Revives US Appeal for Australia Mega Funds
content: Australia’s A$4.1 trillion ($2.7 trillion) pension industry signaled relief over US plans to scrap the so-called “revenge tax,” which would have increased levies on income from assets of foreign investors.

title: Oil Steadies at End of Turbulent Week as Focus Shifts to Tariffs
content: Oil headed for the biggest weekly decline in two years after a ceasefire between Israel and Iran, with focus shifting from the conflict in the Middle East to US trade negotiations.

title: Five Years From Wirecard, Europe’s Shorts Are Still Unloved
content: If you want to short a dodgy company in Europe, good luck keeping it secret.

title: Thai Rate Pause Is Lifeline Saved for Turbulence Ahead, BOT Says
content: The Bank of Thailand’s decision to leave borrowing costs unchanged this week gives it a “monetary lifeline” to deal with challenges ranging from US tariffs and geopolitical tensions to domestic politics, according to Deputy Governor Piti Disyatat.

title: Taiwanese Investors Flee US Bond ETFs as Currency Risks Mount
content: Taiwanese investors are unloading their holdings in US-focused exchange-traded bond funds at the quickest pace since the onset of the Covid pandemic, highlighting a “Sell America” momentum that may further boost the island’s currency.

title: Mexico Steps In to Run Banks Tarred by US Drug Accusations
content: Mexico’s bank regulator stepped in to temporarily run three financial firms on Thursday, an extraordinary measure aimed at protecting customers following money-laundering accusations by US authorities the day before.

title: Japan Braces for Further Pain From US Tariffs, Pledges Support
content: Japan will take additional action to ease the impact of US tariffs on the auto sector as needed and “without hesitation,” its economy minister says.

title: The Asia Trade 06/27/2025
content: "Bloomberg: The Asia Trade" brings you everything you need to know to get ahead as the trading day begins in Asia. Bloomberg TV is live from Tokyo and Sydney with Shery Ahn and Haidi Stroud-Watts, getting insight and analysis from newsmakers and industry leaders on the biggest stories shaping global markets. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Tina Brown: ‘I’m Concerned About American Women’

title: Lutnick Says US-China Trade Truce Signed, 10 Deals Imminent
content: The US and China finalized a trade understanding reached last month in Geneva, US Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick said, adding that the White House has imminent plans to reach agreements with a set of 10 major trading partners.

title: Ramaphosa Accused of ‘Double Standard’ by Key Coalition Partner
content: South African President Cyril Ramaphosa fired a deputy minister from the second-largest party in the ruling coalition on Thursday, a move that renews strain on the stability of his administration.

title: Iran Dismisses Trump’s Claim of Nuclear Talks Resuming Next Week
content: Iran denied that nuclear talks with the US are scheduled to resume, diminishing prospects for diplomacy after President Donald Trump suggested a deal could come as early as next week.

title: Trump Teases ‘Big’ India Trade Deal as Negotiators Harden Stance
content: US President Donald Trump said a “very big” trade deal could be signed soon that would open up the Indian market to American business, as negotiators meet in Washington to break a recent deadlock over key issues.

title: Lee Starts Term With 64% Rating on South Korea Recovery Optimism
content: South Korea’s new President Lee Jae Myung started his presidency with a higher approval rating than recent predecessors, as hopes for an economic recovery rise after months of political turbulence.

title: US Allies Wary of Buying American as They Plan Defense Buildup
content: For European countries that just approved the biggest increase in military spending in decades, “Buy American” is looking a lot less appealing than it once was. They may have no choice.

title: Ireland’s Firms Brace for Economic Hit With Quiet Confidence
content: Hundreds of companies, 200,000 jobs, billions of euro in corporation tax revenue. Add it all up and Ireland’s reliance on US investment for its economic success is starkly clear.

title: Thai Finance Chief to Visit US for Trade Talks, Denying 18% Levy
content: Thai Finance Minister Pichai Chunhavajira will visit the US next week for tariff negotiations in an attempt to clinch a trade deal ahead of Washington’s deadline on July 9.

title: Australian Treasurer Sues Foreign Investor in Rare Earths Miner
content: Australian Treasurer Jim Chalmers has started the first legal case in the Federal Court for an alleged breach of the nation’s foreign investment laws, saying a shareholder in a rare earths company failed to heed his order to sell its stake.

title: House Plans Single Vote to Move Genius and Clarity Crypto Bills
content: House Republicans aim to get the Senate’s landmark stablecoin legislation — known as the Genius Act — to President Donald Trump’s desk for signature as soon as the week of July 7, according to people with direct knowledge of the strategy.

title: South Korea Weighing US Request to Boost Defense Spending
content: South Korea is in talks with the US about raising its defense spending, a key demand of President Donald Trump as he calls on allies to ramp up their outlays on security and lessen the burden on the US.

title: Miami Defies DeSantis by Delaying Mayoral Election a Year
content: Miami’s city commission voted to postpone municipal elections set for November, giving the mayor and two commissioners another year in office in defiance of Governor Ron DeSantis.

title: Cuomo Won’t Quit NYC Mayor’s Race Before Friday Ballot Deadline
content: Andrew Cuomo has no plans to drop out of the New York City mayor’s race by a Friday deadline, according to a person familiar with the matter, meaning that his name will appear on the ballot in November as an independent.

title: Sanchez Suffers Jibes From EU Leaders Who Won’t Forget NATO Yet
content: Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez is hunkering down and trying to ignore the shade coming his way for refusing to sign up to new NATO spending targets demanded by Donald Trump.

title: Macron Says US Strikes on Iran’s Nuclear Program Were Effective
content: French President Emmanuel Macron said the US attacks on Iran’s nuclear facilities had been effective.

title: As Hurricane Season Picks Up, Key Forecasting Tool Access Set to End
content: The US Navy will no longer distribute certain satellite readings, a move that will leave forecasters without important insights into storms’ strength and structure.

title: Trump’s Iran Oil Comments Strain His ‘Maximum Pressure’ Policy
content: President Donald Trump indicated that he might be preparing to ease his “maximum pressure” campaign against Iran, potentially undercutting a central policy dating to his first term and provoking consternation among foreign policy hawks who argue that now is the time to escalate — not lessen — pressure on Tehran.

title: Starmer Eases Welfare Cuts in Blow to Budget and His Authority
content: Keir Starmer agreed to pare back a divisive £5 billion ($6.9 billion) cut to welfare to quiet a rebellion by his own party, a decision that will likely leave both Britain’s fiscal plans and the prime minister’s own leadership in need of repair.

title: How the Senate Parliamentarian Tripped Up Trump’s Tax Bill
content: For Republicans racing to pass President Donald Trump’s mega-bill, the devil is in the procedural details.

title: Carney’s Bill to Fast-Track Major Projects Set to Become Law
content: Prime Minister Mark Carney’s bill to speed up the construction of major projects such as pipelines, mines and electricity systems has passed Canada’s Senate and will soon become law.

title: Kosovo Court Orders Parliament to End Deadlock Within 30 Days
content: Kosovo’s top court ordered lawmakers to complete the inaugural session of parliament within 30 days, pressing politicians to resolve a stalemate which has prevented the formation of a new government since February’s election.

title: Treasury Deal Kills ‘Revenge Tax’ That Spooked Wall Street

title: US & China Race for AI Supremacy
content: The Chinese tech sector has been on a roll since the arrival in January of DeepSeek, the AI startup that stunned the world with a language model that claimed to match or outperform Western rivals, at a fraction of the cost. 'Bloomberg Tech: Asia' anchor Annabelle Droulers reports on how the rapid strides in AI are poised to escalate the tech "cold war" between the US and China. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Bloomberg Tech: Asia 06/27/2025
content:
Bloomberg Tech: Asia brings you the most exciting stories from the region’s fast-moving tech scene. Hosted monthly by Shery Ahn and Annabelle Droulers, the show features in-depth conversations and on-the-ground reporting on the innovations, key players, and emerging voices shaping the future of Asia tech.

The first episode explores the impact of China's AI advancements on competition with the US. We hear from key players in Asia's AI revolution including Manycore, one of China's so-called "Six Dragons" and Tokyo Electron, one of the world's top chip-tool makers. China Growth Capital's Wayne Shiong and Power Dynamics' Jen Zhu Scott also weigh in on the outlook for the AI race and investments in the sector.

 (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Micron HBM Sales Surge, Palantir’s Stock Keeps Climbing | Bloomberg Tech 6/26/2025
content: Bloomberg’s Caroline Hyde and Ed Ludlow discuss Micron’s earnings as its sales surge in its high-bandwidth memory business. Plus, Managing Director of Baird Ted Mortonson discusses opportunities in the defense tech space. Chinese tech giant Xiaomi also says it received more than 200,000 pre-orders for its first electric SUV. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: How Telegram Became a Magnet for Extremists and Crime: QuickTake
content: Messaging service Telegram is one of the most downloaded apps worldwide. Its private chat setting has made it a free space for open discussion in countries with authoritarian regimes. But a relatively light-touch approach to content moderation on Telegram is frustrating governments trying to stop criminal activities and the spread of misinformation that can destabilize societies.

title: Apple’s App Store Gets Makeover in Move to Avoid EU Fines
content: Apple Inc. has offered to overhaul its App Store to appease European Union antitrust watchdogs who issued an ultimatum after doling out a €500 million ($580 million) fine.

title: CareerBuilder Says AI, Hiring Slowdown Crippled Monster Merger
content: The merger of job recruitment sites CareerBuilder and Monster failed, in part, because of a slowdown in corporate hiring and competition from hiring tools driven by artificial intelligence, the company said in a Thursday bankruptcy court filing.

title: Tech Stock Rally Is Just Beginning, Wedbush's Ives Says
content: Dan Ives, Wedbush Securities managing director and global head of tech research, expects tech stocks to perform strongly in the second half of the year. Speaking on "Bloomberg The Close," Ives says AI is creating a "Game of Thrones arms race." He also discusses the outlook for Uber and IBM. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Impossible Foods Wants to Put Plant-Based Burgers on European Menus This Year

content: Revolut Ltd., Europe’s largest digital bank, is acquiring Argentina’s Banco Cetelem, a small local lender owned by BNP Paribas, amid its push into Latin America.

content: The White House said Donald Trump’s decision on a successor for Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell is not near, after the Wall Street Journal reported the president could make a pick as soon as the summer.

title: Trump’s Threat of More Tariffs Makes US Trade Partners Wary of Signing Deals

title: Mortgage Rates in the US Fall for a Fourth Week, Hitting 6.77%
content: Mortgage rates in the US fell for a fourth straight week.

title: Nigeria’s Tinubu Signs New Tax Laws in Latest Reform Push
content: Nigerian President Bola Tinubu has signed four new tax laws, marking the latest chapter in his push to reform the economy of Africa’s most populous nation.

title: Zambia to Borrow Extra $624 Million From Domestic Market in 2025
content: Zambia will borrow an additional 14.8 billion kwacha ($624 million) from the domestic market to cover a bigger-than-expected shortfall in this year’s budget, Finance Minister Situmbeko Musokotwane said.

title: Bailey Says Labour’s Payroll Tax Complicates Inflation Fight
content: The Labour government’s payroll tax is costing the UK jobs, depressing workers’ earnings and pushing up food prices, Bank of England Governor Andrew Bailey said as he warned that the risks to inflation remain “two-sided.”

title: Global Goods Trade Gains as Tariff Fears Speed Imports, WTO Says
content: Global merchandise trade accelerated in the World Trade Organization’s latest assessment, with a surge in imports tied to tariff stockpiling outweighing a slowdown in export orders.

title: US Pending Home-Sales Pick Up in May, With Gains Across Regions
content: Pending sales of previously owned homes in the US picked up in May after a sharp decline a month earlier, although overall activity remained subdued headed into summer.

title: US Merchandise-Trade Deficit Unexpectedly Widens on Exports Drop
content: The US merchandise-trade deficit unexpectedly widened in May on the biggest drop in exports since the onset of the pandemic, while imports were little changed.

title: US GDP Revised Lower as Consumers Slash Services Spending
content: US consumer spending grew in the first quarter at the weakest pace since the onset of the pandemic on a sharp deceleration in outlays for a variety of services.

title: OpenAI CEO, Bank Officials to Speak at Fed Bank-Capital Meeting

title: Fed’s Daly Says Muted Tariff Impact May Open Door to Cut in Fall

title: Tina Brown: ‘I’m Concerned About American Women’

content: Hong Kong’s having a banner year as it marches toward becoming the second-largest market globally for share sales for the first time since 2012.

content: Wall Street traders dodged a flurry of tariff headlines to drive stocks to all-time highs, capping a week that saw a cooling in Middle East risks and signs the US economy is holding up amid subdued inflation. A rally in Treasuries stalled. The dollar advanced.

And, an interview with the Director of the Congressional Budget Office on the agency's role in predicting the fiscal impact of the "Big Beautiful Bill." Plus, will President Trump’s "Gold Card" attract foreign investment to the US?
