title: Trump Says He’ll Pick a Fed Chair Who Wants to Cut Rates
content: President Donald Trump said he would choose a successor for Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell who wants to cut interest rates, a condition that would strike at the heart of the central bank’s independence.

title: Trump on Canada Trade Talks: ‘We Have All the Cards’
content: President Donald Trump explains why he was ending all trade discussions with Canada during remarks with reporters at the Oval Office.

title: Billionaire Michael Dell Reaps $1.2 Billion From Stock Sale
content: Dell Technologies Inc. Chief Executive Officer Michael Dell sold $1.2 billion worth of shares in his namesake computer company, reducing his stake by about 3%, according to a Friday filing.

title: Supreme Court Curbs Judges in Birthright Case as Trump Touts Win
content:
A divided SCOTUS left unresolved a fight over President Trump’s restrictions on automatic birthright citizenship.

The 6-3 ruling said Trump’s restrictions on birthright citizenship at a minimum won’t take effect for 30 days. Erik Larson explains. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: GE Vernova Is Exploring a Sale of Its Proficy Software Business
content: GE Vernova Inc. is exploring a potential sale of its industrial software business known as Proficy, according to people familiar with the matter.

title: Large US Banks Clear the Fed’s Annual Stress Test
content: A group of large US banks comfortably cleared the Federal Reserve’s annual stress test. The 22 banks subjected to this year’s test all remained above minimum capital levels in a hypothetical recession. Sally Bakewell has more on “Bloomberg The Close.”

title: Saks Gets $600 Million Lifeline as Creditors Face Steep Losses
content: Saks Global Enterprises has reached a $600 million debt deal with a number of its existing lenders that would force some creditors to accept losses and push them back in the repayment priority line.

title: Wall Street’s Booming June Is Big Bet Against Economy Doomsayers
content: Wall Street is throwing a summer party with markets just closing out their best cross-asset advance in more than a year on receding fears of a global trade war, igniting a buying frenzy in everything from tech funds to junk bonds.

title: Euro Poised for Best Run Since 2017 as Dollar’s Slump Picks Up
content: The euro is set for its longest stretch of monthly gains in eight years, boosted by rising confidence in Europe’s economic prospects and a hunt for alternatives to the slumping dollar.

title: Canadian Stocks Fall as Trump Ends Trade Talks With Nation
content: Canada’s equities benchmark quickly dropped on Friday after US President Donald Trump said in a social media post that he was ending all trade discussions with the country, claiming that it is implementing a digital services tax.

title: S&P 500 Clinches Record as Traders Shake Off Canada Levy Threat
content: The S&P 500 joined the Nasdaq 100 in the race to all-time highs Friday, erasing a brief dip after President Donald Trump threatened Canada with fresh tariff rates.

title: Boeing Wins Buy Rating as Redburn Sees ‘Healthier’ Company
content: Shares of Boeing Co. are set to make gains as the company speeds up production of commercial aircraft and takes steps to move on from a series of crises in recent years, according to Rothschild & Co. Redburn.

title: US Treasuries Post Third Week of Gains on Fed Rate-Cut Bets
content: US Treasuries closed out a third-straight positive week in a rally fueled by bets the Federal Reserve is ramping up to cut rates at least twice this year.

title: Lula to Go to Top Court to Challenge Overturn of Tax Decree
content: President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva’s administration will appeal to Brazil’s Supreme Court to try to preserve a tax decree that Congress overturned this week, according to two government officials familiar with the matter.

title: Platinum-Backed McGraw Hill Files for IPO Showing Narrowing Loss
content: Platinum Equity-backed McGraw Hill Inc. filed for an initial public offering, a sign that private equity firms are resurfacing to take more of their portfolio companies public.

title: Oil Steadies at End of Turbulent Week as Focus Shifts to Tariffs
content: Oil held steady as traders weighed the uncertain status of nuclear talks between the US and Iran against reports that OPEC+ may extend its run of super-sized production increases.

title: Bruckheimer Pushes Egos Aside to Get 'F1' in Theaters
content: "F1: The Movie" is now in theaters with a star studded cast including Brad Pitt, Damson Idris and Kerry Condon. Produced by seven-time Academy Award winner Jerry Bruckheimer, it is looking to give the summer box office season a speedy start. Bruckheimer sat down with Bloomberg Hot Pursuit Co-Hosts Matt Miller and Hannah Elliott ahead of its release. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: The Future of Venture Capital Investing: Uncharted Summit
content: Michael Loeb, founder and CEO of Loeb Enterprises and host of the Uncharted summit, talks about where he sees the future of venture capital investing and gives his thoughts on how artificial intelligence is shaking up business. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Boaz Weinstein on Card Counting, Private Credit and Night Sweats
content: Boaz Weinstein, founder and chief investment officer of Saba Capital, spoke with Sonali Basak at a blackjack table in Atlantic City. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Trump Ends Trade Talks With Canada
content: President Donald Trump said he was ending all trade discussions with Canada after claiming the country moved to implement a digital services tax, and threatened to impose a fresh tariff rate within the next week. Tyler Kendall reports from the White House. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Germany’s Window of Opportunity Is Wide Open But Not for Long
content: Chancellor Friedrich Merz needs to move fast before headwinds derail his turnaround plans.

title: Labour’s ‘Starmtroopers’ Mount Rebellion Against Their Leader
content: Keir Starmer’s landslide UK general election win last July delivered to the House of Commons what was supposed to be a hand-picked army of loyalists molded in his image, a cadre that earned the moniker “Starmtroopers.” As the prime minister’s first anniversary in power approaches next week, the troops have mutinied, and some now have him and his chancellor in their sights.

title: Protesters Rally in Thai Capital to Demand Premier’s Resignation
content: Thai protesters began to rally in Bangkok on Saturday to demand the resignation of Prime Minister Paetongtarn Shinawatra, as the fallout continued from her controversial phone call with former Cambodian leader Hun Sen.

title: Senate Unveils New Trump Tax Draft With Plans to Vote Soon
content: Senate Republicans unveiled a new version of their $4.2 trillion tax and spending package, moving closer to a vote as they near a July 4 deadline set by President Donald Trump.

content: Canadian Industry Minister Melanie Joly says that the government has ordered Hikvision Canada to cease all operations in the country and close its business, in a statement on X.

content: President Donald Trump said he considered easing sanctions on Iran after a ceasefire but would instead keep economic penalties on the country in place, lashing out at Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei for claiming victory in the war with Israel.

title: Fourth Trump Executive Order Against Law Firm Nullified by Judge
content: A DC federal judge has struck down President Donald Trump’s executive order targeting Houston-founded law firm Susman Godfrey, marking the fourth takedown of an executive order targeting a law firm.

content: President Donald Trump said he thought a ceasefire in Gaza could be “close,” perhaps in the next week.

content: President Donald Trump amped up pressure on Congress to speed passage of his tax-cut bill as Republicans reached a tentative deal on the state and local tax deduction, one of the key sticking points in the negotiations.

title: Congo, Rwanda Sign US-Backed Peace Deal to End Years of War
content: The Democratic Republic of Congo and Rwanda agreed to a US-backed peace deal meant to end years of deadly conflict and promote development in Congo’s volatile eastern region.

title: Mamdani Wants to Meet With Major Business Heads, Wylde Says
content: New York City mayoral candidate Zohran Mamdani will meet with members of New York City’s business community in July, according to one of the city’s most influential power brokers.

title: What Does Supreme Court Ruling on Birthright Citizenship Mean?
content: President Donald Trump is fighting to end automatic citizenship for children born to parents who are in the country unlawfully or on temporary visas, part of his broader crackdown on undocumented immigrants and a change that could overturn more than a century of legal precedent.

title: Trump Ends Canada Trade Talks in Retaliation Over Digital Tax
content: President Donald Trump said he was ending all trade discussions with Canada in retaliation for the country’s digital services tax and threatened to impose a fresh tariff rate within the next week.

content: University of Virginia President James Ryan said he quit instead of fighting the US government amid a Trump administration probe of the school’s diversity, equity and inclusion efforts.

content: The US Supreme Court’s ruling curbing the power of judges to block government actions on a nationwide basis has raised questions about whether dozens of orders that have halted President Donald Trump’s policies will stand.

title: Democrats Urge Rubio to Not Fire Diplomats, End Hiring Freeze
content: Scores of congressional Democrats are urging Secretary of State Marco Rubio to abandon plans to shrink the State Department workforce, end a hiring freeze and resume offering the Foreign Service Officer Test three times a year.

content: The government is appealing a court order letting Harvard University continue enrolling foreign students despite President Donald Trump’s proclamation barring their entry to the US.

title: Alberta Posts Larger-Than-Projected Surplus, Braces for Deficit
content: Alberta posted a larger-than-projected surplus in its most recent fiscal year, providing the oil-rich province with some cushion against an expected trade war-driven shortfall in the current period.

title: Trump Eyes Cuts to Top Spy Agency as He Downplays Iran Intel
content: President Donald Trump is pressing ahead with plans to slash staff at the top US spy agency, determined to act at a time when he’s openly challenged its director and rejected intelligence findings that contradict his public statements.

title: Colombia Holds Key Rate at 9.25% After Two Credit Downgrades
content: Colombia’s central bank resisted government pressure to slash interest rates a day after the nation’s deteriorating fiscal outlook triggered two ratings downgrades.

title: California Democrats Push Reform to Stop Refinery Shutdowns
content: A group of California Democrats is looking to ease the state’s gasoline standards and streamline permitting for refineries in a bid to prevent more fuelmakers from shutting down and raising costs for the state’s drivers.

title: Cuba’s Volleyball Team Barred From US Event in Latest Sport Spat
content: Cuba’s volleyball team was denied visas for a tournament in Puerto Rico, the latest example of a US travel crackdown that the communist government blasted as discriminatory and said could hurt its ability to participate in the Olympics.

title: Trump Stresses July Tariff Threat, Bessent Teases Extension
content: President Donald Trump hardened his threat to raise tariffs on certain countries by his July 9 deadline, while Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent signaled there may be some extensions to wrap up major pacts by the Labor Day holiday.

title: South Africa Presses US on G-20 Absence as Leaders Summit Looms
content: South Africa will ask the US government to confirm its future participation in Group of 20 engagements, after American officials failed to attend a preparatory meeting this week.

title: PwC Plans Cuts, Lower Pay Rises on Tougher Market Conditions: FT
content: PricewaterhouseCoopers LLP is planning layoffs in the UK and lower salary increases amid a broader market slowdown, the Financial Times reports.

title: Fortress $2 Billion Property Bond Likely to Miss Payment Date
content: A corporate entity tied to Fortress Investment Group warned investors that it will likely miss a key deadline to refinance about $2 billion of bonds backed by warehouses leased to Amazon.com, according to people familiar with the matter.

title: Canada’s Digital Services Tax Stays in Place Despite G-7 Deal
content: Canada is proceeding with its digital services tax on technology companies such as Meta Platforms Inc. despite a Group of Seven agreement that resulted in removing the Section 899 “revenge tax” proposal from US President Donald Trump’s tax bill.

title: Porn-Site Age Verification Law Upheld by US Supreme Court
content: The US Supreme Court upheld a Texas law that requires porn sites to verify user age, rejecting arguments that the measure violates the speech rights of adults by requiring them to submit identification online.

title: Apple, Google Told DeepSeek App Is Illegal in Germany
content: Apple Inc. and Google’s Android have been warned by a top German privacy regulator that the Chinese AI service DeepSeek, available on their app stores, constitutes illegal content because it exposes users’ data to Chinese authorities.

title: Supreme Court Upholds $8.6 Billion FCC Telecom Subsidy Fund
content: The US Supreme Court upheld the $8.6 billion Universal Service Fund, the annual slate of subsidies that helps cover the cost of telecom services for low-income people, rural residents, schools and libraries.

title: Argentine Fintech tapi Buys Mastercard Unit in Mexico Expansion
content: Argentine payments services startup tapi has acquired the bill payment and cash-handling operations of Mastercard’s Arcus in Mexico, part of a bid to double-down on Latin America’s second-largest economy.

title: Macquarie-Owned Fiber Provider Taps Debt Advisors Amid Cash Burn
content: UK broadband provider KCOM Group Limited and its lenders are gearing up for debt talks as the business owned by Macquarie burns through cash.

title: Alibaba Unveils Latest AI Service for Images in Push for Users
content: Alibaba Group Holding Ltd. unveiled a new iteration of its artificial-intelligence technology that will make it easier for users to generate and modify images from texts and visuals, as the Chinese e-commerce giant continues its aggressive push into AI.

title: Worldline’s Woes Deepen as Belgium Opens Probe Into Payment Firm
content: Worldline SA has long claimed to have cleaned up its payments business. Now, regulators and investors are testing that narrative after fresh allegations it overlooked fraud among high-risk clients.

content: PricewaterhouseCoopers LLP, one of the world’s largest professional advisory firms, has cut prices for some services as clients raised the fact that the consultancy is using artificial intelligence to complete its work quicker.

title: China’s $50 Billion Chip Fund Switches Tack to Fight US Curbs

title: Heat Wave Threatens European Crops and Power Systems
content: A heat wave will bake western Europe in conditions as much as 10C above the norm in the coming days, threatening harvests, stressing power systems and triggering health alerts.

title: Babbel Names New CEO for AI Age, Says IPO Is Off the Table
content: Babbel’s new chief executive officer said he’s focused on expanding the company’s language-learning product to include emerging artificial intelligence tools, and he doesn’t intend to revive its initial public offering.

title: Congo, Rwanda Sign US-Backed Peace Deal to End Years of War
content: The Democratic Republic of Congo and Rwanda agreed to a US-backed peace deal meant to end years of deadly conflict and promote development in Congo’s volatile eastern region.

title: Big Banks Pass Fed’s Stress Test, Setting Stage for Payouts
content: A group of large US banks comfortably cleared the Federal Reserve’s annual stress test, setting the stage for lenders to boost buybacks and dividends for shareholders.

title: Bessent Plays Down Speculation of Any Early Trump Fed Chair Pick
content: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent played down speculation that President Donald Trump may consider an early move to nominate a successor to Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell, pointing to one potential timeline that could see a name emerge in October or November.

title: Trump Stresses July Tariff Threat, Bessent Teases Extension
content: President Donald Trump hardened his threat to raise tariffs on certain countries by his July 9 deadline, while Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent signaled there may be some extensions to wrap up major pacts by the Labor Day holiday.

title: Romanian Leader Pledges More Budget Measures to Curb Deficit
content: Romania’s premier outlined fresh measures to cut the ballooning budget deficit as the new government seeks to safeguard the country’s investment-grade rating and ease investor concern.

title: US Regulators Says Comments on Key Bank Capital Rule Due Aug. 26
content: The US Federal Reserve and other bank regulators set an Aug. 26 deadline for public comments on a proposal to ease a key bank capital rule, saying they expect the amount of overall capital that big lenders would maintain as a result of their plan would “generally stay the same.”

title: Economists Raise Growth Outlook for Canada as Tariff Threats Ease
content: Analysts boosted their forecasts for economic growth in Canada this year as fears of a drawn-out trade dispute with the US fade.

title: Merz Tells EU Leaders to Beware Growing Dangers of a Debt Crisis
content: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz warned European Union leaders that the mounting debts of governments and companies are fueling the risk of a new financial crisis.

title: US Consumer Spending Drops in May, Price Pressures Remain Muted
content: US consumer spending declined in May by the most since the start of the year, indicating elevated uncertainty around the Trump administration’s economic policies is increasingly weighing on the outlook for growth.

title: US Consumer Sentiment Climbs as Inflation Expectations Improve
content: US consumer sentiment rose sharply in June to a four-month high and inflation expectations improved notably as concerns eased about the economic outlook and personal finances.

title: East African Countries Face Broad Crackdown on Political Dissent
content: When thousands of young Kenyans converged across the nation this week to mark a year since scores of them were killed in protests, police were ready and opened fire, leaving at least 16 dead.

title: Iceland’s Inflation Accelerates Again, Fueled by Airfares
content: Iceland’s inflation unexpectedly picked up for the second month in three, damping expectations for further easing by the Atlantic nation’s central bank.

title: Canada Economy Set for Contraction in Second Quarter
content: The Canadian economy is on track for a modest decline this quarter, yet isn’t deteriorating as fast as some economists feared.

title: UK Budget Reversals Threaten Reeves as Well as Her Fiscal Rules
content: Labour’s costly climbdowns on big policy plans don’t just leave Chancellor of the Exchequer Rachel Reeves with the dilemma of how to find the money to meet her budget rules. They’re also starting to raise questions about her own job security.

title: Turkey Set to Skip Minimum-Wage Hike in Boost for Investors
content: Turkey’s government plans to skip a mid-year increase in the minimum wage, according to people with knowledge of the matter, resisting political pressure to alleviate rising living costs.

title: India Posts Current Account Surplus as Trade Gap Narrows
content: India’s current account returned a better than expected surplus in the January-March quarter as trade deficit narrowed following the revision of gold import data.

title: Spanish Economy Minister Cuerpo Runs for Eurogroup President
content: Spanish Economy Minister Carlos Cuerpo is running to head the Eurogroup, saying global developments require new leadership of the gatherings of euro-zone finance ministers.

title: Warning Signs of Weak Job Creation in the US
content: I’m  Mark Niquette, a US economy reporter in Columbus. Today we’re looking at the US labor market. Send us feedback and tips to ecodaily@bloomberg.net. And if you aren’t yet signed up to receive this newsletter, you can do so  here.

title: Fed’s Kashkari Sees Two Rate Cuts This Year Amid Tariff Unknowns
content: Federal Reserve Bank of Minneapolis President Neel Kashkari said he sees two interest-rate cuts as likely this year — with the first potentially in September — but warned that tariffs could have a delayed impact on inflation and policymakers should remain flexible.

title: China’s Central Bank Says Economy Is on Positive Track But Challenges Persist
content: China’s economy is showing positive signs and confidence is building, but challenges such as insufficient domestic demand and deflationary pressure persist, according to the country’s central bank.

title: Thai Finance Minister Heads to US for Trade Talks Next Week
content: Thai Finance Minister Pichai Chunhavajira will visit the US next week for tariff negotiations in an attempt to clinch a trade deal ahead of Washington’s deadline on July 9.

title: Chile Central Bank Policymaker Sees Good Omens After Long Inflation Fight
content: Chile’s central bank sees a set of factors coming together that will help bring inflation back down to target early in 2026, board member Luis Felipe Cespedes said in an interview.

title: Lots More on What’s Going On in Iran’s Markets (Podcast)
content: Iran is a huge country with a sizable stock market. And yet, years of sanctions and other restrictions mean it’s tough to even look up its stock prices (much less invest there.) In this episode, we catch up with Maciej Wojtal, CEO and CIO of AmtelonCapital, an Amsterdam-based fund that specializes in Iranian stocks. title: Starmer’s Latest U-Turn Risks £3 Billion Hit and More Tax Rises
content: Keir Starmer backed down to a rebellion within his own Labour party over a planned £5 billion ($6.9 billion) cut to disability entitlements, in a costly U-Turn that dents his authority and leaves his chancellor struggling to avoid tax hikes.

title: Trump Officials Met With Walmart on Direct-to-Patient Drug Sales
content: US health officials met with with Walmart Inc., Amazon.com Inc. and other retailers this week as part of an effort to help Americans get their medicines more directly from companies that make them, according to people familiar with the talks.

title: GE Vernova Is Exploring a Sale of Its Proficy Software Business
content: GE Vernova Inc. is exploring a potential sale of its industrial software business known as Proficy, according to people familiar with the matter.

title: Saks Gets $600 Million Lifeline as Creditors Face Steep Losses
content: Saks Global Enterprises has reached a $600 million debt deal with a number of its existing lenders that would force some creditors to accept losses and push them back in the repayment priority line.

title: Boeing Wins Buy Rating as Redburn Sees ‘Healthier’ Company
content: Shares of Boeing Co. are set to make gains as the company speeds up production of commercial aircraft and takes steps to move on from a series of crises in recent years, according to Rothschild & Co. Redburn.

title: Elon Musk Says First Tesla Drove Itself From Factory to Customer
content: Tesla Inc. Chief Executive Officer Elon Musk said a Tesla Model Y SUV drove itself from the company’s factory near Austin to a customer’s home in the company’s latest move to showcase its push into autonomous driving.

title: American Air Working to Fix Issue Causing Broad Flight Delays
content: American Airlines Group Inc. said it was working with its partners to resolve a “technology” issue that was causing flight delays on Friday.

title: Ford Forced to Idle Multiple US Plants on China Magnet Shortage
content: Ford Motor Co. temporarily idled factories in the US over the last three weeks due to a shortage of magnets containing rare earth minerals, key components embroiled in US trade tensions with China.

title: Caitlin Clark Ruled Out for Dallas WNBA Game With $3,000 Tickets
content: Caitlin Clark, the basketball star with the Indiana Fever, won’t play in Friday night’s game against the Dallas Wings, spoiling a matchup against the league’s top draft pick that spurred ballooning ticket prices.

title: California Democrats Push Reform to Stop Refinery Shutdowns
content: A group of California Democrats is looking to ease the state’s gasoline standards and streamline permitting for refineries in a bid to prevent more fuelmakers from shutting down and raising costs for the state’s drivers.

title: Keralty Blasts Petro After Top Colombia Court Sides With Insurer
content: Health group Keralty SAS said it will press ahead with legal action against the Colombian government after a top court overturned the takeover of its insurer in the South American nation.

title: Qatar Withdraws Interest for Rosneft’s German Operations
content: Qatar withdrew its interest in the seized German operations of Russia’s state-controlled oil company Rosneft PJSC, according to people familiar with the matter.

title: Adler Weighs Sale of Prized €3.5 Billion Berlin Rental Portfolio
content: Adler Group SA is weighing the sale of its prized portfolio of Berlin apartments, a deal that would mark a landmark step in the slow unraveling of the scandal-hit German landlord.

title: Miami Brickell City Centre Shopping Mall Sells for $512 Million
content: Simon Property Group Inc. bought the retail and parking segments of Miami’s Brickell City Centre for roughly $512 million.

title: JPMorgan Shares Hit a Record This Week, But Baird Analysts Say Time to Sell
content: JPMorgan Chase & Co. shares have climbed nearly 40% from an April low and set record highs this week on a grab bag of positive developments, but to Baird analysts that’s too far, too fast.

title: Nike Surges After Predicting Its Sales Slump Has Hit Bottom
content: Nike Inc. said its yearlong sales decline is starting to ease, suggesting that Chief Executive Officer Elliott Hill’s strategic moves are paying off.

title: Gabon Signs $3.8 Billion Funding Pact With Afreximbank
content: Gabon signed a $3.8 billion memorandum of understanding with the African Export-Import Bank to fund mineral and infrastructure projects in the central African nation.

title: Federer Becomes a Tennis Billionaire: Business of Sports
content: The tennis great joins Michael Jordan and LeBron James as one of the few athletes to reach billionaire status.

title: Executives Get Combined 141 Years in Prison for Italy PFAS Spill
content: Eleven former executives of companies linked to Miteni SpA were sentenced to a combined 141 years in prison by an Italian court for one of the largest groundwater contaminations of forever chemicals in Europe.

title: Dangote Plans to List Africa’s Biggest Oil Refinery by Next Year
content: Aliko Dangote, Africa’s richest person, plans a stock listing for his Nigerian crude oil refinery by the end of next year to widen the company’s investor base.

title: Santander, Barclays Said to Be Final Bidders for Sabadell’s TSB
content: Banco Santander SA and Barclays Plc are the main contenders left in the race to acquire Banco Sabadell SA’s UK unit TSB, according to people familiar with the matter.

title: Germany Considers Tighter Investment Rules Amid Nord Stream 2 Rumors
content: The German government is examining measures that could help it stop a potential sale of the Nord Stream 2 pipeline after speculation emerged earlier this year over reviving pipeline gas deliveries from Russia.

title: B. Riley Sells Financial Adviser to Private Equity Firm TorQuest
content: B. Riley Financial Inc. has sold its financial advisory services business GlassRatner to Canadian private equity firm TorQuest Partners, adding to a series of asset sales as the financial services firm deals with its woes.

title: Roger Federer's Long-Term Deals Make Him a Tennis Billionaire
content: Former star has net worth of about $1.3 billion, according to Bloomberg Billionaires Index.

title: UK Weighs Easing Impact of Trading Book Capital Rules on Banks
content: The Bank of England is considering ways to dilute the initial impact of new trading book capital rules so the UK can move forward with a wider package of global banking reforms even as the US drags its feet.

title: BBVA Favors Proceeding With Sabadell Bid If Investors Agree
content: BBVA SA is leaning toward proceeding with its takeover offer for Banco Sabadell SA and is sounding out investors to see if they still back the deal, after Spain said the lenders wouldn’t be allowed to fully merge for several years.

title: South Africa’s Kganyago Sees Inflation-Goal Review Finished Soon
content: A review of South Africa’s inflation target by the National Treasury and the nation’s central bank is close to completion, Governor Lesetja Kganyago said.

title: Sainsbury’s Sales Rise Amid Stubborn UK Food Price Inflation
content: J Sainsbury Plc’s sales rose more than expected as the grocer used price-matching and promotions linked to its loyalty program to entice customers with food inflation accelerating across the UK.

title: Korean Stocks Gain on Renewed Optimism Over Corporate Reforms
content: South Korean stocks advanced Tuesday, as shares of holding companies rallied on hopes that revisions to the Commercial Act will be approved by the parliament this week.

title: Norway Pension Fund Blacklists Firms Supplying Israeli Army
content: Norway’s largest private pension fund has excluded two defense companies from its portfolio, citing their ties to the Israeli military and the war in Gaza.

title: ECB Shouldn’t Be Complacent About Inflation, Nagel Says
content: The European Central Bank “shouldn’t be too complacent” about having brought inflation under control, ECB Governing Council member Joachim Nagel tells Bloomberg’s Francine Lacqua in Sintra, Portugal. He also discusses volatility brought on by geopolitics and stresses the need to reduce trade uncertainty. Nagel also talks about the importance of making the euro more attractive to investors.

title: Schroders Group CIO on Diversification and US Exceptionalism
content:
Schroders Group CIO, Johanna Kyrklund, discusses her 2025 playbook for the markets, as investors weigh risks from tariffs and geopolitical tensions.
She appeared on Bloomberg's Insight with Haslinda Amin. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Horizons Middle East & Africa 07/01/2025
content: Horizons Middle East & Africa is your daily spotlight on one of the world's fastest-growing regions. Live from Dubai, we bring you the latest global markets and analysis, plus news-making interviews, with a special focus on MEA. All that and more, as you head to the office in the Gulf, pause for lunch in Hong Kong, or start your day in London or Johannesburg.  (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Absa’s New Chief Plots Turnaround After Years of CEO Tumult
content: Absa Group Ltd.’s new chief executive officer is aiming to turn the bank’s retail unit into the biggest in South Africa, revamp its regional operations and bring stability to a firm that has seen six top managers in as many years.

title: ECB’s Nagel Sees Inflation in ‘Calmer Waters’ But Caution Needed
content: The European Central Bank has brought inflation under control but mustn’t become complacent due to the highly volatile geopolitical backdrop, according to Governing Council member Joachim Nagel.

title: European Banks’ First-Half Stock Gains Are Biggest This Century
content: European bank stocks just completed their strongest first-half since 1997, and in doing so extended what has been a golden run for the sector.

title: Japan’s 10-Year Bond Auction Gives Support Ahead of 30-Year Sale
content: Demand at Japan’s sale of 10-year government notes was relatively strong in a boost to sentiment going into a key auction of 30-year bonds later this week.

title: Aviva’s £3.7 Billion Direct Line Deal Gets UK Regulator’s Nod
content: Aviva Plc’s plan to buy Direct Line Insurance Group Plc for roughly £3.7 billion ($5.09 billion) to create the UK’s largest motor insurer has been given the nod from the country’s competition regulator.

title: Al Marzooqi: $1B Acquisition Cements Tabreed's Position
content: Abu-Dhabi based firm Tabreed has acquired local firm PAL Cooling in a joint venture with CVC DIF in a deal worth $1B. This will help expand Tabreed's portfolio and capabilities as the real estate sector in Abu Dhabi continues to grow. CEO of Tabreed, Khalid Al Marzooqi spoke to Bloomberg's Lizzy Burden on Horizons Middle East and Africa on the acquisition plus their expansion pipeline plans. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Oil Steadies as Market Girds for OPEC+ Production Quota Decision
content: Oil steadied around the lowest level since early June, with the focus turning to how much OPEC+ will increase output quotas this weekend.

title: Fahmy: Syria Distancing from Israel; Negotiating Via US
content: President Trump has signed an executive order terminating US sanctions on Syria, as part of efforts to boost the nation's struggling economy and support the new government after rebels overthrew President Bashar Al-Assad last year. Dalia Fahmy, Director of International Relations & Diplomacy at Long Island University spoke to Bloomberg's Lizzy Burden on Horizons Middle East and Africa about the relations between Israel and Syria. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Taiwan Dollar Surges More Than 2% as Traders Test Central Bank
content: The Taiwan dollar surged more than 2% in another day of volatility for the currency, as exporters’ sales of the greenback tested the central bank’s tolerance for local currency strength.

title: Heavy Rainfall, Severe Weather Expected for Australia’s East Coast
content: Sydney’s airport has been temporarily reduced to a single runway as the city potentially faces more than a month’s worth of rain in coming days as an intense low-pressure system off the east coast batters the city, along with regions already hit by extreme flooding this year.

title: China, Asia EM Stocks Face Hurdles After Blockbuster 1H | The China Show 7/1/2025
content: “Bloomberg: The China Show” is your definitive source for news and analysis on the world's second-biggest economy. From politics and policy to tech and trends, Yvonne Man and Annabelle Droulers give global investors unique insight, delivering in-depth discussions with the newsmakers who matter. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Global Stock Rally Extends in Asia, Dollar Steady: Markets Wrap
content: Stocks kicked off the second half by building on a record-breaking rally as expectations grow that the US economy will withstand uncertainties from President Donald Trump’s tariff agenda.

title: Warburg Nears €800 Million Deal for Ski Helmet Maker Uvex
content: Warburg Pincus is close to acquiring a majority stake in Uvex Group, the German maker of ski helmets and goggles, people with knowledge of the matter said.

title: EU Prepared to Accept US Universal Tariff
content: The European Union is willing to accept a trade arrangement with the US that includes a 10% universal tariff on many of its exports, but wants the US to commit to lower rates on key sectors. The bloc is also pushing the US for quotas and exemptions to effectively lower Washington’s 25% tariff on automobiles and car parts as well as its 50% tariff on steel and aluminum, according to people familiar with the matter. The EU has until July 9 to clinch a trade arrangement with Donald Trump before tar

title: Abu Dhabi Utility Tabreed Considers More Deals After Buying PAL
content: Abu Dhabi-based utility National Central Cooling Co. sees scope for further acquisitions after announcing a $1 billion deal to buy another air-conditioning provider in the United Arab Emirates capital.

title: Shareholders of Saudi’s Acwa Approve $1.9 Billion Rights Issue
content: Saudi Arabia’s Acwa Power Co. will proceed with its 7.1 billion riyals ($1.9 billion) rights issue after gaining the approval of its shareholders, marking a key step in its plan to fund an aggressive expansion in renewable and clean energy projects.

title: Macau Gaming Revenue Soars Past Estimate on Concert Fervor
content: Macau’s monthly gaming revenue rose 19% in June, exceeding analyst expectations as visitors poured in to the world’s biggest gambling hub for Cantonese pop concerts and other entertainment offerings.

title: ECB’s Simkus Warns of Fragile Inflation Path Due to Euro, Energy
content: The European Central Bank has fulfilled its inflation goal but volatility in foreign-exchange and commodities markets means the outlook for prices is murky, according to Governing Council member Gediminas Simkus.

title: Gold Rises for Second Day on US Rate-Cut Bets, Dollar Weakness
content: Gold climbed for a second day on optimism that the Federal Reserve will resume rate cuts this half, while investors continued to monitor US trade talks before a July 9 tariff deadline.

title: China Raises Quota for Foreign Investment, Ending 13-Month Pause
content: China has increased the amount of money that approved investors can put into overseas assets for the first time since May last year as its relaxes its control over capital outflows.

title: Can the Quad Counter China in the Indo-Pacific?
content: Australian Foreign Minister Penny Wong is in Washington to meet US Secretary of State Marco Rubio and their Japanese and Indian counterparts for a meeting of the so-called Quad nations. CSIS Senior Adviser and Australia Chair Charles Edel says the Quad plays a critical role in the Indo-Pacific, as the four nations share concerns about China's growing power.  Edel discussed Canberra's ties with key allies and the impact of Trump's policies on "Bloomberg: The Asia Trade." (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Thai Court Suspends Prime Minister as It Probes Ethics Case
content: Thailand’s Constitutional Court has suspended Prime Minister Paetongtarn Shinawatra from office until it rules on a petition seeking her ouster for alleged ethical violations — the biggest blow yet to her less-than one-year-old government.

title: Poland Likely to Impose Temporary Controls at German Border
content: Poland may impose temporary checks along its border with Germany, Foreign Minister Radoslaw Sikorski said.

title: Trump Takes Aim at Musk Over EV Subsidies; Tesla Shares Slump
content: President Donald Trump lashed out at Elon Musk on Tuesday, accusing the Tesla Inc. and SpaceX chief executive officer of benefiting excessively from government electric vehicle subsidies. Tesla shares tumbled.

title: China Sanctions Former Philippine Senator as Tensions Swell
content: China has sanctioned former Philippine Senator Francis Tolentino, prohibiting him from entering mainland China, Hong Kong and Macau, in a rare move as tensions with Manila rise.

title: Turkey Detains Cartoonist in Prophet Depiction Dispute
content: Turkish police detained a cartoonist late Monday over an illustration in a satirical magazine that authorities allege depicts the Prophet Muhammad.

title: Senate Pulls All-Nighter on Trump Tax Bill With GOP Divided
content: Senate Republican leaders continue to scrounge for votes to pass Donald Trump’s $3.3 trillion tax and spending bill as lingering intraparty fights threaten to upend the legislative centerpiece of the president’s domestic agenda.

title: Trump Lifts Syria Sanctions in Bid to Boost New Government
content: President Donald Trump signed an executive order terminating American sanctions on Syria, aiming to boost the Arab nation’s battered economy and support the new government after rebels overthrew the regime of Bashar Al-Assad last year.

title: The Future of Modern Warfare Is Being Built in Ukraine
content: After more than three years of all-out war with Russia, the country has turned into a factory of weaponry that’s redefining the battlefield.

title: Study Warns Trump’s Plan for US Aid Cuts Risks 14 Million Additional Deaths
content: Deep cuts to the US Agency for International Development and its potential dismantling under President Donald Trump could result in about 14 million additional deaths by 2030, according to a study released in a prominent medical journal.

title: China’s Private Factory Gauge Rebounds After US Trade Truce
content: China’s manufacturing activity rebounded in June, according to a private survey, suggesting relief after a trade-war truce with the US.

title: Trump Blasts Japan on Rice, Hassett Flags Looming Trade Deals
content: President Donald Trump threatened to proceed with ramping up tariffs on Japan, while his top economic adviser said the White House aims to finalize deals with partners after the July 4 holiday.

title: Thai PM Revamps Cabinet in Bid to Steady Wobbly Government
content: Thai Prime Minister Paetongtarn Shinawatra revamped her cabinet, a move aimed at easing a political crisis that brought her government to the brink over her handling of a border dispute.

title: Solar, Wind Industries See Existential Threat in Senate Tax Bill
content: A proposed excise tax would exacerbate the pain from the phaseout of subsidies.

title: Mexico Passes Anti-Money Laundering Bill After US Accuses Banks
content: Mexican lawmakers approved a bill designed to better clamp down on money laundering, days after the US Treasury accused three local financial firms of facilitating transactions of companies linked to drug trafficking.

title: Harvard-White House Talks Stall, Threatening Quick Settlement
content: Harvard University’s talks with the White House have stalled, according to a person familiar with the matter, threatening a quick resolution to a standoff that’s endangering the school’s finances and upending foreign student plans.

title: NYC Passes $116 Billion Budget With Boost to Migrant Legal Aid
content: New York City Mayor Eric Adams reached a deal with the City Council on a $115.9 billion budget, adding new funding for legal services for migrants and more money for early childhood education.

title: Senate Republicans Seek to Ease Solar and Wind Tax Credit Cutoff
content: A group of Senate Republicans is pushing a plan to soften an aggressive planned phase out of subsidies for wind and solar projects under President Donald Trump’s tax-and-spending package.

title: US Plans to Boost Soy Exports to Italy and Form New Task Force
content: Italy will increase its imports of US soybeans as part of a new effort to rebalance trade between the two countries, US Agriculture Secretary Brooke Rollins told reporters Monday after meeting with her Italian counterpart.

title: What Are the Digital Services Taxes Drawing Trump’s Ire?
content: Digital services taxes targeting the revenue of big technology companies have returned as a flash point in President Donald Trump’s efforts to rewrite the rules of global trade.

title: Netanyahu Is Set to Meet Trump at White House on July 7
content: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is expected to meet with President Donald Trump at the White House on July 7, according to Israeli and US officials, as the administration urges its ally to end the war in Gaza and secure the release of the remaining hostages held by Hamas.

title: A Trio of US Treasury Hacks Exposes a Pattern Making Banks Nervous
content: In three major hacks, Treasury didn’t deploy cybersecurity measures that could have prevented the attacks or flagged the intruders sooner, a Bloomberg News investigation found.

title: Thai Political Crisis Deepens as Shinawatras Face Legal Battles
content: Thailand’s most influential political dynasty is facing two high-profile legal battles, with an unfavorable outcome for Prime Minister Paetongtarn Shinawatra likely to deepen a political crisis that’s already pushed her government to the brink of collapse.

title: Musk Lashes Out at Tax Bill Proponents, Threatens to Unseat Lawmakers
content: Elon Musk once again threatened to ramp up his political spending, this time targeting nearly every sitting Republican in Congress who has signaled support for President Donald Trump’s multi-trillion dollar tax bill.

title: Judge Seeks US Assurances on Deportations in Birthright Case
content: A judge overseeing a challenge to President Donald Trump’s restrictions on automatic birthright citizenship asked the US government to confirm it won’t seek to deport impacted children during the Supreme Court’s 30-day pause on enforcement of the directive.

title: EU to Accept Trump Universal Tariff But Seeks Key Exemptions
content: The European Union is willing to accept a trade arrangement with the US that includes a 10% universal tariff on many of the bloc’s exports, but wants the US to commit to lower rates on key sectors such as pharmaceuticals, alcohol, semiconductors and commercial aircraft.

title: Richest 20% Get an Average $6,055 Income Boost in Trump Tax Bill
content: The Senate’s version of President Donald Trump’s proposed tax cut bill will cost the bottom 20% of taxpayers an average of $560 a year while giving an average boost of $6,055 to those at the top end.

title: Trump’s TikTok Buyer Is the Same Group Behind a Previous Stalled Bid
content: The prospective buyer of TikTok’s American operations cited by President Donald Trump is the same investor consortium including Oracle Corp., Blackstone Inc. and venture capital firm Andreessen Horowitz, whose bid for the app had stalled amid US-China trade tensions, according to a person familiar with the matter.

title: Trump, Republicans Rush to Overcome Internal Clashes on Tax Bill
content: Republican Party leaders are rushing to overcome lingering internal fights over President Donald Trump’s massive tax and spending package as Democrats launch attacks to exploit the divisions.

title: Starmer’s Welfare Overhaul Hangs in Balance Ahead of Key Vote
content: UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer is girding for what could be the most consequential vote of his premiership, with Labour rebels warning that the government’s welfare overhaul still risks defeat despite huge concessions to push it through parliament.

title: Chile Peso Gains as Communist Win Is Seen as a Step Too Far for Left
content: Chile’s peso jumped on Monday as a landslide victory for Communist Jeannette Jara in a left-wing presidential primary damped the chances of that alliance winning November’s election.

content: Standard Chartered Plc is facing a $2.7 billion lawsuit from liquidators alleging it played a role in enabling the laundering of billions of dollars misappropriated from Malaysian sovereign wealth fund 1MDB.

title: Starmer’s Welfare Overhaul to Face Key Vote
content: UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer is facing a crucial vote on a welfare overhaul. The PM says the revised package of reforms to disability benefits are necessary to slow the pace of Britain’s welfare costs and get people back to work. Bloomberg’s Lizzy Burden reports.

title: SARB’s Kganyago on South Africa Inflation Target, Policy
content: South African Reserve Bank Governor Lesetja Kganyago said a review of the nation’s inflation target by the National Treasury and the central bank is close to completion. Speaking to Bloomberg’s Francine Lacqua on the sidelines of a European Central Bank forum in Sintra, Portugal, the SARB governor also discussed the broader inflation situation and restrictive monetary policy.

content: Korea Investment Corporation Chairman and CEO, Park Il Young, tells Bloomberg’s David Ingles why the sovereign wealth fund is committed to investing in the US and confident about the outlook for US treasuries and the wider economy.

title: Sen. Mark Warner: Tax Bill Has a Heap of Problems
content: Senator Mark Warner (D) Virginia discusses the Tax Bill and whether or not he expects a floor vote some time soon. Senator Warner talks about the various issues he has with the legislation, including healthcare cuts, and what he expects to see during the Midterm elections next year. Senator Mark Warner speaks with Joe Mathieu on the late edition of Bloomberg's "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

title: How Involved Will Trump Be in Tax Bill Negotiations?
content: Bloomberg's Michael Shephard shares his thoughts on the timeline of the Trump Tax Bill and how much to expect President Trump to be involved in the legislative process as Congress has placed a self-imposed deadline of July 4th to pass the bill. Michael also talks about the President putting pressure on the Federal Reserve to lower interest rates. Michael speaks with Kailey Leinz on the late edition of Bloomberg's "Balance of Power." title: Chip-Design Firm SkyeChip Is Close to a Malaysian IPO, CEO Says
content: Malaysian semiconductor designer SkyeChip Sdn. is “close” to an initial public offering after posting consecutive years of revenue and profit growth, said Chief Executive Officer Fong Swee Kiang.

title: SAP Wins Early Round in US Legal Fight With Celonis
content: SAP SE won an early round in a lawsuit filed in the US by one of Europe’s most valuable startups accusing the German technology giant of illegally wielding its market power.

title: Korea Wealth Fund to Boost Bets on AI Startups, Eyes China Tech
content: South Korea’s sovereign wealth fund plans to increase allocations to tech startups and venture capital funds as part of its broader push to deepen exposure to artificial intelligence and other disruptive technologies.

title: Insurance Firm Accelerant Files for IPO, Disclosing Rising Sales
content: Accelerant Holdings filed for an initial public offering, joining a rush of insurance-related listings in the US.

title: Struggling Semiconductor Firm Wolfspeed Files for Bankruptcy
content: Wolfspeed Inc., a chipmaker caught in President Donald Trump’s push to reshape Biden-era tech subsidies, filed bankruptcy to enact a creditor-backed plan to slash $4.6 billion in debt.

title: A Trio of US Treasury Hacks Exposes a Pattern Making Banks Nervous
content: In three major hacks, Treasury didn’t deploy cybersecurity measures that could have prevented the attacks or flagged the intruders sooner, a Bloomberg News investigation found.

title: Apple Weighs Using Anthropic or OpenAI to Power Siri in Major Reversal
content: Apple Inc. is considering using artificial intelligence technology from Anthropic PBC or OpenAI to power a new version of Siri, sidelining its own in-house models in a potentially blockbuster move aimed at turning around its flailing AI effort.

title: Trump Blasts AT&T for Poor Network Performance During Call
content: US President Donald Trump blasted AT&T Inc. for poor network performance during a conference call he was holding with faith leaders on Monday.

title: Microsoft’s Sales Chief to Take Sabbatical With Layoffs Looming
content: Microsoft Corp.’s top sales executive is planning to take a two-month sabbatical, a move that coincides with an expected wave of terminations targeting his organization.

title: Apple Loses Bid to Dismiss Justice Department Antitrust Suit
content: Apple Inc. lost its bid to throw out an antitrust case brought by the US Justice Department and a group of state attorneys general on Monday, a victory for the aggressive posture taken during the Biden administration and carried on by enforcers under President Donald Trump.

title: Robinhood CEO Sees Crypto, Traditional Finance Merging
content: Robinhood CEO and co-founder Vlad Tenev says he expects crypto and traditional finance merging and announces the company is expanding into the EU on “Bloomberg The Close.”

title: Trump Says TikTok Buyer Group Found | Bloomberg Tech 6/30/2025
content: Bloomberg’s Caroline Hyde and Ed Ludlow discuss President Donald Trump’s claim that he has found a buyer group for TikTok. Plus, Canada withdraws its digital services tax in a move to restart trade talks with the US. And Elon Musk slammed the US Senate's version of President Donald Trump's spending bill for removing electric vehicle tax credits. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Mexican Fintech Klar Raises $190 Million at $800 Million Valuation
content: Mexican fintech Klar said it has raised $190 million through a Series C funding round, led by US private equity firm General Atlantic, that valued the company at more than $800 million.

title: Paramount, Trump Confirm Settlement Talks, Delay Court Case
content: Paramount Global is in advanced talks to settle a lawsuit filed by US President Donald Trump that alleges the company’s CBS network deceptively edited a 60 Minutes interview with then-Vice President Kamala Harris.

title: Trump’s TikTok Buyer Is the Same Group Behind a Previous Stalled Bid
content: The prospective buyer of TikTok’s American operations cited by President Donald Trump is the same investor consortium including Oracle Corp., Blackstone Inc. and venture capital firm Andreessen Horowitz, whose bid for the app had stalled amid US-China trade tensions, according to a person familiar with the matter.

title: Musk’s X Hires Entrepreneur Nikita Bier as Head of Product
content: Elon Musk’s X has hired entrepreneur Nikita Bier as the platform’s new head of product, giving Bier a senior role atop one of the most widely used social apps in the world.

title: Zuckerberg Debuts Meta ‘Superintelligence’ Group, More Hires
content: Meta Platforms Inc. Chief Executive Officer Mark Zuckerberg announced a major restructuring of the company’s artificial intelligence group, including a commitment to developing AI “superintelligence,” or systems that can complete tasks as well as or even better than humans.

title: DailyPay Sells Bonds Tied to Fees on Wages That Workers Tap Instantly
content: Fintech company DailyPay Inc. this month sold $200 million in bonds backed by fees tied to the company’s main service, an app that lets workers access pay as soon as they’ve earned it rather than wait for paychecks.

title: US Charges North Koreans in Plot to Dupe More Than 100 Firms
content: The US Justice Department announced one arrest and charges against nine more people in connection with an alleged scheme in which North Koreans posed as American tech workers to gain lucrative jobs and fund the country’s government.

title: Legal Software Startup Clio to Acquire VLex for $1 Billion
content: Canadian software company Themis Solutions Inc. struck a deal to buy legal data and research company vLex LLC for $1 billion in cash and shares.

title: International Criminal Court Says It’s Contained Cyber Incident
content: The International Criminal Court contained a “sophisticated and targeted” cybersecurity incident that it first identified last week, the organization said in a statement Monday.

title: UK Stands by Digital Tax After Canada Bows to Trump Pressure
content: The UK is currently planning to keep its digital services tax, a person familiar with the matter said, after Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney scrapped their own levy to restart trade talks with President Donald Trump’s administration.

title: Audacy and iHeart Sign Program-Distribution Deal to Compete With Spotify
content: Audacy Inc.  and iHeartMedia Inc., the two largest US radio broadcasters, are teaming up in a program distribution deal designed to reach more listeners and better compete with streaming leader Spotify Technology SA.

title: Oracle Inks Cloud Deal Worth $30 Billion a Year
content: Oracle Corp. said it has signed a single cloud deal worth $30 billion in annual revenue — more than the current size of its entire cloud infrastructure business.

title: Morgan Stanley Reshuffles Tech Investment Banking Leadership
content: Morgan Stanley has appointed Drew Guevara as a global co-head of technology investment banking as part of a broader reshuffle of one of the Wall Street bank’s most storied franchises.

title: US Warns Iran-Tied Hackers Pose Ongoing Risk to American Firms
content: Iran-affiliated hackers remain a potential threat to critical sectors of the US economy, including defense contractors and other American organizations, according to a bulletin published Monday from the FBI, the National Security Agency, the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency and the Defense Cyber Crime Center.

title: Google Is Betting on a Fusion Future in Power Deal With Commonwealth
content: Google will also invest again in Commonwealth, which expects its first commercial plant will generate power in the early 2030s

title: Musk Lieutenants Depart Tesla and Leave Leadership Void
content: Welcome to Tech In Depth, our daily newsletter about the business of tech from Bloomberg’s journalists around the world. Today, Ed Ludlow looks at the challenge facing Elon Musk and Tesla following the departure of top executives.

title: Amazon Misses Out on Switch 2 Sales After Nintendo Pulled Products From US Site
content: Nintendo Co. pulled its products from Amazon.com Inc.’s US site after a disagreement over unauthorized sales, meaning the e-commerce company missed out on the recent debut of Nintendo’s Switch 2 — the biggest game console launch of all time.

title: ECB’s Guindos Says Euro Gain Past $1.20 Would Be Complicated
content: European Central Bank Vice President Luis de Guindos said an advance in the euro beyond $1.20 could prove tricky for policymakers but current levels aren’t cause for concern.

title: UK House Prices Post Sharpest Drop Since 2023 Amid Tax Rise
content: UK house prices fell the most in more than two years in June, in a sign buyers are under pressure after an increase in transaction taxes in April, according to one of Britain’s top mortgage lenders.

title: ECB’s Nagel Sees Inflation in ‘Calmer Waters’ But Caution Needed
content: The European Central Bank has brought inflation under control but mustn’t become complacent due to the highly volatile geopolitical backdrop, according to Governing Council member Joachim Nagel.

title: Macau Gaming Revenue Soars Past Estimate on Concert Fervor
content: Macau’s monthly gaming revenue rose 19% in June, exceeding analyst expectations as visitors poured in to the world’s biggest gambling hub for Cantonese pop concerts and other entertainment offerings.

title: ECB’s Simkus Warns of Fragile Inflation Path Due to Euro, Energy
content: The European Central Bank has fulfilled its inflation goal but volatility in foreign-exchange and commodities markets means the outlook for prices is murky, according to Governing Council member Gediminas Simkus.

title: Singapore Disease Testing Helps Fill the Gap Left by US Funding Cuts
content: Wastewater could offer clues to the next pandemic.

title: ECB Gets Another ‘Moderate Hawk’ as Dutch Central-Bank Veteran Exits
content: Olaf Sleijpen, the European Central Bank’s newest interest-rate setter, is about to continue where his Dutch predecessor left off.

title: China’s Private Factory Gauge Rebounds After US Trade Truce
content: China’s manufacturing activity rebounded in June, according to a private survey, suggesting relief after a trade-war truce with the US.

title: South Korean Exports Rebound in June on Record Chip Sales
content: South Korea’s exports rebounded on the back of record sales of semiconductors, providing a brief boost to the trade-dependent economy as companies accelerated shipments before broad duties on goods shipped to the US are set to rise.

title: Asia Manufacturing Slumps Anew Even as Some Data Show Resilience
content: The slowdown in Asia’s manufacturing activity deepened further in June, a warning sign for the region’s growth prospects as tariffs on shipments to the US are poised to increase next week.

title: Japan’s Business Confidence Beats Expectations Despite Tariffs
content: Confidence among Japan’s large manufacturers edged up in June, reflecting resilience in the face of the escalating US tariff campaign and backing the case for another Bank of Japan interest rate hike this year.

title: Singapore Home Prices Rise for Third Quarter on Domestic Demand
content: Singapore private home prices rose for a third straight quarter, buoyed by local demand.

title: Dalio Calls for Bipartisan Solution to Address US ‘Debt Bomb’
content: There is no way that the US “deficit/debt bomb” problem can be sustainably dealt with unless there is a bipartisan mix of tax revenue increases and spending decreases, Bridgewater Associates founder Ray Dalio wrote in a post on X.

title: New Zealand Firms Remain Upbeat Despite Weak Trading Conditions
content: New Zealand businesses were more upbeat about the future in the second quarter even as their own trading remained sluggish, according to the New Zealand Institute of Economic Research.

title: UK Shop Prices Rise as Higher Taxes, Food Costs Hit Supermarkets
content: UK shop prices rose for the first time in almost a year, with supermarkets in particular hurt by higher taxes and wholesale costs.

title: US Plans to Boost Soy Exports to Italy and Form New Task Force
content: Italy will increase its imports of US soybeans as part of a new effort to rebalance trade between the two countries, US Agriculture Secretary Brooke Rollins told reporters Monday after meeting with her Italian counterpart.

title: Australian Workers Get a Final Boost to Their Retirement Savings
content: From today, Australian workers get a final boost to their mandatory retirement contributions — a key milestone for the country’s A$4.1 trillion ($2.7 trillion) pension system.

title: EU to Accept Trump Universal Tariff But Seeks Key Exemptions
content: The European Union is willing to accept a trade arrangement with the US that includes a 10% universal tariff on many of the bloc’s exports, but wants the US to commit to lower rates on key sectors such as pharmaceuticals, alcohol, semiconductors and commercial aircraft.

title: Argentina Grew More Than Expected After Milei Lifts Controls
content: Argentina’s economy grew more than expected in April as President Javier Milei loosened some currency controls as part of a $20 billion agreement with the International Monetary Fund.

title: ECB Strategy Fixes Help Avoid ‘False Certainty,’ Lagarde Says
content: Tweaks to the European Central Bank’s strategy unveiled Monday will allow policymakers to deliver more nuanced communication in an increasing unpredictable world, President Christine Lagarde said.

title: Starmer’s Welfare Overhaul Hangs in Balance Ahead of Key Vote
content: UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer is girding for what could be the most consequential vote of his premiership, with Labour rebels warning that the government’s welfare overhaul still risks defeat despite huge concessions to push it through parliament.

title: Goldman Sachs Pulls Forward Fed Rate-Cut Forecast to September
content: Goldman Sachs pulled forward its forecast for Federal Reserve interest rate cuts, and is now calling for the central bank to resume reductions in September rather than December, as the inflationary effects of tariffs “look a bit smaller” than expected.

title: Fed’s Bostic Says Tariff Pass-Through May Be Slow, Persistent
content: Federal Reserve Bank of Atlanta President Raphael Bostic said tariff price increases may be incremental instead of a one-time bump, which could result in more persistent upward pressure on inflation.

title: Kenyan Inflation Holds Steady at 3.8% as Water, Power Costs Ease
content: Kenya’s annual inflation rate flatlined in June helped by slower growth in utilities and housing prices.

title: EU Seals New Trade Deal With Ukraine as Tariff-Free Regime Ends
content: The European Union reached a new trade arrangement with Ukraine to replace the special tariff-free regime that was put in place in the wake of Russia’s full-scale invasion.

title: StoneX Intends to Acquire Units of Bank Mired in US Drug Claims
content: StoneX Group Inc. said it’s seeking to acquire US units of Mexican bank Intercam Banco SA, which last week was among three firms accused by the Trump administration of facilitating money laundering for drug traffickers.

title: Bessent Says He Wouldn't Boost Long-Term Bond Sales at Today's Rates
content: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent indicated it wouldn’t make sense for the government to ramp up sales of longer-term securities given where yields are today, though he held out hope that interest rates across maturities will be falling as inflation slows.

title: US Tariff Pause Brings Little Cheer to Lesotho’s Textile Industry
content: A temporary pause on US tariffs has brought little relief to Lesotho’s textile industry, which has suffered layoffs and shuttered factories after orders from America dried up.

title: Australian Home Prices Climb, Fueled by Falling Borrowing Costs
content: Australian home prices climbed for a fifth straight month, fueled by the Reserve Bank’s two interest-rate cuts this year and expectations of more to come.

title: India Remains Key Driver of Global Growth, RBI’s Malhotra Says
content: India’s central bank said the country remains a key driver of global economic growth as domestic inflation continues to align with its target.

title: Mediolanum Sells Its 3.5% Mediobanca Stake Amid Paschi Bid
content: Banca Mediolanum SpA sold its 3.5% stake in Mediobanca SpA for €548.4 million ($646 million), exiting its position in the investment bank currently at the center of a takeover bid by Banca Monte dei Paschi di Siena SpA.

title: Renault Takes $11 Billion Non-Cash Loss in Nissan Change
content: Renault SA will recognize an estimated €9.5 billion ($11.2 billion) non-cash loss after changing the way it accounts for its stake in ailing Japanese carmaker Nissan Motor Co.

title: BBVA Sticks With Sabadell Bid Despite Madrid’s Merger Ban
content: BBVA SA decided to keep its takeover offer for Banco Sabadell SA alive even though the Spanish government’s decision to ban a merger for several years has cast doubt over how it will pan out.

title: UK Power Grids Investor Returns Set to Jump Amid Expansion Push
content: The UK energy regulator set out a plan to increase the returns that investors can get on equity put into grid companies helping underpin a huge push to upgrade critical infrastructure during the next five years.

title: BNP Paribas Completes Acquisition of Axa’s Asset Management Unit
content: BNP Paribas SA has finalized its purchase of Axa SA’s investment unit, creating one of Europe’s largest asset managers.

title: Milan Travel Guide: Where to Stay, What to Do, See and Eat
content: Forget the Milan you know, the one dominated by the fashion hordes and global business set in gleaming towers. The Milan to love is the one you haven’t met—until now.

title: Macau Gaming Revenue Soars Past Estimate on Concert Fervor
content: Macau’s monthly gaming revenue rose 19% in June, exceeding analyst expectations as visitors poured in to the world’s biggest gambling hub for Cantonese pop concerts and other entertainment offerings.

title: Singapore Disease Testing Helps Fill the Gap Left by US Funding Cuts
content: Wastewater could offer clues to the next pandemic.

title: Chinese Automakers Grab Record Hybrid Market Share in Europe
content: Chinese automakers continued to expand their European foothold in May, capturing the highest share ever of hybrid-car sales and the biggest slice of the electric-vehicle market in 10 months.

title: Sapura Energy Restructuring in ‘Final Stages,’ Company Says
content: Malaysian oil and gas contractor Sapura Energy Bhd.’s restructuring plan to restore financial stability is entering its “final stages,” according to the company’s first-quarter earnings statement.

title: Three Senior Mizuho FX/Rates Traders Exit in Singapore, London
content: Three senior executives have left Mizuho Financial Group Inc.’s foreign-exchange and rates trading teams in Singapore and London, according to people familiar with the matter.

title: Hershey to Remove Synthetic Dyes From Its Snacks by End of 2027
content: Hershey Co. will remove synthetic dyes from its snacks by the end of 2027, the latest in a string of major food companies that have announced similar moves.

title: Singapore Home Prices Rise for Third Quarter on Domestic Demand
content: Singapore private home prices rose for a third straight quarter, buoyed by local demand.

title: Natixis Aims to Double Japan Banking Staff as Market Booms
content: Natixis SA hired senior managers from JPMorgan Chase & Co. and Societe Generale SA for its new banking business in Japan and plans to double Tokyo staff in coming years as it expands the operation.

title: New World Shares Jump Following Record $11.2 Billion Loan Deal
content: New World Development Co. shares surged to the highest level this year after the company closed a record $11.2 billion loan refinancing package, helping ease investor anxiety.

title: Hong Kong Steps Up Defense of FX Peg as Fixed Range Tested Again
content: Hong Kong’s de facto central bank ramped up purchases of the city’s currency as it sought to defend a peg that has been strained by volatility in the greenback.

content: Insight with Haslinda Amin, a daily news program featuring in-depth, high-profile interviews and analysis to give viewers the complete picture on the stories that matter. The show features prominent leaders spanning the worlds of business, finance, politics and culture. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: KKR to Buy Australian Agriculture Firm ProTen From Aware Super
content: KKR & Co. agreed to acquire Australian agriculture infrastructure company ProTen Pty from Aware Super, in another Asia-Pacific deal by the US private equity firm.

content: Politics drove markets, but you needed a rearview mirror to see what was ahead.

title: Hong Kong Debuts Hit Highest Since 2022 on Share-Sale Rush
content: Listings in Hong Kong hit the highest since December 2022 last month, as a rally in the Asian financial hub’s stocks drove a rush for share sales.

title: South Korea’s Stock Market Is Having a Moment
content: Investors have flocked in as the new president looks likely to take up long-awaited reforms.

title: Manhattan Home Sales Surge 17% With Cash Buyers Leading the Way
content: Manhattan home sales in the second quarter were stronger than they’ve been in almost two years, boosted by cash buyers undeterred by the economic uncertainty created by President Donald Trump’s trade war.

title: Thai Turmoil Threatens Early Gains in World’s Worst Stock Market
content: Prime Minister Paetongtarn Shinawatra’s suspension from office has eased near-term political risks for Thailand, but investors remain wary about the country’s prospects and market outlook.

title: Stablecoin Push Gains Ground in China in New Challenge to US
content: China faces growing calls from policy advisers and economists to explore using stablecoins for cross-border payments, as the US moves to entrench the dollar’s dominance through the still-emerging technology.

title: Poland to Weigh Green Bond Potential After €1.2 Billion Sale
content: Poland should continue to look at green bonds as a means of financing over the longer term after selling its first such securities in more than six years, according to the country’s debt chief.

title: Major Chinese Ports Keep Iranian Oil Flowing Despite Sanctions
content: Some of China’s largest ports have received Iranian crude this year, supporting a multi-billion oil trade and highlighting a significant gap in US efforts to curb funds for Tehran’s military and to uphold existing sanctions.

title: What’s the Hong Kong Dollar Peg and Why Is It Causing Such a Stir?
content: Pegged to the US dollar since 1983, the Hong Kong dollar is usually a dull currency. Except when it’s not, like this year.

content: Before the trading day starts we bring you a digest of the key news and events that are likely to move markets. Today we look at:

title: Starmer Emerges From Welfare Bout Weaker and Billions in Red
content: Keir Starmer dramatically abandoned his flagship welfare reforms to avoid a historic defeat, leaving the UK prime minister’s authority badly damaged and his government facing a widening fiscal hole to fill.

title: Lithuania Eyes Troops Visit Pact With Philippines, Slams China
content: Lithuania will consider a visiting forces agreement with the Philippines, as it builds security ties with the Southeast Asian nation while criticizing Beijing’s actions in the South China Sea.

title: State Capture, Graft Holding Back Kenya’s Economy, AfDB Says
content: Kenya needs to tackle graft that’s draining the nation’s finances and undermining economic growth, according to the African Development Bank.

title: Dalai Lama Confirms Institution Will Continue With Successor
content: The 14th Dalai Lama, spiritual leader of the Tibetans, has confirmed that the centuries-old institution will continue after his death and his office has the “sole authority” to find the successor.

title: Paramount Settles Trump’s ‘60 Minutes’ Suit for $16 Million
content: Paramount Global reached a settlement with President Donald Trump over a lawsuit that alleged election interference by the company’s CBS news network when it showed two different versions of a 60 Minutes interview with then-Vice President Kamala Harris in October.

title: The American Toymaker Suing Trump Over Destructive Tariffs
content: Today on the Big Take Asia podcast: US companies are grappling with tariff challenges on their Chinese supply chains. How one toymaker is fighting back.

title: Mexico Senate OKs Security Bills Modeled on Sheinbaum’s Approach
content: Mexico’s Senate approved several government-backed security bills that aim to bolster crime fighting by improving investigation and intelligence capacities, an approach the opposition says risks allowing invasive surveillance.

title: UK Royals Can Sacrifice More Than Queen Victoria’s Train
content: The cost of funding for King Charles and his family announced as Labour rebels reject benefit cuts.

title: Stablecoin Push Gains Ground in China in New Challenge to US
content: China faces growing calls from policy advisers and economists to explore using stablecoins for cross-border payments, as the US moves to entrench the dollar’s dominance through the still-emerging technology.

title: Israel Urges China to Pressure Iran to Rein In Nuclear Ambitions
content: Israel urged China to use its economic and political sway to rein in Iran’s military and nuclear ambitions.

title: Thai Leader’s Suspension Deals New Blow to Battered Economy
content: Thailand’s ruling coalition was already fraying when a court suspended Prime Minister Paetongtarn Shinawatra on Tuesday, raising fresh doubts about her survival, the country’s economy and the future of a dynasty that has loomed over the Southeast Asian nation for decades.

title: US Tells Court It Can’t Locate Man Wrongly Sent to El Salvador
content: The Trump administration told a federal appeals court it has been unable to locate a man wrongly deported to El Salvador a week after a three-judge panel ordered that he be returned to the US.

title: US Halts Key Ukraine Weapons Deliveries Amid Russian Barrage
content: The Trump administration is halting the transfer of artillery rounds and air defenses to Ukraine, depriving the country of much-needed weapons as it endures stepped-up missile and drone attacks from Russia.

title: Trump Tariff Risks Put Asian Stocks’ Strong July Record to Test
content: A seasonal lift for Asian equities in July may be hard to come by this year as tariff and macroeconomic concerns dampen sentiment.

title: Trump Says Israel Agreed to Terms for 60-Day Gaza Ceasefire
content: President Donald Trump said Israel has agreed to the conditions needed for a 60-day ceasefire in Gaza, adding that the plan would now be presented to Hamas.

title: Macron Opens Iran Talks With Putin in First Call Since 2022
content: French President Emmanuel Macron and Vladimir Putin agreed to coordinate their approach on Iran in their first phone call since 2022, marking a rare overture from a European head to the Russian leader.

title: Mexico Congress Backs Bill to Overhaul Telecoms Regulations
content: Mexico’s lower house approved the general text of a watered-down bill to overhaul telecommunications regulations, after the proposal’s initial draft provoked objections that the government was seeking to censor critical media.

title: Costa Rica Court Votes to Revoke Presidential Immunity
content: A Costa Rican court voted to revoke President Rodrigo Chaves’s immunity in a case of alleged influence peddling.

title: FBI to Keep Headquarters in Washington as Lawmakers Protest
content: The Federal Bureau of Investigation plans to move its headquarters to the Ronald Reagan Building complex in Washington, scuttling Biden administration plans approved by Congress to move the agency to the Maryland suburbs.

title: What’s in the Trump Tax Bill That Just Passed the Senate
content: President Donald Trump’s multitrillion-dollar tax and spending package moved closer to reality after it passed the Senate Tuesday.

title: Senate Tax Bill Strikes Clean Energy But Leaves Room for Relief
content: The Senate version of President Donald Trump’s tax-and-spending bill would soften the blow for wind and solar developers, which had feared a sharp reduction in subsidies that helped spur a renewable power boom in the past few years. But the bill now faces conservatives in the House of Representatives eager to kill those credits.

title: Trump Tax Bill Hits Republican Resistance in House Ahead of Vote
content: Donald Trump’s multitrillion-dollar tax bill is running into Republican resistance in the House as moderate and ultraconservative GOP lawmakers threaten to defy the president and sink his domestic agenda.
